c: Abu Jaafar Muhammad bin Jarir bin Yazid told us: Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: We have already explained the meaning of His statement, Alif, Lam, Meem, in the past, so that there is no need to repeat it here. Likewise, the explanation of His statement, God.

x: As for the meaning of His saying:
h
There is no god but Him

, it is report from God, the Almighty, the Majestic, informing His servants that divinity is specific to Him, not to any other gods or equals, and that worship is not appropriate or permissible except for Him, due to His uniqueness in lordship and His oneness in divinity, and that everything below Him is His kingdom, and everything other than Him is His creation, and He has no partner in His authority and kingdom, as an argument from Him, the Most High, to them that since that is the case, then it is not permissible for them to worship anyone other than Him, nor to associate anyone with Him in His authority, since every worshipped thing other than Him is His kingdom, and everything that is glorified other than Him is His creation, and it is upon the slave to single out obedience to his Master, and to direct his service to his Master and Provider, and to know who among His creation was - on the day that He revealed that to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by His revelation of that to him, and His sending it to them on His tongue, may God bless him and grant him peace - who persisted in the worship of an idol or statue, or the sun or the moon, or a human being or an angel.

Or other things that the children of Adam were established upon to worship and deify - and he took him instead of his Owner and Creator as a god and lord, that he is established upon misguidance, and has deviated from the right path, and is not following the straight path, by diverting worship to someone other than him, and no one has divinity other than him.

It has been mentioned that God began the revelation of this Surah with the same opening with which He began: denying that divinity belongs to anyone other than Him, and describing Himself with the same description He had at the beginning, as an argument against a group of Christians who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Najran and argued with him about Jesus, may God’s prayers be upon him, and they blasphemed against God. So God, the Almighty, revealed about their affair and the affair of Jesus from this Surah more than eighty verses from its beginning, as an argument against them and against those who had the same statement as them, for His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they refused except to remain in their misguidance and disbelief, so He called them to the Mubahalah, but they refused and asked for the acceptance of the jizyah from them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted it from them, and they returned to their country.

However, even if this is the case, and they are the ones intended by the pilgrims, then whoever among the rest of creation is like them in disbelief in God and taking anything other than God as a lord and a god to be worshipped, they are generalized by the argument with which God Almighty argued with the one about whom these verses were revealed, and they are refuted by the Criterion with which He distinguished between him and them for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mentioning the narration from the one we mentioned, his saying about the revelation of the opening of this surah, that it was revealed about those whose description we described from among the Christians: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated that Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated that Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar said: A delegation from Najran came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace): sixty riders, among them fourteen of their nobles.

Among the fourteen were three men to whom their affairs would be referred: Al-ʿAqib, the leader of the people, their opinion-maker and their counsellor, and the one from whose advice they would not depart except, and his name was ʿAbd al-Masih. Al-Sayyid was their chief, the one who would carry out their travels and gather them, and his name was al-Ayham. Abu Haritha ibn ʿAlqamah, the brother of Bakr ibn Waʿil, was their bishop, rabbi, imam and head of their schools. Abu Haritha had been honoured among them and had studied their books until he had perfected his knowledge of their religion. The Christian kings of Rome honoured him, supported him, served him, built churches for him and bestowed favours upon him, because of what they had heard of his knowledge and his efforts in their religion. Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr said: They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and entered upon him in his mosque when he had prayed the afternoon prayer.

They were wearing the clothes of the Habrat, cloaks and robes, with the beauty of the men of Balharith ibn Kaʿb. He said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who saw them that day said: We have not seen a delegation like them after them! When the time for their prayer came, they stood up to pray in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave them! So they prayed facing the east. He said: The names of the fourteen of them to whom their matter would be entrusted were: Al-Aqib, who is Abd al-Masih, Al-Sayyid, who is Ayham, Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah, the brother of Bakr ibn Wa’il, Aws, Al-Harith, Zayd, Qays, Yazid, Nabih, Khuwaylid, Amr, Khalid, and Abdullah. And Yahanis: with sixty riders. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to them: Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah, Al-Aqib, Abd al-Masih, and Al-Ayham Al-Sayyid, and they are Christians who follow the Surat Al Imran 3:2 Allah - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. religion of the king, with differences in their matter.

They say: He is God, and they say: He is the son of God, and they say: He is the third of three, and the same is the saying of the Christians. They argue in their statement: He is God, that He used to revive the dead, heal the sick, inform of the unseen, and create from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird, and all of that is by God’s permission to make him a sign for the people. They argue that he was the son of God by saying that he had no father who knew, and he spoke in the cradle, something that no one from the children of Adam had done before him. They argue that he is the third of three by saying that God Almighty said: We did, We commanded, We created, and We decreed. They say: If he were one, he would not have said: I did, I commanded, I decreed, and I created. But he is He, Jesus, and Mary. In all of this, they say that the Qur’an was revealed, and God mentioned to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, their saying in it.

When the two rabbis spoke to him, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Become Muslims! They said: We have become Muslims. He said: You have not become Muslims, so become Muslims! They said: Yes, we became Muslims before you! He said: “You have both lied. What prevents you from becoming Muslims is your calling God the Almighty to have a son, your worship of the cross, and your eating pork.” They said: Who is his father, O Muhammad? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained silent and did not answer them. So God revealed about their statement and the differences in their entire affair the beginning of Surat Al Imran, up to eighty-some verses. He said: “Alif, Lam, Meem.
h
God - there is no god except Him

, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.” So he began the Surah by declaring Himself, the Blessed and Exalted, innocent of what they said, and His Oneness in creation and command, with no partner for Him in that - in response to their innovated disbelief, and the creation of rivals with Him - and as evidence against them for what they said about their companion, so that he might show them their misguidance.
So he said:
h
God - there is no god except Him
, meaning: He has no partner with Him in His affair.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God - there is no god except Him

, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: The Christians came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and argued with him about Jesus, son of Mary, and said to him: Who is his father? And they said lies and slander against God, there is no god except Him, He has not taken a wife or a son. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Do you not know that there is no son except that he resembles his father? They said: Yes! He said: Do you not know that our Lord is alive and does not die, and that Jesus will die? They said: Yes! He said: Do you not know that our Lord is in charge of everything, He protects it, preserves it, and provides for it? They said: Yes! He said: Does Jesus own any of that? They said: No! He said: Do you not know that nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from God, the Almighty? They said: Yes! He said: Does Jesus know anything of that except what he knows? They said: No! He said: Our Lord formed Jesus in the womb as He willed, do you know that? They said: Yes. He said: Do you not know that our Lord does not eat food, drink, or relieve himself? They said: Yes! He said: Do you not know that Jesus was carried by his mother as a woman carries, then given birth to him as a woman gives birth to her child, then nourished as a child is nourished, then he would eat food, drink, and relieve himself? They said: Yes! He said: How can this be as you claim? They said: So they recognized it, but they refused except in denial, so God the Almighty revealed: God - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.

x: The readings differed on this. So I read it as the countries read: The Living, the Self-Sustaining. Omar bin Al-Khattab and Ibn Masoud read it, as reported from them: The Living, the Standing. It was mentioned on the authority of Alqamah bin Qais that he used to recite: The Living, the Eternal.

c: Abu Kuraib told us that, he said, Uthman bin Ali told us that Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, he said:
m: I heard Alqamah reciting: The Living, the Eternal. I said: Did you hear it? He said: I do not know.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Waki’ told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Alqamah,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Alqamah
m: that something different was said, which is: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Alqamah that he recited: The Living, the Standing.

x: The reading that is not permissible other than it in our view is what the Muslims’ readings have transmitted widely, without any association or collusion, by inheritance, and what was established in their copies of the Qur’an, and that is the reading of the one who reads: The Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of his saying: the living.
Some of them said: The meaning of that from God Almighty is that He described Himself as eternal, and denied death - which is permissible for all of His creation other than Him - from Him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, Salamah bin Al-Fadl told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jaʿfar bin Al-Zubayr:
m: The Living is the one who does not die, and Jesus died and was crucified according to their saying, meaning according to the saying of the rabbis who argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Christians of Najran.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: The Living, he said: He says: The Living One who does not die.

x: Others said: The meaning of the Living, which God Almighty meant in this verse, and with which He described Himself, is that He is able to manage everything He wants and desires, and nothing He wants is impossible for Him, and that He is not like those who have no management among the gods and rivals.

Others said: The meaning of this is that He has eternal life, which has always been His attribute and will always be so. They said: He described himself as having life, because he has life - just as he described it as having knowledge, because it has knowledge - and as having power, because it has power.

The meaning of this, in my opinion, is that He described Himself as having eternal life that does not perish or cease, and He denied that which is the case with every living thing among His creation, which is perishing and the cessation of life when its time comes. So He informed His servants that He is the One who deserves to be worshipped and regarded as a god by His creation, and the Living One who does not die or perish, just as everyone who takes someone other than Him as a lord dies, and everyone who claims someone other than Him is perished. He argued with His creation that whoever perishes will disappear and die and perishes, so He is not a god who deserves to be worshipped other than the God who does not perish or die, and that the god is the eternal One who does not die, perish, or perish, and that is God,
h
there is no god but Him

We have mentioned the difference in readings in this regard, and what we choose from it, and what is the reason for which we chose what we chose from it. As for the interpretation of all the aspects that we mentioned that the recitation was recited with, they are close.
The meaning of all of that is: the guardian of everything, its provision, its management, and its disposition as He wills and loves of change, alteration, increase, and decrease, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa bin Maimun told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, may He be glorified: The Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: The One who is in charge of everything.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Al-Qayyum is the one who takes care of everything, protects it, preserves it, and provides for it.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: standing in one place. They directed it to the permanent standing with no disappearance or transition, and that God Almighty only denied about Himself, by describing Himself in this way, change and movement from one place to another, and the occurrence of the change that occurs in humans and all of His creation other than them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: The Self-Sustaining, the One who maintains His place of authority over His creation, will not cease. And Jesus, according to their statement - meaning according to the statement of the rabbis who argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of Najran about Jesus - has departed from the place he was in, and has gone away from it to another.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations is what Mujahid and Al-Rabiʿ said, that this is a description from God Almighty of Himself as the One who is in charge of everything, in His provision and protection from it, His guardianship, management and disposition of it according to His power, from the Arabs’ saying: So-and-so is in charge of the affairs of this town, meaning by that: the one who is in charge of managing its affairs. As for Al-Qayyum - if that is its meaning - it is a fa'ul from the saying of the speaker: God takes care of the affairs of His creation. Its original form is Al-Qayyum, except that the first waw of Al-Qayyum, since it was preceded by a silent ya' which is moving, was changed to a ya', so it and the ya' that came before it were made into a double ya'. This is because the Arabs do this with a moving waw if it is preceded by a silent ya'. As for the word qiyam, its root is qiywam, which is the active participle of qama yaqoum.

The moving waw of qiywam was preceded by a silent ya, so they were both made into a double ya. If Al-Qayyum were a fa’ul, it would be Al-Qawm, but it is Al-Fa’i’ul. Likewise, Al-Qayyum, if it were Al-Fa’il, it would be Al-Qawam, as it was said: Al-Sawm and Al-Qawwam, and as God, the Most High, said: Be persistently standing firm for God, witnesses in justice (al-Ma’idah 5:8), but it is Al-Fa’i’al, so it was said: Al-Qayyum. As for the value, it is the fa’il from qama yaqoom, preceded by a silent ya’, so they were made into a double ya’, as it was said: So-and-so is the master of his people from saada yasud, and this is good food from jaada yajud, and the like. And he came with these words because he intended to Surat Al Imran 3:2 Allah - there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. exaggerate in praise, so al-Qayyum, al-Qiyam, and al-Qayyim are more eloquent in praise than al-Qa’im.

And ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, chose to read it, God willing, as al-Qayyam, because that is the most common language of the people of Hijaz in words with three letters from the letter ya’ and the letter waw. So they say to a man who wanders a lot: al-Sayyagh, and they say to a man who wanders a lot: al-Diyar. And it has been said that the statement of God, the Most High: Leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dwelling
r
is actually dawar, an active participle from dar yadawar, but it was revealed in the language of the people of Hijaz, and it was confirmed as such in the Qur’an.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed on this.
So I read it as the countries read: The Living, the Self-Sustaining.
Omar bin Al-Khattab and Ibn Masoud read it, as reported from them: The Living, the Standing.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that is not permissible other than it in our view is what the Muslims’ readings have transmitted widely, without any association or collusion, by inheritance, and what was established in their copies of the Qur’an, and that is the reading of the one who reads: The Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.
As for the interpretation of all the aspects that we mentioned that the recitation was recited with, they are close.

And ‘Umar, may God be pleased with him, chose to read it, God willing, as al-Qayyam, because that is the most common language of the people of Hijaz in words with three letters from the letter ya’ and the letter waw.

x: God Almighty says: O Muhammad, your Lord and the Lord of Jesus and the Lord of all things, is the Lord who sent down to you the Book - meaning by the Book the Qur'an - in truth meaning: in truth regarding what the people of the Torah and the Gospel differed about, and regarding what your disputers from the Christians of Najran and all the polytheists other than them disagreed with you about, confirming what was before it meaning by that the Qur'an, that it confirms what came before it of the books of God that He sent down to His prophets and messengers, and confirms what the messengers of God brought from Him. Because the one who sent down all of that is one, so there is no difference in it, and if it had been from someone other than Him, there would have been a lot of difference in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Confirming what came before it. He said: What came before it of a book or a messenger.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Confirming what came before it, what came before it of a book or a messenger.

c: Muhammad bin Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jaʿfar bin al-Zubayr:
m: The Book was revealed to you in truth, meaning: in truth regarding what they differed about.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Book has been sent down to you in truth, confirming what was before it, he says: the Qur’an, confirming what was before it of the books that had come before it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: The Book has been revealed to you in truth, confirming what was before it, meaning: confirming what came before it of Book and Messenger.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And He sent down the Torah to Moses, and the Gospel to Jesus.

Before, he says: before the book that He sent down to you, and by his saying: guidance for the people, he means a clarification for the people from God in what they differed about regarding the oneness of God and the belief in His messengers, and our description of you, O Muhammad, as My prophet and messenger, and in other than that of the laws of God's religion, such as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel * before as guidance for mankind. They are two books that God sent down, in which there is clarification from God, and protection for whoever takes it, believes in it, and acts according to what is in it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel, the Torah to Moses, and the Gospel to Jesus, just as He sent down the books to those who came before him.

x: By that, God Almighty means: And He revealed the distinction between truth and falsehood in what the parties and people of religions differed about in the matter of Jesus and others. We have previously explained that al-Furqan is the two verbs from their saying: God distinguished between truth and falsehood, He separated between them by giving victory to truth over falsehood, either by a conclusive argument, or by force and dominance with hands and power. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation, except that some of them directed its interpretation to that he separated between truth and falsehood in the matter of Jesus, and some of them: to that he separated between truth and falsehood in the rulings of the laws. It was mentioned that he said: Its meaning is: the separation between truth and falsehood in the matter of Jesus and the parties.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
And He sent down the Criterion

, meaning: the distinction between truth and falsehood in what the parties differed about regarding the matter of Jesus and others. It was mentioned that he said: The meaning of this is: the separation between right and wrong in the rulings and laws of Islam.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And He sent down the Criterion

, meaning the Qur’an. He sent it down to Muhammad, and with it He distinguished between truth and falsehood. He made lawful what He made lawful and prohibited what He made unlawful, and He established His laws in it, and defined His limits in it, and imposed His obligations in it, and clarified His explanation in it, and commanded obedience to it, and forbade disobedience to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And He sent down the Criterion
, he said: The Criterion is the Qur’an, distinguishing between truth and falsehood.

x: The interpretation that we mentioned from Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr in this regard is more correct than the interpretation that we mentioned from Qatada and al-Rabiʿ, and that the meaning of al-Furqan in this context is: God distinguished between His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who argued with him about the matter of Jesus, and about other matters of his, with a conclusive argument that would nullify their excuse and the excuse of their peers from among the people of disbelief in God. We said that this statement is more correct, because God’s statement about His sending down the Qur’an - before His statement about His sending down the Torah and the Gospel in this verse - had already preceded with His statement:
h
He has sent down to you

, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it (al-Baqarah 2:176). There is no doubt that that Book is the Qur’an and nothing else, so there is no point in repeating it again, since there is no benefit in repeating it, other than His mentioning it and reporting about it from the beginning.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Those who denied God’s signs and evidence of His oneness and divinity, and that Jesus was His slave, and took Christ as a god and lord or called him a son of God, will have a severe punishment from God on the Day of Resurrection. Surat Al Imran 3:4 Before, as guidance for mankind,
h
and He sent down the Criterion

. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah will have a severe punishment. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution. And those who disbelieved are those who denied the signs of God, and the signs of God are the signs, evidence, and proofs of God. This statement from God the Almighty indicates the meaning of His statement:
h
And He sent down the Criterion

, that it refers to the distinction that is an argument for the people of truth against the people of falsehood. Because He followed that with His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God, meaning: those who denied that distinction and criterion that He sent down to distinguish between the truthful and the false, for them is a severe punishment, a warning from God to those who oppose the truth after it has become clear to them, and who go against the path of guidance after the argument has been established against them.

c: Then He informed them that
m: He is Mighty in His authority, and that no one among them can prevent Him from being punished, and no barrier can come between Him and it, and no one can oppose Him in it, and that He is Possessor of Retribution against those who deny His arguments and proofs after they have been established for them, and after they have become clear to him and he knows them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: “Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God will have a severe punishment. And God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.” That is, God will take revenge on those who disbelieve in His verses after knowing them and recognizing what He has brought in them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of God will have a severe punishment, and God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution....

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from God. He says: How could it be hidden from Me, O Muhammad - and I am the Knower of all things - what these Christians of Najran who argue with you about the signs of God, regarding Jesus, son of Mary, in their statement that they say about him, be like them?! Like: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from God, meaning: He knows what they want, what they plot, and what they are imitating in their saying about Jesus, since they made him a lord and a god, while they have knowledge of him other than that, out of deception of God and disbelief in Him.

By this He, may His praise be glorified, means: God is He who forms you and makes you into ghostly images in the wombs of your mothers as He wills and loves, making this one male and this one female, this one black and this one red. By this He makes His servants know that all that is contained in the wombs of women is from among those whom He formed and created as He willed, and that Jesus, son of Mary, is among those whom He formed in his mother’s womb and created in it as He willed and loved, and that if He were a god, he would not be among those contained in his mother’s womb, because the wombs do not contain the Creator of what is in the wombs, but rather they contain the created beings, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills

, meaning: Jesus was among those who were formed in the wombs, and they do not deny or reject that, just as others among the children of Adam were formed. So how can he be a god when he was in that position?

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills
, meaning: He formed Jesus in the form however He willed.

x: Others said about this:

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement:
h
It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills

, he said: When the sperm falls into the wombs, it flies in the body for forty days, then it becomes a clot for forty days, then it becomes a lump of flesh for forty days. Then when it reaches the age of creation, God sends an angel to shape it. The angel brings dust between his two fingers and mixes it in the lump of flesh, then kneads it with it, then shapes it as he is commanded, and says: Male or female? Wretched or happy? What is his provision? What is his lifespan? What is his legacy? What are his misfortunes? God says, and the angel writes. Then when that body dies, it is buried where that dust was taken.
b.via: some of the companions of the Prophet

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills
, God, our Lord, is able to form His servants in the wombs however He wills, whether male or female, black or red, complete in creation or incomplete.

x: This statement is a glorification from God Almighty of Himself that He should have a peer or equal in His Lordship, or that divinity should be permissible for anyone other than Him, and a denial from Him of those who said what they said about Jesus, from the delegation of Najran who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and all those who were like them in their saying about Jesus, and all those who claimed that there was a god with God or acknowledged the Lordship of anyone other than Him. Then He, may His praise be glorified, informed His creation of His description, and a warning from Him to whoever worships anyone other than Him, or associates anyone with Him in His worship, so He said: He is the Almighty, to whom no one can help anyone who wants to take revenge on Him, nor can anyone save him from Him, nor can he resort to Him, and that is due to His might before which every creature is humbled, and to which every existing thing submits.

c: Then He informed them that
m: He is the Wise in His management and His excuses to His creation, and in following up His proofs against them, so that whoever among them is destroyed may perish with clear evidence, and whoever among them is revived with clear evidence, as: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, he said: Then he said - meaning the Lord Almighty - in purification of Himself and in unification of Himself from what they made with Him: There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise. He said: The Almighty is in His victory over those who disbelieve in Him if He wills, and the Wise is in His excuse and argument to His servants.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise. He says: Almighty in His vengeance, Wise in His command.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book

, is that God, from whom nothing is hidden on earth or in heaven, is the One who sent down to you the Book, meaning by the Book, the Qur’an. We have previously explained the reason why the Qur’an was called a book, so there is no need to repeat it here. As for his saying: Some of it are clear verses, he means: Some of the Book is verses. He means by verses the verses of the Qur’an. As for the decisive verses, they are those who have ruled with clarification and detail, and have established their arguments and evidence for what they have made evidence for of what is permissible and what is forbidden, promise and threat, reward and punishment, command and deterrence, report and example, sermon and lessons, and the like. Then, the Most High described these decisive verses as: They are the mother of the Book.

He meant by that: They are the origin of the Book in which is the pillar of religion, the obligations and limits, and everything else that creation needs in the matter of their religion, and what they are charged with of obligations in their immediate and future lives. He called them the mother of the book because they are the bulk of the book and the place where its people can turn when they need it. The Arabs do the same, they call the gathering of most of something its mother. So they call the banner of the people that gathers them in armies: their mother, and the manager of most of the affairs of the village and town: its mother. We have explained this previously, so there is no need to repeat it. And He made the Mother of the Book singular, and did not make it plural, saying: They are the Mothers of the Book. And He said: They because He meant all the decisive verses the Mother of the Book, not that each verse of them is the Mother of the Book.

If that meant that each verse of them is the Mother of the Book, then it would have undoubtedly been said: They are the Mothers of the Book. And similar to the statement of God, the Exalted, the Majestic: They are the Mother of the Book, according to the interpretation that we said about the unification of the mother, which is the report of they, is His statement, the Exalted, the Majestic: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign (al-Mu’minun 23:50). And He did not say: Two signs, because its meaning is: And We made both of them a sign. Since the meaning was one in what they made a lesson for creation. If what was meant was the report about each one of them separately, that He made a lesson for creation, then it would have been said: And We made the son of Mary and his mother two signs, because there was a lesson for them in each one of them. That is because Mary was born without a man, and her son spoke and spoke in the cradle as a baby, so there was a sign for the people in each one of them.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was said: They are the mother of the book, and it was not said: They are the mothers of the book as a narration, as a man says: I have no supporters, so you say: I am your supporters, or: I have no peer, so you say: We are your peers. He said, and it is similar: Leave me with two dates, and he recited for a man from Faqas: I was exposed to a place where the solution was exposed to the mare in length You did not hesitate to kill me Solve, i.e., it is solved by it. According to the story, because it was in the accusative case before that, as one says: It was called: Prayer, prayer, narrating the saying of the speaker: Prayer, prayer. He said: Some of them said: It is: That I killed, but he made it an ayn, because that in his language takes its place as about, and the accusative is for the imperative, as if you said: A beating for Zayd. Surat Al Imran 3:7 It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book.
In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. But none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say, "We believe in it." All of it is unspecific. From our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding.

This is a statement that has no meaning. Because all of these testimonies that he cited are undoubtedly stories that he narrated, based on what he narrated about the saying of others and the words that he uttered. And it is known that God, may He be glorified and praised, did not narrate from anyone His saying: The Mother of the Book. So it is permissible to say: He narrated that in the form of a story from someone who said it in the same way. As for his saying: And another, it is the plural of another. Then the Arabists differed about the reason why the word akhr was not declined.
Some of them said: Akhir was not declined because it is an adjective, and its singular is akhirah, just as kana’ and kan’a were not declined because they are adjectives.

Others said: The reason for not declining the other is because of the addition of the ya’ in its singular, and that all of them are built on their singular in not declining. They said: The reason for not declining the other is that it was not declining, just as it was not declining the red and white, in the indefinite and definite, because of the increase in the length in them and the hamza with the waw. Then the plural of red and other was separated, so the plural of other was built on its singular and it was said: fa’l and akhr, so it was not declining it just as it was not declining the other, and the plural of red and white was built in a way that was different from its singular and was declining, so it was said: hamr and baid, so because of the difference in their state in the plural, their parsing differed according to them in declension. And because their two states in the singular are the same, their two states in it are the same.

As for his saying: similar, its meaning is: similar in recitation, different in meaning, as God Almighty said: And they will bring it similar (al-Baqarah 2:25), meaning in appearance, different in taste - and as He said, informing about someone from the Children of Israel who said: Indeed, the cows are similar to us (al-Baqarah 2:70), meaning: similar to us in description, even if its types differ. The interpretation of the statement, then, is: He from whom nothing is hidden on earth or in heaven, is the One who sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Qur’an, in which there are verses that are clear and precise in their explanation. They are the foundation of the Book upon which you and your nation are based in religion, and to which you and they turn in what He has enjoined upon you and upon them of the laws of Islam. There are other verses that are similar in recitation but different in meaning.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement:
h
Some of it are verses that are clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific
. What are the clear verses of the Book, and what are the unspecific?

Some of them said: The decisive verses of the Qur’an, which are acted upon, and they are the abrogating or confirming rulings, and the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an, which are abandoned and abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Awam told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Some of it are clear verses, he said: They are the three verses from here: Say, ‘Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you’ (al-An’am 6:151, 152), to three verses, and the one in the Children of Israel: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him (al-Isra’ 17:23-39), to the end of the verses.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Salih told us: Muawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book.” The precise verses are its abrogating verses, its lawful and unlawful verses, its limits and obligations, and what is believed in and acted upon. He said: And others are ambiguous. The ambiguous verses are its abrogated verses, its beginning and end, its examples and divisions, and what is believed in but not acted upon.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book

, to and others unspecific, the clear verses, which are the mother of the Book, are the abrogating verses that are accepted and acted upon. And the unspecific verses are the abrogated verses that are not accepted.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book

; in it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book until His saying: All is from our Lord. As for the clear verses: they are the abrogating verses that are acted upon, and as for the ambiguous verses, they are the abrogated verses.
b.via: some of the companions of the Prophet

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book
; in it are
h
verses that are clear - they are the foundation of the Book

. The clear verses are the abrogating verses that are acted upon, what God has made lawful in it and forbidden in it what He has forbidden. As for the ambiguous verses, they are the abrogated verses that are not acted upon or believed in.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: clear verses, he said: The clear is that which is acted upon.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book

. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.” He said: The precise verses are the abrogating verses that are acted upon, and the unspecific verses are the abrogated verses that are not acted upon or believed in.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Verses that are clear - they are the foundation of the Book
, he said: the abrogating verses, and others unspecific, he said: what was abrogated and left to be recited.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said:
m: The decisive verse is that which has not been abrogated, and the ambiguous verse is that which has been abrogated.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Verses that are clear - they are the foundation of the Book
, he said: the abrogating, and others that are unspecific, he said: the abrogated.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh narrating, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Some of it are clear verses, meaning the abrogating verses that are acted upon, and others are ambiguous, meaning the abrogated verses, which one believes in but does not act upon.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Some of it are clear verses, he said: what has not been abrogated, and others are ambiguous, he said: what has been abrogated.

x: Others said: The decisive verses of the Book are those in which God has made clear what is permissible and what is forbidden, and the ambiguous verses are those in which some of them resemble others in meaning, even if their wording differs.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Some of it are clear verses, what is in it of what is permissible and what is forbidden, and other than that it is ambiguous, some of it confirms the other, and it is like his statement:
h
And He misguides thereby none but the wicked (al-Baqarah 2
:26), and like his statement:
h
Thus does God place defilement upon those who do not believe (al-An’am 6
:125), and like his statement: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness
r
(Muhammad 47:17)

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: The clear verses of the Book are those that do not bear more than one interpretation, and the ambiguous verses are those that bear more than one interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr told me:
m: h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book

; in it are verses that are precise, in which is the proof of the Lord, the protection of the servants, and the repelling of opponents and falsehood, and they cannot be changed or distorted from what they were placed upon, and others that are ambiguous, in truth, and they can be changed, distorted, and interpreted, and God has tested the servants with them, as He tested them with regard to what is permissible and what is forbidden, and they should not be diverted to falsehood nor distorted from the truth.

x: Others said: The meaning of Muhkam is what God has made clear in the verses of the Qur’an, and the stories of the nations and their messengers who were sent to them, so He explained that to Muhammad and his nation. And Mutashabih is what the words of their stories are confused in when repeated in the surahs, by telling it with the agreement of the words and the difference of the meanings, and by telling it with the difference of the words and the agreement of the meanings.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, and he recited: “Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from One Who is Wise and Acquainted”
r

, he said: And he mentioned the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in twenty-four verses of it, and the hadith of Noah in twenty-four verses of it. Then he said: This is from the report of the unseen
r

, then he mentioned and to Aad, and he recited until he reached and seek forgiveness of your Lord, then he moved on. Then he mentioned Salih, Abraham, Lot, and Shuaib and finished with that. This is an explanation of that, an explanation of whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail. He said: And the ambiguous, he mentioned Moses in many places, and it is ambiguous, and it is all one meaning. And similar: Walk in it (al-Mu’minun 23:27), Carry it
r

, Walk your hand (al-Qasas 28:32), And put your hand in (al-Naml Surat Al Imran 3:7 It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. But none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say, "We believe in it." All of it is unspecific. From our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding. 27:12), A serpent that crawls
r

, A manifest serpent (al-A’raf 7:107 - al-Shu’ara 26:32). He said: Then he mentioned Hud in ten verses of it, and Salih in eight verses of it, and Abraham in another eight verses, and Lot in eight verses of it, and Shu’aib in thirteen verses, and Moses in four verses. All of this is decided between the prophets and their people in this surah, so that ends with one hundred verses of Surah Hud. Then he said: This is from the report of the towns which We relate to you, from it standing and harvested
r

. And he said in the similarities of the Qur’an: Whoever God intends to be afflicted and misguided, He says: What is the matter with this that it should not be like this? And what is the matter with this that it should not be like this?

x: Others said: Rather, the decisive verses of the Qur’an are those whose interpretation the scholars have known and whose meaning and explanation they have understood. And the ambiguous are those which no one has a way to know, of which God has kept His knowledge to Himself and not His creation, such as the report about the time of the emergence of Jesus, son of Mary, and the time of the rising of the sun from the West, and the establishment of the Hour, and the end of the world, and the like, for no one knows that. And they said: God called the ambiguous verses of the Book the disjointed letters at the beginning of some of the chapters of the Qur’an, such as Alif, Lam, Meem, Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad, Alif, Lam, Ra, and the like, because they are similar in wording and correspond to the letters of the abjad system. And some of the Jews at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hoped to attain knowledge of the duration of Islam and its people through them, and to know the end of the eating of Muhammad and his nation, so God proved their claim to be false by that, and informed them that what they sought to know from that through these ambiguous letters they would not attain nor through anything else, and that no one knows that except God.

This is a statement that was mentioned on the authority of Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Riʿab: that this verse was revealed about him. We have mentioned the narration on his authority and on the authority of others who said something similar to his statement, in the interpretation of that in the interpretation of His statement: “Alif, Lam, Meem. This is the Book about which there is no doubt” (al-Baqarah 2:2).

This statement that we mentioned on the authority of Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah is more similar to the interpretation of the verse. That is because all the verses of the Qur’an that God the Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, He only revealed to him as an explanation for him and his nation and as guidance for the worlds. It is not permissible for there to be in it something that they do not need, nor for there to be in it something that they need, and then they would not have a way to know its interpretation. Since that is the case, then everything in it is in need of its creation, even if in some of it there is something that they do not need in some of its meanings - [and even if need compels it in many meanings] - and that is like the statement of God the Almighty: The Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earned through its faith any good
r
(Al-Anʿam: 158)

So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed his nation that the verse that God the Almighty informed His servants that if it comes, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before, is the rising of the sun from the west. What the servants needed to know about this was knowledge of the time of benefit of repentance, without specifying it by the number of years, months, and days. God made this clear to them through the evidence of the Book, and explained it to them through the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an explanation. What they did not need to know about it was knowledge of the amount of time between the time of the revelation of this verse and the time of the occurrence of that verse, for that is something they did not need to know in religion or in this world. This is the knowledge that God, may He be glorified and exalted, has kept to Himself without His creation, so He concealed it from them.

This and what is similar to it is the meaning that the Jews sought to know during the time of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation before His saying: Alif, Lam, Meem and Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad and Alif, Lam, Ra and Alif, Lam, Ra and the like of the disjointed, ambiguous letters, about which God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed them that they would not comprehend the interpretation of that before Him, and that no one knows its interpretation except God. Since the ambiguous is what we have described, then everything other than it is decisive. Because it will not be devoid of being decisive in that it has one meaning and no interpretation other than one interpretation, and hearing it has dispensed with the need for an explanation to clarify it, or it will be decisive, even if it has many aspects and interpretations and is manipulated into many meanings, so the indication of the intended meaning from it is either from the explanation of God Almighty about it, or the explanation of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his nation.
And the knowledge of that will not be lost from the scholars of the nation for what we have explained.

We have already explained the interpretation of that with evidence that testifies to the correctness of what we have said about it. And we are mentioning the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation about it, and that is because they differed in its interpretation.
Some of them said: The meaning of his saying: They are the mother of the Book is that they are the ones in which are the obligations, limits, and rulings, similar to what we said about it.
Who said that?

c: Imran bin Musa Al-Qazzaz narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Warith bin Saeed narrated to us, he said: Ishaq bin Suwaid narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya bin Yaʿmar that he said
m: about this verse: They are the foundation of the Book. Yahya said: They are those in which are the obligatory duties, the prescribed punishments, and the pillar of the religion. He gave an example for that, saying: The mother of towns is Mecca, and the mother of Khurasan is Merv, and the mother of travelers, those who entrust their affairs to Him, and He takes care of them in their travels. He said: That is their mother.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: They are the mother of the Book, he said: They are the entirety of the Book.

x: Others said: Rather, he means by that: the openings of the surahs from which the Qur’an is extracted.
Who said that?

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us, he said, Ishaq bin Suwaid told us, on the authority of Abu Fakhita, that he said
m: about this verse: Among it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book. He said: The foundation of the Book is the openings of the chapters, from which the Qur’an is extracted - “Alif, Lam, Meem. That is the Book” (al-Baqarah 2:1-2), from which Al-Baqarah was extracted, and “Alif, Lam, Meem. God - there is no god except Him” from which Al Imran was extracted.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: As for those in whose hearts there is a deviation from the truth and a deviation from it. It is said: So-and-so deviated from the truth, so he deviates from it with deviation, deviation, deviation, and deviation. And God made him deviate - if He made him incline - so He makes him deviate. And from this is the saying of the Most High: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate do not incline them from the truth, after You have guided us
r
(Al Imran 3:8)
. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: As for those in whose hearts is deviation, meaning: deviation from guidance.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: In their hearts is deviation, he said: doubt.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: As for those in whose hearts is deviation, he said: from the people of doubt.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us,
m: on the authority of Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud and on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: As for those in whose hearts is deviation, deviation is doubt.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He said: Deviation means doubt. Ibn Jurayj said: Those in whose hearts is deviation means the hypocrites.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And they follow that which is ambiguous

, is that which has ambiguous words and whose meanings are changed by various interpretations, in order to realize - by claiming false interpretations in that - what they are upon of misguidance and deviation from the path of truth, in order to deceive those whose knowledge of the various interpretations of that and the changes in its meanings is weak, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they follow that which is ambiguous
in it, so they interpret the clear verses according to the ambiguous, and the ambiguous according to the clear verses, and they become confused, so God confused them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
And they follow that which is ambiguous
in it, meaning: that which has been distorted and changed in it, in order to believe in what they have innovated and introduced, so that it will be an argument for what they said and a doubt.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they follow that which is ambiguous thereof
, he said: The chapter from which they went astray and perished, seeking its interpretation.

x: Others said about this:

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement: And they follow that of it which is ambiguous, they follow the abrogated and the abrogating verses and say: Why is it that this verse was acted upon by such and such in place of this verse, so the first was left and this other was acted Surat Al Imran 3:7 It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. But none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say, "We believe in it." All of it is unspecific. From our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding. upon? Why was this verse not acted upon before the first verse that abrogated came? And why does He promise the punishment of whoever does an action that He will punish him [in] the Fire, and in another place: whoever does it, it does not necessitate the Fire?

x: The interpreters differed about who was meant by this verse.

Some of them said: He meant the delegation of Christians from Najran who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and argued with him as they argued with him, and disputed with him by saying: Do you not claim that Jesus is the spirit of God and His word? And they interpreted what they said about him as blasphemy.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: who said: They - meaning the delegation who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Christians of Najran - went and argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Do you not claim that he is the Word of God and a spirit from Him? He said: Yes! They said: That is enough for us! Then God Almighty revealed:
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation
, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam
r
(Al Imran 3:59)
, the verse.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed about Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab, his brother Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and the group who debated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the amount of time he and his nation would eat, and they wanted to know that from his saying: Alif, Lam, Meem, Alif, Lam, Meem, Alif, Lam, Ra, and Alif, Lam, Ra. So God, may He be glorified and exalted, said about them:
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

- meaning these Jews whose hearts are inclined from guidance and truth - they follow that which is ambiguous therein meaning: the meanings of these separate letters that are open to being changed in different ways and interpretations, seeking discord. We mentioned the narration of this before, at the beginning of the surah in which the cow is mentioned.

Others said: Rather, God Almighty has punished every innovator in His religion with an innovation that contradicts what He sent His Messenger, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with, by interpreting some verses of the Qur’an that are open to interpretation, even if God has made that clear: either in His Book or on the tongue of His Messenger.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation
, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord, and whenever Qatada would recite this verse:
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, he would say: If they are not the Kharijites and the Sabaiyyah, then I do not know who they are! By my life, there was among the people of Badr and Hudaybiyyah who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Muhajireen and the Ansar, report for those who seek information, and a lesson for those who seek to learn, for those who have reason and insight. The Khawarij came out and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were many at that time in Medina, Syria, and Iraq, and his wives were alive at that time. By God, if a male or female Kharijite ever emerged from them, they were not satisfied with what they were upon, nor did they agree with them in it. Rather, they would talk about the faults of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and the description he gave them. They would hate them in their hearts, and be hostile to them with their tongues. By God, their hands would be severe against them when they met them. By my life, if the matter of the Kharijites was guidance, they would have united, but it was misguidance and dispersed. Likewise, if it was from other than God, you would find much disagreement in it. The adherents of this matter presented it a long time ago. Did they ever succeed in it or prosper? Glory be to God! How can the last of these people not take the first of them as a lesson? If they were upon guidance, God would have made it manifest, triumphed, and aided it. But they were upon falsehood, which God denied and refuted. They are as I have seen them; whenever a generation emerged from them, God refuted their argument, refuted their stories, and shed their blood. If they concealed it, it would be a sore in their hearts and a grief upon them. If they declare it, God will shed their blood. By God, that is an evil religion, so avoid it. By God, Judaism is an innovation, Christianity is an innovation, Kharijism is an innovation, and Sabianism is an innovation. No book was sent down concerning them, nor was any prophet prescribed them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. The people sought an interpretation, but they made a mistake in the interpretation and struck discord, so they followed that of it which was ambiguous, and they perished because of that. By my life, there were among the companions of Badr and Hudaybiyyah those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan. And he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on his authority.

c: Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, they said: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘
h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book
’ until His saying: ‘And none will remember except those of understanding.’ He said: So if you see those who argue about it, they are the ones God meant, so beware of them.”

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Ayoub, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘
h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book

’ until ‘And none will remember except those of understanding.’ She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So if you see those who argue about it - or he said: argue about it - they are the ones whom God meant, so beware of them.” Matar said, on the authority of Ayoub, that he said: So do not sit with them, they are the ones whom God meant, so beware of them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, with a similar meaning.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha,
m: the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific,’ the entire verse. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you see those who follow that which is unspecific in it, and those who dispute about it, then they are the ones whom God meant, those about whom God said, so do not sit with them.’”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said:
m: I heard Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrating, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book.’ Then he recited to the end of the verses, and said: ‘If you see those who follow that which is ambiguous in it, then they are those whom God has named, so beware of them.’”

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They follow that which is ambiguous in it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has warned you, so if you see them, recognize them.”

c: Ali told us: Al-Walid told us, on the authority of Nafi’ bin Umar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, Aisha told me:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you see them, beware of them. Then he recited:
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation
, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, and they do not act according to its clear verses.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, he said, my uncle told us, he said, Shabib ibn Saeed told me, on the authority of Ruh ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of Aisha:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about this verse: ‘As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it.
h
And none knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge
.’ He said: So if you see them disputing about it, then they are the ones God meant, so beware of them.”

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Khalid bin Nizar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha,
m: regarding this verse,
h
It is He who has sent down to you the Book
, the verse, he follows it, recites it, then says: So if you see those who dispute about it, then beware of them, for they are the ones whom God meant.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book to the end of the verse. He said: They are those whom God has named, so if you see them, beware of them.

x: What is indicated by the apparent meaning of this verse is that it was revealed about those who argued with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the ambiguous parts of what was revealed to him in the Book of God, either about the matter of Jesus or about the period of his life and the life of his nation. It is more likely that it was revealed about those who argued with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the ambiguous parts of his life and the life of his nation. Because His statement,
h
And none knows its interpretation except God

, indicates that this is information about the period of time that they wanted to know from the ambiguous parts that none knows except God. As for the matter of Jesus and its causes, Surat Al Imran 3:7 It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. But none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say, "We believe in it." All of it is unspecific. From our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding. God informed His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his nation of that and made it clear to them. So it is known that He did not mean by it anything except what was hidden from him regarding the terms of life.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: seeking polytheism.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Seeking discord, he said: wanting polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: Seeking discord, meaning polytheism.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: seeking doubts.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Seeking discord, he said: doubts, by which they were destroyed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Seeking discord, doubts. He said: They were destroyed by it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Seeking discord, he said: doubts. He said: And doubts are what they destroyed with.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: Seeking discord, meaning confusion.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: the intention of doubts and confusion. The meaning of the statement then is: As for those in whose hearts is aversion to the truth and injustice towards it, they follow the verses of the Book whose wording is ambiguous and whose meanings are open to interpretation - by its openness to different meanings - intending to confuse themselves and others, using it as evidence for their falsehood to which their hearts are inclined, rather than the truth which God has made clear and clarified with the decisive verses of His Book.

Even though this verse was revealed about those we mentioned about whom it was revealed from the people of polytheism, it is intended by it for every innovator in the religion of God with an innovation and his heart inclines towards it, interpreting some of the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an, then arguing and debating with it the people of truth, and deviating from the clear evidence of the decisive verses, intending thereby to confuse the people of truth from the believers, and seeking knowledge of the interpretation of what is ambiguous to him from that, whoever he may be, and whatever type of innovator he may be: from the people of Christianity or Judaism or Zoroastrianism, or whether he is a Sabian, or a Kharijite, or a Qadari, or a Jahmi, like the one who, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So when you see those who argue with it, they are the ones God meant, so beware of them, and as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - and the Khawarij were mentioned to him and what they twist
m: about the Qur’an, so he said: They believe in its clear verses and perish when they see its ambiguous verses! And Ibn Abbas recited:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God
, the verse.

x: We said that the statement we mentioned is the more correct of the two interpretations, with his saying: Seeking discord, because those about whom this verse was revealed were polytheists, and they only wanted, by seeking an interpretation of what they sought an interpretation of, to confuse the Muslims and to use it as evidence against them, to turn them away from the truth that they were upon. So there is no meaning in saying: They did that seeking polytheism, and they were polytheists.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the interpretation that God Almighty meant by His saying: and seeking its interpretation.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: the term that the Jews wanted to know of the expiration of the period of the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the matter of his nation, from the separate letters of the abjad system, such as Alif, Lam, Meem, Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad, Alif, Lam, Ra, Alif, Lam, Ra, and other similar terms.
Who said that?
