c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
m: As for his statement:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God
, he means its interpretation on the Day of Resurrection, except God.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: the consequences of the Qur’an. They said: They only wanted to know when the one who abrogates the rulings that God Almighty had legislated for the people of Islam before his coming would come, so he abrogates what he had legislated before that.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And seeking its interpretation, they wanted to know the interpretation of the Qur’an - which is its consequences - God said:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God
, and its interpretation, its consequences, when will the abrogating verse come and abrogate the abrogated?

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And seeking an interpretation of the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an, they interpret it - since it has aspects and variations in interpretations - according to what is in their hearts of deviation, and what they have committed of misguidance.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And seeking its interpretation, and that is based on the misguidance they committed in their saying: We created and We decreed.

x: The statement made by Ibn ʿAbbas, that the people sought the interpretation of the ambiguous verses, which is to know the expiration of the period and the time of the Hour - and what we mentioned from al-Suddi, that they sought and wanted to know the time of its occurrence before its coming - is more correct. Even though al-Suddi neglected the meaning of that in terms of diverting it to limiting it to the meaning that the people sought to know the time of the coming of the abrogator of what had been decreed before that. We said: The people’s request to know the time that came before His coming, the knowledge of which was hidden from them and others, through the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an, is more deserving of the interpretation of His statement: and seeking its interpretation, because we have previously demonstrated that God, may He be glorified, informed us that only God knows that interpretation.

There is no doubt that the meaning of his saying: We have decided, we have done, has been understood by many of the ignorant polytheists, not to mention the people of faith and those who are deeply rooted in knowledge among them.

By that, He, the Most High, means: No one knows the time of the Hour, the end of the period of Muhammad and his nation’s eating, and what will happen, except God, not anyone else among the human beings who hoped to comprehend the world of that through calculations, astrology, and divination. As for those firmly grounded in knowledge, they say: We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord - they do not know that, but the superiority of their knowledge in that over others is the knowledge that God is the one who knows that, not anyone else among His creation.

The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this. Is those firmly rooted conjoined with the name God, meaning that they are required to have knowledge of the interpretation of the ambiguous, or are they being mentioned again, meaning that they are being told that they say: We believe in the ambiguous and we believe that only God knows the knowledge of that?

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: No one knows the interpretation of that except God alone, the One with whose knowledge He is alone. As for those firmly grounded in knowledge, the report about them began with them saying: We believe in the ambiguous and the clear, and that all of that is from God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Khalid bin Nizar told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those firmly rooted in knowledge say
, ‘We believe in it.’ She said: It was part of their firmness in knowledge that they believed in its clear and ambiguous verses, and they did not know its interpretation.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God
h
and those firmly grounded in knowledge
say: We believe in it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told me, he said, Hisham bin Urwah said:
m: My father used to say about this verse, None knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge, that those firmly rooted in knowledge do not know its interpretation, but they say, “We believe in it. All of it is from our Lord.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Abu Nahik al-Asadi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge
, he says: You are connecting this verse, and it is disconnected:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God
h
And those firmly rooted in knowledge say
, ‘We believe in it. All is from our Lord,’” so their knowledge ended with what they said.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Dukayn told us, he said, Amr ibn Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Muhab told us, he said:
m: I heard Umar ibn Abdul Aziz say: And those firmly rooted in knowledge, the knowledge of those firmly rooted in knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur’an ended with them saying, We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord.
b.via: Amr ibn Uthman ibn Abdullah ibn Muhab

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, on the authority of Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God
, he said: Then he began and said:
h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge

say, ‘We believe in it, all is from our Lord,’ and they do not know its interpretation. Surat Al Imran 3:7 It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. But none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say, "We believe in it." All of it is unspecific. From our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: None knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge. And despite their knowledge of this and their firmness in knowledge, they say: “We believe in it. It is all from our Lord.”
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said:
m: I am one of those who know its interpretation.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge
know its interpretation, and they say: We believe in it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge
know its interpretation, and they say: We believe in it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge
know its interpretation and say: We believe in it.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And none knows its interpretation what he meant, what he meant, “except God
h
and those firmly grounded in knowledge

say, ‘We believe in it. It is all from our Lord.’” So how can it differ, when it is one statement from one Lord? Then they returned the interpretation of the ambiguous to what they knew of the interpretation of the decisive one, in which no one has an interpretation except one interpretation, so the Book was consistent with their statement and some of it confirmed some of it, so the proof was implemented, the excuse was made clear, falsehood was removed, and disbelief was stamped out.

x: Whoever says the first opinion on this, and says that those firmly rooted in knowledge do not know the interpretation of that, but rather God has informed us about their faith and belief that it is from God, then he raises those firmly rooted in knowledge by the beginning according to the Basrans, and makes its predicate: They say, ‘We believe in it.’ As for the opinion of some of the Kufians, it is by the pronoun from mentioning them in they say. And according to the opinion of some of them: by the whole predicate about them, which is: they say. Whoever said the second statement, and claimed that the firm ones know its interpretation, connected the firm ones to the name God, and thus raised them by connecting them to Him.

What is correct in our view is that they are raised by the sentence of their predicate after them, which is: they say, because we have previously explained that they do not know the interpretation of the ambiguous verse that God Almighty mentioned in this verse. And it is, as I have heard, in my father’s reading:
h
And those firmly rooted in knowledge say
, as we mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to read it. And in ʿAbdullah’s reading: Its interpretation is only with God,
h
and those firmly rooted in knowledge say
As for the meaning of interpretation in the speech of the Arabs, it is explanation, reference and destination.

i: Some narrators recited the verse of Al-A’sha:
x: She interpreted her love as the love of my two brothers, and they became friends.

Its origin is from: The thing ended up like this - if it became and returned, it is interpreted first, and I interpreted it means I turned it into it. It has been said that his statement: And the best interpretation (An-Nisa’: 59- al-Isra’ 17:35) means a reward. This is because the reward is what the people’s matter ended up to and became. What he means by his saying: He interpreted her love: is the explanation of her love and its reference. What he means by that is that her love was small in his heart, then it went from smallness to greatness, and it continued to grow until it became old, like a small seedling that continued to grow until it became old and great like its mother. This verse may be chanted: However, her love for him was a consequence of the two quarrelings, so they became friends.

He means by those firmly rooted in knowledge, the scholars who have mastered their knowledge and comprehended it and memorized it by heart, and no doubt or ambiguity enters their knowledge and understanding of what they have learned. The origin of this is: the firmness of something in something, which is its stability and penetration into it. It is said from it: faith is firm in the heart of so-and-so, so it is firmly and firmly established. A report was narrated about their description from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is: Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli narrated that Muhammad bin Abdullah narrated that Fayyad bin Muhammad al-Raqi narrated that Abdullah bin Yazid bin Adam narrated that Abu al-Darda’ and Abu Umamah said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Who is firmly grounded in knowledge? He said: He whose oath is true, whose tongue is truthful, whose heart is upright, and whose stomach is chaste.
That is the one firmly grounded in knowledge.”

c: Al-Muthanna and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi told me, they said: Na’im ibn Hammad told us, he said: Fayyad al-Raqi told us, he said: Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Awdi told us, he said:
m: He had met the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Anas ibn Malik, Abu Umamah and Abu al-Darda told us: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those who are firmly grounded in knowledge, so he said: He whose oath is faithful, whose tongue is truthful, whose heart is upright, and whose stomach and private parts are chaste, then that is the one who is firmly grounded in knowledge.”

x: A group of interpreters said: God Almighty called these people who are firmly grounded in knowledge, because they said: We believe in it, all of it is from our Lord.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
And those firmly rooted in knowledge say
, ‘We believe in it.’ He said: Those firmly rooted in knowledge are those who say, “We believe in it. It is all from our Lord.”

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And those firmly rooted in knowledge, they are the believers, for they say: We believe in it, in its abrogating and abrogated verses, all from our Lord.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, Abdullah bin Salam said: Those firmly rooted in knowledge, and their knowledge is their saying. Ibn Jurayj said:
h
And those firmly rooted in knowledge say
, ‘We believe in it,’ and they are the ones who say, Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate
r
(Al Imran 3:8)
. And they say, Our Lord, indeed You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt
r
(Al Imran 3:9)

. As for the interpretation of his statement: They say, ‘We believe in it,’ it means that those firmly grounded in knowledge say: We believe in what is ambiguous in the verses of the Book, and that it is true even if we do not know its interpretation. And: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Salamah bin Nabit told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge
say, ‘We believe in it.’ He said: The decisive and the ambiguous.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: All is from our Lord, is all the clear and ambiguous verses of the Book, from our Lord, which is His revelation and revelation to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: All is from our Lord, he said: He means what was abrogated from it and what was not abrogated.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And none knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge
, they said: All is from our Lord, they believed in its ambiguous verses and acted upon its clear verses.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement: All is from our Lord. They say: The decisive and the ambiguous are from our Lord.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge
say, ‘We believe in it, all from our Lord.’ We believe in the definitive and believe in it, and we believe in the ambiguous and do not believe in it, and it is all from God.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those firmly grounded in knowledge
, they act upon it. They say: We act upon the decisive verses and believe in them, and we believe in the ambiguous verses and do not act upon them, and all of them are from our Lord.

x: The Arab scholars differed regarding the ruling on the word kull if it is implied in it.
Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is permissible to delete the intended meaning that was with it, to which all is added in this place, because it is a noun, as He said:
Indeed, we are all in it

meaning: We are all in it. He said: All cannot be implied in it, and it is an adjective. It is not said: I passed by the people all. Rather, it is implied if you make it a noun. If We are all in it was an adjective, it would not be permissible, because the implied meaning in it is weak and cannot be possible in every place.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa considered the omission of it whether it is an adjective or a noun, the same. Because it is not permissible to delete what comes after it, according to him, unless it is sufficient in itself for what it was added to from the implicit. And it is not permissible for it to be sufficient from it in one case, and not sufficient in another. He said: The way of the whole and the part in indicating what comes after them by themselves and their sufficiency from it is one meaning in every case, whether it is an adjective or a noun.

This second statement is more appropriate to analogy, because if it is sufficient in itself, then it is omitted from it in a case because it Surat Al Imran 3:7 It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific.
h
But as for those in whose hearts is deviation

, they follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. But none knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge. They say, "We believe in it." All of it is unspecific. From our Lord, and none will remember except those of understanding. indicates it, so the rule regarding it is that whenever it is found indicating what comes after it, it is sufficient from it.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: None will remember, take heed, and refrain from saying about the ambiguous verses of God’s Book what they have no knowledge of, except those of understanding and reason. And: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: And none will remember except those of understanding. He said: And none will remember in such a case, meaning: in referring the interpretation of the ambiguous to what has been known of the interpretation of the definitive, so that they agree on one meaning, except those of understanding.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Verses that are clear - they are the foundation of the Book, he said: the abrogating verses, and others unspecific, he said: what was abrogated and left to be recited.

Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord, and whenever Qatada would recite this verse: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation, he would say: If they are not the Kharijites and the Sabaiyyah, then I do not know who they are!

Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ayoub, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘It is He who has sent down to you the Book’ until ‘And none will remember except those of understanding.’

Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book.

Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said: I heard Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrating, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book.’

Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Khalid bin Nizar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, regarding this verse, It is He who has sent down to you the Book, the verse, he follows it, recites it, then says: So if you see those who dispute about it, then beware of them, for they are the ones whom God meant.
And it is, as I have heard, in my father’s reading: And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, as we mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to read it.
Some narrators recited the verse of Al-A’sha: She interpreted her love as the love of my two brothers, and they became friends.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that those firmly grounded in knowledge are responsible for: We believe in what is ambiguous in the verses of the Book of God, and that it and the decisive verses of His are from the revelation and inspiration of our Lord. They also say: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, meaning that they say, desiring that their Lord remove from them what He has afflicted those whose hearts have deviated from following the ambiguous verses of the Qur’an, seeking temptation and seeking its interpretation that no one knows but God: “Our Lord, do not make us like those whose hearts have deviated from the truth and have turned away from Your path. “Let not our hearts deviate,” do not tire of them and turn them away from Your guidance after You have guided us and granted us success in believing in the definitive and ambiguous verses of Your Book.

And grant us, O our Lord, from Yourself mercy, meaning: from Yourself mercy, meaning by that: grant us from Yourself success and steadfastness in what we are upon of acknowledging the definitive and ambiguous verses of Your Book. Indeed, You are the Bestower, meaning: You are the One who gives Your servants success and guidance to remain steadfast in Your religion and to believe in Your Book and Your Messengers, as.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, meaning: do not let our hearts become bored even if we become bored with our events, and grant us from Yourself mercy.

x: In the praise of God, the Most High, of these people with what He praised them with, of their desire for Him not to make their hearts deviate, and to give them mercy from Him to help them to remain steadfast in what they are upon of good insight into the truth upon which they are established, what reveals the error of the saying of the ignorant Qadarites: that God’s deviation of the heart of those of His servants whose hearts He has deviated from His obedience and His inclination towards them from it is injustice. Because if that were as they said, then those who said, Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, would be more deserving of blame than praise. Because if the statement were as they said, then the people would have only asked their Lord, by asking Him not to make their hearts deviate, not to wrong them or be unjust to them. And that is ignorance on the part of the questioner, because God, the Most High, does not wrong His servants or be unjust to them.
He has informed His servants of that and denied it of Himself by saying, And your Lord is not unjust to His servants
r
(Fussilat 41:46)

. There is no reason for his question to be in the manner that he informed them that he was. In the corruption of what they said about that, there is clear evidence that it is justice from God Almighty: to turn away from His obedience to whoever has his heart turned away from His obedience. Therefore, he deserves praise from whoever desires Him not to turn him away, for directing the desire to those who deserve it, and placing his question in its place, with the apparent reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his desire to his Lord in that, with his position with Him and his honor upon Him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Bahram, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O Changer of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion!’ Then he recited: ‘Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us,’ to the end of the verse.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Bahram, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Asma’, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal narrated to us, Abdul Hamid bin Bahram Al-Fazari narrated to us, Shahr bin Hawshab narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Umm Salamah narrating: “The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) used to say frequently in his supplication: ‘O God, the Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.’ She said: I said: O Messenger of God, does the heart indeed change? He said: ‘Yes, God has not created a human being from among the children of Adam except that his heart is between two of His fingers. If He wills, He makes it steadfast, and if He wills, He makes it deviate. So we ask God, our Lord, not to make our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to bestow upon us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower.’ She said: I said: O Messenger of God, will you not teach me a supplication that I can make for myself? He said: ‘Yes, say: O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say frequently: ‘O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.’ Some of his family said to him: ‘Does he fear for us when we have believed in you and what you have brought?’ He said: ‘The heart is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Gracious, Blessed and Most High, and He says with them like this.’ Abu Ahmad moved his two fingers.

x: And al-Tusi put it between his two fingers.”

c: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told me, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Anas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, often said: ‘O Changer of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.’ We said: ‘O Messenger of God, we have believed in you and confirmed what you brought, so should we be afraid?’ He said: ‘Yes, for the hearts are between two of God’s fingers, and He, Blessed and Exalted be He, turns them.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, he said, Bishr ibn Bakr told us, and Ali ibn Sahl told me, he said, Ayoub ibn Bishr told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Jabir, he said: I heard Busr ibn Ubaydullah say, I heard Abu Idris al-Khawlani say: I heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an al-Kalabi say: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘There is no heart but that it is between two fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills, He makes it steadfast, and if He wills, He causes it to deviate.’” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O Changer of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion. And the scale is in the hand of the Most Merciful, He raises some people and lowers others until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Omar bin Abdul Malik Al-Ta’i told me, he said, Muhammad bin Ubaidah told us, he said, Al-Jarrah bin Malih Al-Bahrani told us, on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Samurah bin Fatik Al-Asadi -
m: who was among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The scales are in the hand of God. He raises some people and lowers others, and the heart of the son of Adam is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills, He makes it deviate, and if He wills, He makes it straight.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Haywah bin Shuraih, he said, Abu Hani Al-Khawlani told me:
m: that he heard Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Habli say: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas say: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The hearts of the children of Adam are all between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, like a single heart, which He directs as He wills.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, says: ‘O God, Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience.’”

c: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Asad bin Musa narrated to us, he said: Abdul Hamid bin Bahram narrated to us, he said: Shahr bin Hawshab narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Umm Salamah narrating: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say frequently in his supplication: O God, make my heart firm upon Your religion. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, do hearts change? He said: Yes, there is no human being created by God from among the children of Adam except that his heart is between two fingers of God’s fingers. If He wills, He makes it steadfast, and if He wills, He causes it to deviate. So we ask God, our Lord, not to make our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to bestow upon us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower.”

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that they also say - along with their saying: We believe in what is ambiguous in the verses of our Lord’s Book, all the decisive and ambiguous verses in it are from our Lord -: O our Lord, “Indeed, You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise.” This is one of the words about which mentioning what was mentioned makes it unnecessary to mention what was left out. That is because the meaning of the words is: Our Lord, You will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, so forgive us on that Day and pardon us, for You do not fail to fulfill Your promise: whoever believes in You, follows Your Messenger, and does what You have commanded him to do in Your Book, You will forgive him on that Day. Rather, this is a request from the people to their Lord to make them steadfast in their good insight, in faith in God and His Messenger, and in what He brought them of His revelation, until He takes them with their best deeds and faith.

For if He does that to them, Paradise will be obligatory for them, because He has promised whoever does that to among His servants that He will admit him into Paradise. The verse, even though it was presented as a report, its interpretation by the people is: a question, a supplication, and a desire to their Lord. As for the meaning of his saying: On a Day about which there is no doubt, it is: There is no doubt about it. We have explained that with evidence of its authenticity in what has passed before. The meaning of his saying: for a day is on a day. That is the day on which God will gather His creation to pass judgment between them in the place of presentation and reckoning. The appointment is a verbal noun, from the word promise.

What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieved, is that those who denied the truth that they knew of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Jews of the Children of Israel and their hypocrites and the hypocrites of the Arabs and their disbelievers, in whose hearts is deviation, so they follow the ambiguous verses of God’s Book seeking discord and seeking its interpretation, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God, meaning by that that their wealth and children will not save them from God’s punishment if He inflicts it upon them - immediately in this world for their denial of the truth after it has become clear to them, and their following the ambiguous verses seeking confusion - so that it repels it from them, and that will not avail them at all against it, and in the Hereafter they are fuel of the Fire, meaning by that: its firewood.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Indeed, those who disbelieved, their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against God when Our punishment comes to them, like the way and custom of the people of Pharaoh, and those before them of the nations who denied Our signs, so We seized them for their sins, and destroyed them when they denied Our signs, so their wealth and their children did not avail them at all against God when Our punishment came to them, like those who were hastened to be punished for their denial of their Lord before the people of Pharaoh: of the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Lot, and their likes.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
Like the way of Pharaoh’s people
Some of them said: It means: Like their Sunnah.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like the way of Pharaoh’s people
, he said: Like their way.

x: Some of them said: It means: like their work.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
h
Like the way of Pharaoh’s family
, he said: Like the work of Pharaoh’s family.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like the way of Pharaoh’s family
, he said: Like the work of Pharaoh’s family.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh
, he said: Like their actions, like their denial when they denied the messengers, and he recited the statement of God: Like the habit of the people of Noah
r
(Ghafir 40:31)
, that you should be afflicted with the same punishment that afflicted them from God. He said: The habit is the action.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Tamila Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah and Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like the way of Pharaoh’s family
, he said: Like the actions of Pharaoh’s family,
h
like the way of Pharaoh’s family

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Munjab,
m: who said: Bishr bin Amara narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Like the practice of Pharaoh’s family
, he said:
h
Like the practice of Pharaoh’s family

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: like the denial of the people of Pharaoh.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they denied Our signs, so God seized them for their sins, he mentioned those who disbelieved and the actions of their denial, like the denial of those before them in denial and rejection.

x: The origin of the word da’ab comes from da’bat fi al-amr da’ban, meaning you are addicted to work and toiling in it.

i: Then the Arabs transferred its meaning to: the affair, the matter, and the habit, as Imru’ al-Qais ibn Hajar said:
x: And my recovery is a shed tear, so is there a recourse against the drawing of a scholar? As usual, from Umm Al-Huwairith before her and her neighbor Umm Al-Rabab in Masal He means by his saying: As is your habit, your affair, and your action. It is said: This is my habit and your habit forever.
He means by it: My action and your action, my affair and your affair, my affair and your affair. It is said from it: I have always been persistent and persistent.

c: It was narrated from the Arabs by hearing:
m: I have always been persistent, with a heavy hamza and a vowel, just as it was said: This is poetry and a river, so the second letter was moved because it is a letter from the six letters, so the correct word is al-dābt since its second letter is from the six letters, just as the poet said: He has a sandal that does not smell like dogs, and if you put it in the company of the scum, it will smell it. As for his saying: And God is severe in penalty, he means by it: And God is severe in His punishment for whoever disbelieves in Him and denies His messengers after the proof has been established against him.

x: The readings differed in this regard.
Some of them read it:
h
Say to those who disbelieve
h
You will be overcome

and gathered together' with the letter ta', as a way of addressing those who disbelieved that they will be overcome. They argued for their choice of reading it with the letter ta' by saying: There has already been for you a sign in two companies
r
(Al Imran 3:13)
. They said: In this is evidence that His saying:
h
You will be overcome

is also addressed to them. This is the general reading of the readers of Hijaz, Basra, and some of the Kufians. It may be permissible for someone whose intention in this verse is that those promised to be overcome are those to whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was commanded to say this, to read it with the letter ya' and the letter ta', because the address in the revelation when it was revealed was to others. So it is similar to the saying of the speaker in speech: I said to the al-Nas 114:
h
You will be overcome
, and I said to them: They will be overcome.
It was mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading:
h
Say to those who disbelieve
, ‘If you desist, you will be forgiven,’ and in our reading: If they desist, they will be forgiven (al-Anfal 8:38).

A group of the people of Kufa read it as: They will be defeated and herded, meaning: Say to the Jews: The polytheists of the Arabs will be defeated and herded to Hell. Whoever reads it in this way with this interpretation, does not allow anything other than the letter ya in his reading.

What we choose from the readings in this regard is the reading of those who read it with the letter ta’, meaning: Say, O Muhammad, to those who disbelieved from the Jews of the Children of Israel who follow what is ambiguous in the verses of the Book that I revealed to you, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation:
h
You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell
, and an evil resting place. We chose to read it this way, rather than reading it with the letter ya, because of the indication of His statement:
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in two companies (Al Imran 3
:13), that by His statement:
h
You will be overcome
, they are addressing their speech with His statement:
h
There has certainly been for you

, so attaching the speech to a similar speech is more appropriate than addressing its opposite in the report about an absent person. Another is that: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid, narrated to me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated the Quraysh on the day of Badr and entered Medina, he gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa’ and said: ‘O group of Jews, convert to Islam before you are afflicted with what afflicted the Quraysh!’

They said: ‘O Muhammad, do not let your soul deceive you that you killed a group of Quraysh who were ignorant and did not know how to fight. By God, if you had fought us, you would have known that we are the people, and that you have not done what we have done!!’ So God, the Almighty, revealed regarding that from their statement: ‘
h
Say to those who disbelieve
, “You will surely be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place” until His saying: ‘For those with insight.’”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, he said:
m: When God afflicted the Quraysh on the day of Badr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered the Jews in the market of Banu Qaynuqa when he arrived in Medina. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Yunus.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: “It was about the Banu Qaynuqa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered them in the market of Banu Qaynuqa, then he said: O group of Jews, beware of God’s punishment like that which befell the Quraysh, and submit, for you have come to know that I am a prophet sent by God. You will find that in your book and in God’s covenant with you! They said: O Muhammad, you see that I am like your people! Do not be deceived by the fact that you met a people who had no knowledge of war and that you gained an opportunity over them! By God, if we fight you, you will know that we are the people.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad,
m: the client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: These verses were revealed only about them:
h
Say to those who disbelieve
h
You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell
, and wretched is the resting place’ to for those with insight.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Say to those who disbelieve
h
You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell

, and an evil resting place,’ Phinehas the Jew said on the day of Badr: Do not let Muhammad be deceived by the fact that he defeated and killed Quraysh! Quraysh are not good at fighting, so this verse was revealed:
h
Say to those who disbelieve
h
You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell
, and an evil resting place.’

x: All of these reports indicate that those addressed by His statement,
h
You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell
, and wretched is the resting place, are the Jews to whom it is said,
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in two companies (Al Imran 3
:13), the verse - and it indicates that reading it with the ta’ is more appropriate than reading it with the ya’. The meaning of his saying:
h
And you will be gathered together
, is that you will be gathered and brought to Hell. As for his saying:
h
And what an evil resting place
, what an evil bed is Hell to which you will be herded.
Mujahid used to say something like:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what an evil resting place
, he said: What an evil resting place they have prepared for themselves.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

evidence.text: Abu Ja'far said: The readings differed in this regard.
Some of them read it: Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome and gathered together' with the letter ta', as a way of addressing those who disbelieved that they will be overcome.
This is the general reading of the readers of Hijaz, Basra, and some of the Kufians.

It may be permissible for someone whose intention in this verse is that those promised to be overcome are those to whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was commanded to say this, to read it with the letter ya' and the letter ta', because the address in the revelation when it was revealed was to others.
It was mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading: Say to those who disbelieve, ‘If you desist, you will be forgiven,’ and in our reading: If they desist, they will be forgiven (al-Anfal 8:38).
A group of the people of Kufa read it as: They will be defeated and herded, meaning: Say to the Jews: The polytheists of the Arabs will be defeated and herded to Hell.
Whoever reads it in this way with this interpretation, does not allow anything other than the letter ya in his reading.

Abu Jaʿfar said: What we choose from the readings in this regard is the reading of those who read it with the letter ta’, meaning: Say, O Muhammad, to those who disbelieved from the Jews of the Children of Israel who follow what is ambiguous in the verses of the Book that I revealed to you, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation: You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell, and an evil resting place.

We chose to read it this way, rather than reading it with the letter ya, because of the indication of His statement: There has certainly been for you a sign in two companies (Al Imran 3:13), that by His statement: You will be overcome, they are addressing their speech with His statement: There has certainly been for you, so attaching the speech to a similar speech is more appropriate than addressing its opposite in the report about an absent person.

Abu Jaʿfar said: All of these reports indicate that those addressed by His statement, You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell, and wretched is the resting place, are the Jews to whom it is said, There has certainly been for you a sign in two companies (Al Imran 3:13), the verse - and it indicates that reading it with the ta’ is more appropriate than reading it with the ya’.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Say, O Muhammad, to those who disbelieved among the Jews who are among your al-Balad 90:There has already been for you a sign, meaning: a sign and indication of the truth of what I say: that you will be overcome, and a lesson, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: There has certainly been a sign for you, a lesson and reflection.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly, except that he said: and thinking. In two groups, meaning, in two parties and groups, and a group is a group of people, met for war, and one of the two groups was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who were with him who witnessed the Battle of Badr, and the other was the polytheists of Quraysh, a group fighting in the way of God, a group fighting in obedience to God and for His religion, and they were the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and another was disbelieving, and they were the polytheists of Quraysh, as:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met

. One company was fighting in the way of God,” the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Badr, and the other was disbelieving, the disbelieving group of Quraysh.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad,
m: the client of Zaid ibn Thabit, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met
. One company was fighting in the cause of God,” Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and the other was disbelieving, Quraysh on the day of Badr.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in two companies
, he said: In Muhammad and his companions, and the polytheists of Quraysh on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met
, one company fighting in the cause of God, he said: That was on the day of Badr, when the Muslims and the infidels met.

x: And it was raised: A group fighting in the way of God. And it was said before that: In two groups, meaning: One of them fights in the way of God - in the beginning, as the poet said: I was like two legs, one healthy and the other in which time had thrown away the leg and it had failed. As Ibn Mufrij said: I was like two men: one healthy man and one with a doubtful illness. As for the healthy one, it is Azd Shanu’ah, and as for the paralyzed one, it is Azd Oman. The Arabs do the same with every repeated word that precedes it, if the predicate of the repeated word is a predicate: they return it to the first case once, and start it up again in the nominative case, and put it in the accusative case in the complete form of the defective verb. All of that was made genitive, so it was made genitive in response to the beginning of the sentence, as if he meant if he made that genitive: So I was like two men: like this one, a healthy man and a sick man.

And likewise the genitive case in his saying: a group is permissible in response to his saying: in two groups that met, in a group fighting in the way of God. Although this is permissible in Arabic, I do not permit reading it in this way, because the evidence from the readings is unanimously agreed upon to the contrary. If his saying: a group had come in the accusative case, it would also have been permissible based on his saying: There was for you a sign in the two companies that met, which were different.

The reading of this differed. So he read it as the people of Medina read: You will see them with a taa, meaning: There has been for you, O Jews, a sign in the two groups that met, one group fighting in the way of God, and the other disbelieving. You will see the polytheists twice as many as the Muslims, with your own eyes. He meant by that to admonish them, saying: There is a lesson for you, O Jews, in what you saw of the small number of Muslims and the large number of polytheists, and the victory of these, despite their small number, over those, despite their large number. The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra and some of the Meccans read it as: They see them twice as many with a ya’, meaning: The Muslims who fight in the cause of God see the disbelieving group as twice as many Muslims in terms of power. So the interpretation of the verse according to their reading is: There has already been for you, O group of Jews, a lesson and reflection on the two groups that met, one group fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving.
These Muslims, despite their small number, see these polytheists, despite their large number.

What is the interpretation of the reading of the one who reads it with the letter ya? Which of the two groups saw its companion twice as much? Is it the Muslim group that saw the polytheist woman twice as much, or is it the polytheist woman that saw the Muslim woman likewise, or is it someone else who saw one of them likewise?
The people of interpretation differed on that.

Some of them said: The group that saw the other group as being like themselves, the Muslim group saw the number of the polytheist group as being like myself, the number of the Muslim group, God Almighty made it less in their eyes until they saw it as being like themselves, then He made it less in another situation so they saw it as being like themselves.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
m: h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met

. One company was fighting in the cause of God and the other was disbelievers. They saw them twice their number with their own eyes.” He said: This was the day of Badr. Abdullah Ibn Masoud said: We looked at the polytheists and saw them becoming weaker than us, then we looked at them and did not see them surpass us by a single man. This is the saying of God, the Almighty: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and He made you as little in their eyes. (al-Anfal 8:44) The meaning of the verse according to this interpretation is: There has been for you, O community of Jews, a sign in two groups that met: one of them was Muslim and the other was disbelieving. The disbelieving group was numerous, while the Muslim group was few in number. The small group saw the large group as being many times their number, that they were only multiplied by one multiplier, so they saw them as twice their number. So one of the two multipliers at that time was the number that was equal to the number of the group that saw them, and the other multiplier was the double that was greater than their number. This is one of the two meanings of the diminution with which God Almighty informed the believers that He had made them small in their eyes. The other meaning of it is the second reduction, according to what Ibn Masoud said: which is that he showed them the number of polytheists as being the same as their number, not exceeding them. So that is the second reduction about which God Almighty said: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes (al-Anfal 8:44).

x: Others of this opinion said: Those who saw the polytheists as equal to themselves were the Muslims. However, the Muslims saw them as they were in number and did not diminish them in their eyes, but God supported them with His victory. They said: Therefore, God Almighty said to the Jews: There has certainly been a lesson for you in them, frightening them with that that what happened to the people of Badr might happen to them from them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met - one company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving

, was revealed to alleviate the suffering on the Day of Badr, for the believers on that day were three hundred and thirteen men, and the polytheists were twice as many, so God the Almighty revealed: “
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met - one company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving

. They saw them twice as many with their eyes,” and the polytheists were six hundred and twenty-six, so God supported the believers. So this was what was meant to alleviate the suffering of the believers.

x: This narration contradicts what the reports have agreed upon about the number of polytheists on the day of Badr. This is because people differed about their number in two ways. Surat Al Imran 3:13 There has already been for you a sign in the two companies that met - one company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving. They saw them as twice their number, by the sight of the eye.
h
And God supports
with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.

Some of them said: Their number was a thousand, and some of them said: Between nine hundred and a thousand. It was mentioned that they numbered a thousand: Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamadani narrated, Musʿab ibn al-Miqdam narrated, Israʿil narrated, Abu Ishaq narrated, on the authority of Haritha, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out for Badr, and we got there before the polytheists. We found two men there, one of whom was from Quraysh and a freedman of Uqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. As for the Quraysh man, he escaped, but we captured the freedman of Uqbah. We asked him, How many are these people? He replied, By God, they are many and very strong. When the Muslims said that, they would beat him until they took him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said to him, How many are these people? He replied, By God, they are many and very strong.

The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, tried hard to tell him how many they were, but he refused. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him, How many camels do they slaughter? He replied, Ten every day. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, These people are one thousand.

c: Abu Saeed bin Yusha’ al-Baghdadi told me, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: We captured a man from them - meaning from the polytheists - on the day of Badr, so we said: How many were you? He said: One thousand. It was mentioned that their number was between nine hundred and one thousand: Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Ibn Ishaq narrated, Yazid ibn Ruman narrated, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a group of his companions to the water of Badr to seek report for him from it. They found a messenger from Quraysh who included Aslam, the slave of Banu al-Hajjaj, and Urayd Abu Yasar, the slave of Banu al-ʿAs. They brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How many are the people? They said: Many! He said: What is their number? They said: We do not know! He said: How many do they slaughter each day? They said: Nine days, ten days. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people are between nine hundred and a thousand.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: “
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met - one company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving -

they saw them twice as many as they were, with their own eyes.” That was on the day of Badr, when the polytheists were a thousand or close to them, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were three hundred and some men.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met
, up to his statement: as seen by the eyes, he said: They were weakened by them, so they killed seventy of them and took seventy captive, on the day of Badr.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement: “
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met - one company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving

; they saw them twice as many as they were, with their own eyes.” He said: That was on the day of Badr, and the polytheists were nine hundred and fifty, and the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were three hundred and thirteen.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told me, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were three hundred and a few, and the polytheists were between nine hundred and a thousand.

x: All of those we mentioned contradict the statement we narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the number of polytheists on the day of Badr. Since what was said by the one whose statement we narrated - who mentioned that their number was more than nine hundred - is correct, then the first interpretation that we stated based on the narration we narrated from Ibn Masʿud is more appropriate for interpreting the verse.

Others said: The number of polytheists was more than nine hundred, so the Muslims saw their number differently than it was. They said: God made the Muslims see the number of polytheists as small, as a sign for the Muslims. They said: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
They will see them twice their number
, those addressed by His saying:
h
There has certainly been for you a sign in two companies

. They said: They are the Jews, except that He returned from addressing to reporting on the absent, because God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say that to them, so it was good to address them once, and report on them another time, as He said:
Until, when you were in the ship and it sailed with them with a good wind

They said: If someone were to say to us: How is it said: They see them twice as many as they see with their own eyes, when you know that the polytheists at that time were three times as many as the Muslims?

We said to them: It is like the speaker who says while he has a slave: I need his like, so you need him and his like. Then he says: I need twice his like, so that is report about his need for his like, and for my like that is the like. And it is like the man who says: I have a thousand and I need twice its like. So he needs three. So when he intended for the thousand to be included in the meaning of the like, the like became two, and the two became three.

i: He said:
x: And similar to it in speech: I see you like you, as if he said: I see you twice as much, and I see you twice as much.
Meaning: I see you twice as much. They said: This is in the meaning of three like them.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that God saw the number of the disbelieving group as twice the number of the Muslim group. This is also contrary to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation. Because God Almighty said in His Book: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes and He made you as few in their eyes (al-Anfal 8:44), so He informed that each of the two groups made its number small in the sight of the other.
Others read it as: You will see them with a damma on the ta, meaning: God will show you them twice as many.

The most correct of these readings is the reading of the one who read: they see them with a ya’, meaning: and another is a disbeliever, the Muslims see them twice as many - meaning: twice the number of Muslims, because God made them less in one case, so their guessing of them was like that, then He made them less in their eyes than the first guessing, so they guessed them as the number of Muslims, then a third guessing, so they guessed them as less than the number of Muslims, like:

c: Abu Saeed Al-Baghdadi told me, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: They seemed small in our eyes on the day of Badr, so much so that I said to a man next to me: Do you think they are seventy? He said: I think they are a hundred. He said: So we captured one of them and we said: How many were you? He said: A thousand.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Qatada
m: that he used to say: If you could see them, they would be twice as many as you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told me, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that.

x: In the two reports that we have narrated on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, there is a clear indication of the difference in the Muslims’ estimates of the number of polytheists at different times. So God, the Almighty, informed the Jews about the difference in the circumstances of their numbers with the Muslims, as they had it with them, despite the Jews’ knowledge of the total number of the two groups, informing them that He is the supporter of the believers with His victory, lest they be deceived by their numbers and their strength, and so that they may beware of Him, lest He inflict on them punishment at the hands of the believers, like what He inflicted on the polytheists of Quraysh at Badr. As for his saying: the vision of the eye, it is a source of: I saw it. It is said: I saw it with an opinion and a vision, and I saw in a dream a good vision, not a flow. It is said: He is from me the vision of the eye and the vision of the eye, in the accusative and nominative, meaning: where my sight falls on it, and it is from the opinion like it.
And the people are visions, if they sit where they see each other. So the meaning of that is: they see them - where their sight catches them and their eyes see them - twice as much as them.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And God supports

, strengthens, with His victory whomever He wills. This is from the saying of the one who says: I have supported so-and-so with such-and-such, if I have strengthened and aided him, so I support him with support. And from it is the saying of God, the Most High: And remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength
r
, meaning: the possessor of strength.

The interpretation of the statement is: You, O group of Jews, were in two groups that met, one of them fighting in the way of God and the other disbelieving, the Muslims saw them as twice their number with their own eyes, so We supported the Muslim group, who were few in number, against the disbelieving group, who were many in number, until they defeated them - a consideration and a reflection, and God strengthens with His victory whomever He wills.

And He, the Most High, said: Indeed in that, meaning: in what we did with those whose situation we described: of our support for the Muslim group despite their small number, over the disbelieving group despite their large number, is a lesson, meaning: for the one who thinks and takes heed, for whoever understands and remembers and sees the truth, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed in that is a lesson for those of insight, meaning: They had a lesson and thought in these people. May God support them and slaughter them against their enemy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

evidence.text: Although this is permissible in Arabic, I do not permit reading it in this way, because the evidence from the readings is unanimously agreed upon to the contrary.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.

So he read it as the people of Medina read: You will see them with a taa, meaning: There has been for you, O Jews, a sign in the two groups that met, one group fighting in the way of God, and the other disbelieving.

The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra and some of the Meccans read it as: They see them twice as many with a ya’, meaning: The Muslims who fight in the cause of God see the disbelieving group as twice as many Muslims in terms of power.

So the interpretation of the verse according to their reading is: There has already been for you, O group of Jews, a lesson and reflection on the two groups that met, one group fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving.
If someone says: What is the interpretation of the reading of the one who reads it with the letter ya?
Abu Jaafar said: Others read it as: You will see them with a damma on the ta, meaning: God will show you them twice as many.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these readings is the reading of the one who read: they see them with a ya’, meaning: and another is a disbeliever, the Muslims see them twice as many - meaning: twice the number of Muslims, because God made them less in one case, so their guessing of them was like that, then He made them less in their eyes than the first guessing, so they guessed them as the number of Muslims, then a third guessing, so they guessed them as less than the number of Muslims, like:

x: God Almighty means: He has made attractive to people the love of what they desire of women, children, and all that is counted. He only wanted to rebuke the Jews who preferred the world and the love of leadership in it, over following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after they knew of his truthfulness. Al-Hassan used to say: Whoever adorns it, no one is more critical of it than its Creator.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me that Abu Naim told us that Abu Al-Ash'ath told us
m: on his authority.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Hafs bin Umar bin Sa'd, that Umar said:
m: When the verse, The love of desires has been made attractive to people, was revealed, I said, Now, O Lord, when You have made them attractive to us, then the verse was revealed, Say, 'Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who fear God, there are gardens beneath which rivers flow.
r
(Al Imran 3:15)
, the verse. As for Qantar, it is the plural of Qintar.

x: The interpreters differed on the amount of the qintar.
Some of them said. It is one thousand two hundred ounces.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Mahmin, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd, on the authority of Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said:
m: A qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Husayn told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Jaʿd, on the authority of Muʿadh,
m: similarly.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: he told us - meaning Hafs ibn Maysarah - on the authority of Abu Marwan, on the authority of Abu Taybah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Malik Al-Muzani told us, he said, Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab told me, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, he said:
m: The qintar is one thousand two hundred ounces.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: similarly.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya Al-Dharee’ told me, he said, Shababah told us, he said, Mukhallad bin Abdul Wahid told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Maimouna, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A qintar is one thousand and two hundred ounces.’”

x: Others said: A qintar is one thousand and two hundred dinars.
Who said that?

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A qintar is one thousand two hundred dinars.”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: A qintar is one thousand two hundred dinars.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A qintar is one thousand and two hundred dinars, and of silver it is one thousand and two hundred mithqals.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: The qintars are the qintars, meaning a lot of money in gold and silver. A qintar is one thousand two hundred dinars, and a qintar is one thousand two hundred mithqals of silver.

x: Others said: A qintar is twelve thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A qintar is twelve thousand dirhams, or a thousand dinars.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: A qintar is a Surat Al Imran 3:14 Adorned for people is the love of desires - of women and children and heaped-up sums of gold and silver
h
and branded horses
and livestock and tilth. That is
h
the enjoyment of worldly life
, but Allah has with Him the best return. thousand dinars, and of silver it is twelve thousand dirhams.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: The qintar is twelve thousand.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: A qintar is twelve thousand.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said,
m: he told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Twelve thousand.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: A qintar is a thousand dinars, the blood money for one of you.

x: Others said: It is eighty thousand dirhams, or one hundred pounds of gold.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said:
m: A qintar is eighty thousand.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said:
m: The qintar is eighty thousand.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: We used to say that a qintar is one hundred pounds of gold, or eighty thousand of silver.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: A qintar is one hundred pounds of gold, or eighty thousand dirhams of silver.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, who said:
m: A qintar is one hundred pounds.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: A qintar is one hundred pounds, which is eight thousand mithqals.

x: Others said: A qintar is seventy thousand.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: heaped-up qintars, he said: A qintar is seventy thousand dinars.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Umar bin Hawshab told us, he said:
m: I heard Ata al-Khurasani say: Ibn Umar was asked about the qintar, so he said: Seventy thousand. And others said: It is a bull’s weight of musk filled with gold. Mention who said that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Salim bin Nuh told us, he said, Saeed Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Abu Nadhra, he said:
m: A bull’s musk filled with gold.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Abu Al-Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah:
m: A bull’s musk filled with gold.

x: Others said: It is a lot of money.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, he said:
m: h
The heaped-up qinātir
means a lot of money, some of it on top of some.

x: Some scholars of Arabic language have stated that the Arabs do not define a qintar as a specific amount of weight, but rather say: it is a certain amount of weight.
It may be that way, because if it had been limited in its extent at that time, there would not have been all this difference among the early interpreters of it.

The correct thing to say about that is: It is a lot of money, as Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said, and its weight should not be set by any arbitrary limit. What was said was said from what we narrated. As for al-Muqantara, it is doubled, as if the qintars are three, and al-Muqantara is nine.
It is as al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: a lot of money, some of it on top of some, like:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The heaped-up qintars of gold and silver, and the heaped-up qintar is a lot of money, some of it on top of the other.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
The heaped-up qinātir
, meaning a lot of money of gold and silver.

x: Others said: The meaning of
h
the heaped-up qinātir
is: the minted dirhams or dinars.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi.
m: As for his saying: Al-Muqantara, he says: The ones that were struck until they became dinars or dirhams.

c: It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying:
h
