And if you have given one of them a great amount (An-Nisa’

: 20), a report whose chain of transmission is sound, we would not attribute it to anyone else. That is what: Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, he said, Zuhair ibn Muhammad told us, he said, Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash and Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And if you have given one of them a great amount (An-Nisa’
: 20), he said: A thousand hundred, meaning: two thousand.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-masumah.
Some of them said: She is the shepherdess.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: The marked horses, he said: the shepherds, the ones that graze.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: It is the shepherd, meaning: the one who is at large.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Talha Al-Qannad, he said,
m: I heard Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abza say: The shepherdess.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And the branded horses
, he said: the shepherds.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And the branded horses
* are those set free to graze.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hassan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
And the branded horses
, he said: The grazing horses.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: He used to say: The grazing horses.

x: Others said: Al-Masuma means: the beautiful.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, he said, Mujahid said:
m: The one marked is the one who is well-marked.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
and branded horses
, he said: the well-marked and beautiful ones.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And branded horses
, he said: Well-marked.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Al-Muthama.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri’ told us: Saeed ibn Abi Ayoub told us, on the authority of Bashir ibn Abi Amr al-Khawlani, who said:
m: I asked Ikrimah about marked horses. He said: Their marking means their beauty.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told me, on the authority of Bashir bin Abi Amr Al-Khawlani, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: The branded horses, he said: Their branding is good.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The branded horses and livestock, the wonderful. This hadith was told to me by Amr bin Hammad, other than Musa. He said: The shepherdess.

x: Others said: The marked horses, the marked ones.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And the marked horses, meaning the marked ones.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the marked horses, and their mark, their color.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
and branded horses
, he said: The mark on the faces of horses.

x: Others said: Al-Masmouma is prepared for jihad.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And the branded horses
, he said: those prepared for jihad.

x: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting his statement: and the marked horses is the one marked with marks, the beautiful, the splendidly beautiful to whoever sees them. Because marking in the speech of the Arabs means to inform. Surat Al Imran 3:14 Adorned for people is the love of desires - of women and children and heaped-up sums of gold and silver
h
and branded horses
and livestock and tilth. That is
h
the enjoyment of worldly life

, but Allah has with Him the best return. So the beautiful horses are marked by God informing them of the beauty of their colors, marks and appearances, and they are also the marked. And from that is the saying of Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan in describing horses: In your conscience, the arrows are marked with the likeness of jinn It means the labels, the parameters, and Labid’s saying: And on the morning of the two-century valley, we came to them in a state of tumult, during which the rising tide appeared.

The meaning of the interpretation of the one who interpreted that: the pure, the taught, and the wonderful, are one. As for the statement of those who interpreted it to mean: the shepherdess, then he went with the statement of the one who said: I named the livestock, so I name them Isama, if I made them graze the grass and herbs, as God Almighty said: And from it is a tree in which you graze (al-Nahl 16:5a), meaning: you graze, and from it is the statement of Al-Akhtal: Like Ibn Buza'ah or someone like him, you are better off with Ibn Warjmah Al-Ajmal He means by that: the shepherd of camels. So if it is meant that the livestock are the ones that grazed, it is said: The livestock grazed, meaning shepherded, and for that reason it is said: Grazing camels, meaning shepherding, but it is not widespread in their speech: I grazed the livestock, meaning I pastured them, but rather it is said when that is meant: She fed them.

If this is the case, then the interpretation of the marked one is that it is the one marked with the meanings we described above, which is more correct. As for what Ibn Zayd said: that it is prepared in the way of God, it is an interpretation of the meaning of marked, isolated.

Al-Anʿam is the plural of Naʿam, and they are the eight pairs that he mentioned in his book: of sheep, goats, cows, and camels. As for tillage, it is planting. The interpretation of the words: The love of desires for women, children, such-and-such, livestock and crops has been made attractive to people.

By His Most High’s saying, That, He means everything mentioned in this verse, such as women, sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, branded horses, livestock, and crops. So He used His saying, That, as a metaphor for all of them. This indicates that That includes many things with different meanings, and it is used as a metaphor for all of that. As for His statement:
h
The enjoyment of worldly life

, it is report from God that all of that is something that its people enjoy in this world while they are alive, so they attain it in it, and make it a connection in their livelihood, and a reason for fulfilling their desires, the love of which has been made attractive to them in their immediate world, without it being a provision for their afterlife, and a means of drawing them closer to their Lord, except for what is taken in His path, and spent from it in what He has commanded.
As for his saying:
h
And with God is the best return
, He, may His praise be glorified, means by that:
h
And with God is the best return
, meaning: the best return, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And with God is the best place to return, meaning the best place to return, which is Paradise. It is a source on the example of mafʿal from the saying of the speaker: The man returned to us, when he came back, so he returns, returning, returning, returning, and returning, except that the position of the fa’ in it is hamzated, and the ‘ayn is changed from waw to alif with its movement to fathah. Since its fate was the fat-ha, and its movement was transferred to the letter before it - which is the fa' of the verb - it was changed and became an alif, as it was said: He said, so the 'ayn of the verb became an alif, because its fate was the fat-ha. And al-ma'ab is like al-maqal, al-ma'ad, and al-majal, all of that is maf'al, and the movement of its 'ayn was transferred to its fa', so its waw or ya' became an alif because of the fat-ha of what preceded it.

x: If someone says: How can it be said: And with God is the best destination, when you know what painful torment and severe punishment He has with Him on that day? Say: This is intended for a specific group of people, and its meaning is: And God has a good destination for those who fear their Lord.

c: And He has informed us
m: of that in the verse that follows it.

x: What is the best place to return?
It is what He, the Most High, described him with, which is the return to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein he will abide eternally, and to purified spouses and the approval of God.

He, may His praise be glorified, means: Say, O Muhammad, to the people for whom the love of desires of women and children has been made attractive, and all that our Lord, may His praise be glorified, mentioned: Shall I inform you, I will inform you and teach you, of something better than that, meaning: something better and more excellent for you, than that, meaning: of what has been made attractive to you in this world, the love of desires of women and children and heaped-up sums of gold and silver, and the types of wealth that are the pleasures of this world. Then the Arab scholars differed about the place where the question reached in this speech.
Some of them said: This ended with His saying: Of that, then He began the report about what is for those who feared their Lord, so it was said:
h
For those who feared their Lord are gardens
beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, so that is why He raised the gardens. Whoever says this statement, does not permit anything in his statement:
h
Gardens beneath which rivers flow except the nominative

, because it is the predicate of a subject that is not rejected by his statement: with good, so the accusative is permissible in it. And even though it is the predicate of a subject according to them, it clarifies the meaning of good that God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the al-Nas 114:Shall I inform you of it? And the gardens, according to this statement, are raised by the lam in his statement:
h
For those who fear their Lord

. And others of them said something similar to this statement, except that they said: If you make the lam in his statement: For those a connection of informing, then the accusative and the nominative are permissible in the gardens: the accusative is in response to the good, and the nominative is on the basis that his statement: For those who fear is the predicate of a subject, as we have explained before.
Others said: Rather, the ultimate question is his statement:
h
With their Lord
, then he began: Gardens beneath which rivers flow. They said: The interpretation of the statement is: “Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that
h
for those who fear their Lord
?” Then it is as if it was said: What is for them? Or: What is that? So he said: It is Gardens beneath which rivers flow, the verse.

The most correct of these statements in my opinion is the statement of those who made the interrogative a finite one when he said: Better than that, and the predicate after it is a subject about who has the gardens with his saying:
h
For those who feared their Lord are gardens

, so the way out of that is the way out of the predicate, and it is an explanation of the meaning of the good that he said: Shall I inform you of it? So the speech then has no need for a pronoun. Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: As for his statement: abiding therein forever, it is in the accusative case as a definite noun. The meaning of his statement: for those who feared God, for those who feared God and obeyed Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience,
h
with their Lord
, meaning by that: for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow
h
with their Lord

. And the gardens, the orchards, and we have explained that with evidence previously, and that his saying: Underneath which rivers flow, means: beneath the trees, and that eternity in it is the perpetuation of remaining in it, and that the purified spouses are the women of Paradise who have been purified from every harm that befalls the women of the people of this world, from menstruation, semen, urine, postpartum bleeding, and the like of that harm, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
His saying:
h
And the pleasure of God
, means:
h
and the pleasure of God

, and it is a source from the saying of the speaker: May God be pleased with so-and-so, so he is pleased with him with an imperfect pleasure and pleasure and satisfaction and contentment. As for the pleasure with the damma of the ra, it is the language of Qais, and it is how Asim used to read.
God Almighty mentioned among the good things He mentioned for those who feared Him, His pleasure, because His pleasure is the highest level of honor for the people of Paradise, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said:
m: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, God Almighty will say: I will give you something better than this. They will say: O our Lord, what is better than this? He will say: My pleasure. And His statement: And God is All-Seeing of the servants, meaning by that: God is All-Seeing of those of His servants who fear Him and are in awe of Him, and obey Him, and prefer what He has of what He has prepared for those who fear Him over the love of what has been made attractive to them in this world of the desires of women and children and all the rest of what He, the Most High, has enumerated, and of those who do not fear Him and are in awe of Him, but disobey Him and obey Satan and prefer what has been made attractive to them in this world of the love of the desires of women and children and money, over what He has of eternal bliss. He, the Most High, is All-Knowing of every group of them, until He rewards all of them when they return to Him with their reward, the doer of good for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil.

x: The meaning of this is: Say, Shall I inform you of something better than that for those who fear God? [those who] say, Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
h
Those who say

may have two possible syntactic meanings: the accusative case in response to the first those, and the nominative case in the beginning, since it was at the beginning of another verse other than the one in which the first those was, so its nominative case is similar to the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties (al-Tawbah 9:111), then He said at the beginning of the verse that follows it: Those who repent and worship (al-Tawbah 9:112). If it had come in the accusative case, it would have been permissible. The meaning of His statement:
h
Those who say
, ‘Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins’:
h
Those who say
, We have believed in You and in Your Prophet and what he brought from You.

“So forgive us our sins,” means: So cover our sins for us, by pardoning them and leaving us alone for them, and save us from the punishment of the Fire, ward off Your punishment from us by the Fire, lest You punish us with it. The meaning of this is: Do not punish us, O our Lord, with the Fire. They only specified the issue to protect them from the torment of Hell, because whoever is removed from Hell on that day will have won salvation from the torment of God and a good final destination. The origin of his saying: Qana is from the saying of the speaker: May God protect so-and-so from such-and-such, meaning: He protected him, so He protected him. So if someone asks about this, he says: Protect me from such-and-such.

By his saying the patient ones, he means those who were patient in hardship, distress, and times of battle. By the truthful he means those who were truthful to God in their words by affirming their acknowledgement of Him and His Messenger and what He brought from Him, by doing what He commanded them to do and refraining from what He forbade them from doing. By the obedient it means those who are obedient to Him. We have already explained all of these letters and their meanings with evidence of the correctness of what we have said about them, and with reports from those who have said something about them, in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: The patient, the truthful, the obedient, and the spenders. “The truthful” are people whose mouths are truthful, whose hearts and tongues are upright, and who are truthful in secret and in public. The patient are people who are patient in obeying God and are patient in abstaining from His prohibitions. The obedient are those who are obedient to God. As for the spenders, they are those who pay the zakat of their wealth, and who devote it to the way God has commanded them to do it, and who spend their wealth in the ways that God, the Most High, has permitted them to spend it in. As for the patient and the truthful, and the rest of these letters, they are in the accusative case in response to His statement:
h
Those who say
, ‘Our Lord, we have believed.’ The accusative case in these letters indicates that His statement:
h
Those who say
is in the accusative case in response to His statement: For those who fear their Lord.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the people who have this description.
Some of them said: They are the ones who pray at dawn.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And those who seek forgiveness before dawn, they are the people of prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And those who seek forgiveness in the hours of the pre-dawn hours, he said: They pray in the hours of the pre-dawn hours.

x: Others said: They are those who seek forgiveness.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Harith bin Abi Matar, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Hatib, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I heard a man in the early hours of the morning in a corner of the mosque saying: O Lord, You commanded me and I obeyed You, and this is early morning, so forgive me. So I looked and saw that it was Ibn Masoud.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said:
m: I asked Abd al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir about the statement of God Almighty: And those who seek forgiveness before dawn, he said: Sulayman bin Musa told me, he said, Nafi’ told us: Ibn Umar used to stay up at night in prayer and then say: O Nafi’, have we reached dawn? He would say: No, so he would repeat the prayer, and if I said: Yes, he would sit and seek forgiveness and supplicate in the morning.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of some of the Basrans, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: We were commanded to seek forgiveness seventy times in the early hours of the morning.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, he said, Abu Yaqub Al-Dhabi told us, he said:
m: I heard Jaʿfar bin Muhammad say: Whoever prays at night and then seeks forgiveness at the end of the night seventy times, he will be recorded among those who seek forgiveness at dawn.

x: Others said: They are those who witness the dawn prayer in a group.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said,
m: Ismail bin Muslima, the brother of Al-Qa’nabi, told us, he said, Ya’qub bin Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said, I said to Zaid bin Aslam: Who are those who seek forgiveness at dawn? He said: They are those who witness the dawn prayer.

x: The most appropriate of these sayings to interpret his statement:
h
Those who seek forgiveness at dawn is the saying of the one who said

: They are those who ask their Lord to cover up their disgrace therein. By magic is the plural of magic. The most obvious meaning of this is that they ask Him through supplication. It may also mean that they seek His forgiveness through work and prayer, but the most obvious meaning is what we mentioned about supplication.
By that, may His praise be glorified, He means:
h
God bears witness
that there is no god but Him, and the angels and those with knowledge bear witness. So the angels are connected to the name God, and that is open with witness.

Some of the Basrans interpreted his saying, God witnessed, as meaning God decreed, and raised the angels, meaning: and the angels are witnesses and people of knowledge. Thus, the reading of the people of Islam was read with the opening of the alif of annahu, based on what I mentioned about the application of shahad in the first annahu, and the breaking of the alif of the second in and its beginning. Except that some of the later scholars of Arabic read it all with the opening of both alifs, meaning:
h
God bears witness

that there is no god but Him, and that the religion with God is Islam - so he connected annahu with the first annahu, then he deleted the conjunction waw, which is intended in the speech. He argued for that by saying that Ibn Abbas read it:
h
God bears witness

that there is no god but Him, the verse. Then he said: annahu al-din, with the breaking of the first anna, and the opening of the second anna by applying shahad to it, and he made the first anna an objection in the speech, not applying shahad to it, and that Ibn Masoud read
h
God bears witness

that there is no god but Him with the opening of annahu and the breaking of annahu from: Indeed the religion with God is Islam - based on the meaning of applying the testimony to the first annahu, and the second anna is the beginning.

So he claimed that by his reading of them with the opening, he intended to combine the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud. So he contradicted in his reading what he read of that, as I described, all the readings of the people of Islam, past and present, by claiming an interpretation on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud, he claimed that they said it and read it. It is not known what he claimed against them with a sound or weak narration. And sufficient evidence of the error of his reading is that it departs from the reading of the people of Islam.

The correct reading, since the matter is as we have described, is to open the alif of the first that and break the alif of the second that, I mean from his saying: Indeed, the religion with God is Islam, as a beginning.

c: It was narrated from Al-Saddī
m: in his interpretation of that, a statement that indicates the correctness of what was read in that by those we mentioned, from the people of Arabic, in the opening of that from his saying: Indeed, the religion, which is what: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
h
God bears witness
that there is no god but Him, and the angels bear witness to there is no god but Him, the Almighty, the Wise, he said:
h
God bears witness

, He, the angels, and the scholars among the al-Nas 114:that the religion with God is Islam. This interpretation indicates that the testimony is only effective in the second one in his saying: The religion in the sight of God is Islam. So according to this interpretation, two aspects of interpretation are permissible in the first: One of them: that it is in the accusative case as a condition, meaning: God testifies that He is One - so it is open in the sense of the genitive according to the doctrine of some Arab scholars, and in the sense of the accusative according to the doctrine of some of them - and the testimony is working on the second that, as if you said: God testifies that the religion with God is Islam, because He is One. Then it is presented because He is One, so you open it according to that interpretation. The second aspect: That the first in is broken in the sense of beginning, because it is an objection to it, and the testimony is based on the second an. So the meaning of the statement is:
h
God bears witness

- for there is no god but Him - and the angels, that the religion with God is Islam, like the saying of the speaker: I bear witness - for I am right - that you are innocent of what you are blamed for. So the first in is broken, because it is an objection, and the testimony is based on the second an.

x: As for his saying: establishing justice, it means: He is the one who oversees justice among His creation. Al-Qist is justice, from their saying: He is just and has been just, if he is fair. And the word standing is used for cutting. Some grammarians of Basra claimed that it is a state of Huwa in La ilaha illa Hu. Some grammarians of Kufa claimed that it is a state of the name of God which is with his saying:
h
God bears witness

, so its meaning is: God, the one who establishes justice, bears witness that there is no god but Him. It was mentioned that it is also in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: And those of knowledge who establish justice, then the alif and lam Surat Al Imran 3:18
h
God bears witness

that there is no god except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice. There is no god except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. were deleted from al-Qa'im, so it became indefinite and it is an attribute of a definite noun, so it was put in the accusative.

The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is the opinion of those who make it definitively an attribute of God, may He be glorified, because the angels and those of knowledge are conjoined with Him. Likewise, what is correct is that His saying, standing, is a state of it. As for the interpretation of his saying: There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise, it is a denial that there is anything worthy of worship other than the One who has no partner in His kingdom. By the Mighty he means the One from whom nothing He wills is impossible, and no one who punishes or takes revenge on Him can defeat Him. He is the Wise in His management, so no defect enters Him.

The meaning of this verse, may His praise be exalted, was to deny what the Christians who argued with the Messenger of God (may God's prayers and peace be upon him) attributed to Jesus regarding his sonship, and what the rest of the polytheists attributed to him regarding his having a partner and taking others as lords besides Him.

c: So God informed them
m: about Himself that He is the Creator of everything other than Him, and that He is the Lord of everything that every disbeliever and polytheist has taken as a lord besides Him, and that this is what He, His angels, and the people of knowledge among His creation bear witness to. So the Most High began with Himself, to glorify Himself and to purify Him from what those polytheists we have mentioned attributed to Him - what they attributed to Him, just as He has prescribed for His servants to begin their affairs by mentioning Him before mentioning others, thus disciplining His creation. What is meant by the speech is the report of the testimony of those whom He has chosen from among His creation and sanctified Him: from among His angels and the scholars of His servants.

c: So He informed them that
m: His angels - whom the worshippers other than Him from among the polytheists venerate and many of them worship - and the people of knowledge among them, deny what they are upon and are established in their disbelief and their saying about Jesus, and the saying of whoever among the rest of creation has taken a lord other than Him, so He said: The angels and the people of knowledge have testified that there is no god but Him, and that whoever takes a lord other than God is a liar, as an argument from Him for His Prophet, peace be upon him, against those who argued with him from the delegation of Najran about Jesus. He objected to the mention of God and His description, as I have explained, as He, the Most High, said: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God (al-Anfal 8:41), opening the speech with His name, so he opened with His name and praise of Himself the testimony to what we have described: of denying divinity for anyone other than Him, and the polytheists’ denial of Him. As for what the one we described said: that he meant by his saying, he testified, he ruled - this is something that is not known in the language of the Arabs or the non-Arabs, because testimony is one meaning, and ruling is something else. In a similar manner to what we said about this, some of the predecessors said about this.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
God bears witness

that there is no god but Him, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, contrary to what they said - meaning: contrary to what the Christian delegation of Najran said, establishing justice, meaning fairness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: with justice, with fairness.

evidence.text: Thus, the reading of the people of Islam was read with the opening of the alif of annahu, based on what I mentioned about the application of shahad in the first annahu, and the breaking of the alif of the second in and its beginning.

Except that some of the later scholars of Arabic read it all with the opening of both alifs, meaning: God bears witness that there is no god but Him, and that the religion with God is Islam - so he connected annahu with the first annahu, then he deleted the conjunction waw, which is intended in the speech.
He argued for that by saying that Ibn Abbas read it: God bears witness that there is no god but Him, the verse.
So he claimed that by his reading of them with the opening, he intended to combine the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud.

So he contradicted in his reading what he read of that, as I described, all the readings of the people of Islam, past and present, by claiming an interpretation on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud, he claimed that they said it and read it.
And sufficient evidence of the error of his reading is that it departs from the reading of the people of Islam.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading, since the matter is as we have described, is to open the alif of the first that and break the alif of the second that, I mean from his saying: Indeed, the religion with God is Islam, as a beginning.

It was narrated from Al-Saddī in his interpretation of that, a statement that indicates the correctness of what was read in that by those we mentioned, from the people of Arabic, in the opening of that from his saying: Indeed, the religion, which is what: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: God bears witness that there is no god but Him, and the angels bear witness to there is no god but Him, the Almighty, the Wise, he said: God bears witness, He, the angels, and the scholars among the al-Nas 114:that the religion with God is Islam.

It was mentioned that it is also in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: And those of knowledge who establish justice, then the alif and lam Surat Al Imran 3:18 God bears witness that there is no god except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice.

x: The meaning of religion in this context is obedience and humility, from the poet’s saying: And on the day of sorrow, when Ma'ad was gathered, and the people, except us, were in debt. He means by that: obedient in a humiliating manner.

i: From this is the saying of Al-Qatami:
x: Nour was condemning you Meaning: humiliate him, and the saying of Al-A’sha Maymun bin Qais: He is Dan Al-Rabab when they hated the religion, so he was defeated by the Battle of Wasil.

He means by his saying: He became submissive - and by his saying: They hated religion, obedience. Likewise, Islam is submission with humility and reverence. The verb aslama means: to enter into peace, just as it is said: the people became barren if they entered into famine, and arba’a if they entered into spring. Likewise, aslamu means to enter into peace, which is submission with humility and abandoning resistance. If that is the case, then the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam is that the obedience that is obedience in His sight is obedience to Him, and the tongues and hearts’ acknowledgment of servitude and humility to Him, and their submission to Him in obedience to what He has commanded and forbidden, and their humility to Him in that, without being arrogant towards Him, nor deviating from Him, without associating any other of His creation with Him in servitude and divinity.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Basharqal told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam, and Islam is the testimony that there is no god but God, and the acknowledgment of what He brought from God, and it is the religion of God that He legislated for Himself, and with which He sent His messengers, and to which His saints guided, and He does not accept anything other than it, and He does not reward anything other than it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said, Abu Al-ʿAliyah told us
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam, he said: Islam is sincerity to God alone, and worshipping Him without partner, and establishing prayer, and paying zakat, and all the other obligatory duties. This is followed.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, We have submitted (al-Hujurat 49:4), he said: We entered into peace, and left war.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zajir:
m: The religion in the sight of God is Islam, meaning: what you are upon, O Muhammad, of monotheism for the Lord and belief in the messengers.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: And those who were given the Gospel - which is the Book that God mentioned in this verse - did not differ about the matter of Jesus, and their fabrications against God in what they said about him of the statements that increased their differences among themselves, and their word was scattered, and they separated from one another until some of them made the blood of others permissible, except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves, meaning: except after they knew the truth in what they differed about regarding his matter, and they were certain that they were lying in what they said about him of great slander.

So God informed His servants that they did what they did of falsehood, and they said of the statement that is disbelief in God, knowing that what they said was wrong, and that they did not say that out of ignorance of its error, but they said it and differed about it in the way they are, transgressing against one another, and seeking leadership, kingship, and authority, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves

, he said: Abu Al-ʿAliyah said: except after the Scripture and knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity between themselves, meaning: jealousy for the world, and seeking its kingdom and authority, so some of Surat Al Imran 3:19 Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.
h
And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves
. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah - then indeed, Allah is swift in account. them killed others for the world, after they had been the scholars of the people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: that he used to recite this verse a lot: “Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.
h
And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves

.” He said: Out of jealousy for the world, and seeking its kingdom and authority. By God, we were given what was against us before. Who could be against us after he takes the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet from us? But we were given before it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: who said: When death approached Moses, he called seventy rabbis from the rabbis of the Children of Israel, and entrusted them with the Torah, and made them trustees over it, each rabbi a part of it, and Moses appointed Joshua bin Nun as his successor. Then when the first century passed, and the second passed, and the third passed, division arose among them - and they were those who were given knowledge from the sons of those seventy - until blood was shed among them, and evil and disagreement occurred. And all of that was on the part of those who were given knowledge, out of envy among them for the world, seeking its power, its kingdom, its treasuries and its adornments, so God set their tyrants over them, and God said: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam, until His saying: And God is Seeing of His servants. This statement of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas indicates that he had in mind that what was meant by his statement,
h
And those who were given the Scripture did not differ
, was the Jews from the Children of Israel, not the Christians among them, and others.

x: Others attributed this to the Christians who were given the Gospel.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
And those who were given the Scripture did not differ
except after knowledge had come to them, which came to you, meaning: that God is the One who has no partner - out of envy among themselves, meaning by that the Christians.

x: What he means by that is: Whoever denies the proofs and signs of God which He has set up as a reminder for those who understand, and evidence for those who consider and remember, then God will record for him the deeds that he did in this world, and will reward him for them in the Hereafter, for He, the Most High, is Swift in account, meaning: Swift in counting. The meaning of that is that He preserves the deeds of every worker, and He has no need to make a contract as His creation makes them with their palms, or to assist them with their hearts, but He preserves that for them, without cost or effort, or suffering as others suffer from being held accountable.
In a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of swift in reckoning, Mujahid used to say:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And whoever disbelieves in the signs of God - then indeed, God is swift in account, he said: His counting is against them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And whoever disbelieves in the signs of God - then indeed, God is swift in account, his counting.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that he used to recite this verse a lot: “Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.

x: By that, the Most High means: If, O Muhammad, a group of Christians from Najran argue with you about the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him, and dispute with you about him falsely, then say: I submit to God alone with my tongue, my heart, and all my limbs. And the Most High specifically commanded him to say: I submit my face to God, because the face is the most honorable limb of the son of Adam to Him, and in it is his splendor? His glorification. So if his face submits to something, then that which is less honorable to him from the limbs of his body has submitted to it. As for his saying:
h
And whoever follows me
, he means:
h
And whoever follows me
submits, his face to God with me.
And whoever is connected to the ta’ in I submitted, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: If they argue with you, meaning: with what they bring you of falsehood, such as their saying: We created, We did, We made, and We commanded, then it is only a false semblance and they have recognized the truth in it, “then say: I have submitted my face to God, and so have those who follow me.”

x: By that, the Most High means: And say, O Muhammad, to those who were given the Scripture, from the Jews and Christians, and the unlettered ones, from the polytheists of the Arabs who did not have a book, Have you submitted? He says: Say to them: Have you singled out monotheism and devoted worship and divinity to the Lord of the Worlds, without all the other rivals and polytheisms that you associate with Him in your worship of them and your acknowledgment of their Lordship, while you know that there is no Lord other than Him and no god other than Him? Then if they submit, he says: If they submit to singling out monotheism for God and devoting worship and divinity to Him, then they have been guided, meaning: they have found the path of truth and taken the right path.
How was it said: If they submit, they are guided after a question? Is it permissible in this manner to say to a man: Will you stand? If you stand, I will honor you?

That is permissible, if the speech is intended as a command, even if it is used as a question, as God the Most High said: “And he averts you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. Will you not desist?” (al-Ma’idah 5:91), meaning: desist. And as God the Most High said, informing us about the disciples that they said to Jesus: O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven? (al-Ma’idah 5:112), but it is only a question, as a man says: Will you be sufficient for us? meaning: desist from us, and as a man says to another man: Where, where? meaning: Stay and do not move.
Therefore, it is permissible in the interrogative as it is permissible in the imperative in the reading of Abdullah:
h
Shall I guide you

to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment? * Then you will believe. (al-Saff 61:10-11) We interpret it as a command, while in our reading it is a declarative. So the recompense in our reading is based on his saying:
h
Shall I guide you
, and in Abdullah’s reading it is based on his saying: Believe, because it is the interpretation.
And in a similar sense to what we said about that, some of the people of interpretation said:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And say to those who were given the Scripture and the unlettered ones, those who do not have a book, Have you submitted? And if they submit, then they are rightly guided, the verse.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hasan narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, he said: The unlettered ones are those who do not write.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His statement:
h
And if they turn away

, is if they turn their backs, averse to what you are calling them to of Islam and sincere monotheism for God, Lord of the Worlds, then you are only a messenger conveying the message, and you are not required to do anything except convey the message to whomever I have sent you to from among My creation, and to perform what I have charged you with of obedience, and God is Seeing of the servants, meaning by that: God is All-Knowing of those among His servants who accept what I have sent you to bring to them and obey you in Islam, and those among them who turn away from it, averse, and reject what I have sent you to bring to Surat Al Imran 3:20 So if they argue with you, say, "I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have those who follow me." And say to those who were given the Scripture and the unlearned, "Have you submitted?"
And if they submit, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the notification. And Allah is Seeing of His servants. them and disobey you by refusing to accept Islam.

evidence.text: Therefore, it is permissible in the interrogative as it is permissible in the imperative in the reading of Abdullah: Shall I guide you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment? * Then you will believe.
(al-Saff 61:10-11) We interpret it as a command, while in our reading it is a declarative.
So the recompense in our reading is based on his saying: Shall I guide you, and in Abdullah’s reading it is based on his saying: Believe, because it is the interpretation.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Those who disbelieve in the signs of God, that is, they deny God’s proofs and signs and lie about them, from among the people of the two books, the Torah and the Gospel, such as:

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, he said:
m: Then he gathered together all the people of the two books, and mentioned what they had innovated and invented, from the Jews and the Christians, and he said: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly until His saying: Say, ‘O God, Owner of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will.’ As for His saying: and kill the prophets unjustly, he means by that - that they were killing the messengers of God who were sent to them to forbid what they were doing of disobeying God, and to commit what they were committing of the matters that God had previously warned them against in their books, such as Zachariah and his son John, and the prophets of God who were similar to them.

x: There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Medina, Hijaz, Basra, Kufa, and all the other reciters of the cities read it as: And they kill those who enjoin justice, meaning killing.

Some of the later reciters of Kufa read it: And they fight, meaning fighting, interpreting it as the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud. He claimed that it was in Abdullah’s copy of the Qur’an: And they fought. So the one whose matter we described from the recitation read with that interpretation: And they fight.

The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read it: and they kill, because the evidence from the readings unanimously agrees with it, along with the interpretation coming from the people of interpretation that this is its interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Muqal bin Abi Maskeen,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And they kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people

, he said: The revelation would come to the Children of Israel and they would mention their righteous ones - and no book would come to them - and they would be killed, and men from among those who followed them and believed them would rise up and mention their people and they would be killed, and they are: those who enjoin justice among the people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people
, he said: These are the People of the Book, the followers of the prophets used to forbid them and remind them, so they would kill them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said
m: regarding His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people, he said: There were people from the Children of Israel who did not read the Book, and the revelation would come to them and they would remind their people and they would be killed for that, so they are: those who enjoin justice among the people.

c: Abu Ubaid al-Wasabi Muhammad ibn Hafs told me, he said, Ibn Himyar told us, he said,
m: Abu al-Hasan, a client of Banu Asad, told us, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb al-Khuza’i, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, which people will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection? He said: A man who killed a prophet, or a man who enjoined evil and forbade good. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people, until he reached and they have no helpers. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Ubaidah, the Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets at the beginning of the day in one hour, so one hundred and twelve men from the army of the Children of Israel stood up and enjoined good upon those they killed and forbade evil, so they were all killed at the end of the day on that day, and they are the ones whom God, the Almighty, mentioned.

x: The interpretation of the verse is: Those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets unjustly, and kill those who command them to be just in the commands and prohibitions of God, those who forbid them from killing the prophets of God and committing sins against Him.

What He means by His statement, may His praise be exalted: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment, is to inform them, O Muhammad, and to make them aware that they will have a painful punishment from God, which is the painful.

evidence.text: The majority of the people of Medina, Hijaz, Basra, Kufa, and all the other reciters of the cities read it as: And they kill those who enjoin justice, meaning killing.
Some of the later reciters of Kufa read it: And they fight, meaning fighting, interpreting it as the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud.
So the one whose matter we described from the recitation read with that interpretation: And they fight.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read it: and they kill, because the evidence from the readings unanimously agrees with it, along with the interpretation coming from the people of interpretation that this is its interpretation.

x: As for His statement:
h
Those are the ones whose deeds have been in vain in this world and the Hereafter

, what He means by His statement: Those is those who disbelieve in the signs of God. The meaning of that is: those whom We mentioned are those whose deeds have been in vain, meaning: their deeds have become void, in this world and the Hereafter. As for in this world, they did not attain praise or commendation from the people because they were on misguidance and falsehood, and God did not raise their mention because of them, rather He cursed them and exposed their veils, and revealed what they had hidden of their ugly deeds on the tongues of His prophets and messengers in His books that He sent down to them, so He left for them as long as this world remained blameworthy, and that is its in vainness in this world. As for in the Hereafter, He has prepared for them in it the punishment described in His Book, and He informed His servants that their deeds will become waste with no reward because they were disbelievers in God, so the reward of their people is eternity in Hell. As for his saying:
h
And they have no helpers
, he means: And these people have no helper to support them from God, if He takes revenge on them for their previous crimes and their audacity towards him, and rescues them from Him.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, those who have been given a portion of the Scripture, meaning: those who have been given a portion of the Scripture, calling to the Book of God.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the Book that God meant when He said: They call to the Book of God.

Some of them said: It is the Torah. He called them to be satisfied with what is in it, since the groups that claimed the books acknowledged it and what is in it: that they were the rulings of God before what was abrogated from them was abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Yunus narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said:
m: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid ibn Thabit narrated to me, he said: Saeed ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the school house upon a group of Jews, and called them to God. Then Nu’aym ibn Amr and Al-Harith ibn Zayd said to him: What religion are you on, O Muhammad? He said: On the religion and faith of Abraham. They said: Abraham was a Jew! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Come to the Torah, for it is between us and you! But they refused him, so God Almighty revealed: ‘
h
Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture

? They are invited to the Book of God to judge between them, then a party of them turns away, while they turn away. ’ up to His saying: ‘They were inventing nothing. ’” Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of the family of Zayd, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the school house, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Come to the Torah, and he also said: Then God revealed about them:
h
Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture
? The rest of the hadith is like the hadith of Abu Kurayb.

x: Some of them said: Rather, this is the Book of God that He revealed to Muhammad, and a group of them were only invited to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that he might judge between them with justice, but they refused.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture

? They are invited to the Book of God to judge between them, then a party of them turns away, and they are averse. Those are the enemies of God, the Jews. They were invited to the Book of God to judge between them, and to His Prophet to judge between them, and they find it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, then they turned away from it, and they are averse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? The verse. He said: They are the Jews. They were called to the Book of God and to His Prophet, and they find it written with them, then they turn away and are averse!

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture

? They are invited to the Book of God to judge between them. He said: The People of the Scripture were invited to a Book to judge between them with truth, and in the limits. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would invite them to Islam, but they would turn away from that.

x: The most correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is that God, the Most High, informed us about a group of Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his time, who had been given knowledge of the Torah, that they were called to the Book of God, which they acknowledged was from God - which is the Torah - in some of the matters over which they and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disputed. It is possible that their dispute over which they disputed, and then they were called to the ruling of the Torah in it, but they refused to respond to it, was the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the matter of his prophethood. It is possible that this was the matter of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and his religion. It is possible that this was what they were called to regarding the matter of Islam and the recognition of it.

It is possible that this was in a specific case, for all of this was something over which they had disputed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he called them to the ruling of the Torah, but they refused to respond to it and some of them concealed it. There is no indication in the verse as to which of these was which, so it is permissible to say: it is this and not that. And we do not need to know that, because the meaning that they were called to rule on is that which was obligatory upon them to respond to in their religion, but they refused it, so God, the Most High, informed us about their apostasy, their denial of what was in their book, and their rejection of what He had taken from them in their covenants and agreements to establish and act upon. So they will not be in their denial of Muhammad and what he brought of the truth, like them in their denial of Moses and what he brought, while they supported him and acknowledged him.
The meaning of his statement:
h
Then a group of them will turn away and they will be averse

, is that they will turn away from the Book of God, which calls for its ruling, turning away from it and turning away, while they are knowledgeable about its truth and its proof. We only said that this book is the Torah, because they were denying the Qur’an, and believing in the Torah, according to their claim. So the proof against them, by denying what they claimed to be true, was more eloquent, and the excuse was more conclusive.
God, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Because they said

, that those who were called to the Book of God to judge between them with truth in what they disputed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only refused to respond to the ruling of the Torah and what is in it of truth, because of their saying: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days, which are forty days, and these are the days in which they worshipped the calf, then our Lord will bring us out of it, being deceived by them, because of what they were inventing, meaning: by what they were inventing of lies and falsehoods, in their claim that they were the sons of God and His beloved, and that God had promised their father Jacob that none of his children would enter the Fire except by swearing an oath. So God belied them for all of their sayings, and informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they are the people of the Fire and will abide therein eternally, apart from the believers in God and His Messengers and what they brought from Him.
And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
That is because they said

, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.’ They said: The Fire will not touch us except for the fulfillment of the oath in which we set up the calf, then the oath and the punishment will be cut off from us. God Almighty said: And what they used to invent deceived them in their religion. That is, they said: We are the children of God and beloved.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding His statement:
h
That is because they said

, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days,’ the verse, he said: They said: We will not be tormented in the Fire except for forty days, he said: He means the Jews - he said: Qatada said something similar - and he said: They are the days in which they set up the calf. God Almighty says: And what they used to invent deceived them in their religion, when they said: We are the children of God and His beloved.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said, his statement:
h
And they were deceived in their religion by what they used to invent
, he said: They were deceived by their statement: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: How then, when We gather them together? What will be the state of these people who said this statement and did what they did of turning away from the Book of God, being deceived by their Lord, and fabricating lies? This is from God, the Most High, a severe warning and a harsh threat to them. What he means by his saying: How then, when We gather them together verse: How great is the punishment and torment that they will encounter from God when He gathers them together on a day when every worker will be given the reward of his work according to what he deserves, and no one will be wronged on it, because he will only be punished for what he has committed, and he will only be held accountable for what he has done. He will reward the good-doer for his goodness, and the evil-doer for his evil. No one among His creation will fear injustice or oppression from Him on that day.
How was it said: How will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and not said: on a Day about which there is no doubt?

Because the meaning of the lam in this place is different from the meaning of fi. That is because if the place of the lam was fi, the meaning of the statement would be: So how is it when We gather them on the Day of Resurrection, what will be their torment and punishment? And that is not the meaning of the lam’s inclusion, but its meaning with the lam is: So how is it when We gather them for what will happen on a day about which there is no doubt, and what will happen on that day when God will separate the judgment between His creation, what will be their torment and painful punishment then? So with the lam in for a day about which there is no doubt there is an intention of an action, and a desired predicate that was left out, the indication of the lam’s inclusion in the day is sufficient for it, from it. And that is not the case with fi, so the lam was chosen and included in the day, not in fi.
As for the interpretation of his saying:
h
There is no doubt about it

, it is: There is no doubt about its coming. We have demonstrated that this is the case with sufficient evidence, while mentioning who said that in its interpretation in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. He meant by his saying: And I will pay back, and God will pay back, every soul will be compensated for what it has earned, meaning: what it has done of good and evil, and they will not be wronged, meaning that the doer of good will not be reduced in reward for his good deeds, nor will the wrongdoer be punished for no crime other than his own.

As for the interpretation of: Say, O God, it is: Say, O Muhammad: O God. The Arab scholars differed on the accusative case of the mim in Allahumma, which is a vocative, and the rule for a singular vocative that is not an adjective is the nominative case, and on the inclusion of the mim in it, which is originally God without the mim.

Some of them said: The two meems were added to it because it is not used to call out with Ya as it is to call out nouns that do not have Alif or Lam. This is because nouns that do not have Alif or Lam are called out with Ya, as in the case of someone saying: Ya Zaid and Ya Amr. He said: So the meem was made a replacement for Ya, as they said: Fam, Ibnum, Hum, Zarqam, Sithaam, and similar nouns and attributes from which the letter is deleted and then replaced with a meem. He said: Likewise, Ya was deleted from Allahumma which is used to call out nouns that are as we have described, and the meem was made a replacement for it at the end of the noun.

Others denied this statement of theirs, and said: We have heard the Arabs calling Allahumma with ya as you call Him, and there is no mim in it. They said: If the one who said this statement was correct in his claim, the Arabs would not have included ya, and they came up with the opposite of it. And they recited about that, as heard from the Arabs: What do you have to say every time you pray or say Oh God? Our Sheikh, respond to us as a Muslim It is narrated:سبحهorکبر. They said: We have not seen the Arabs add such a meem except in the lightened form in the defective nouns such as: al-famm, ibnam, and hum. They said: We see that it is a word to which am was added, meaning: O God, grant us goodness, so it was common in speech and mixed with it. They said: The damma in the ha’ from the hamza of am, when it was left, it moved to what preceded it. They said: We see that the Arabs’ saying:هلمة يليناis like it.

It wasهلمة, did am was added to it, so it was left in the accusative case. They said: Some Arabs say when they drop the meem: O God forgive me and O God forgive me with the hamza of the alif from God once, and connected it another time. So whoever deletes it makes it follow its original form, because it is an alif and lam, like the alif and lam that enter into definite nouns as extra. And whoever hamzas it thinks that it is from the letter, since it does not fall from it, and they recited in the hamza of the alif from it: Blessed is he and whoever named him after you, O God They said: O God, it has become so common in speech that its ‘mim’ has been lightened in some languages.

i: And they recited:
x: As an oath from Abu Riyah, may God hear it, the great ones And the narrators chant that: The adults listen to it Some of them recited it: God hears it and God is great Abu Jaʿfar said: He means by that: O Possessor of the Kingdom, O He who has the kingdom of this world and the Hereafter exclusively and without anyone else, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr,
m: his saying: Say, O God, Owner of the Kingdom, meaning, Lord of the servants, the King, none judges them but You. As for his saying:
h
You give the kingdom to whomever You will
, it means:
h
You give the kingdom to whomever You will
, so you own it and give it power over whomever You will. And His statement:
h
And You take away the kingdom from whomever You will
, means:
h
And You take away the kingdom from whomever You will
. So He left out mentioning that You take it away from him, being satisfied with the indication of His statement:
h
And You take away the kingdom from whomever You will

, upon it, just as it is said: Take what you will, and be in whatever you will, meaning: Take what you will to take, and be in whatever you will to be, and just as the Most High said: In whatever form He willed He assembled you (al-Infitar 82:8), meaning: In whatever form He willed to assemble you, He assembled you. It was said that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him Surat Al Imran 3:26 Say, "O God, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and You take the kingdom away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You abase whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent." peace, in response to his question to his Lord to give the kingdom of Persia and Rome to his nation.

x: Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he mentioned to us: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked his Lord, may His praise be glorified, to make for him the kingdom of Persia and Rome in his nation, so God Almighty revealed: ‘Say: O God, Possessor of the kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will’ to ‘Indeed, You are over all things competent.’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, to make the kingdom of Persia and Rome in his nation, then he mentioned something similar.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid
m: that he used to say: The meaning of kingship in this context is: prophethood. He mentioned the narration about it:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: You give the kingdom to whom You will and take the kingdom away from whom You will, he said: Prophethood.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: He, may His praise be glorified, means: And You honor whom You will, by giving him kingship and authority, and extending power to him, and You humiliate whom You will, by taking away his kingdom and giving his enemy power over him. In Your hand is good, meaning: All of that is in Your hand and to You.

No one has the power to do that, because You are capable of everything, unlike the rest of Your creation, and unlike those whom the polytheists among the People of the Book and the illiterate Arabs took as a god and lord whom they worship besides You, such as the Messiah and the rivals whom the illiterate took as lords, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You give sovereignty to whomever You will
, the verse, meaning: that is in Your hand, not to anyone else. Indeed, You are over all things competent, meaning: no one else has the power to do this except You, by Your authority and power.

evidence.text: And they recited: As an oath from Abu Riyah, may God hear it, the great ones And the narrators chant that: The adults listen to it Some of them recited it: God hears it and God is great Abu Jaʿfar said: He means by that: O Possessor of the Kingdom, O He who has the kingdom of this world and the Hereafter exclusively and without anyone else, as:

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: tawalaj means to enter. It is said from it: So-and-so entered his house, if he entered it, so he enters it, wajjan, wajjan, wajjan, and I entered it, if I brought it in. What he means by his saying:
h
And you enter the night into the day is that you include the hours of the night that you have decreased in the hours of the day

, so you increase the decrease of this by the increase of that, and and you enter the day into the night, and you include the hours of the day that you have decreased in the hours of the night, so you increase in the hours of the night what you have decreased in the hours of the day, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: The night enters the day and the day enters the night, until the night is fifteen hours and the day is nine hours, and the day enters the night until the day is fifteen hours and the night is nine hours.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: What is missing from the day, He makes it into the night, and what is missing from the night, He makes it into the day.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night
, he said: What is missing from one of them in the other, they follow one another - or: they alternate, Abu Asim was not sure - that is from the hours.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The night enters the day and the day enters the night, what is missing from one of them in the other, they alternate in that of the hours.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: his saying:
h
He makes the night enter the day and makes the day enter the night
, the decrease of the night is due to the increase of the day, and the decrease of the day is due to the increase of the night.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night
, he said: It is a deficiency of one in the other.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night

. He said: The night takes from the day, and the day takes from the night. He says: The decrease of the night is in the increase of the day, and the decrease of the day is in the increase of the night.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night
, meaning that one of them takes it from the other, so that the night is sometimes longer than the day, and the day is sometimes longer than the night.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night
, he said: This is long and this is short. He took from this and inserted it into this, until this became long and this became short.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The interpretation of that is that He brings forth the living thing from the dead sperm, and He brings forth the dead sperm from the living thing.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: It is the sperm that comes out of the man while it is dead and he is alive, and the man comes out of it alive while it is dead.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: Living people are from sperm, and sperm is dead, and He brings forth the living from people, and the livestock.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Surat Al Imran 3:27 You merge the night into the day and merge the day into the night, and You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And the living comes out of the dead and the dead comes out of the living. So the sperm is dead, it comes out of a living person, and a living person comes out of a dead sperm.

c: Muhammad bin Omar bin Ali bin Ata’ al-Muqaddami told me, he said, Ash’ath al-Sijistani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: The sperm comes forth from the man, and the man from the sperm.
