c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: He brings forth the living from this dead sperm, and He brings forth this dead sperm from the living.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living

, the verse, he said: Living people are from sperm, and sperm is dead from living people, and likewise from livestock and plants. Ibn Jurayj said: And I heard Yazid ibn Uwaimir narrating, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: His bringing forth sperm from man, and His bringing forth man from sperm.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And you bring forth the living from the dead and you bring forth the dead from the living

, he said: The sperm is dead, so living things come out of it. And you bring forth the dead from the living, the sperm comes out from these living things, and the seed is dead, from it comes a living thing. And you bring forth the dead from the living, from this living thing comes a dead seed.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that He brings forth the palm tree from the seed, the seed from the palm tree, the ear of corn from the grain, the grain from the ear of corn, the eggs from the chicken, and the chicken from the eggs.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Abu Tamila told us, Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And brings forth the living from the dead
, he said: It is the egg that comes forth from the living while it is dead, then the living comes forth from it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: The palm tree from the seed and the seed from the palm tree, and the grain from the ear of corn and the ear of corn from the grain.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that he separates the believer from the unbeliever, and the unbeliever from the believer.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, meaning the believer from the disbeliever and the disbeliever from the believer, and the believer is a servant with a living heart, and the disbeliever is a servant with a dead heart.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Al-Hasan said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: He brings forth the believer from the disbeliever, and brings forth the disbeliever from the believer.

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said, Abdul Warith told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Amr, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: he recited:
h
And you bring forth the living from the dead and you bring forth the dead from the living
, he said: You bring forth the believer from the disbeliever, and you bring forth the disbeliever from the believer.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told me, he said, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman,
m: or on the authority of Ibn Masʿud - and I think it is most likely that it was on the authority of Salman - he said: God Almighty kneaded the clay of Adam for forty nights - or he said: forty days - then he moved his hand into it, and all that was good came out in his right hand, and all that was bad came out in his other hand, then he mixed them, then he created Adam from it, and from that he brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, brings forth the believer from the disbeliever, and brings forth the disbeliever from the believer.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon one of his wives, and there was a woman of beautiful grace. He said: Who is this? She said, One of your aunts! He said: My aunts in this town are strange! And which of my aunts are these? She said, Khalida, daughter of al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth. He said: Glory be to Him who brings the living out of the dead! She was a righteous woman, and her father was an unbeliever.”

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, he said: Did you know that the disbeliever gives birth to a believer, and that the believer gives birth to a disbeliever? He said: It is like that.

x: The most correct of the interpretations that we mentioned regarding this verse is the interpretation of the one who said: He brings forth the living human being and the living livestock and beasts from the dead sperm - and that is bringing forth the living from the dead - and He brings forth the dead sperm from the living human being and the living livestock and beasts, and that is bringing forth the dead from the living. This is because every living thing that has part of its body leave it, that part that has left it is dead. So the sperm is dead because it has left the body of the one from whom it came, then God creates from it a living human being and living animals and cattle. And this is the ruling on every living thing that has part of it leave it, so that that part that has left it is dead. This is similar to His statement:
h
How can you disbelieve in God while you were dead and He gave you life

Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life, then to Him you will be returned. (al-Baqarah 2:28) As for the interpretation of those who interpreted it as meaning the grain from the ear of corn, the ear of corn from the grain, the egg from the hen, the hen from the egg, the believer from the disbeliever, and the disbeliever from the believer, then even if that has an understandable aspect, it is not the most prevalent and apparent in people’s usage in speech. Directing the meanings of the Book of God Almighty to the apparent used by people is more appropriate than directing them to the hidden and little used. There are different readings of this.
A group of them read it as:
h
And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living
, with emphasis and the emphasis on the ya of dead, meaning that He brings forth the living thing from the thing that has died and from that which has not died.

Another group of them read: He brings forth the living from the dead and He brings forth the dead from the living with a light ya from dead, meaning that the living thing comes forth from the thing that has died, not the thing that has not died, and the dead thing comes forth, not the thing that has not died, from the living thing. This is because the word dead is heavily pronounced with the letter ya in Arabic: that which has not died and will die, and that which has already died. As for the word mayyit with a lightened mayyit, it is the one who has died. So if they want to describe it, they say: You will die tomorrow, and They will die. And likewise, everything that has not yet existed, the noun is derived from it in this example. It is said: He is generous with himself, and He is good with that. And if the meaning of the noun is wanted, it is said: He is generous with himself, and He is good with himself.

If that is the case, then the more correct of the two readings in this verse is the reading of the one who stressed the ya’ of al-mayyit. Because God, the Most High, brings forth the living from the sperm that has left the man and become dead, and He will bring it forth from it after it leaves him while it is in the man’s loins. And brings forth the dead from the living, the sperm that becomes dead when it leaves the living man, and before it leaves him it was alive. So stressing it is more expressive of praise and more complete of commendation.
By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that He gives to whomever He wills of His creation and is generous to him, without holding accountable the one to whom He gives.
Because He does not fear that His treasures will be diminished, nor that what is in His hand will perish, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And You provide for whomever You will without account
, he said: He brings forth provision from Him without account, and He does not fear that what He has will decrease, may He be blessed and exalted.

x: The interpretation of the verse is: O God, O Possessor of the Kingdom, You give the Kingdom to whomever You will, and You take the Kingdom away from whomever You will, and You honor whomever You will, and You humiliate whomever You will. In Your hand is goodness, for You are over all things competent. Except for the one whom the atheists claim to be their God and Lord and worship Him instead of You, or take Him as a partner with You, or that He is Your son. In Your hand is the power that does these things and with which You are able to do all things. You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night, so You decrease from this and increase from that, and You decrease from this and increase from that, and You bring forth a dead person alive and a living person dead,
h
and You provide for whomever You will without account
from Your creation.
No one is able to do that except You, and no one is able to do it except You, as:

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: You merge the night into the day and merge the day into the night, and You bring forth the living from the dead and bring forth the dead from the living. That is, with that power, meaning: with the power by which You give kingship to whomever You will? You take it away from whomever You will,
h
and You provide for whomever You will without account

. No one can do that except You, and no one does it except You. That is, if You gave Jesus authority over the things by which they claim that he is a god: such as reviving the dead, healing illnesses, creating birds from clay, and reporting the unseen, so that We might make him a sign for the people, and a confirmation of his prophethood with which You sent him to his people - then from My authority and power is that which I have not given him: the possession of kings, and the command of prophethood and placing it where You will, and the merger of the night into the day and the day into the night, and the bringing forth of the living from the dead and the dead from the living, and the provision of whomever You will, whether Surat Al Imran 3:27 You merge the night into the day and merge the day into the night, and You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living, and You provide for whom You will without account. righteous or wicked, without account. All of that was not given to me by Jesus, nor did I give him possession of it, so there was no lesson or evidence for them in that: if he was a god, all of that would have been up to him, and in their knowledge he was fleeing from kings, and moving from one country to another from them in the countries!!

evidence.text: A group of them read it as: And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, with emphasis and the emphasis on the ya of dead, meaning that He brings forth the living thing from the thing that has died and from that which has not died.
Abu Jaʿfar said: If that is the case, then the more correct of the two readings in this verse is the reading of the one who stressed the ya’ of al-mayyit.

x: This is a prohibition from God Almighty to the believers that they should take the infidels as helpers, supporters, and supporters. That is why yatakhadhu was broken because it is in the place of the jussive of the prohibition, and because the dhal in it was broken because of the quiescent letter that it encountered while it was quiescent. The meaning of this is: O believers, do not take the infidels as your backers and supporters, befriending them in their religion, and supporting them against the Muslims instead of the believers, and pointing out to them their faults, for whoever does that, has nothing to do with God, meaning by that: he has disavowed God and God has disavowed him, by his apostasy from his religion and his entry into disbelief, unless you guard against them with a precaution, unless you are in their authority and fear them for yourselves, so you show them allegiance with your tongues, and harbor enmity for them, and do not support them in what they are upon of disbelief, and do not help them against a Muslim by action, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers

, he said: God Almighty forbade the believers from being kind to the disbelievers or taking them as allies rather than the believers, unless the disbelievers are dominant over them, so they show them kindness and differ from them in religion. This is His statement:
h
Unless you fear them out of fear

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-Hajjaj ibn Amr, an ally of Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf, Ibn Abi al-Haqiq, and Qays ibn Zayd, had entrapped a group of the Ansar in order to tempt them away from their religion. Rafa’ah ibn al-Mundhir ibn Zunbar, Abdullah ibn Jubayr, and Sa’d ibn Khaithama said to those al-Nas 114:Avoid these Jews, and beware of sticking to them and keeping company with them lest they tempt you away from your religion! But those people refused to do anything but keep company with them and keep company with them, so God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers
until His saying: And God has power over all things.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers
, he said: The believer should not take the disbeliever as an ally rather than the believers.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies to
h
except that you fear them out of fear

. As for allies, he is loyal to them in their religion, and he shows them the weakness of the believers. So whoever does this is a polytheist, and God has disavowed him, unless he fears out of fear. So he shows loyalty to them in their religion, and disavowal of the believers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Unless you fear them with a fear
, he said: Fear is speaking with the tongue, while his heart is reassured by faith.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Unless you fear them with a fear
, he said: As long as the blood of a Muslim is not shed, and his money is not made permissible.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers
, except out of worldly appeasement and opposition.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Surat Al Imran 3:28
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies
instead of the believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah,
h
except that you fear them with fear
. And Allah warns you of Himself, and to Allah is the final destination.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers
, to
h
except that you fear them with fear
, he said: Abu Al-ʿAliyah said: Fear is with the tongue and not with action.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Unless you fear them with a fear

, he said: Taqiyyah is with the tongue. Whoever is compelled to speak about something that is a sin against God, and he speaks it out of fear for himself, while his heart is at peace with faith, then there is no sin upon him. Taqiyyah is only with the tongue.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Unless you fear them with a fear

, then fear is with the tongue. Whoever is led to speak of something that is a sin against God, and he speaks it out of fear of people while his heart is at peace with faith, then that will not harm him. Fear is with the tongue.

x: Others said: The meaning of
h
unless you fear them with fear
is unless there is a kinship between you and him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers unless you fear them out of fear
. God forbade the believers from befriending the disbelievers or taking them as allies rather than the believers. God said:
h
Unless you fear them out of fear
. The womb from the polytheists, without taking them as allies in their religion, unless he maintains the ties of kinship among the polytheists.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies
, he said: It is not permissible for a believer to take a disbeliever as an ally in his religion. And his statement:
h
Except that you fear them out of fear
, he said: That there is a kinship between you and him, so you maintain ties with him for that reason.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
Unless you fear them with fear
, he said: Treat them well in this world, by being kind to them and other things. But no in religion.

x: What Qatada said is an interpretation that has a point, but it is not the point that is indicated by the apparent meaning of the verse: Except that you fear the disbelievers with a fear. The most common meaning of this statement is: Except that you fear them with a fear. So the fear that God mentioned in this verse is fear of the disbelievers and not of anyone else. Qatada explained that its interpretation is: Except that you fear God because of the kinship that is between you and them with a fear, so that you maintain ties of kinship. This is not the most common meaning of the statement. The interpretation in the Qur’an is based on the most common meaning that appears from the well-known speech of the Arabs used regarding them. There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement:
h
Except that you fear them with fear
. This was read by the majority of the people of the countries:
h
Unless you fear them with fear
, based on the estimation of a verb such as: gluttony, slowness, and repose, from I feared.
Others read it as: Except that you fear them with a fear, on the model of fa’ila.
The reading that is the reading according to us is the reading of those who read it:
h
Except that you fear them with fear
, because the proof of that is established that it is the correct reading, through the widespread transmission from which error is prevented.

By that, the Most High means: And God frightens you from Himself, lest you commit His sins or befriend His enemies. Indeed, to God belongs your return and your destiny after your death, and on the Day of Judgment when you will be brought to account. By that, He means: When you come to Him and have disobeyed what He has commanded you to do, and have done what He has forbidden you to do, such as taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, you will be afflicted with a punishment from your Lord that you cannot bear. He says: So fear Him and beware lest that befall you from Him, for He is severe in punishment.

evidence.text: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: Except that you fear them with fear.
This was read by the majority of the people of the countries: Unless you fear them with fear, based on the estimation of a verb such as: gluttony, slowness, and repose, from I feared.
Others read it as: Except that you fear them with a fear, on the model of fa’ila.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that is the reading according to us is the reading of those who read it: Except that you fear them with fear, because the proof of that is established that it is the correct reading, through the widespread transmission from which error is prevented.

x: By that, the Most High means: Say, O Muhammad, to those whom you have commanded not to take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, If you conceal what is in your hearts of friendship with the disbelievers and keep it secret, or if you reveal that from your souls with your tongues and actions and make it apparent, God knows it, so nothing is hidden from Him.

He says: So do not harbor affection for them and do not show friendship with them, lest you be afflicted with a punishment from your Lord that you cannot bear, because He knows your secret and your public, so nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He is recording it from you until He rewards you for it with good for good, and with evil like it, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: He informed us that He knows what they kept secret of that and what they declared, so He said: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it. As for His statement:
h
And He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth

, it means that since nothing is hidden from Him, whether it is in the heavens or the earth or wherever it is, then how can what is in your hearts of inclination towards them with affection and love, or what you show them with assistance in action and word, be hidden from Him - O people who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers? As for his saying: And God is over all things competent, it means: And God is capable of hastening your punishment for your loyalty to them and your support of them against the believers, and of whatever He wills of all matters. Nothing He wants is difficult for Him, and nothing He seeks is forbidden to Him.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means:
h
And God warns you of Himself

on a day when every soul will find what it has done of good present and abundant, Whatever evil it has done, it will wish that between it and that was a great distance, meaning a distant end, for your destiny, O people, on that day is to Him, so beware of Him for yourselves from your sins.
Qatada used to say about the meaning of his saying: Presented, what:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
On the Day every soul will find present what it has done of good
, he said: abundant.

x: Some of the Arabists have claimed that the meaning of this is: And remember the day when you will find. He said: That is why it came in this way, because the Qur’an was revealed for the purpose of commanding and reminding, as if it was said to them: Remember such and such, because in the Qur’an in more than one place it says: And fear such and such a day, and such and such a time. As for ma that comes with amalt, it means who, and it is not permissible for it to be a recompense, because tajd occurs before it. As for his saying: and what evil you did, it is conjoined with his saying: ma the first, and amalt is a relative clause meaning the nominative, because it was said: wish. The interpretation of the words:
h
On the Day every soul will find present what it has done of good

, and what it has done of evil it will wish that there were a period of time between it and that. The term is the goal that it ends at, and from it is the saying of Al-Tarmah: Every living creature has completed its lifespan, and dies when its term has expired.
It means: the end of his life, and:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
And whatever evil you have done
, you wish that between it and that was a great distance, a distant place.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: A long time, he said: a deadline.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whatever evil you have done

, you would wish that between it and that was a great distance, he said: One of them would be pleased that he would never encounter that action of his, because that was his desire. As for in this world, it was a sin that he enjoyed.

x: God Almighty says:
h
And God warns you of Himself

: lest you make Him angry with you by doing what He is angry with you, and then you meet Him on a Day when every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, wishing that there were a great distance between it and it, while He is angry with you, and you will be afflicted with His painful punishment that you cannot bear.

c: Then the Almighty informed us that
m: He is compassionate and merciful to His servants, and that part of His compassion for them is His warning them of Himself, frightening them with His punishment, and forbidding them from the sins He forbade them from, such as: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement:
h
And God warns you of Himself
, and God is Kind to His servants, he said: From His kindness to them is that He warned them of Himself.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the reason for which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed about a people who said during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We love our Lord. So God Almighty commanded His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: If you are truthful in what you say, then follow me, for that is a sign of your truthfulness in what you said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Bakr ibn al-Aswad, he said,
m: I heard al-Hasan say: Some people said during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, we love our Lord! So God Almighty revealed: Say, ‘If you should love God, then follow me, and God will love you and forgive you your sins.’ So He made following His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a sign of His love and a punishment for those who oppose Him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ali bin Al-Haitham told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, he said,
m: I heard Al-Hasan say: Some people said during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, we love our Lord! So God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed the Qur’an about that: Say, ‘
h
If you love God

, then follow me, and God will love you and forgive you your sins.’ So God made following His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a sign of His love and a punishment for those who oppose Him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you love God

, then follow me, and God will love you. He said: There were people who claimed that they loved God, saying: We love our Lord! So God commanded them to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and made following Muhammad a sign of loving Him.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you love God the verse

, he said: There were people during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who claimed that they loved God, so God wanted to make their words a confirmation of their actions, so He said:
h
If you love God the verse
, so following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a confirmation of their words.

x: Others said: Rather, this is a command from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the Najran delegation who came to him from the Christians: If what you are saying about Jesus is a great statement, you are only saying it out of glorification of God and love for Him, so follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: Say, ‘
h
If you love God

,’ meaning: if this is what you say - meaning: about Jesus - out of love for God and glorification of Him, then follow me, and God will love you and forgive you your sins, meaning: what has passed of your disbelief, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is that of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr. Because no mention was made of people who claimed that they loved God or that they glorified Him, except for the delegation of Najran, in this surah or before this verse. So his statement,
h
If you love God

, then follow me, is an answer to their statement, according to what al-Hasan said. As for what Al-Hasan narrated about that which we have mentioned, we do not have any authentic report about it, so it is permissible to say that it is so, even if there is no indication in the surah that it is as he said. Unless Al-Hasan meant by the people who he mentioned that they said that during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the delegation of Najran from the Christians, then that would be from his statement similar to our choice about it. Since this is not a report as we have said, nor is there in the verse evidence for what we have described, then it is more appropriate for us to attach its interpretation to what is indicated by the verses of the surah, and that is what we have described.

Because what precedes this verse from the beginning of this surah and what follows it is a report about them, and an argument from God to His Prophet Muhammad, Surat Al Imran 3:31 Say, "If you love Allah, then follow me, Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." may God bless him and grant him peace, and evidence of the length of their statement about the Messiah. So it is necessary that it also be diverted in meaning to something similar to what precedes it and the meaning of what follows it.

Since the matter is as we have described, the interpretation of the verse is: Say, O Muhammad, to the delegation of Christians of Najran: If you are as you claim, that you love God, and that you venerate the Messiah and say about him what you say, out of love for your Lord, then fulfill what you say, if you are truthful, by following me, for you know that I am a messenger to you from God, just as Jesus was a messenger to the one to whom He was sent. If you follow me and believe in what I have brought you from God, He will forgive you your sins, pardon you for the punishment for them, and pardon you for what has passed of them, for He is Forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, Merciful to them and to others of His creation.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Say, O Muhammad, to these delegations of Christians from Najran: Obey God and the Messenger Muhammad, for you have known with certainty that he is My Messenger to My creation. I sent him with the truth. You will find it written with you in the Gospel. If they turn away, then turn away from what you have called them to of that, and turn away from it.

So inform them that God does not love those who disbelieve and deny what they know of the truth, and reject it after knowing it, and that they are from them, by their denial of your prophethood, and their denial of the truth that you are upon, after their knowledge of the correctness of your matter, and the reality of your prophethood, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: Say, ‘Obey God and the Messenger,’ for you know him - meaning the delegation of Christians from Najran - and you find him in your book, but if they turn away in their disbelief, then God does not like the disbelievers.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that God chose Adam and Noah and selected them for their religion, and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran for the religion they followed, because they were the people of Islam.

c: So God Almighty informed us that
m: He chose the religion of those we mentioned over all other religions that contradicted it. What he meant by and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran were the believers. We have shown that a man’s family is his followers, his people, and whoever follows his religion. And with what we said about that, it was narrated that Ibn Abbas used to say it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over the worlds, he said: They are the believers from the family of Abraham, the family of Imran, the family of Yasin, and the family of Muhammad. God Almighty says: Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him
r
(Al Imran 3:68)
, and they are the believers.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds, two prophets whom God chose over the worlds.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran over the worlds, he said: God mentioned two righteous households and two righteous men, so He preferred them over the worlds, so Muhammad was from the family of Abraham.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham to his statement: And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, he said: God preferred them over the worlds with prophethood, over all people. They were the pious prophets chosen by their Lord.

x: What he means by that is that God chose the family of Abraham and the family of Imran, some descendants of others. The word dhariya is in the accusative case, as it is derived from and the family of Abraham and the family of Imran, because dhariya is indefinite, and the family of Imran is definite. If it was said that it was in the accusative case to repeat the selection, it would be correct. Because the meaning is: He chose offspring, some from others. Rather, He made some of them from others in loyalty in religion, and support for Islam and the truth, as He, the Most High, said: And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another (al-Tawbah 9:71), and He said in another place: The hypocrites, men and hypocrites, are from one another (al-Tawbah 9:67), meaning: that their religion is one and their way is one, so likewise His statement: offspring, some of them from others, only means: offspring of one religion, some of them the religion of another, and their word is one, and their religion is one in the monotheism of God and obedience to Him, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Some of them are descendants of others, meaning: in intention, action, sincerity, and monotheism for Him. And his saying: And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, means by that: God is the One who hears the words of Imran’s wife, and the One who knows what she conceals in her soul, since she vowed to Him what was in her womb, dedicated.

x: He means by His saying, may His praise be exalted:
h
When the wife of Imran said
, ‘My Lord,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb

, dedicated [for Your service], so accept this from me.’ So when is a relative clause of Hearer. As for the wife of Imran, she is the mother of Mary, daughter of Imran, the mother of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him.
Her name, as we have been told, was Hannah, daughter of Faqudh ibn Qabil, as well:

c: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his lineage. And others besides Ibn Hamid said: The daughter of Faqoud - with a dal - the son of Qabil. As for her husband, Imran, he is: Imran, son of Jashem, son of Amon, son of Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, son of Ahzig, son of Jotham, son of Azariah, son of Amaziah, son of Jaush, son of Ahazihu, son of Jarem, son of Jehaphashat, son of Asber, son of Abijah, son of Rehoboam, son of Solomon, son of David, son of Isha. Likewise: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, regarding his lineage. As for his saying: My Lord,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb

, dedicated, its meaning is: I have made a vow to You, O Lord, that what is in my womb is dedicated to Your worship. He means by that: I have dedicated it to Your service and to the service of Your holiness in the church, free from the service of everything other than You, devoted to You specifically. The word editor is in the accusative case as a state of what is in the description of the mention of the one who. So accept from me, meaning: So accept from me what I have vowed to You, O Lord. For You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, meaning: For You, O Lord, are the All-Hearing of what I say and pray for, the All-Knowing of what I intend in my soul and desire. Nothing is hidden from You, both the secret and the public of my affair. The reason for the vow of Hannah, daughter of Faqud, the wife of Imran, which God mentioned in this verse, as far as we have been informed, is:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying:
m: Zakariya and Imran married two sisters. The mother of John was with Zakariya, and the mother of Mary was with Imran. Imran died, and the mother of Mary was pregnant with Mary, who was a fetus in her womb. He said: And, as they claim, she had been prevented from having children until she grew old, and they were a family with a high status from God, the Most High. So while she was in the shade of a tree, she saw a bird feeding its chick, and her soul moved for the child, so she supplicated to God to grant her a child, and she became pregnant with Mary, and Imran died. When she knew that there was a fetus in her womb, she made it a vow to God, and a vow is to worship it for God, and to make it a prisoner in the church, and not to benefit from it in any worldly matters.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, he said,
m: then he mentioned the wife of Imran and her saying: My Lord,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated, meaning I have vowed it, she says: I have made it free for the worship of God, not benefiting from it in any worldly matters, so accept it from me, for You are the Hearing, the Knowing.

c: Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad Al-Tafawi told me, he said, Muhammad bin Rabia told us, he said, Al-Nadr bin Arabi told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: freed, he said: a servant of the pledge.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: A servant of the church.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Ismail told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated to Your service, he said: I have devoted it to worship.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated, he said: I put it in the church, and devoted it to worship.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated, he said: To the church, to serve it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
to be dedicated, he said: purely, without any worldly matter mixed with it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
to be dedicated, he said, for the pledge and the church.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated, he said: dedicated for worship.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
When the wife of Imran said
, ‘My Lord,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb

, dedicated to Your service,’ the verse. Imran’s wife had dedicated to God what was in her womb, and they only freed males. When a freed person was set free, he was placed in the church and would not leave it, taking care of it and sweeping it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated, he said: She vowed her child to the church.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
When the wife of Imran said
, ‘My Lord,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb

, dedicated [to Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’” He said: That was because the wife of Imran became pregnant, and she thought that what was in her womb was a boy, so she gave him to God, dedicated to Him, who would not work in this world.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: The wife of Imran freed for God what was in her womb. He said: They only freed males, so when the freed man was freed, he was placed in the church and would not leave it, taking care of it and sweeping it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated, he said: I have dedicated her child to God and to those who study the Book and learn it.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza: that he informed him on the authority of Ikrimah - and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: that the wife of Imran was an old barren woman called Hannah, and she was unable to bear children, so she began to envy other women for their children, so she said: O God, I have vowed in gratitude that if You grant me a son, I will give him in charity to the Holy House, so that he will be one of its custodians and servants. He said: And his saying:
h
I have vowed to You what is in my womb
, dedicated - that is, to the free woman, the daughter of free women - dedicated to the church, to serve it.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Mansur, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When the wife of Imran said
, the entire verse, he said: She vowed what was in her womb, then she set her free.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
So when she delivered her

, is when Hannah the vowed woman delivered, and that is why it was made feminine. If the ha’ had referred back to what in His statement: Indeed, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated, then the statement would have been: So when she delivered him, she said, My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female. The meaning of his saying:
h
I gave birth to her
is:
h
I gave birth to her

. It is said: A woman gave birth. She said, ‘My Lord, I have delivered a female child,’ meaning: The vowed woman gave birth to a female child, and God knows best what she delivered. There are different readings of this. The general reading is: She gave birth, as report from God Almighty about Himself: that He knows what she gave birth to, without her saying: My Lord, I have given birth to a female.
Some of the ancients read it as: And God knows best what she gave birth to, as a statement about Mary’s mother, that she was the one who said: And God knows best what she gave birth to from me.

The more correct of the two readings is what the evidence has transmitted widely. Its reading is clear, and they do not dispute its correctness. This is the reading of the one who reads, And God knows best what I have placed, and it is not objected to by the anomaly from it. The interpretation of the statement is: And God knows best of all His creation what she has given birth to. Then He, the Most High, returns to the report of her statement, and that she said - in apology to her Lord for what she had vowed in her pregnancy and freed it for the service of her Lord -: And the male is not like the female, because the male is stronger for service and more capable of it, and the female is not fit in some circumstances to enter the Holy Place and perform the service of the Church, because of what befalls her of menstruation and postpartum bleeding, And I have named her Mary, as:

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayy:
m: “And when she delivered her, she said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female.’ And God knew best what she delivered. And the male is not like the female.” That is, when she made her a vow to him, he said, Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me: And the male is not like the female, because the male is stronger in that regard than the female.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the male is not like the female. It was not possible for a woman to do that, meaning that she should be set free for the church, and placed in it, and she should take care of it and sweep it and not leave it, because of what befalls her of menstruation and harm. Then she said: And the male is not like the female.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: She said, ‘My Lord, I have delivered a female,’ and they only freed the boys - he said: And the male is not like the female, and I have named her Mary.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: The wife of Imran had dedicated to God what was in her womb, and she was hoping that He would give her a boy, because a woman could not do that - meaning, stand in the church and not leave it, and sweep it - because of the harm that would befall her.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: That the wife of Imran thought that what was in her womb was a boy, so she gave him up to God. But when she gave birth, she was a girl, so she said, apologizing to God: My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female. “And the male is not like the female,” she said: Only boys are set free. God said: And God knows best what she has delivered, so she said: Indeed, I have named her Mary.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza: that he told him on the authority of Ikrimah - and Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: “And when she gave birth to her, she said: My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female.” And the male is not like the female, he meant: during menstruation, and it is not appropriate for a woman to be with men, her mother says that.

x: What she means by her saying: And I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You, is that I make her refuge and the refuge of her offspring from the accursed Satan in You. The origin of the sanctuary is the habitat, refuge, and stronghold. So God responded to her, and God protected her and her offspring from the accursed Satan, and did not give him any power over her.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abdah bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No newborn is born without Satan striking him with that stab, and the child cries out for it, except for Mary, the daughter of Imran, for when she gave birth to her she said: ‘My Lord, I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan the accursed.’ So a veil was drawn up in front of her and he struck it.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every child born from the children of Adam has a stab from Satan, and the child cries out, except for Mary, the daughter of Imran, and her son, for her mother said when she gave birth to her: ‘I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan the accursed,’ and a veil was drawn between them, and the veil was stabbed.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Qusayt, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Humayd narrated that Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated on the authority of Amr on the authority of Shuʿayb ibn Khalid on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab who said: “I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘There is no child of Adam who is born except that Satan touches him at birth, and he begins to cry out in agony because of his touch, except for Mary and her son.’” Abu Hurayrah said: Read, if you wish, ‘I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed.’

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me, on the authority of Ajlan,
m: the freed slave of Al-Mishma’il, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every child born from the children of Adam is touched by Satan with his finger, except for Mary and her son.”

c: Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman bin Wahb told me, he said, my uncle Abdullah bin Wahb told me, he said, Amr bin Al-Harith told me:
m: Abu Yunus Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hurairah, told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every son of Adam is touched by Satan on the day his mother gives birth to him, except Mary and her son.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Imran told me, that Abu Yunus told him, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No child is born except that Satan touches him, and he begins to cry out from the touch of Satan, except Mary and her son.’ Then Abu Hurayrah said: ‘Read, if you wish, “And I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the outcast.”’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told me, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No child is born except that Satan squeezes him once or twice, except for Jesus, son of Mary, and Mary.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘Indeed, I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed.’”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun ibn al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: No child was born without crying out, except for the Messiah, son of Mary. Satan did not have power over him or threaten him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Al-Mundhir bin al-Nu'man al-Aftas narrated to us:
m: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Jesus was born, the devils came to Iblis and said: The idols have lowered their heads! He said: This is about something that has happened! He said: Stay where you are. So he flew until he reached the ends of the earth, but he did not find anything. Then he came to the seas and did not find anything. Then he flew again and found that Jesus had been born near a donkey's well, and behold, the angels had surrounded him. So he returned to them and said: A prophet was born last night. No female has ever conceived or given birth except that I was in her presence, except for this one. So despair of idols being worshipped after this night, but come to the children of Adam from the side of lightness and haste.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed. “And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God Surat Al Imran 3:36
h
So when she delivered her

, she said, "My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female. And Allah is most knowing of what she delivered. And the male is not like the female. And indeed, I have named her Mary, and indeed, I seek refuge for her and her offspring in You from Satan, the accursed." bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Satan stabbed every son of Adam in his side, except for Jesus, son of Mary, and his mother. A veil was placed between them and him, and the stab struck the veil. Nothing reached them. And it was mentioned to us that they did not commit sins as the rest of the sons of Adam do. And it was mentioned to us that Jesus walked on the sea as he walked on land, because of what God Almighty gave him of certainty and sincerity.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And I seek refuge in You for her and her offspring from Satan, the accursed. He said: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Satan has stabbed every human being in the side except Jesus and his mother, for they did not commit sins as the children of Adam commit them.” He said: And Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in praising his Lord: And He has protected me and my mother from Satan, the accursed, for he has no power over us.

c: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, he said, Shu’ayb bin Al-Layth told us, he said, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Harmaz, that he said: Abu Hurayrah said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The devil stabs every son of Adam in the side when his mother gives birth to him, except for Jesus, son of Mary. He went to stab him, but he stabs the veil.’”

c: Al-Rabi’ told us, he said, Shu’aib told us, he said, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Hormuz, that he said: Abu Hurairah said:
m: Have you seen this cry that a baby cries when his mother gives birth to him? It is from it.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Faraj told me, he said, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, he said, Al-Zubaidi told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no child of Adam who is born except that Satan touches him when he is born, and he cries out in agony.”

evidence.text: The general reading is: She gave birth, as report from God Almighty about Himself: that He knows what she gave birth to, without her saying: My Lord, I have given birth to a female.
Some of the ancients read it as: And God knows best what she gave birth to, as a statement about Mary’s mother, that she was the one who said: And God knows best what she gave birth to from me.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings is what the evidence has transmitted widely.
This is the reading of the one who reads, And God knows best what I have placed, and it is not objected to by the anomaly from it.

x: He means by that: that God, may He be glorified, accepted Mary from her mother Hannah, and her liberation of her for the church and her service and the service of her Lord, with good acceptance. Acceptance is a verbal noun derived from: her Lord accepted her. The verbal noun is derived from: her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance. The Arabs often do this: they use verbal nouns based on the roots of verbs, even if their verbal nouns differ in the verbs due to the addition of an additional letter. This is like their saying: So-and-so spoke. If the verbal noun were derived from the verb, it would be said: So-and-so spoke. And from this is His saying: And He caused it to grow with a good growth, and He did not say growing with a good growth.

c: It was reported on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala that he said:
m: We did not hear the Arabs pronounce the qaf with a damma in the word qubool, and the standard was to pronounce the damma, because it is a verbal noun such as: al-dukhul (entrance) and al-khuruj exit. He said: I did not hear of another letter in the speech of the Arabs that resembles it. I was told about that on the authority of Abu Ubaid, who said:

c: al-Yazidi informed me, on the authority of Abu Amr.
m: As for his statement: And He caused her to grow a good growth, its meaning is: And her Lord caused her to grow in His food and provision a good growth, until she was fully formed and became a mature, complete woman, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, God Almighty said:
m: So her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance, he said: He accepted from her mother what she wanted for the church, and her reward in it, and caused her to grow, he said: She grew in God’s nourishment.

x: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: And He took care of her. The people of Hijaz, Medina and Basra generally read it as: And he took her under his care, with a light fa. Meaning: Zachariah took her under his care, based on the words of God Almighty: They cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary.
r
(Al Imran 3:44)
This was read by most of the Kufians: And Zakariya took care of her meaning: God took care of her, Zakariya.
The most correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: and he guaranteed her with a shaddah.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: And He took care of her.
The people of Hijaz, Medina and Basra generally read it as: And he took her under his care, with a light fa.
(Al Imran 3:44) This was read by most of the Kufians: And Zakariya took care of her meaning: God took care of her, Zakariya.
Abu Jaafar said: The most correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: and he guaranteed her with a shaddah.

x: As for his statement:
h
There Zachariah called upon his Lord

, its meaning is: at that time, that is, when Zachariah saw what he saw with Mary of the provision that God had provided for her, and His grace that He had given her without any human being intervening in that for her, and his seeing with her the fresh fruit that was not on the ground at the time he saw it with her, he desired a child, despite his advanced age, from the barren woman. He hoped that God would provide him with a child from her, given the condition they were in, just as He provided Mary, despite her being free from people, with what He provided her of the fruit of summer in winter and the fruit of winter in summer, even though it was not something like what was customary in the world at that time, but rather what is known among people is other than that, just as the birth of a barren woman is not the customary thing among people.
So he desired from God, may He be glorified, a child, and asked Him for good offspring.
This is because the people of Zachariah’s household - as we have been told - had become extinct at that time, as:

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When Zakariya saw her condition, meaning: summer fruits in winter, and winter fruits in summer, he said: God has given her this at the wrong time. He is able to grant me good offspring! And he desired a child, so he stood up and prayed, then he called upon his Lord secretly and said: “My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head is shining with gray hair, and I have never been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy. And indeed, I fear my relatives after me, and my wife is barren. So grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, one pleasing to You.”
r
(Maryam 19:4-6)
, and he said: “My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed,
h
You are the Hearer of supplication

.” And he said: My Lord, leave me not alone, though You are the Best of inheritors. (al-Anbiya 21:89) Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Yaʿla ibn Muslim told me, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When Zakariya saw that - meaning the summer fruits in the winter, and the winter fruits in the summer - with Mary, he said: He who brings this to Mary at a time other than its time is able to grant me a son. God Almighty said: Thereupon Zakariya called upon his Lord. He said: That was when he called.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: So he entered the prayer niche and closed the doors, and communed with his Lord, saying: My Lord, indeed my bones have become feeble and my head is shining with gray hair until His saying: My Lord, be pleased
r
(Maryam 19:4-6)
, Then the angels called to him while he was standing praying in the prayer niche, ‘Indeed, God gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from God’ the verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, some of the people of knowledge told me:
m: Then Zachariah called out at that time after he had grown old and had no children, and his family had died out, and he said: “My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring. Indeed,
h
You are the Hearer of supplication
.” Then he complained to his Lord and said: My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head is shining with gray hair to And make him, my Lord, pleasing
r
(Maryam 19:4-6)

, Then the angels called out to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary the verse. As for his saying: My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring, he means by offspring the lineage, and by goodness the blessed, as:
b.via: some of the people of knowledge

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He said, ‘My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring,’ meaning: blessed. As for his saying: From You, he means: From You. As for offspring, it is a plural, and it may have the meaning of one, and in this case it is one. That is because God Almighty in another place, informing about the supplication of Zachariah: Then grant me from Yourself a protector
r
(Maryam 19:5)

, did not say: protectors - which indicates that he asked for one. Rather, he feminized Tayyiba because offspring is feminine, as the poet said: Your father is a caliph, another woman gave birth to him, and you are a caliph, that is perfection He said: Another woman gave birth to him, so he made it feminine, although it is a male, because the word caliph is feminine, as the other said: Do not despise a silent mountain snake, which, when bitten, is not venomous. So he made the word jabaliya feminine because the word snake is feminine, then he returned to the meaning and said: If it bites, because he meant a male snake. This is only permissible in cases where the name so-and-so does not fall under the same category, such as beast, “offspring,” and caliph. But if a man is named with one of these things, and it is in the meaning of so-and-so, it is not permissible to make his action or description feminine. As for his saying:
h
You are the Hearer of supplication
, its meaning is:
h
You are the Hearer of supplication
, except that Hearer is more praiseworthy, and it means: He who hears it. Some Basra grammarians claimed that its meaning is: You hear what you are called to.

x: The interpretation of the verse is that at that time Zachariah called upon his Lord and said: My Lord, grant me from Yourself a blessed son. Indeed, You are the One who hears the supplication of whoever calls upon You.

The readings differed in the reading of that. The majority of the people of Medina and some of the people of Kufa and Basra read it as: The angels called him with the feminine ending taa, meaning the plural of angels. The Arabs do the same with a group of males, if their verbs come before them, they feminize their verbs, especially the nouns that have feminine endings in their words, like their saying: The Talhats came.

A group of the people of Kufa read it with the letter Ya, meaning Gabriel called him, so they mentioned it for interpretation, just as we mentioned earlier that they feminize the masculine verb for the word, so they also mention the feminine verb for the word.
And they considered that, in my opinion, as a reading, which is mentioned as the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, which is what:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Hammad told us, that
m: Ibn Masoud’s reading was: Gabriel called to him while he was standing praying in the prayer niche. Likewise, a group of interpreters interpreted his statement:
h
Then the angels called him

x: Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The angels called him, and he was Gabriel, or: The angels said, and he was Gabriel,
h
God gives you good tidings of John

x: If someone were to say: How is it permissible to say, according to this interpretation: The angels called him, and angels is a plural, not a singular? It was said: This is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, to report about one person in the plural manner, as it is said in speech: So-and-so went out on the cold mules, but he only rode one mule, and he rode the ships, but he only rode one ship. And as it is said: Who did you hear this report from? It is said: From the people, but he only heard it from one man. It has been said that from this is his saying: Those to whom the people said, ‘The people have gathered against you’
r
(Al Imran 3:173)

, and the speaker was - as mentioned - one, and his saying: And when harm touches a person (al-Rum 30:33), and the people have one meaning. And this is permissible according to them in what is not intended as one intention.

The correct thing to say in my opinion regarding the recitation of this is that they are two well-known recitations, I mean the taʿ and the yaʿ, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. This is because there is no difference in the meaning of this due to the difference in the two recitations, and they are both eloquent among the Arabs. This is because if what is meant by the angels is Gabriel, as narrated from ʿAbdullah, then the feminine gender in its verb is eloquent in the speech of the Arabs due to its pronunciation, if the verb precedes it. And it is permissible to make it masculine due to its meaning. If it is intended to refer to the plural of angels, then it is permissible to make the verb feminine, which is before it, due to its wording. This is because when the Arabs put their verb before a large group, they make it feminine, so they say: The women said.

And it is permissible to make their verb masculine, based on the singular, if its verb comes before it, so it is said: The men said. As for the correct interpretation of it, it is to say: God, the Most High, informed that the angels called him. What is apparent from that is that it was a group of angels, not one, and Gabriel was one. It is not permissible to interpret the Qur’an except according to the most apparent of the speech used in the tongues of the Arabs, not the least, as long as there is a way to do that. And there is no need to divert that to one meaning, which requires seeking a way out through the hidden speech and meanings. And what we have said about this interpretation was said by a group of scholars, including: Qatada, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and a group of others. We have mentioned what they said about this previously.
The interpretation of his saying:
h
And he was standing
is: The angels called him while he was standing praying. So his saying:
h
And he was standing is report about the time when the angels called Zachariah

. His saying: prays is in the accusative case as a state of standing, and it is raised with the letter ya. As for the mihrab, we have explained its meaning, and that it is the front of the mosque. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
God gives you good tidings
. The general reading is: that God with the opening of the alif of that with the calling being on it, meaning: the angels called him with that.

Some of the readers of Kufa read it: Indeed God gives you good report with a kasra on the alif, meaning: The angels said: Indeed God gives you good report, because the call is a statement. They mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah it is: “The angels called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary: ‘O Zachariah, indeed God gives you good report.’” They said: “If the call is invalidated from being an agent in his statement: “O Zachariah,” then it is also invalidated from being an agent in in. The correct reading of this in our view is:
h
God gives you good tidings

, with the opening of an with the call being made to him, meaning: the angels called him with that. The reason that the reciters used to prove the kasra of in is not that Abdullah used to recite it like that, so they recited it like that, [they have a reason]. That is because if Abdullah recited it like that, then he recited it, according to them, because the call of Zakariya interrupted between in and his saying, so he called him.

And if he interrupted between them, then the Arabs then use the call in an and nullify it. As for nullification, it is because it nullified the work of the one called before it, so they treated what comes after it as it did in the length of its work. As for the working, it is because the call is a real action, like all other actions. As for our reading, the calling of Zakariya with O Zakariya is not an objection between that and his saying so she called him. Since that is not between them, the eloquent speech of the Arabs, when you put the name of the one calling in the accusative case with the saying I called and they apply it to it, is to apply it likewise to that after it. Even though it is permissible to invalidate its function. So his saying she called him has been used as a nickname for Zakariya, so it is also correct that it be applied to that and an agent in it. Although this is the widespread reading in the reading of the Islamic countries, and the group that comes as an argument is not objected to by the anomaly.
As for his saying:
h
He gives you good tidings
, the readings differed in its reading. The people of Medina and Basra generally read it as:
h
God gives you good tidings

, with emphasis on the shin and a damma on the ya, in the manner of God giving Zachariah good tidings of a son, as people say: I gave so-and-so good tidings of such-and-such, meaning: I brought him good tidings of good tidings of that.

i: A group of Kufan readers and others read it as: God gives you good report, with the opening of the ya’ and the closing of the shin and its softening, meaning: that God will make you happy with a child He will give you, from the words of the poet:
x: I gave my children good report when I saw a letter that came to you from Al-Hajjaj, the book of which was being read.

It has been said: Bishrat is the language of the people of Tihamah from Kinanah and others from Quraysh, and that they say I gave so-and-so good report of such-and-such, so I give him good report, and Are you going to give so-and-so good report? And the following verse is recited for them about that: And if you see those who are ascending to the heavens covered in dust, their palms are in a barren valley. So help them, and give them the good report they gave you, and if they are in distress, then give them the good report. When they come to the matter, the correct speech of their speech is without the letter alif, so it is said: Bring good report to so-and-so, and they hardly say: Bring good report to him about such-and-such, nor Bring good report to him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Hamid bin Qais
m: that he used to read: Yabashkir with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the sheen and a light sukoon on it. And: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, on the authority of Muadh al-Kufi, he said: Whoever reads: He gives them good tidings with a heavy ya then it is from good tidings. And whoever reads: He gives them good tidings, with a light ya in the accusative case, then it is from surur, “yasarhum.”

x: The reading that is the reading according to us in this regard is with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the shin, meaning giving good tidings. Because that is the common language and widespread speech known among the people, even though all the readers of the regions agree on the reading of So what are you giving good tidings of? (al-Hijr 15:54) with a shaddah. The correct reading in all other similar words in the Qur’an is that it should be like it in the shaddah and with a damma on the ya’. As for what was narrated from Muadh Al-Kufi about the difference between the meaning of alleviation and emphasis in that, we did not find the people of knowledge of the speech of the Arabs knowing it from a correct perspective, so there is no meaning to what was narrated from him about that. Jarir bin Atiyah said: Oh, Bashar, it is your right to preach good report. Why don’t you get angry for us, you who are a prince?

It is known that by his saying: good report, he meant beauty, freshness and joy, so he said good report and did not say humanity, and this has shown that the meaning of lightening and heaviness in that is one.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God gives you good tidings of Yahya

, he said: The angels gave him good tidings of that. As for his saying: by Yahya, it is a noun, its root is Surat Al Imran 3:39 Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from Allah
h
and a master
, chaste,
h
and a prophet from among the righteous

." yaf’al, from the saying of the speaker: Hayy so-and-so is alive, so he is Yahya, and that is when he lives. So Yahya yaf’al is from their saying Hayyi. It was said: God Almighty called him that because he interpreted his name as: He revived him with faith.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
