God gives you good tidings of Yahya
, meaning: a servant whom God brought to life through faith.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God gives you good tidings of John
, he said: He was only called John because God gave him life through faith.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means:
h
God gives you good tidings
, O Zachariah, of John as your son,
h
confirming a word from God

, meaning: Jesus, son of Mary. The accusative case of his saying: confirming is a severance from Yahya, because confirming is an adjective for it, and it is indefinite, and Yahya is indefinite. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad Al-Tafawi told me, he said, Muhammad bin Rabi’ah told us, he said, Al-Nadr bin Arabi told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The wife of Zachariah said to Maryam 19:I feel that which is in my womb moving for that which is in your womb! He said: So the wife of Zachariah gave birth to John, and Mary gave birth to Jesus, and that is why he said:
h
Confirming a word from God
, he said: John is confirming Jesus.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Al-Raqashi,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
He gives you good tidings
of John,
h
confirming a word from God
, he said: confirming Jesus, son of Mary.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Sulayman told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, he said, Qatada told us
m: regarding his statement:
h
Confirming a word from God
, he said: Confirming Jesus.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Confirming a word from God
, meaning: Confirming Jesus, son of Mary, and following his Sunnah and method.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Confirming a word from God
, meaning: Jesus, son of Mary.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Confirming a word from God
, he says: Confirming Jesus, son of Mary, he says, according to his Sunnah and his method.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
Confirming a word from God
, he said: He was the first man to believe in Jesus, and he is a word from God and a spirit.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Confirming a word from God
, he believes in Jesus.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Indeed,
h
God gives you good tidings of John
h
confirming a word from God
. John was the first to believe in Jesus and testify that he was a word from God. John was Jesus’ cousin, and he was older than Jesus.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Confirming a word from God
, he said: Jesus, son of Mary, is the word from God, his name is the Messiah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: His statement,
h
Confirming a word from God

, he said: Jesus and John were maternal cousins, and John’s mother used to say to Maryam 19:I find that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb! So that was his belief in Jesus: his prostration in his mother’s womb. And he was the first to believe in Jesus and the word of Jesus, and John was older than Jesus.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
God gives you good tidings of John
h
confirming a word from God
, he said: The word he confirmed was Jesus.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: I met the mother of Yahya, the mother of Jesus, and one of them was pregnant with Yahya, and the other was pregnant with Jesus, and the wife of Zachariah said: O Mary, I sense that I am pregnant! Mary said: I sense that I am also pregnant! The wife of Zachariah said: Then I have found what is in my womb prostrating to what is in your womb! So that is his saying:
h
Confirming a word from God

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
God gives you good tidings of John
h
confirming a word from God
, he said: confirming Jesus, son of Mary.

x: Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Basra claimed that the meaning of his saying:
h
Confirming a word from God

is a book from God, from the Arabs’ saying: So-and-so recited to me such-and-such a word, meaning: such-and-such a poem, out of his ignorance of the interpretation of the word, and his audacity in translating the Qur’an according to his own opinion.
By His Most High’s saying,
h
and a master

, He means, and noble in knowledge and worship. And the master was appointed in apposition to his saying: believing. The interpretation of the words: God gives you good report of John, confirming this,
h
and a master
The active master is from the saying of the speaker: he ruled, he rules, like:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And a master
meaning, by God, a master in worship, patience, knowledge, and piety.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Muslim told us, Abu Hilal told us, Qatada told us
m: regarding his statement:
h
and a master
, he said: The master, I do not know of anyone who said: in knowledge and worship.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The master is the forbearing.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: h
And a master
, he said: the forbearing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And a master
, he said: the pious master.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And a master
, he said: The master is generous to God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, he said:
m: Al-Raqashi claimed that the master is the generous one to God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And a master
, he said: The master is the forbearing and pious.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And a master
, he said: He says: Pious and forbearing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a master
, he said: Forbearing and pious.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Zayd,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a master
, he said: The noble master.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And a master
, he said: The master is the knowledgeable jurist.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And a master
, he said, he says: forbearing and pious.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And a master
, he said: The master is the one who is not overcome by anger.

x: He means by that: abstaining from intercourse with women, from the saying of the speaker: I was prevented from such-and-such, if he refrained from it. And from that is their saying: So-and-so was prevented from reading, if he refrained from reading and was not able to do so. And likewise the enemy was prevented, the people detained them and prevented them from doing anything. And for that reason the one who does not go out with his companions is called hasur, as Al-Akhtal said: And a drinker who wins the cup, make me regret neither the presence nor the bracelet It is narrated: Basar. It is also said of the one who does not reveal his secret and keeps it to himself, Hasur, because he prevents his secret from being revealed, as Jarir said: The informers have brought me down, and they have found a tight-lipped confidant in your secret, O Umaym. The origin of all of this is one, which is prevention and confinement.
And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Khalaf told us, he said, Hammad bin Shuaib told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a gentleman and a chaste man
, he said: The chaste man is the one who does not come to women.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saʿid, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: Ibn al-ʿAs told me:
m: “He heard the Messenger Surat Al Imran 3:39 Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the sanctuary, "Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from Allah
h
and a master
, chaste,
h
and a prophet from among the righteous

." of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Every son of Adam will come on the Day of Resurrection with a sin, except for what was of Yahya ibn Zakariya.’ He said: ‘Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his hand to the ground, took a small stick, and said: ‘That is because he did not have what men have except something like this stick.’ And with that, God called him master and chaste.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Anas bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, he said,
m: I heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say: There is no one who will not meet God on the Day of Resurrection with a sin except Yahya bin Zakariya. He was chaste, and had something like a tuft of hair. Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi narrated, Umar ibn Jaʿfar narrated, Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saʿid, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ibn al-ʿAs - either Abdullah or his father - said: No one will meet God except as a sinner, except Yahya ibn Zakariya. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab said: “
h
And a gentleman and a chaste man
,” he said: The chaste man is the one who does not have intercourse with women, and he has nothing with him except the hem of a garment.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: regarding his statement: and chaste, he said: The chaste is the one who does not desire women. Then he struck the ground with his hand and took a date pit and said: He had nothing with him except something like this.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: The one who is chaste is the one who does not come to women.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed,
m: similarly.

c: Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad told me, he said, Muhammad bin Rabia told us, he said, Al-Nadr bin Arabi told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And chaste, he said: the one who does not come to women.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The chaste person does not approach women.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, he said:
m: Al-Raqashi claimed: The chaste is the one who does not approach women.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: The one who is impotent is the one who does not give birth and has no water.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And barren, that he said: It is that which has no water.

c: Bishr told us, Suwaid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And chaste, we used to say that chaste is the one who does not approach women.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Sulayman told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, he said, Qatada told us
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a gentleman and a chaste man
, he said: The chaste man is the one who does not come to women.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The one who is impure is the one who does not have water coming down.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Yazid:
m: And chaste, he said: The chaste is the one who does not come to women.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And chaste, he said: Chaste is the one who does not want women.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: And chaste, he said: He does not approach women. As for his saying:
h
And a prophet from among the righteous

, it means: a messenger from his Lord to his people, informing them of His commands and prohibitions, His lawful and unlawful things, and conveying to them what He sent him with to them. By his saying: of the righteous, he means of his righteous prophets. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of prophecy and its origin, with evidence and proof indicating the correct statement about it, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
The majority of the people of Medina and some of the people of Kufa and Basra read it as: The angels called him with the feminine ending taa, meaning the plural of angels.

A group of the people of Kufa read it with the letter Ya, meaning Gabriel called him, so they mentioned it for interpretation, just as we mentioned earlier that they feminize the masculine verb for the word, so they also mention the feminine verb for the word.
And they considered that, in my opinion, as a reading, which is mentioned as the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, which is what:

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct thing to say in my opinion regarding the recitation of this is that they are two well-known recitations, I mean the taʿ and the yaʿ, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct.
This is because there is no difference in the meaning of this due to the difference in the two recitations, and they are both eloquent among the Arabs.
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: God gives you good tidings.
The general reading is: that God with the opening of the alif of that with the calling being on it, meaning: the angels called him with that.
Some of the readers of Kufa read it: Indeed God gives you good report with a kasra on the alif, meaning: The angels said: Indeed God gives you good report, because the call is a statement.
They mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah it is: “The angels called to him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary: ‘O Zachariah, indeed God gives you good report.’”
The correct reading of this in our view is: God gives you good tidings, with the opening of an with the call being made to him, meaning: the angels called him with that.
The reason that the reciters used to prove the kasra of in is not that Abdullah used to recite it like that, so they recited it like that, [they have a reason].
That is because if Abdullah recited it like that, then he recited it, according to them, because the call of Zakariya interrupted between in and his saying, so he called him.
As for our reading, the calling of Zakariya with O Zakariya is not an objection between that and his saying so she called him.
Although this is the widespread reading in the reading of the Islamic countries, and the group that comes as an argument is not objected to by the anomaly.
As for his saying: He gives you good tidings, the readings differed in its reading.

The people of Medina and Basra generally read it as: God gives you good tidings, with emphasis on the shin and a damma on the ya, in the manner of God giving Zachariah good tidings of a son, as people say: I gave so-and-so good tidings of such-and-such, meaning: I brought him good tidings of good tidings of that.

A group of Kufan readers and others read it as: God gives you good report, with the opening of the ya’ and the closing of the shin and its softening, meaning: that God will make you happy with a child He will give you, from the words of the poet: I gave my children good report when I saw a letter that came to you from Al-Hajjaj, the book of which was being read.
And the following verse is recited for them about that: And if you see those who are ascending to the heavens covered in dust, their palms are in a barren valley.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that is the reading according to us in this regard is with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the shin, meaning giving good tidings.
Because that is the common language and widespread speech known among the people, even though all the readers of the regions agree on the reading of So what are you giving good tidings of?
The correct reading in all other similar words in the Qur’an is that it should be like it in the shaddah and with a damma on the ya’.

x: It means that Zachariah said, when the angels called him: God gives you good tidings of John, confirming a word from God and a noble and chaste man, and a prophet from among the righteous. “
h
How can I have a boy

when I have reached old age?” Meaning: Whoever has reached the age you have reached has not had a child, and my wife is barren. A barren woman is one who does not give birth. It is said of her: a barren woman, and a barren man, as Amer bin Tufail said: What a poor young man! If I am blind, barren and a coward, what excuse do I have before every court!! As for al-Kabir, it is a source: kabar, so he grows up with great pride. It was said: I have reached old age, and he said in another place: I have reached old age
r
(Maryam 19:8)
, because whatever has reached you, you have reached. Rather, its meaning is: I have grown old, and it is like the saying of the one who says: I have reached exhaustion, meaning: I am in exhaustion.
How could Zachariah, the Prophet of God, say: My Lord,
h
how can I have a boy

when I have reached old age and my wife is barren, when the angels gave him the good report that God had given him? I doubt their truthfulness. That is something that should not be said of those who believe in God! How about the prophets and messengers? Or was that from him a denunciation of the power of his Lord? That would be a greater affliction!
That was from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, not as I thought, but rather what he said was what he said of that, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When he heard the call - meaning Zachariah, when he heard the angels’ call with the good report of John - Satan came to him and said to him: O Zachariah, the voice that you heard is not from God, it is from Satan mocking you! If it were from God, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals it to you in other matters! So he doubted his position and said:
h
How can I have a boy

, a male? He said: From where? And I have reached old age and my wife is barren. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Satan came to him and wanted to spoil the blessing of his Lord for him, so he said: Do you know who called you? He said: Yes! The angels of my Lord called me! He said: Rather, that was Satan! If this was from your Lord, He would have concealed it from you as You concealed Your call! He said: My Lord, make for me a sign. So what he said was what he said about that, and his recourse to his Lord in what he recourse to Him in his saying:
h
How can I have a boy
? because of the whispering that had mingled with his heart from Satan until he imagined that the call he heard was a call from someone other than the angels, so he said: My Lord,
h
how can I have a boy

? seeking confirmation in his matter, so that it would be established for him by a sign that God would show him in that - that it was good report from God on the tongues of His angels, and for that reason he said: My Lord, make for me a sign. It may be possible that he said that as a question to his Lord: How will the child he was given the good report come about? From his wife? Since she was barren - or from another woman? So that would be different from the way that Ikrimah, Al-Suddi and those who said something similar to them said.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: Thus is God, is that He described Himself with, that it is easy for Him to create a child from an old man who has despaired of having a child, and from a barren woman from whom there is no hope of giving birth, just as He created you, Zachariah, before creating a child from you, and you were nothing, because He is God, for whom it is not difficult to create something He wills, and it is not impossible for Him to do something He wills, because His power is the power that is not like any power, just as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Thus does God do what He wills, and I created you before, and you were nothing.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant report about Zachariah. Zachariah said: My Lord, if this call that I was called to, and the voice that I heard, is the voice of Your angels and good tidings from You to me, then make for me a sign - he says: a sign - that this is so, so that what Satan has whispered to me and cast into my heart, that this is the voice of someone other than the angels and good tidings from someone other than You, may be removed from me, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: My Lord, make for me a sign. He said: He said - meaning Zachariah -: O Lord, if this voice is from you, then make for me a sign. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of the verse, and that it is a sign, so there is no need to repeat it. The Arabs differed about the reason for the Arabs leaving out the hamza, and it is their custom to hamza every yaa that comes after a silent alif.

x: Some of them said: He left out the hamza because it was a verse, and the emphasis was difficult for them, so they replaced it with an alif because of the openness before the emphasis, just as they said: Anyone, may God disgrace him.

Others of them said: Rather, it is a defective agent. They were asked: Why do the Arabs make the diminutive of it as ‘Ayyah’ and not ‘Uwayyah’? They said: That was said, just as it was said about Fatima: this is Fatima. They were told: They only make the diminutive of ‘Fa’ila’ as ‘Fa’ila’ if it is a noun with the same meaning as ‘so-and-so’ and ‘so-and-so’. Otherwise, it is not part of their diminutive of ‘Fa’ila’ as ‘Fa’ila’.

Others said: It is a verb whose first yaa was changed to an alif, as was done with haja and qamah. It was said to them: The Arabs only do that with three children. And those who denied what they said said: If it were as they said, it would have been said about a date pit of a flute, and about a life of a snake.

c: So God punished him - as he told us
m: - by asking for a sign, after the angels had spoken to him with the good report. He made his sign, in confirmation of what he had heard of the good report from the angels about John that it was from God, a sign from himself. God Almighty combined with it the sign that he had asked his Lord for, in order to clarify to him the truth of the good report that it was from God, and to purify him of his error and the mistake in his saying and question.
b.via: So God punished him - as he

x: A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture.’ He was punished with that because the angels spoke to him directly about that, and gave him the good report of John, so he asked for the sign after the angels had spoken to him. So he took hold of his tongue, and he was unable to speak except by gesture and indication. Then God, the Most High, said, as you hear: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, God gives you good tidings of John, confirming, he said: The angels spoke to him, and he said: My Lord, give me a sign. He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture,” meaning: except by gesture, and it was a punishment with which he was punished, since he asked for the sign while the angels spoke to him directly with what they had given him the good tidings of.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: My Lord, make for me a sign. He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. He said: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that he was punished, because the angels spoke to him face to face, and gave him the good report of John, so he asked for the sign after that, and he took hold of his tongue.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that he was punished because the angels spoke to him and gave him the good report of Yahya. They said: God gives you good report of Yahya. So after the angels spoke to him, he asked for a sign, and his tongue was seized, so he was unable to speak except in signs - he said: he gestured. Surat Al Imran 3:41 He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much
h
and glorify Him in the evening
and the morning."

c: Abu Ubaid Al-Wasabi told me, he said, Muhammad bin Hamir told us, he said, Safwan bin Amr told us, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr,
m: regarding his statement: He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture.’ He said: He stuck his tongue in his mouth until it filled it, then God released him after three days.

x: The Qur’anic reading chose the accusative in His statement: that you will not speak to people, because the meaning of the statement is: He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days to come. So it was an that accompanies the future, not an that accompanies nouns and makes them accusative. If the meaning was: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days, meaning: that you will be in this state for three days, then the correct way to say it would be in the nominative case. Because an would then have the meaning of being heavy, so it would be lightened. But that was not permissible, because it was described as having the other meaning. As for the symbol, the most common meaning for Arabs is: gesture with the lips. It may also be used to gesture with the eyebrows and eyes sometimes, but this is not common among them. The hidden part of speech that is like whispering in a lowered voice may be called: the symbol, and from this is the saying of Juwayyah ibn A’idh: The heroes spoke in a symbolic way and their murmur was like a roar.
It is said: So-and-so symbolized, so he symbolizes, symbolizes, and symbolizes, and it is said: He struck him a blow and he was shaken by it, meaning he was shaken by death.

i: The poet said:
x: I fell from it, throwing myself on my back The people of interpretation differed about the meaning that God Almighty meant in His statement about Zechariah, saying: Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture, and what meanings of gesture did He mean by that?
Some of them said: What he meant by that is: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by moving your lips, without symbolizing speech with your tongue.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: except a sign, he said: moving the lips.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Three days except a gesture, he said: his gesture with his lips.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: Rather, God meant by that: gesture and indication.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
Except by a sign
, he said: a gesture.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Except by a sign
, he said: The sign is to point with his hand or his head, and not speak.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Except by a sign
, he said: The sign is that he took hold of his tongue and began to speak to the people with his hand.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Except a symbol, he said: And a symbol is a sign.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: My Lord, make for me a sign. He said, Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture, the verse, he said: He made his sign that he would not speak to the people for three days except by gesture, except that he would remember God. And the gesture is the sign, he points to them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except by gesture, except by allusion.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Except a symbol, he says: an indication.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer said:
m: Except a symbol, except a sign.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture.’ He said: He held his tongue, and he began to gesture with his hand to his al-Nas 114:Glorify God morning and evening.

x: What he meant by that is: God, the Most High, said to Zachariah: O Zachariah, Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture, without being mute, disabled, or sick. And remember your Lord often, for you will not be prevented from remembering Him, and nothing will come between you and glorifying Him and other things of remembering Him. And: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb, who said: If God had given permission to anyone to abandon remembrance, He would have given permission to Zachariah when He said, “Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord often,” also. As for his saying:
h
And glorify Him in the evening
, it means: glorify your Lord by worshipping Him in the evening.

i: The evening is from when the sun declines until it sets, as the poet said:
x: You cannot find shade from the cold of the morning, nor can you taste the shade from the cold of the evening.

The shade begins to return at noon and ends at sunset. As for al-ibraq, it is a source of saying: So-and-so went out early to do something, so he goes out early, and that is if he goes out for it between the break of dawn and the time of the forenoon, then that is ibkar. It is said about it: So-and-so went out early and he went out early. From ibkar is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabi’ah: Yes, you are leaving early From the early morning, Jarir said: Salma rose early, so she could do her best and break the stick after her prince met It is said of this: the first date palm to ripen early, and the first to ripen early, and the first of the fruits: the first to ripen. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And glorify Him in the evening
and the morning, he said: The morning is the beginning of dawn, and the evening is the decline of the sun until it sets.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: “And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. When the wife of Imran said, ‘My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated to Your service.’”
h
And when the angels said
, ‘O Mary, God has chosen you.’ The meaning of his saying: He chose you is that He selected you and chose you for His obedience and the honor He has given you. His saying:
h
And purify you

, means: purify your religion from the doubt and impurities that are in the religions of the women of the children of Adam. And He chose you over the women of the worlds, meaning: He chose you over the women of the worlds in your time, through your obedience to Him, so He preferred you over them, as was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said:
h
The best of its women
is Mary, daughter of Imran, and
h
the best of its women
is Khadija, the savior of Khuwaylid, meaning by his saying:
h
The best of its women
, the best of the women of the people of Paradise.

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me that Muhadhir bin Al-Mura’ told us that Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ja’far, who said:
m: I heard Ali in Iraq say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say:
h
The best of its women
is Mary, daughter of Imran, and
h
the best of its women
is Khadija.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Al-Mundhir bin Abdullah Al-Hizami told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Jaafar bin Abi Talib:
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best of the women of Paradise is Mary, daughter of Imran, and the best of the women of Paradise is Khadija bint Khuwaylid.
b.via: Abdullah bin Jaafar bin Abi Talib

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when the angels said

, ‘O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds,’ he mentioned to us “that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘Mary, the daughter of Imran, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija, the daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad, are sufficient for you from among the women of the worlds.’” Qatada said: he mentioned to us “that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘The best women who rode camels are the righteous women of Quraysh, the most compassionate towards their children in their youth, and the most attentive to their husbands in their wealth.’” Qatada said: he mentioned to us that he used to say: If I had known that Mary rode camels, I would not have preferred anyone over her.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds, he said: Abu Hurairah used to narrate that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best women who rode camels were the righteous women of Quraysh, the most compassionate towards their children, and the most attentive to their husbands in matters of wealth. Abu Hurairah said: And Mary never rode a camel. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his saying:
h
And when the angels said

, ‘O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.’ He said: Thabit al-Bunani used to narrate, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best women of the worlds are four: Mary, daughter of Imran, Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima, daughter of Muhammad.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Amr bin Murrah told us, he said,
m: I heard Murrah Al-Hamdani narrating, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Many men have attained perfection, but none of the women have attained perfection except Mary, Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija bint Khuwaylid, and Fatima bint Muhammad.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Al-Aswad Al-Masry told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of ‘Amara bin Ghaziya, on the authority of Muhammad bin ‘Abdullah bin ‘Amr bin ‘Uthman: That Fatima bint Husayn bin ‘Ali told him:
m: “Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered one day while I was with ‘Aisha, and he whispered to me privately so I cried, then he whispered to me privately so I laughed, then ‘Aisha asked me about that, so I said: You have been hasty! I will tell you the secret of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace!! So she left me. Then when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, ‘Aisha asked her, and she said: Yes, he whispered to me privately and said: Gabriel used to review the Qur’an once every year, and he has reviewed the Qur’an twice, and there is no Surat Al Imran 3:42
h
And when the angels said

, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds." prophet except that his age was half the age of the one who was before him, and ‘Isa, my brother, lived a hundred and twenty years, and this is sixty for me, and I think I will die in this year of mine, and no woman among the women of the worlds has suffered as much as I have suffered, and you should not be less patient than a woman!” She said: So I cried, then… He said: You are the lady of the women of Paradise, except for the Virgin Mary. So he died that year.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Al-Aswad told us, he said: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith: that Abu Ziyad Al-Himyari told him:
m: that he heard Ammar bin Saad say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Khadija was preferred over the women of my nation, just as Mary was preferred over the women of the worlds.” And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying:
h
And purify you
, it is: And purify your religion from filth and doubt, said Mujahid.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Indeed, God has chosen you and purified you, he said: He made you pure in faith.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And He chose you over the women of the worlds, he said: That is for the worlds on that Day. And the angels - according to what Ibn Ishaq mentioned - were saying that to Mary verbally.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me:
m: Mary was a prisoner in the church, and with her in the church was a boy named Joseph, whose mother and father had made him a prisoner and a Nazirite, so they were both in the church. And when Mary’s water and Joseph’s water ran out, they would take their two jugs and go to the desert where they could drink sweet water, and fill their two jugs, then return to the church, and the angels were facing Mary at that time: O Mary, God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. So when Zachariah heard that, he said: The daughter of Imran has a special status!!

x: What He, may He be glorified, meant by His saying - reporting what His angels said to Maryam 19:O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, is to devote obedience to your Lord alone. We have demonstrated the meaning of Qunut with evidence in what has passed before. The difference between the people of interpretation regarding it in this place is similar to their difference regarding it there, and we will also mention the statement of some of them regarding this place.
Some of them said: The meaning of Qunti is to prolong the stagnation.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord, he said: Prolong the stagnation, meaning the devoutness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Be devout to your Lord, he said, Mujahid said: Prolong the stagnation in prayer, meaning the qunut.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: When it was said to her: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord, she stood until her heels swelled.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abdullah bin Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: When it was said to her: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord, she stood until her feet swelled.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Be devout to your Lord, he said: Prolong your stagnation. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord. He said: Qunut means stillness. He says: Stand up for your Lord in prayer. He says: Stand still for your Lord: meaning stand up for Him in prayer, and prostrate and bow with those who bow.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord, he said: She used to pray until her feet swelled.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Al-Awza’i told us:
m: O Mary, be devout towards your Lord. He said: She would stand until pus flowed from her feet.

x: Others said: It means: Be sincere to your Lord.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: O Mary, be devout to your Lord, he said: Be sincere to your Lord.

x: Others said: It means: Obey your Lord.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Be obedient to your Lord
, he said: Obey your Lord.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Be obedient to your Lord
, obey your Lord.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every letter in the Qur’an in which supplication is mentioned is obedience to God.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Mansour, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, he said, he says: Worship your Lord.

x: We have also explained the meaning of bowing and prostration with evidence indicating its validity, and that they mean humility to God, and submission to Him in obedience and worship. The interpretation of the verse, then, is: O Mary, devote your worship of your Lord to Him alone, and be humble in obeying and worshipping Him along with those of His creation who are humble before Him, in gratitude to Him for the honour He has bestowed upon you of selection, purification from impurities, and preference over the women of your time.

By His saying that, the Most High means: the report that He informed His servants about the wife of Imran and her daughter Mary, and Zachariah and his son John, and all that He related in the verses from His saying: Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah, then He, the Most High, gathered all of that together with His saying: that, and said: This report is from report of the unseen, meaning: from report of the unseen. By the unseen, he means that it is the hidden report of the people that you, O Muhammad, and your people did not know about, and only a few of the rabbis and monks of the People of the Book knew about. Then the Almighty informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He revealed this to him, as proof of his prophethood, and to confirm his truthfulness, and to cut off from Him the excuse of those who deny his message from the infidels of the People of the Book, who know that Muhammad did not reach the year of this report, despite its concealment, and did not attain knowledge of it, despite its being hidden from its people, except by God informing him of that.

Since it was known to them that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was illiterate and did not read books, so he would reach knowledge of that from books, nor was he a companion of the People of the Book, so he would take his knowledge from them. As for al-Ghayb, it is a noun derived from the saying: So-and-so was absent from such-and-such, so he is absent from it in an unseen or hidden way. As for his saying:
h
We reveal it to you

, its interpretation is: We send it down to you. The origin of inspiration is the revelation of the one who inspires to the one to whom it is inspired. This may be by writing, a sign, a gesture, by inspiration, or by a message, as the Most High said: And your Lord inspired the bee (al-Nahl 16:68), meaning: He inspired it with that and inspired it.

i: And as He said:
x: When I inspired the disciples (al-Ma’idah 5:111), meaning: I inspired them with the knowledge of that. And as the rajaz poet said: The decision inspired her and she settled down.
Meaning that He sent it to her as a command, and as He, the Most High, said:
Then He inspired them to glorify God morning and evening

meaning: He sent it to them as a gesture. The origin of it is what I described, of sending it to them. His sending it to them may be as a gesture, or it may be in writing. And from that is His statement: And indeed, the devils inspire their allies (al-An’am 6:121), they send it to them as a whisper, and His statement: And this Qur’an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches (al-An’am 6:19), he sent it to me by Gabriel, peace be upon him, bringing it to me from God, the Most High. As for revelation, it is what happens from the one who reveals to the one to whom it is revealed. That is why the Arabs called writing and writing revelation, because it happens in what is written and is fixed in it, as Ka’b ibn Zuhair said: The Persians and the horizons came from him poems that remained as the revelation remains in the deaf stone It means: the book fixed in stone.

And from this it is said in the book in particular, if the writer wrote it: revelation without an alif, and from this is the saying of Ru’bah: As if after the winds that hit him and the thorns of the darkness are making him stumble Miniature Gospel of the Incarnate Lords Abu Jaʿfar said: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
And you were not with them

, is that you were not, O Muhammad, with them, so you know what we teach you of their report that you did not witness, but you only know that and you attain knowledge of it, by our informing you of it. The meaning of his saying: with them is with them. The meaning of his saying:
h
When they throw
, is
h
when they throw
their pens. As for their pens, they are their arrows that the children of Israel drew from the casters for Mary’s guardianship, as we explained before in His statement:
h
And Zechariah was her guardian
. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham bin Amr told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were not with them
, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said,
m: Abu Asim told Surat Al Imran 3:44 This is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad].
h
And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary
. Nor were you with them when they disputed. us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
They cast their pens
, Zakariya and his companions, they cast lots with their pens for Mary when she entered upon them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary

, nor were you with them when they disputed, Mary was the daughter of their leader and master, and the Children of Israel quarrelled over her, so they drew lots with their arrows as to which of them should be responsible for her, and the one who drew lots was Zakariya, who was her sister’s husband, so Zakariya took her under his care, meaning: he took her into his care.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They cast their pens
, he said: They drew lots for Mary, as to which of them would take charge of her, and Zachariah drew lots for them.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary

, and that when Mary was born in the mosque, the people of the place of prayer drew lots for her while they were writing the revelation, so they drew lots with their pens as to which of them should be responsible for her, so God Almighty said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary
, nor were you with them when they disputed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: When they cast lots with their pens as to which of them would be responsible for Mary, they cast lots with their pens as to which of them would be responsible for Mary, and Zakariya drew lots.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were not with them when they cast their pens

, he said: When they cast lots for Mary, and it was hidden from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when God informed him. It was said: Which of them will be responsible for Mary because the casting of lots by the lottery of Mary was only to see which of them was more deserving of her responsibility and more entitled. So in the Almighty’s saying: When they cast their lots, there is an indication of something omitted from the statement, which is: to see which of them will be responsible, and to make that clear and know. If someone thought that the accusative case of which one is required, since that is its meaning, then he thought wrong. This is because looking, investigating, and knowing with which one requires questioning and inquiry, and the share of which one in inquiry is the beginning and the length of the work of the question and inquiry about it. This is because the meaning of the speaker’s saying: I will see which one of them stood up, is that I will inquire of the al-Nas 114:Which one of them stood up. And similarly their saying: I will know. We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of guarantees is dammah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this context.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And you, O Muhammad, were not with the people of Mary, when they disputed over her, as to which of them had more right to her and more deserving of her. This is from God, the Almighty, and even if it was addressed to His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, it is a rebuke from Him, the Almighty, to those who denied him from among the People of the Book.
He says: How can the disbelievers doubt you among them when you inform them of this report and you did not witness it,
h
and you were not with them
on the day they did these things, and you are not one of those who read the books and knew their report, nor sat with their people and heard their report? as:

c: Ibn Samid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
And you were not with them

when they disputed, meaning you were not with them when they disputed about it. He informed him of the hidden knowledge that they had concealed from him, in order to confirm his prophethood and to be an argument against them for what he would bring them of what they had concealed from him.

x: What He meant by His statement, may His praise be exalted:
h
When the angels said
, and you were not with them when they were disputing, and you were not with them either
h
when the angels said
: O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings. And evangelism is telling someone good report. His saying:
h
With a word from Him

, meaning with a message from God and report from Him, and it is from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so conveyed to me a word that pleased me, meaning: He told me report that made me happy, as God Almighty said:
And His word which He conveyed to Mary
meaning: God conveyed the good report to Mary about Jesus, He conveyed it to her. The interpretation of the words: And you, O Muhammad, were not with the people
h
when the angels said
to Maryam 19:O Mary, God gives you good tidings from Him, which is a child for you whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary.
Some people said - and this is the saying of Qatada - that the word that God Almighty said: By a word from Him, is His saying: Be.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us that, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us that, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
With a word from Him

, he said: His statement: Be. God Almighty called it His Word, because it was from His Word, just as it is said when God decrees something: This is God’s decree and judgment, meaning: This happened from God’s decree and judgment. And as He, the Most High, said: And the command of God is to be done (An-Nisa’: 47 - al-Ahzab 33:37), meaning: what God commanded, and it is the commanded thing that was from God Almighty’s command.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a name for Jesus, which God called him by, just as He called the rest of His creation by whatever names He wished.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: may God be pleased with him, that he said: The word is Jesus.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When the angels said
, ‘O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him,’ he said: Jesus is the word from God.

x: The first opinion is closest to the truth, in my opinion. It is that the angels gave Mary the good report of Jesus from God Almighty, through His message and His word that He commanded her to convey to her: that God will create from her a son without a husband or a stallion. Therefore, God Almighty said:
h
His name is the Messiah

, so He mentioned it and did not say: her name, so it is feminine. The word is feminine, because the word is not intended to mean the name that means so-and-so, but rather it means the good report, so its euphemism was mentioned just as the euphemism for offspring, beast, and titles is mentioned, as we have explained before in what has passed. So, as we said earlier, he interpreted that as meaning: God gives you good report, then he explained that the good report is a child named the Messiah.
Some of the grammarians of Basra have claimed that he mentioned it and said:
h
His name is the Messiah

, and he said: By a word from Him, and the word, according to him, is Jesus, because it is in the same meaning, as the Most High said: That a soul should say, ‘Oh, how I regret it!’ (al-Zumar 39:56), then he said: Yes, My signs have come to you, but you denied them! (al-Zumar 39:59), and as it is said: Dhu al-Thadiyah, because his hand was short and close to his breasts, so he made it as if its name was a breast, and if it were not for that, the ha’ would not have been included in the diminutive. Some grammarians of Kufa said something similar to what we mentioned from the grammarians of Basra: that the ha’ is from the mention of the word, and he disagreed with him on the meaning for which he mentioned his saying: His name, and the word came before it. So he claimed that he only preceded: His name, and the word came before it, and he did not say: its name, because it is the custom of the Arabs to do that with descriptions, titles, and names that are not used to define the named, like so-and-so and so-and-so, and that, like the offspring and the caliph and the beast, and for that reason it was permissible for him to say: good offspring and good offspring, and it was not permissible to say: Talhah came - and Mughirah stood.

Some of them denied the weakness of those who made the weakness in that with the word dhi al-thadiyah, and they said: The ha was inserted in dhi al-thadiyah because what was meant by that was a piece of the breast, just as it was said: We were in meat and wine, meaning a piece of it. This statement is similar to what we said about that. As for his saying,
h
His name is the Messiah

, Jesus, son of Mary, He, may His praise be glorified, informed His servants about the lineage of Jesus, and that he is the son of his mother Mary, and with that He denied what the atheists in God, may His praise be glorified, among the Christians, added to him, of their attributing his sonship to God Almighty, and what his mother, who was slandered by the Jews, was accused of, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told me that Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
When the angels said
, ‘O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, held in high esteem in this world and the Hereafter
h
and among those brought near

.’” That is, this is how his affair was, not what they say about him. As for the Messiah, it is a passive participle that was changed from mafool to fa’il, and it is anointed, meaning: God anointed him and purified him from sins. That is why Abraham said: the Messiah is the truthful one.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: He wiped with the blessing.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, he said, Saeed said:
m: He was called the Messiah because he was anointed with blessing.

x: He means by his saying: honorable, one who has a high status and position with God, and honor and dignity. From this, the man who is honored and respected by kings and people is called honorable. It is said from it: So-and-so was not honorable, but he was honorable and respected, and he has a high status with the sultan, and prestige is reversed, its waw was moved from the beginning to the place of the ayn in it, so it was said: prestige, but it is actually a face, and a verb from prestige is prestige, he will meet me with something greater than this. It is heard from the Arabs: I fear that he will meet me with something greater than this, meaning: that he will meet me in the face with something greater than this. As for the accusative case of al-Wajeeh, it is based on the separation from Isa, because Isa is definite, and Wajeeh is indefinite, and it is from his description.

If it were lowered in response to the word, it would be permissible. And what we said - that the interpretation of that is: respected in this world and the hereafter with God - Muhammad bin Jaʿfar said, as far as we have been informed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: A respected person, he said: A respected person in this world and the hereafter with God. As for his saying:
h
And among those brought near
, it means that he is among those whom God will bring near on the Day of Resurrection, so He will make him dwell in His vicinity and bring him close to Him, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among those brought near
, meaning: among those brought near to God on the Day of Resurrection.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hassan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
And among those brought near
, meaning: among those brought near to God on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

x: As for his saying:
h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle
, its meaning is: God gives you good tidings of a word from Him whose name is the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, held in high esteem by God and speaking to the people in the cradle.

So, and he speaks, even though it is in the nominative case, because it is in the form of he does without any factors in it, it is in the accusative case, and it is similar to the poet’s saying: I will eat it with a severe bite, meaning in its markets and unjustly As for the cradle, it means the infant’s bed during breastfeeding, such as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle

, he said: the infant’s bed while he is breastfeeding. As for his saying: and an old man, it is: and he is mature, above the age of youth, and below old age. It is said of it: -an old man- and an old woman, as the rajaz poet said: I will not return after that, Kariya, practicing old age and youth What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult

, is that he will speak to the people as a child in the cradle, indicating the innocence of his mother from what the slanderers accused her of, and as proof for him of his prophethood, and as an adult after he has been exposed to the revelation of God that He reveals to him, and His commands and prohibitions, and what He sends down to him from His Book. God the Almighty informed His servant of this about the Messiah, and that it was thus, even though the majority of people speak of them as adults and elders, as an argument against those who say about him from the unbelievers in God, the false Christians, and that he was since He created him a newborn child, then an adult, changing in events, and changing with the passage of time and days, from childhood to adulthood, and from one state to another, and that if he was as the atheists said about him, that would not have been permissible for him. Thus, he belied what the delegation from the people of Najran said, who argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about him, and he argued with them about his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed them that he was like all the children of Adam, except for the honor that God distinguished him with from them, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult

, and he will be among the righteous. He will inform them of the states in which he will change during his life, just as the children of Adam change during their lives, young and old, except that God singled him out with speech in his cradle as a sign of his prophethood and to make known to the servants the locations of His power.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle
and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous, meaning: He will speak to them when they are young and old.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult
, he said: He will speak to them as a child and as an adult.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And an old man
h
and among the righteous
, he said: The old man is the forbearing.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: He spoke to them, young and old, and the elderly. Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid said: The elderly person is the forbearing one.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult
, he said: He spoke to them in the cradle as a child, and he spoke to them as an adult.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying: and an old man is that he will speak to them when he appears.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard him - meaning Ibn Zayd - say regarding His statement:
h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult

, he said: Jesus spoke to them in the cradle, and he will speak to them when he kills the Antichrist, and he will be an adult at that time. And the word and an old man is in apposition to the word and he speaks to people. As for his saying:
h
And among the righteous
, he means: among their number and their friends, because the righteous are from one another in religion and virtue. Surat Al Imran 3:46
h
And he will speak to the people in the cradle
and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He meant that Mary said - when the angels said to her, God gives you good tidings of a word from Him: My Lord, how can I have a child? From what perspective can I have a child? From a husband whom I may marry and a husband whom I may marry, or do you begin to create him without a husband or a male partner, and without a man touching me? So God said to her: Thus does God create what He wills, meaning: Thus does God create from you a child for you without touching a male partner, and He makes him a sign and a lesson for the people, for He creates what He wills and does what He wills, so He gives a child to whomever He wills without a male partner or with a male partner, and He forbids that to whomever He wills of women, even if she has a husband, because it is not difficult for Him to create something that He wants to create, rather it is that He commands when He wants something what He wants [to create], and He says to it: Be, and it is, whatever He wills, from what He wills, and however He wills, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: She said, ‘My Lord, how will I have a son when no man has touched me?’ He said, ‘Thus does God create what He wills.’ He does what He wills, and creates what He wills, whether human or non-human. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ from whatever He wills and however He wills, and it is, whatever He wills.

x: The readings differed in the reading of that. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Medina and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as: And He teaches him with a ya, in response to his saying: Thus does God create what He wills and And He teaches him the Book. So they attached the report of his saying: And He teaches him to the same report of his saying: He creates what He wills and his saying: Then He only says to it, ‘Be’ and it is. The majority of the Kufians and some of the Basrans read it:
h
And We teach him
with a nun, as a continuation of his statement: We reveal it to you, as if he said: That is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you
r
(Al Imran 3:144)
, and He teaches him the Book, and they said: What comes after We reveal it is in its connection to His statement: Be, and it is, then he connected it with his statement:
h
And We teach him
, to it.

The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is that they are two different readings, but not different meanings. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in that, because the meaning of the two readings is the same, in that it is report from God that He taught Jesus the Book, and what was mentioned was that He taught him. This is the beginning of the report from God Almighty to Mary about what He will do with the child that He gave her the good report of in terms of honor, high status, and virtue. He said: Thus God will create from you a child without a male or a husband, and He will teach him the Book, which is the script that he writes with his own hand, and wisdom, which is the Sunnah that We reveal to him in other than a book, and the Torah, which is the Torah that was revealed to Moses, and it was among them from the time of Moses, and the Gospel, the Gospel of Jesus, and it was not before him, but God informed Mary before the creation of Jesus that He would reveal it to him.

He informed her of that and named it for her, because she had known in what was revealed of the books that God would send a prophet to whom a book called the Gospel would be revealed. So God Almighty informed her that that prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose description she had heard, and whom He had promised His prophets before that He would send down to him the book called the Gospel, was the child whom He had given her and given her the good report of.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: And we teach him the Book, he said: In his hand.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We taught him the Book and wisdom, he said: Wisdom is the Sunnah.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We taught him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel
, he said: Wisdom is the Sunnah, and the Torah and the Gospel, he said: Jesus used to read the Torah and the Gospel.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And We will teach him the Book and wisdom. He said: Wisdom is the Sunnah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr, he said:
m: He informed her - meaning God informed Mary - what He intended by it, so He said: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah, which had been with them since the time of Moses, and the Gospel, another book that He brought to him, the knowledge of which they did not have, except that He mentioned that it had been from the prophets before him.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Medina and some of the reciters of Kufa read it as: And He teaches him with a ya, in response to his saying: Thus does God create what He wills and And He teaches him the Book.

The majority of the Kufians and some of the Basrans read it: And We teach him with a nun, as a continuation of his statement: We reveal it to you, as if he said: That is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you (Al Imran 3:144), and He teaches him the Book, and they said: What comes after We reveal it is in its connection to His statement: Be, and it is, then he connected it with his statement: And We teach him, to it.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement regarding this, according to us, is that they are two different readings, but not different meanings.

So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in that, because the meaning of the two readings is the same, in that it is report from God that He taught Jesus the Book, and what was mentioned was that He taught him.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And a Messenger
, is that We will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel.

i: So He left out mentioning And we will make him because the speech indicates it, as the poet said:
x: I saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear.
And his saying:
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
, meaning: And we make him a messenger to the Children of Israel, that he is my prophet, my bearer of good tidings, and my warner, and my proof of my truthfulness in that:
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
, meaning: with a sign from your Lord that fulfills my words, and verifies my report that I am a messenger from your Lord to you, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And a messenger to the Children of Israel, ‘Indeed,
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
,’ meaning: he confirms my prophethood with it, that I am a messenger from Him to you.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And a messenger to the Children of Israel, ‘Indeed,
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
.’ Then he explained what the sign is, saying: Indeed, I will create for you. The interpretation of the words: And a messenger to the Children of Israel, saying,
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
, that
h
I create for you from clay
