something like the form of a bird. Bird is the plural of bird. There are different readings of this.
Some of the people of Hijaz read it: Like the form of a bird, so I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, in the sense of monotheism.
Others read it as: Like the form of a bird, so I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, with both of them being interchangeable.

The reading that I like the most in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: Like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, with both of them being in agreement, because that was one of the characteristics of Jesus, that he would do that with the permission of God, and that it was in accordance with the script of the Mushaf. Following the script of the Mushaf while the meaning is correct and the reading is widespread in it, is more in agreement with me than contradicting the Mushaf. The creation of Jesus was not like the creation of birds, as: Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Ibn Ishaq narrated: Jesus, peace be upon him, sat one day with some young men of the scribes. He took some clay and said: Shall I make a bird out of this clay? They said: Can you do that? He said: Yes! By the permission of my Lord. Then he prepared it, and when he had made it into the shape of a bird, he blew into it and said: Become a bird by the permission of God.

So it came out flying between his hands. The young men were happy with that and mentioned it to their teacher, who spread it among the people. It grew up and the Children of Israel became concerned about it, but when his mother feared for him, she carried him on her donkeys and fled with him. It was mentioned that when he wanted to create a bird from clay, he asked them: Which bird is the hardest to create?
They told him: The bat, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: regarding His statement:
h
I create for you from clay
, as it were, the figure of a bird. He said: Which bird is most difficult to create? They said: The bat, for it is only flesh. He said: So he did.

x: If someone says: How is it said: Then I will breathe into it, when it has been said: I will create for you from clay something like the form of a bird? It was said: Because the meaning of the statement is: Then blow into the bird. If it were: Then blow into it, it would be correct and permissible, as he said in al-Ma’idah 5:Then blow into it (al-Ma’idah 5:110): He means: Then blow into the form. It was mentioned that this is in one of the two readings, then blow into it, without in. The Arabs may do the same and say: Many a night has I spent, and I spent it.

i: The poet said:
x: No pocket was torn, no one was mourning, no horses cried for you when you were plundered.

Meaning: May it not rise up against you, and as another said: One of the sons of Eid God continued to drink sweet juice until the trumpet was blown Abu Jaafar said: What he means by his saying: And I heal, is and I cure. It is said: God healed the sick person, if He cured him of it, so He heals him, and He healed the sick person, so he recovers, and it may also be said: The sick person was cured, so he recovers, two well-known languages.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of blind.
Some of them said: He is the one who does not see at night, but sees during the day.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I heal the blind
, he said: The blind is the one who sees during the day but does not see at night, so he is blind.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his example.

x: Others said: He is the blind man whose mother gave birth to him like that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: We were told that the blind is the one who was born blind and with his eyes closed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I heal the blind and the leper
, he said: We used to say that the blind is the one who is born blind, with his eyes closed. Al-Munjab narrated, he said:

c: Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The blind person is the one who is born blind.

x: Others said: Rather, he is the blind one.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And I heal the blind
, he is the blind.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: The blind man.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I heal the blind
, he said: The blind is the one who is blind.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Mansour, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I heal the blind
, he said: the blind.

x: Others said: He is Al-A'mash.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I heal the blind
, he said: Al-A’mash.

x: What is known among the Arabs as the meaning of kamah is blindness. It is said: Kamahat aynah his eye became blind, and Akamahtahu ana I blinded it, as Suwaid ibn Abi Kahl said: His eyes became white and he was cursing himself when he removed them. And from it is the saying of Ru’bah: I went crazy, so he turned back like a blind man in the confusion of a confused, stuttering person.

c: God Almighty informed us
m: about Jesus, peace be upon him, that he would say that to the Children of Israel, as evidence from him with these lessons and signs for them regarding his prophethood. That is because: leprosy and blindness have no cure, and a doctor can cure them with treatment. So that was one of his proofs of the truth of his saying:
h
He is a Messenger of God
, because it is one of the miracles, along with the other signs that God gave him as Surat Al Imran 3:49 And a messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying], Indeed,
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
, in that I design for you out of clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by permission of God.
h
And I heal the blind and the leper
, and I bring the dead to life by permission of God.
h
And I inform you of what you eat

and what you store In your homes. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers. evidence of his prophethood. As for what Ikrimah said, that blindness is the blindness, and what Mujahid said, that it is poor eyesight at night, they are meaningless. Because God does not provide an argument to His creation that would allow them to oppose Him. If one of the arguments Jesus provided to the Children of Israel regarding his prophethood was that he acquitted the blind man, or the one who sees during the day but does not see at night, they would have been able to oppose him by saying: What is your argument in this, when there are people among us who treat that, and they are not prophets or messengers of God? This is evidence of the correctness of what we have said, that the blind is the blind person who does not see anything, neither at night nor during the day. And what Qatada said - that he was born like that - is more similar, because no human being can claim a cure for such a thing, except for the one to whom God has given what He gave to Jesus, and likewise the cure for the leper.

x: Jesus revived the dead by supplicating to God.
He supplicated for them, and God answered him, as:

c: Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar told me, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me:
m: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Jesus was twelve years old, God revealed to his mother, who was in the land of Egypt, and she had fled from her people when she gave birth to him to the land of Egypt: Take him up to Syria. So she did what she was commanded to do. She remained in Syria until he was thirty years old, and his prophethood lasted three years, then God raised him up to Him. Wahb claimed that fifty thousand sick people would gather around Jesus in a single group. Whoever was able to reach him would reach him, and whoever was not able to reach him, Jesus would come to him walking, and he would only treat them by calling upon God. As for his saying:
h
And I inform you of what you eat
, he means:
h
And I inform you of what you eat

, of what I did not see or witness with you at the time you ate it, and what you store, meaning by that: And what you raise and hide and do not eat. He teaches them that among his proofs of his prophethood, along with the miracles that he informed them that he would bring, is proof of his prophethood and his truthfulness in his report that God sent him to them: the creation of birds from clay, the healing of the blind and the leper, and the revival of the dead by God’s permission, which no human being can bear, except for whom God has given that as knowledge for him of his truthfulness, and a sign for him of the truth of his words, from among his prophets and messengers and whomever he loves of his creation, his informing of the unseen, which no human being whose way is his way can attain.

x: If someone were to say: What was the proof for his truthfulness in his saying to them:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses

, when we have seen the astrologer and the fortune teller often tell that and get it right? It was said: The astrologer and the fortune-teller are known to those who inform them of that, that they inform of the extraction of it through some of the causes leading to its knowledge. This was not the case with Jesus, peace be upon him, and the rest of the prophets and messengers of God. Rather, Jesus informed of it without extraction, nor seeking to know it by trickery, but rather by God informing him of it, without a previous origin that he followed, or built upon, or resorted to, as the astrologer resorts to his calculation, and the fortune-teller to his vision.
So this is the distinction between the knowledge of the prophets of the unseen and their informing of it, and the knowledge of the rest of those who lie about God, or claim knowledge of that, as:

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: When Jesus reached the age of nine or ten or thereabouts, his mother enrolled him in school, as they claim. He was with a schoolmaster who taught him as he taught boys. He would not go and teach him anything that boys were taught except that he would rush to his knowledge before he taught it to him. He would say: Are you not amazed at the son of this widow? I would not go and teach him anything except that I would find him more knowledgeable about it than I am!!

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When Jesus grew up, his mother sent him to learn the Torah, so he would play with the boys, the boys of the village in which he was, and he would tell the boys what their fathers did.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Salim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses
, he said: Jesus, son of Mary, when he was in the book, was informing them of what they eat in their houses and what they store.

c: Al-Qasim Qan narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, Ismail bin Salim narrated to us,
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses
. He said: Jesus, son of Mary, used to say to the boy in the book: O so-and-so, your family has hidden such-and-such food for you, so will you feed me from it?

x: This is how the prophets acted and their arguments. They only came with the arguments they came with in a way that could be reached by some tricks, not in the way that others came with, but rather in a way that the creation knows that it cannot be reached from that way by a trick except from God. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement:
h
And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your homes
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses
, he said: What you ate last night, and what you hid of it. Jesus, son of Mary, says it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said - meaning his statement:
h
And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses
, he said: The food and the thing they store in their houses, unseen, God taught him about it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses
, he said: What you eat, what you ate last night of food, and what you hid of it.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: He - meaning Jesus, son of Mary - used to tell the boys while he was with them in the Book what their fathers did, what they raised for them, and what they ate. He would say to the boy: Go, your family raised for you such and such, and they eat such and such. So the boy would go and cry to his family until they gave him that thing. They would say to him: Who told you this? He would say: Jesus! So that is the saying of God, the Almighty:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses

. So they kept their boys away from him, and said: Do not play with this magician! So they gathered them in a house, and Jesus came looking for them, and they said: They are not here. He said: What is in this house? They said: Pigs. Jesus said: That is how they are! So they opened the door for them, and behold, they were pigs. So that is the saying of God, the Almighty: On the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary (al-Ma’idah 5:78).

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what you store in your houses
, he said: What you hide for fear that the one who holds it will fail to do so.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying:
h
And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your homes
, is what you eat from the table that is sent down to you, and what you store from it.
Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses

. When the people asked for a table, it was a table on which fruit from Paradise would be brought down wherever they were. So the people were commanded not to betray themselves in it, nor to hide it, nor to store it for the next day, as a trial with which God tested them. So whenever they did something of that, Jesus, son of Mary, would inform them of it, saying:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store

, he said: I will inform you of what you eat from the table and what you store from it. He said: So when the command was revealed to them in the table, they were to eat and not store, so they stored and betrayed, and they were made into pigs when they stored and betrayed, so that is what His statement is: But whoever among you disbelieves thereafter - then I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone in the worlds (al-Ma’idah 5:115). Ibn Yahya said, Abd al-Razzaq said, Muammar said, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Khalas ibn Amr, on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir, that. The root of the verb is yadhkharoon, which is derived from the verb yaftaʿalun, which is derived from the saying of the speaker: dhakhrit al-shayʿ with the letter dhal, so I am idhkharoo. Then it was said: yadhkhar, as it was said: yadhkur from: dhakr al-shayʿ, meaning yadhtakhr. When the dhal and the taʿ came together, and they are close in articulation, it became difficult for the tongue to pronounce them, so one of them was assimilated into the other, and they became a double dal, which they made equal between the dhal and the taʿ. Some Arabs prefer the dhal over the taʿ, so they assimilate the taʿ into the dhal, and say: wa ma tadhkharoon, which is madhkhar laka, and it is masculine. The language in which the reading is done is the first, which is the assimilation of the dhal into the ta’, and their replacement with a double dal. It is not permissible to read in any other language, because it is evident that it was transmitted from the reading in it, and it is the Judi language, as Zuhair said: The generous one who gives you his bounty pardoning you, and sometimes wrongs you and oppresses you. It is narrated with the letter ḍād, meaning: it is performed from injustice, and it is also narrated with the letter ṭā.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Indeed, in My creation from clay of birds by the permission of God, and in My healing of the blind and the leper, and My bringing the dead back to life, and My informing you of what you eat and what you store in your homes, beginning without calculation or astrology, or divination or fortune-telling, as a lesson for you and for reflection, so that you may reflect on that and consider that I am truthful in what I say to you: Surat Al Imran 3:49 And a messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying], Indeed,
h
I have come to you with a sign from your Lord
, in that I design for you out of clay [that which is] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by permission of God.
h
And I heal the blind and the leper
, and I bring the dead to life by permission of God.
h
And I inform you of what you eat
and what you store In your homes.

Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers. I am a messenger from your Lord to you, and you know by it that I am truthful in what I call you to of God’s commands and prohibitions, if you are believers, meaning: If you believe in God’s proofs and signs, and acknowledge His Oneness, and in His Prophet Moses and the Torah that He brought to you.

evidence.text: Some of the people of Hijaz read it: Like the form of a bird, so I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, in the sense of monotheism.
Others read it as: Like the form of a bird, so I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, with both of them being interchangeable.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that I like the most in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: Like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird, with both of them being in agreement, because that was one of the characteristics of Jesus, that he would do that with the permission of God, and that it was in accordance with the script of the Mushaf.
Following the script of the Mushaf while the meaning is correct and the reading is widespread in it, is more in agreement with me than contradicting the Mushaf.
It was mentioned that this is in one of the two readings, then blow into it, without in.
The language in which the reading is done is the first, which is the assimilation of the dhal into the ta’, and their replacement with a double dal.

It is not permissible to read in any other language, because it is evident that it was transmitted from the reading in it, and it is the Judi language, as Zuhair said: The generous one who gives you his bounty pardoning you, and sometimes wrongs you and oppresses you.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord,
h
and I have come to you

confirming what came before me of the Torah, and for that reason He put confirming in the accusative case as a state of I have come to you. What indicates that it is in the accusative case, based on his statement:
h
And I have come to you

, without being in apposition to his statement: honorable, is his statement: for what is before me of the Torah. If it were in apposition to his statement: honorable, the statement would have been: and confirming what is before it of the Torah,
h
and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you

. It was said: And confirming what came before me of the Torah, because Jesus, peace be upon him, believed in the Torah and acknowledged it, and that it was from God. And so were all the prophets, they believed in all that came before them of the books of God and His messengers, even if some of their laws differed, due to God’s contradiction between them in that.

Although Jesus was - as far as we have been informed - acting according to the Torah and did not contradict any of its rulings, except what God made light for its people in the Gospel, of what was severe for them in it, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Muqam told me:
m: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: Jesus was following the law of Moses, peace be upon them both, and he used to sabbath and face Jerusalem. So he said to the Children of Israel: I did not call you to a letter contrary to what is in the Torah, except to make permissible for you some of what was forbidden to you, and to remove from you some of the burdens.

c: Bishr told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And confirming what came before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you
, what Jesus brought was softer than what Moses brought, and what Moses brought had been forbidden to them the meat of camels and otters, and some birds and whales.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And confirming what came before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you

, he said: What Jesus brought was softer than what Moses brought. He said: And what was forbidden to them in what Moses brought of the Torah was the meat of camels and goats, but he made it lawful for them through the tongue of Jesus - and fats were forbidden to them, but were made lawful for them in what Jesus brought - and some fish, and some birds that do not have a tail, and some things that he had forbidden to them and made it very difficult for them, so Jesus came to them with a lightening of it in the Gospel. So what Jesus brought was softer than what Moses brought, may God’s prayers be upon him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you
, he said: camel meat and fat. When Jesus was sent, he made them lawful for them, and he sent to the Jews, but they differed and dispersed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And confirming what was before me of the Torah, meaning: what preceded me from it -
h
and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you
, meaning: He informed you that it was forbidden to you, but you abandoned it, then He made it lawful for you as an relief for you, so you attain its ease, and are released from its consequences.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you
, he said: He had forbidden them some things, then Jesus came to them to make lawful for them what was forbidden to them, seeking thereby their thanks.

x: He means by that: I have come to you with an argument and a lesson from your Lord, by which you will know the truth of what I am saying to you, such as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And I have come to you
with a sign from your Lord, he said: What Isa explained to them of all things, and what his Lord gave him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And I have come to you
with a sign from your Lord, what Jesus explained to them of all things. What he means by his saying: from your Lord is from your Lord.

x: What he means by that is: I have come to you with a sign from your Lord by which you will know with certainty my truthfulness in what I say. So fear God, O children of Israel, in what He has commanded you to do and forbidden you to do in His Book which He sent down to Moses. So fulfill the covenant which you made with Him in it, and obey, in what I have called you to do of believing in what my Lord and your Lord has sent me with to you. So worship Him, for He has sent me to you with that, and with making lawful some of what was forbidden to you in your Book. And that is the straight path and the firm guidance in which there is no crookedness.

as: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: “So fear God and obey me. Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord,” disavowing what they say about him - meaning: what the Christians say about him - and arguing for his Lord against them, “So worship Him. This is a straight path,” meaning: this is what I have led you to and brought to you.

There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. The majority of the reciters of the regions read: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him, with a kasra on the alif of in as the beginning of the report.

Some of them read: That God is my Lord and your Lord, with the opening of the alif of that, with the interpretation: And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that God is my Lord and your Lord, by rejecting that for the sign, and replacing it with it.

The correct reading according to us is what the regions read, which is to break the alif of in at the beginning, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings on the correctness of that. And what they agree upon is proof, and what the one who is separate from them does not do is an opinion, and an opinion cannot be used to object to proof. Although this verse appears to be a report, it contains the conclusive proof from God to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the delegation from Najran who argued with him, by God Almighty informing us that Jesus was innocent of what was attributed to him of his attribution to someone other than what he described himself with, that he was a servant of God like all of His servants on earth, except for what God Almighty had singled him out with of prophethood and the proofs that He gave him as evidence of his truthfulness - just as He gave all of the messengers other than him of signs and proofs of their truthfulness - and as evidence of his prophethood.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him.
The majority of the reciters of the regions read: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him, with a kasra on the alif of in as the beginning of the report.

Abu Jaafar said: The correct reading according to us is what the regions read, which is to break the alif of in at the beginning, due to the consensus of the proof from the readings on the correctness of that.

x: What he meant by the words of God Almighty: When Jesus perceived disbelief on their part, is that when Jesus found disbelief on their part. Sensation is existence, and from it God Almighty said:
Do you sense any of them?

i: As for the sense, without an alif, it means annihilation and killing, and from it is His saying: When you were killing them by His permission
r
(Al Imran 3:152)
Sense also means compassion and tenderness, and from it is the saying of Al-Kumait:
x: Does he who weeps for the house hope that it will feel for him, or does he weep for the house with the green water of tears?

He means by his saying: that you feel for him, that you feel compassion for him. The interpretation of the statement: When Jesus found - from the Children of Israel to whom God sent him - denial of his prophethood, rejection of his words, and turning away from what he called them to of God’s command, he said:
h
Who are my supporters to God

? Meaning by that: Jesus said: Who are my supporters against those who deny God’s proof, turn away from His religion, and deny the prophethood of His Prophet, to God Abd al-Razzaq, may He be glorified? What he means by his saying: to God is with God. It is good to say: to God, meaning: with God, because it is the custom of the Arabs that when they join something to something else, then they want to report on them by joining one of them to the other if it is joined to it, they sometimes replace with with to, and sometimes you report on them with with, so you say: The herd to the herd is camels, meaning: if you join the herd to the herd, they become camels.

But if the thing is with the thing, they do not say it Ibn Bashar-to, and they do not replace with with to. It is not permissible to say: So-and-so came and he has money, meaning: and with him is money. And just as we said in the interpretation of his saying:
h
Who are my supporters to God
?, a group of people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Who are my supporters for God
? He means: with God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: From my supporters to God, he says: with God. As for the reason why Jesus, peace be upon him, sought help from those of the disciples who sought help, there is a difference of opinion among scholars about this.

x: Some of them said: The reason for that was:

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When God sent Jesus and commanded him to call people to Islam, the Children of Israel banished him and expelled him. So he and his mother went out to travel the earth. He stayed in a village with a man, and he hosted them and treated them well. There was a tyrannical and aggressive king in that city. One day that man came, and he was worried and sad. He entered his house and Mary was with his wife. Mary said to her: What is the matter with your husband? I see that he is sad! She said: Do not ask! She said: Tell me! Perhaps God will relieve his distress! She said: We have a king who appoints a day for each man among us, during which he feeds him and his soldiers and gives them wine to drink. If he does not do so, he will punish him. His turn has come on the day he wants us to make for him, and we do not have the time for that! She said: Then tell him not to worry, for I will command my son to supplicate for him, and that will suffice. Mary said to Jesus about that. Jesus said: O mother, if I do that, it will be bad. She said: Do not worry, for he has been good to us and honored us! Jesus said: Then tell him: When that is near, fill your pots and jars with water, then inform me. He said: When he filled them, he informed him. So he called upon God, and what was in the pots was transformed into meat, broth, and bread, and what was in the jars into wine, the likes of which people had never seen before, and it was food. When the king came, he ate. When he drank the wine, he asked: Where is this wine from? He said to him: It is from such and such a land. The king said: My wine was brought from that land, so it is not like this one! He said: It is from another land. When he confused the matter with the king, he became angry and said: I will tell you, I have a young boy who does not ask God for anything except that He gives it to him, and he called upon God, and He turned the water into wine. The king said, and he had a son whom he wanted to appoint as his successor, but he died a few days before that, and he was the most beloved of creation to him, so he said: A man prayed to God until He turned water into wine, so that He would answer his prayer and revive my son! So he called Jesus and spoke to him, and asked him to pray to God to revive his son, so Jesus said: Do not do that, for if he lives it will be evil. The king said: I do not care, do I not see him? I do not care what happens. Jesus, peace be upon him, said: If I revive him, will you let me and my mother go wherever we want? The king said: Yes. So he prayed to God and the boy lived. When the people of his kingdom saw that he had lived, they called out with weapons and said: We ate this, and when his death approached, he wants to appoint his son as his successor, so he can eat us as his father ate!! So they fought, and Jesus and his mother went, and a Jew accompanied them. The Jew had two loaves of bread, and Jesus had one loaf of bread, so Jesus said to him: Share with me. The Jew said: Yes. When he saw that Jesus had only one loaf of bread, he regretted it. When they slept, the Jew wanted to eat the loaf. When he had eaten a bite, Jesus said to him: What are you doing? He said: Nothing! So he threw it away, until he had finished the whole loaf. When morning came, Jesus said to him: Bring your food! So he brought a loaf of bread. Jesus said to him: Where is the other loaf? He said: I only had one. Jesus kept quiet about him. They set off and passed by a shepherd. Jesus called out: O shepherd, slaughter a sheep from your flock for us. He said: Yes, send your companion to get it. Jesus sent the Jew, and he brought the sheep. They slaughtered it and roasted it. Then he said to the Jew: Eat, but do not break a bone. So they ate. When they were full, Jesus threw the bones into the skin, then struck it with his staff and said: Get up, by God’s permission! The sheep bleated. He said: O shepherd, take your sheep. The shepherd said to him: Who are you? He said: I am Jesus, son of Mary. He said: You are the magician! And run away from him. Jesus said to the Jew: By Him who revived this sheep after we ate it, how many loaves of bread did you have with you? He swore that he only had one loaf of bread. They passed by a cow owner, and Jesus called out and said: O cow owner, slaughter a calf from your cow for us. He said: Send your companion to get it. The Jew said: Go, Jew, and bring it. So he went and brought it. He slaughtered it and roasted it while the cow owner was watching. Jesus said to him: Eat, but do not break a bone. When they had finished, he threw the bones into the hide and struck it with his staff and said: Get up, by God’s permission. It got up lowing. He said: Take your calf. The Jew said: Who are you? He said: I am Jesus. He said: You are the magician! Then run away from him. The Jew said: O Jesus, you revived it after we ate it! Jesus said: By Him who revived the sheep after we ate it, and the calf after we ate it, how many loaves of bread did you have with you? He swore by God that he had only one loaf of bread with him. So they set out until they reached a village. The Jew settled at the top of it and Jesus at the bottom. The Jew took a staff like Jesus’ staff and said, I now raise the dead! Now the king of that city was very ill. The Jew went out calling, Who wants a doctor? Until he came to the king of that village and was informed of his illness. The Jew said, “Bring me in to him, and I will cure him. If you see that he is dead, I will revive him.” It was said to him, “The king’s illness has exhausted all doctors before you. There is no doctor who has treated him and his medicine has not been of any use except that he has been ordered to be crucified.” He said, Bring me in to him, and I will cure him. So he was brought in to him and he took hold of the king’s leg and struck him with his staff until he died. The Jew kept striking him with his staff while he was dead and saying, Rise, by God’s permission! So he was taken to be crucified. When Jesus was reached, he came to him while he was being raised on the cross and said, Tell me, if I revive your friend, will you leave me my friend? They said, Yes. Then God revived the angel for Jesus, so he stood up and brought down the Jew and said: O Jesus, you are the one who has bestowed the greatest favor upon me, and by God I will never leave you.

c: Jesus said - according to what Muhammad bin Al-Hussein bin Musa narrated to us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi - to the Jew:
m: I ask you by the One who revived the sheep and the calf after we ate them, and revived this one after it had died, and brought you down from the trunk after you were raised on it to be crucified, how many loaves of bread did you have with you? He said: So he swore by all of this that he had only one loaf of bread. He said: No problem! So they set off until they passed by a treasure that had been dug by wild beasts and animals. The Jew said: O Jesus, to whom does this money belong? Jesus said: Leave it, for he has people who would perish because of it. The Jew's soul began to yearn for the money, and he hated to disobey Jesus, so he set off with Jesus. Four men passed by with the money, and when they saw it, they gathered around it. Two of them said to their companions: Go and buy us food, drink, and animals to carry this money on. So the two men went and bought animals, food, and drink. One of them said to his companion: Would you like us to poison our companions in their food, so that when they eat they die, and the money will be between me and you? The other said: Yes! So they did. The other two said: When we bring the food, let each one go to his companion and kill him, and the food and animals will be between me and you. So when they brought their food, they went and killed them, then they sat down to the food and ate from it, and they died. Jesus was informed of that, so he said to the Jew: Bring it out so that we may divide it. So he brought it out, and Jesus divided it among three. The Jew said: O Jesus, fear God and do not wrong me, for it is only you and me!! What are these three? Jesus said to him: This is for me, this is for you, and this third is for the owner of the loaf. The Jew said: If I tell you about the owner of the loaf, will you give me this money? Jesus said: Yes. He said: I am he. Jesus said: Take my share and your share and the share of the owner of the loaf, for it is your share of this world and the hereafter. So when he carried it, he walked with it for a while, then the earth swallowed it up. Jesus, son of Mary, set out and passed by the disciples while they were fishing. He said: What are you doing? They said: We are fishing. He said: Why don’t you walk so that we may catch Surat Al Imran 3:52 So when Jesus perceived disbelief on their part, he said, "Who will be my helpers to Allah?"
h
The disciples said

, "We are the helpers of Allah. We have believed in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims." people? They said: Who are you? He said: I am Jesus, son of Mary. So they believed in him and set out with him. This is what God Almighty said: Who are my helpers for the sake of God?
h
The disciples said
: “We are helpers of God. We have believed in God, and bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission].”

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Mansur, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when Jesus perceived disbelief on their part
, he said, ‘Who will be my helpers for God?’ The verse means: He sought help, so the disciples helped him, and he prevailed over them.

x: Others said: The reason Jesus sought help from those who sought help was because those who sought help from the disciples against him wanted to kill him.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So when Jesus perceived disbelief on their part, he said: They disbelieved and wanted to kill him, and that was when his people sought help, “He said: Who will be my helpers for God?
h
The disciples said

: We are the helpers of God.” Ansar is the plural of Nasir, just as Ashraf is the plural of Sharif, and Ashhad is the plural of Shahid. As for the disciples, the people of interpretation differed about the reason for which they were called disciples.

x: Some of them said: They were called that because of the whiteness of their clothes.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me:
m: Among what my father narrated, he said: Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Maysarah, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: They were called the disciples because of the whiteness of their clothes.

x: Others said: They were called that because they were short people who used to whiten their clothes.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Abu Artah, he said:
m: The disciples are the washermen who transform the clothes, they wash them.

x: Others said: They are the elite and chosen ones of the prophets.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ruh bin Al-Qasim:
m: Qatada mentioned a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: He was one of the disciples. So he was asked: Who are the disciples? He said: Those for whom the caliphate is fit. Al-Munjab narrated, he said:

c: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When the disciples said
, he said: The chosen ones of the prophets.

x: The most similar of the statements we mentioned about the meaning of the disciples is the statement of the one who said: They were called that because of the whiteness of their clothes, and because they were washermen. This is because the houris among the Arabs are extremely white, and therefore the disciples of food were called hawari because of their intense whiteness, and from this the man with extremely white eyes was called ahwar, and the woman was called hawra. It may be possible that the disciples of Jesus were called by what we mentioned, because of their white clothes, and that they were short, so they were known for their companionship with Jesus, and his choosing them for himself as companions and supporters, so this name was given to them, and was used until every special man from his companions and supporters was called hawari, and therefore the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet has a disciple, and my disciple is Al-Zubayr.

Meaning his special one. The Arabs call women who live in villages and cities Hawariyyat, and they are called that because of the predominance of whiteness in them. An example of this is the saying of Abu Jalada Al-Yashkari: Tell the anecdotes to make others cry, but only barking dogs make us cry. What he means by his saying:
h
The disciples said
, is that those who were described as we mentioned, of their whitening their clothes, said: We believe in God, we believe in God, and you bear witness, O Jesus, that we are Muslims.

This is report from God Almighty that Islam is the religion with which He sent Jesus and the prophets before him, not Christianity or Judaism. It is God’s exoneration of Jesus from those who claimed Christianity and followed it, just as He exonerated Abraham from all religions other than Islam.
This is an argument from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the delegation of Najran, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: “And when Jesus perceived disbelief and aggression on their part, he said, ‘Who will be my helpers to God?’
h
The disciples said

, ‘We are the helpers of God. We have believed in God.’” This is what they said, by which they attained favor from their Lord, And bear witness that we are Muslims, not as these people who argue with you about it say - meaning the delegation of Christians from Najran.

x: This is report from God Almighty about the disciples that they said: Our Lord, we have believed, meaning: we have confirmed, in what You have revealed, meaning: in what You revealed to Your Prophet Jesus from Your Book, and we have followed the Messenger, meaning by that: we have become followers of Jesus in Your religion with which You sent him, and his helpers in the truth with which You sent him to Your servants. And His statement:
h
Then register us with the witnesses

, means: so establish our names with the names of those who have testified to the truth, and acknowledged Your monotheism, and believed in Your messengers, and followed Your commands and prohibitions, so include us among them and with them in what You honor them with of Your honor, and place us in their place, and do not include us among those who disbelieved in You, and turned away from Your path, and disobeyed Your commands and prohibitions.

By this, His creation, may He be glorified and exalted, knows the path of those whose words and actions He is pleased with, so that they may follow their path and approach, and attain the same degrees of His honor that they have attained. And by this He denies those who claim that the prophets of God were not of the same religion, and He uses it as evidence against the delegation who argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of Najran: that it was said that those of the followers of Jesus, may God be pleased with them, were different from what they said, and their approach was different from their approach, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses, meaning: This was their statement and their faith.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And the plotting of those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel, and they are those from whom God mentioned that Jesus sensed disbelief. Their plot, which God described them with, was to conspire with each other to attack and kill Jesus.
This was because Jesus, peace be upon him, after his people had expelled him and his mother from among them, returned to them, as follows:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Then Jesus walked with them, meaning: with the disciples who were fishing, and they believed in him and followed him when he called them, until he came to the Children of Israel at night, and he cried out to them, and that is what He said: So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved (al-Saff 61:14). As for God’s plot against them: according to what Al-Suddi mentioned, He cast the likeness of Jesus on some of his followers until the plotters killed him with Jesus, and they thought he was Jesus, and God Almighty had raised Jesus before that, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then the Children of Israel besieged Jesus and nineteen of the disciples in a house. Jesus said to his companions: Who will take my image so that he may be killed and have Paradise? So one of them took it and ascended with Jesus to heaven. This is what God says: And they planned, and God planned, and God is the best of planners. When the disciples came out, they saw them nineteen, so they told them that Jesus had ascended to heaven. They began to count the people and found that they were missing one man from the number, and they saw the image of Jesus among them, so they doubted him. Based on this, they killed the man, thinking that he was Jesus, and crucified him. This is what God, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared to them so
r
(An-Nisa’: 157)
. It may be possible that the meaning of God’s deception of them is His luring them so that the Book may reach its term, as we have explained in God’s statement: God mocks them (al-Baqarah 2:15).

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant:
h
And God’s plan

against the people who tried to kill Jesus, despite their disbelief in God and their denial of Jesus in what he brought them from their Lord, when God, may His praise be glorified, said: I will take you, so when is a conjunction of His saying:
h
And God’s plan
, meaning:
h
And God’s plan

against them when God said to Jesus: I will take you and raise you to Me, so He took him and raised him to Him. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of death that God Almighty mentioned in this verse.
Some of them said: It is the death of sleep, and the meaning of the statement according to their doctrine was: I am the one who puts you to sleep and raises you up in your sleep.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
I will cause you to die

, he said: He means the death of a dream, God raised him up in his dream. Al-Hasan said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Jews: Jesus did not die, and he will return to you before the Day of Resurrection.”

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: I will seize you from the earth and raise you up to Me. They said: The meaning of death is taking, just as one says: I took from so-and-so what I owed him, meaning: I took it and took it back. They said: The meaning of his statement:
h
I will take you and raise you up
, is: I will seize you from the earth alive to My side, and I will take you to what I have without death, and I will raise you up from among the polytheists and those who disbelieve in you.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, he said, Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Matar al-Warraq,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
I will cause you to die
, he said:
h
I will cause you to die
from this world, and it is not a death.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
I will cause you to die
, he said:
h
I will cause you to die
from the earth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve, he said: So He raised him to Himself, He will take him to Himself and purify him from those who disbelieve.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me: Kaab Al-Ahbar said:
m: God Almighty would not kill Jesus, son of Mary. Rather, God sent him as a caller and a bearer of good tidings, calling to Him alone. When Jesus saw how few followed him and how many denied him, he complained about that to God Almighty. So God revealed to him:
h
I will take you and raise you up
to Me, and no one I raise up is dead. I will send you to the one-eyed Antichrist and you will kill him. Then you will live after that for twenty-four years, then
h
I will cause you to die

the death of a living person. Kaab Al-Ahbar said: This confirms the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where he said: How can a nation perish when I am at the beginning and Jesus is at the end?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: O Jesus, I will take you, meaning: I will take you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, Indeed,
h
I will take you and raise you up

to Me, he said: I will take you up means I will take you. He said: And ‘I will take you up’ and I will raise you up are one and the same. He said: And he has not yet died, until the Antichrist is killed, and he will die. And he recited the statement of God Almighty, And he will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, he said: God raised him up to Him before he was an adult. He said: And he will descend as an adult.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty: O Jesus, indeed
h
I will take you and raise you up
to Me, the entire verse, he said: God raised him up to Him, so he is with Him in heaven.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
I will cause you to die
a death.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
I will cause you to die
, meaning:
h
I will cause you to die

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, that he said: God caused Jesus, son of Mary, to die three hours a day until He raised him up to Him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The Christians claim that he died seven hours during the day, then God revived him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: When God said, O Jesus, I will raise you up to Me and purify you from those who disbelieved, and I will take you after I have brought you down to the world. He said: This is from the word al-Muqaddam which means al-Dajjal and the word al-Mukhtaar which means al-Arqad presentation.

The most correct of these sayings, according to us, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: I will seize you from the earth and raise you to me, because of the continuous reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Jesus, son of Mary, will descend and kill the Antichrist, then he will remain on the earth for a period of time that has been mentioned, the narration differs regarding its length, then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hanzala ibn Ali al-Aslami, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God will send down Jesus, son of Mary, as a just judge and a fair leader. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and wealth will be so abundant that no one will be able to take it. He will walk through Ar-Rawha’ as a pilgrim or a pilgrim, or he will perform both.”

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Dinar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Adam, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The prophets are brothers by bloodlines, their mothers are different but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him, and he is my successor over my nation. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him: he is a man of medium build, reddish and white, with straight hair, as if his hair were dripping, even if it was not wet, between two Egypts. He will crush the cross, kill the pig, and wealth will be abundant, and people will fight for the sake of Islam until God destroys all religions in his time, and God destroys in his time the lying Messiah of misguidance, the Antichrist. It will occur in the safe land until lions graze with camels, tigers with cows, and wolves with sheep, and boys play with snakes, none of them harming the other. He will remain on the earth for forty years, then…” He dies, and the Muslims pray over him and bury him.

x: It is known that if God Almighty had caused him to die, He would not have caused him to die another death, so that two deaths would be added to him, because God Almighty only informed His servants that He would create them, then cause them to die, then bring them back to life, as He, the Most High, said: “It is God who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will bring you back to life. Is there among your associates any who do anything of that?” (al-Rum 30:40). The interpretation of the verse is: God said to Jesus: O Jesus, I will seize you from the earth, raise you to Me, and purify you from those who disbelieved and denied your prophethood. This report, even if it is reported in the form of a report, contains from God Almighty an argument against those who argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Jesus from the Najran delegation, that Jesus was not killed or crucified as they claimed, and that they and the Jews who acknowledged that and claimed against Jesus - are lying in their claim and assertion, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr: Then he informed them
m: - meaning the delegation from Najran - and responded to them regarding what they had acknowledged to the Jews about his crucifixion, how he raised him up and purified him from them, so he said: When God said, O Jesus,
h
I will take you and raise you up

to Me. As for He who purifies you from those who disbelieve, it means: He who cleanses you, He who delivers you from those who disbelieved in you and denied the truth that you brought them from the Jews and all other religions, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: And He will purify you from those who disbelieved, he said: When they intended to do to you what they intended.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And purifies you from those who disbelieve
, he said: He purifies him from the Jews, Christians, Magians, and the disbelievers of his people.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And He will make those who followed you on your path and your religion of Islam and its nature, above those who denied your prophethood and opposed their path [from] all the people of religions, so they denied what you brought and turned away from Surat Al Imran 3:55 When God said, "O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.
h
Then to Me is your return
, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ." acknowledging it, so their fate is above them, prevailing over them, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection
, they are the people of Islam who followed him according to his nature, religion, and Sunnah, and they will continue to be victorious over those who oppose them until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection
, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection
, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection
, he said: He will support those who follow you in Islam, over those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection
. As for those who follow you, it is said: They are the believers, and it is said: Rather, they are the Romans.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection

, he said: He will make those who follow him superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. He said: The Muslims are superior to them, and He will make them superior to those who abandoned Islam until the Day of Resurrection.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And He will make those who follow you from among the Christians superior to the Jews.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God: And He will purify you from those who disbelieve, he said: those who disbelieved from the Children of Israel, and will make those who follow you, he said: those who believed in him from the Children of Israel and others, superior to those who disbelieved, the Christians are superior to the Jews until the Day of Resurrection. He said: There is no country in which there are Christians, except that they are superior to the Jews, in the East or the West, they are humiliated in all countries.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Then to Me, then to God, O you who differ about Jesus, is your return, meaning: your destiny on the Day of Resurrection, so I will judge between you, meaning: then I will judge between all of you in the matter of Jesus with truth, in that over which you differed, of his matter. This is one of the speeches that was diverted from reporting on the absent to addressing the female, and that is because his saying:
h
Then to Me is your return

, was intended to report on the followers of Jesus and the disbelievers in him. The interpretation of the statement: And I will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is the return of the two groups: those who follow you and those who disbelieve in you, so judge between them concerning that over which they used to differ. But the statement was returned to the address due to the precedence of the statement, in the manner of what we mentioned of the statement that comes out in the form of a narration, as He said:
Until, when you were in the ship and it sailed with them with a good wind
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
As for those who disbelieve

, is those who denied your prophethood, O Jesus, and opposed your religion, and denied the truth that you brought them, and said falsehood about you, and attributed you to someone other than what they should attribute you to, from the Jews and Christians and all other kinds of religions, then I will punish them with a severe punishment, as for in this world, with killing, captivity, humiliation and poverty, and as for in the Hereafter, with the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever, and they will have no helpers, meaning: And they will have no one to prevent the punishment of God, nor anyone to repel His painful punishment for them with strength or intercession, because He is the Almighty, the Possessor of Retribution.
As for His statement:
h
And as for those who believed and did righteous deeds

, He, the Most High, means: As for those who believed in you, O Jesus - he says: believed you - and acknowledged your prophethood and what you brought them of the truth from Me, and professed Islam with which I sent you, and did what I imposed of My obligations on your tongue, and what I established of My laws, and what I established of My traditions, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they did righteous deeds

, he said: They performed My obligations. He will give them their full reward, meaning: He will give them the full reward for their deeds, without reducing or diminishing anything from it. As for His statement:
h
And God does not love the wrongdoers

, it means: God does not love the one who wrongs another person’s right, or puts something in the wrong place. Thus, He, the Most High, denied that He would wrong His servants, so He would reward the wrongdoer among those who disbelieved with the reward of the righteous who believed in Him, or He would reward the righteous among those who believed in Him, followed His commands, and refrained from what He forbade and obeyed Him with the reward of the wrongdoers among those who disbelieved in Him, denied His messengers, and disobeyed His commands and prohibitions. He said: Indeed, I do not love the wrongdoers, so how could I wrong My creation? This statement from God, the Most High, even if it was mentioned in the form of a report, is a threat from Him to those who disbelieve in Him and His messengers, and a promise from Him to those who believe in Him and His messengers, because He is the most knowledgeable of both groups that He will not diminish this believer’s right, nor will He wrong his dignity by placing it among those who disbelieved in Him and disobeyed His commands and prohibitions, so that by placing it among those who do not deserve it, He would be unjust.

x: What He, may He be glorified, means by His saying, That, is this report that His Prophet informed about Jesus and his mother Mary, and her mother Hannah, and Zechariah and his son John, and what he related about the affair of the disciples and the Jews of the Children of Israel, We recite it to you, O Muhammad, meaning: We recite it to you, O Muhammad, on the tongue of Gabriel, peace be upon him, by revealing it to you, of the signs, meaning: of the lessons and arguments against those who argued with you from the delegation of the Christians of Najran, and the Jews of the Children of Israel who denied you and denied what you brought them of the truth from Me,
h
and the Reminder
, meaning: and the Qur’an, the Wise, meaning: of the wisdom that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between you and those who ascribe the Messiah to someone other than his lineage, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: This is what We recite to you of the verses and the wise remembrance, the decisive, decisive truth, which was not mixed with falsehood, from the report about Jesus and what they differed about regarding his affair, so do not accept any report other than it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: This is what We recite to you of the verses and the wise remembrance, he said: the Qur’an.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the Reminder
, meaning: the Qur’an, the Wise, which has been perfected in its wisdom.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: What He, may He be glorified, means by His saying, That, is this report that His Prophet informed about Jesus and his mother Mary, and her mother Hannah, and Zechariah and his son John, and what he related about the affair of the disciples and the Jews of the Children of Israel, We recite it to you, O Muhammad, meaning: We recite it to you, O Muhammad, on the tongue of Gabriel, peace be upon him, by revealing it to you, of the signs, meaning: of the lessons and arguments against those who argued with you from the delegation of the Christians of Najran, and the Jews of the Children of Israel who denied you and denied what you brought them of the truth from Me, and the Reminder, meaning: and the Qur’an, the Wise, meaning: of the wisdom that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between you and those who ascribe the Messiah to someone other than his lineage, as:

x: He, may His praise be exalted, means: The resemblance of Jesus in My creating him without a male - and he informed the delegation from the Christians of Najran about it, O Muhammad - is to me like the resemblance of Adam whom I created from dust and then said to him: Be, and he was without a male, male, or female. He says: So My creating Jesus from his mother without a male is not more amazing than My creating Adam without a male or female, and My command when I commanded him to be, he was flesh. He says: So is My creation of Jesus: I commanded him to be, and he was.

The interpreters mentioned that God Almighty revealed this verse as an argument to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the delegation of Christians from Najran who argued with him about Jesus.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Aamer, he said:
m: The people of Najran were the most vehement of Christians in their words about Jesus, so they used to argue with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty revealed this verse in Surat Al Imran 3:“Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is like that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was,” until His saying:
h
Then we invoke the curse of God upon the liars

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam

. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.” That is because a group of people from Najran came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among them were the master and the last. They said to Muhammad: Why do you mention our companion? He said: Who is he? They said: Jesus, you claim that he is the servant of God! Muhammad said: Yes, he is the servant of God. They said to him: Have you seen the likeness of Jesus, or have you been informed of him? Then they left him, and Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him with the command of our Lord, the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, and said: Say to them when they come to you:
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam
, to the end of the verse.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam

. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.” It was mentioned to us that the two masters of the people of Najran and their bishops, Sayyid and Aqib, met the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about Jesus. They said: Every human has a father, so what is the matter with Jesus who has no father? So God, the Most High, revealed this verse about Abd al-Razzaq: “
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam
. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.” Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi:
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam

whom He created from dust. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent and the people of Najran heard about him, four of their best men came to him. Among them were: al-Aqib, al-Sayyid, Masarjis, and Marihaz. They asked him what he said about Jesus. He said: He is the servant of God, His spirit, and His word. They said: No! But he is God. He descended from His kingdom and entered the womb of Mary, then came out of her and showed us His power and His command. Have you ever seen a human being created without a father? Then God, the Exalted, revealed to Abd al-Razzaq: “
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam
. He created him from dust;
h
then He said to him
, ‘Be,’ and he was.” Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: “Indeed,
h
the likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam

. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.” He said: It was revealed about Al-‘Aqib and Al-Sayyid from the people of Najran, and they were both Christians. Ibn Jurayj said: It has reached us that a delegation from the Christians of Najran came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them Al-Sayyid and Al-‘Aqib, and they were the two leaders of the people of Najran at that time. They said: O Muhammad, why do you insult our companion? He said: Who is your companion? They said: Jesus, son of Mary, you claim that he is a servant! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, he is the servant of God and His word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him. They became angry and said: If you are truthful, then show us a servant who gives life to the dead, heals the blind, and creates from clay something like the form of a bird and breathes life into it, the verse, but he is God. He remained silent until Gabriel came to him and said: O Muhammad, They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the Messiah, the son of Mary’ (al-Ma’idah 5:17, 72) the verse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Gabriel, they asked me to tell them about the likeness of Jesus. Gabriel said: The likeness of Jesus is like that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. When morning came, they returned, and he recited to them the verses.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: The likeness of Jesus before God, so listen, “is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.”

x: If they say, Jesus was created without a male, then I created Adam from dust with that power without a female or a male, so he was as Jesus was, flesh and blood and hair and skin, so the creation of Jesus without a male is not more amazing than this.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about the statement of God, the Almighty: “The likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust,” he said: Two Najranis came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: Do you know that anyone was born without a male, so Jesus is like that? He said: So God, the Almighty, revealed: “The likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.” Did Adam have a father or a mother!! Just as you created this one in the womb of this one?

x: If someone were to say: How did he say: Like the likeness of Adam, He created him, when Adam is a definite noun, and definite nouns cannot be connected? It was said: His statement:
h
He created him from dust is not a connection to Adam
, but rather it is a statement about his matter in the form of an explanation of the example he gave, and how he was. As for his statement:
h
Then He said to him

, ‘Be,’ and he was, he said, and he was, and he began the report about the creation of Adam, and that is the report about a matter that had been decided. He brought out the report about him in the same way as the report about what had passed, so He, may His praise be glorified, said: He created him from dust,
h
then He said to him

, ‘Be,’ because it means that God informed His Prophet that He created things by saying, Be, then He said, and he was, as a starting report, and the report about Adam’s matter had ended with His saying, Be.
The interpretation of the statement is: “
h
The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam

. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be.’” And know, O Muhammad, that whatever your Lord said to him, Be, will come to pass. Since his statement, Like Adam, He created him from dust, then said to him, ‘Be,’ indicates that the speech is intended to inform the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and all of His creation that what He created will be, from a beginning without origin, beginning, or element, the meaning of the speech is sufficient, and it was said, and it will be, so the future was connected to the past in that meaning. Some Arab scholars said: Fiyakun is a nominative case, and its meaning is: Be, and it was. It is as if he said: Then it is.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: What I have informed you of regarding the report of Jesus, and that his example is like that of Adam, whom He created from dust, then his Lord said to him, Be, that is the truth from your Lord.
He says: It is the report that is from your Lord,
h
so do not be among the doubters
, meaning: Do not be among those who doubt that this is so, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The truth is from your Lord
h
so do not be among the doubters
