, meaning: Do not be in doubt about Jesus, that he is like Adam, the servant and messenger of God, the word of God and His spirit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: his statement:
h
The truth is from your Lord
h
so do not be among the doubters

, meaning: Do not be in doubt about what We have told you, that Jesus is the servant and messenger of God, a word from Him and a spirit, and that his likeness before God is like that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, Be, and he was.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
The truth is from your Lord
, what came to you of the report about Jesus,
h
so do not be among the doubters
, meaning: The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not doubt it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
So do not be among the doubters

, he said: The doubters are the ones who doubt. And doubt, suspicion, and suspicion are one and the same, like when you say: Give me, hand me over, and come. This is different in speech, but it is one and the same.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
So whoever disputes with you about him

, is whoever disputes with you, O Muhammad, about the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary. The letter ha in his saying: in it refers back to the mention of Jesus. It is possible that it refers back to the truth about which God Almighty said: The truth is from your Lord. What he means by his saying:
h
After what has come to you of knowledge

, after what has come to you of the knowledge that I have made clear to you about Jesus that he is the servant of God, then say, ‘Come,’ come, let us call, our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us supplicate earnestly, he says: then let us curse. It is said in speech: What is wrong with him? May God curse him, meaning: May God curse him. What is wrong with him? May God curse him, meaning curse. Labid said, and he mentioned a people who perished and said: Time looked at them and prayed Meaning: He called for their destruction.
So we invoke the curse of God upon the liars, from us and from you, that he is Jesus, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So whoever disputes with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge

, meaning: about Jesus: that he is the servant of God and His Messenger, from the word of God and His spirit, then say, ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons,’ until his statement: against the liars.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
So whoever disputes with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge
, meaning: after I have told you about his story and how his affair was, say, ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons,’ the verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
So whoever disputes with you about him after the knowledge that has come to you
, he said: Whoever disputes with you about Jesus after the knowledge that has come to you about him.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Then we supplicate and invoke the curse of God upon the liars. He said: From us and from you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, and Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Ziyad al-Hadrami,
m: “on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Juz’ al-Zubaidi: that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I wish there was a veil between me and the people of Najran so that I could not see them and they could not see me!” because of the severity of their arguments with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Indeed, what I have informed you of, O Muhammad, about the matter of Jesus, and I have related to you from his report, and that he is My servant and My messenger and My word which I bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Me, is the true story and report, so know that. And know that there is no god for creation who deserves their worship through His ownership of them except your god whom you worship, and He is God, the Almighty, the Wise. What he means by his saying: The Mighty, is the Mighty in his vengeance on those who disobeyed him and went against his command, and claimed a god other than him, or worshipped a lord other than him, the Wise, in his management, nothing that he managed could be weak, and nothing that could be wrong with it.

If they turn away means: If those who argued with you about Jesus turn away from what came to you, the truth from your Lord in Jesus and other than him from all the guidance and clarification that God gave you will die, so they turned away from him and did not accept him, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters, meaning: Indeed, God is All-Knowing of those who disobey their Lord and do in His land and country what He forbade them from, and that is their corruption. God Almighty says: He is All-Knowing of them and their deeds, He counts them against them and preserves them, until He rewards them for them with their reward. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: h
This is the true story
, meaning: This that you have brought of the report about Jesus, is the true story, from his command.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
This is the true story
. This that we said about Jesus, is the true story.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
This is the true story
, he said:
h
This is the true story

about Jesus. It is not appropriate for Jesus to go beyond this or exceed it: to go beyond being the word of God that He bestowed upon Mary, and a spirit from Him, and the servant and messenger of God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
This is the true story

, that which we said about Jesus is the truth, and there is no god but God, the verse. When God, the Most High, decided between His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the delegation of Christians from Najran, with a decisive judgment and just ruling, He ordered him, if they turned away from what he had called them to, which was to acknowledge the oneness of God, that He has no son or wife, and that Jesus is His servant and messenger, and refused except to argue and dispute, to call them to a mutual cursing. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that, they were defeated and refused to mutual cursing, and called for reconciliation, as in: Ibn Humayd narrated, Jarir narrated, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Amir, who said: So he - meaning the Prophet - ordered that they be cursed - meaning the people of Najran - by saying: But whoever disputes with you concerning him after what has come to you of knowledge, the verse. So they promised to curse him and they promised him the next day. So they went to Sayyid and Al-Aqib, and they were the wisest of them, so they followed them. So they went to a wise man among them and mentioned to him what they had left the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - for. He said: What did you do! And he regretted it, and said to them: If he was a prophet and then he cursed you, God would never be angry with you, and if he was a king and he prevailed over you, he would never let you live. They said: How can we, when we have made a promise? So he said to them: When you go to him in the morning and he presents to you what you left him for, say: We seek refuge in God! If he calls you again, say to him: We seek refuge in God! And perhaps he will excuse you from that. When they came in the morning, the Prophet (peace be upon him) embraced Hassan and took Al-Hussain by the hand, and Fatima walked behind him. He called them to the same thing they had left him on the day before, and they said: We seek refuge in God! Then he called them and they said: We seek refuge in God! He said repeatedly: If you refuse, then submit and you will have what the Muslims have and you will be subject to what the Muslims are subject to, as God the Almighty said. If you refuse, then pay the jizyah willingly and you will be humiliated, as God the Almighty said. They said: We have no control over anything but ourselves! He said: If you refuse, then I will throw it out to you equally, as God the Almighty said. They said: We do not have the strength to fight the Arabs, but we will pay the jizyah. He said: So he imposed on them every year two thousand garments: a thousand in Rajab and a thousand in Safar. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: The bearer of good tidings has come to me of the destruction of the people of Najran, even the birds on the trees - or: the sparrows on the trees - if they agreed to curse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us:
m: I said to Al-Mughira: People narrate in the hadith of the people of Najran that Ali was with them! He said: As for Al-Sha’bi, he did not mention him, so I do not know whether it was due to the bad opinion of the Umayyads regarding Ali, or whether it was not in the hadith! Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
h
This is the true story

, until His saying: Then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims,’ so he called them to justice and cut off their argument. When the report from God about him came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him Surat Al Imran 3:63 But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah is Knowing of the corrupters. peace, and the final judgment between him and them, and his command to do what he commanded of cursing them if they rejected him, he called them to that, and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, let us consider our matter, then we will come to you with what we want to do with regard to what you have called us to. So they turned away from him, then they were alone with al-ʿAqib, who had their own opinion, and they said: O ʿAbd al-Masih, what do you think? He said: By God, O group of Christians, you have known that Muhammad is a prophet sent, and he has brought you the final word about your companion. You have known that no people have ever cursed a prophet and their elders remained and their young ones did not grow up. If you do this, it will be your extermination. If you have refused to adhere to your religion and continue with what you say about your companion, then say farewell to the man and then return to your country until he shows you the time of his opinion. So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you and to leave you in your religion and return to our religion. But send with us a man from your companions whom you are pleased with for us, so that he may judge between us in matters in which we have differed regarding our wealth, for you are pleasing to us.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Isa bin Farqad told us, on the authority of Abu al-Jarud, on the authority of Zayd bin Ali,
m: regarding his statement: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, the verse, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali, Fatima, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn were there.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: So whoever disputes with you about it after what has come to you of knowledge, the verse. So he - meaning the Prophet - took the hand of al-Hasan, al-Husayn and Fatimah, and said to Ali: Follow us. So he went out with them. But the Christians did not go out that day, and they said: We fear that this is the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and the call of the Prophet is not like any other!! So they stayed behind from him that day, and the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: If they went out, they would be burned! So they made peace with him on a peace treaty: that he would be entitled to eighty thousand from them, and if the dirhams were not enough, then in the offers: a robe for forty, and that he would be entitled to thirty-three shields, thirty-three camels, and thirty-four horses fighting every year, and that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, would guarantee them until we delivered them to them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called a delegation from the Najran delegation of Christians, and they were the ones who argued with him about Jesus, but they turned away from that and feared,” and it was mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if the punishment has come upon the people of Najran, and if they did that, they would have been uprooted from the earth.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: But whoever disputes with you about it after what has come to you of knowledge, say, ‘Come, let us call our sons and your sons,’ he said: It has reached us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to call the people of Najran, and when they saw him go out, they were afraid and dispersed and returned. Muammar said, Qatada said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted the people of Najran, he took the hands of Hasan and Husayn and said to Fatima: Follow us. When the enemies of God saw that, they returned.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If those who challenge the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to challenge him, they would return without finding any family or money.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Zakariya told us, on the authority of Adi, he said, Ubaidullah bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if they cursed me, not a single one of them would be present for a year without God destroying the liars.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd told us, he said:
m: “It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you were to curse the people, whom would you be referring to when you said: ‘Our sons and your sons’? He said: Hasan and Husayn.”

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, al-Mundhir bin Tha’laba told us, he said, Alba’ bin Ahmar al-Yashkari told us, he said:
m: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Then say, “Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women,” the verse, the Messenger of God sent for Ali and Fatima and their two sons, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and called the Jews to curse them. A young man from the Jews said: Woe to you! Did you not make a covenant yesterday with your brothers who were transformed into apes and pigs?! Do not curse! So they stopped.”

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Say, O Muhammad, to the People of the Book, who are the People of the Torah and the Gospel, Come, come, to a just word, meaning: to a word of justice between us and you, and the just word is that we unify God and do not worship anyone other than Him, and we disavow every deity other than Him, and do not associate anything with Him. And His statement:
h
And let not some of us take others as lords
, meaning: let not some of us owe obedience to others in what they have been commanded to do of disobedience to God, and glorify Him by prostrating as he prostrates to his Lord.
h
But if they turn away

, meaning: if they turn away from what I have called them to of the just word that I have commanded you to call them to, and they do not respond to it, then say, O believers, to those who turn away from that, Bear witness that we are Muslims.
The interpreters differed about who this verse was revealed about.
Some of them said: It was revealed about the Jews of the Children of Israel who were around the city of the Messenger of God.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews of Medina to the right word, and they were the ones who argued about Abraham.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews to the word of justice.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: It has reached us that the Prophet of God called the Jews of Medina to do that, but they refused, so he fought them. He said: He called them to the words of God Almighty: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture
, come to a word that is equitable between us and you,’ verse.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about the delegation of Christians from Najran.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr:
m: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture

, come to a word that is equitable between us and you’ the verse, until His saying: Then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims,’ he said: So he called them to justice, and cut off the argument from them - meaning the delegation of Najran.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them - meaning the delegation of Christians from Najran - and said:
h
O People of the Book
, come to a word that is equitable between us and you, the verse.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told me, he said, Ibn Zayd told us, he said:
m: He, may His praise be glorified, meant: This is the true story, about Jesus - as we have explained previously - he said: So they refused - meaning the delegation from Najran - so he said: Call them to something easier than this, say:
h
O People of the Scripture
, come to a word that is equitable between us and you, and he recited until he reached: Lords besides God, but they refused to accept this or the other.

x: We said that by His statement,
h
O People of the Book
, He meant the People of the Two Books, because they are all from the People of the Book, and the Most High did not specify some of them with His statement,
h
O People of the Book

, over others. So it is not more appropriate that it be directed to the People of the Torah than it is to the People of the Gospel, nor are the People of the Gospel more appropriate that it be intended to the exclusion of others from the People of the Torah. Since neither group is more appropriate to that than the other, because there is no evidence that it is the one specified by that from the other, nor is there a sound trace, then it is obligatory that every People of the Book be meant by it. Because singling out worship for God alone and sincerely establishing monotheism for Him is obligatory upon every one of God’s creation who is commanded and forbidden.

And the name People of the Book applies to the People of the Torah and the People of the Gospel, so it was known from that that He meant both groups. As for the interpretation of his saying: Come, it is: come forward and arrive. Rather, it is the verb tafa’ala from al-‘ulu high, so it is as if the one who says to his companion: Come to me Surat Al Imran 3:64 Say, "
h
O People of the Scripture
, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allah and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords besides Allah."
h
But if they turn away

, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims [in submission]." is saying tafa’ala from al-‘ulu, just as it is said: Come near to me from closeness, and come close to me from nearness. And his saying: to a just word. It is the word of justice, and just is one of the attributes of the word. The Arab scholars differed on the reason for following the word sawa in the parsing, as it is a noun and not an adjective.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is a genitive case because it is an attribute of the word, which is justice, and he meant: level. He said: If he had meant istiwa, it would have been accusative. If he wanted to make it istiwa and genitive, it is permissible, and he could make it an attribute of the word, like creation because creation is the created. And creation can be an attribute and a noun. And he makes istiwa like the level. God Almighty said: Which We have made for mankind equal, the one who dwells therein and the one who travels therein (al-Hajj 22:25), because the level is for the other, and it is a noun not an attribute, so it is governed by the first, and that is if he meant by it istiwa. If he meant by it istiwa, it is permissible for it to be governed by the first. And the nominative case in this meaning is good, because it does not change from its state and is not dualized, nor pluralized, nor feminine, so it is similar to the nouns that are like justice, contentment, and side, and the like.

They said: [In His statement]: That We may make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds - equal in their life and their death (al-Jathiyah 45:21), so the level is for life and death with this, the subject. If you wish, you can apply it to the first, and make it an advanced attribute, as if it were from the cause of the first and was applied to it. This is if you make it in a level meaning. The nominative is the face of the speech as I explained to you. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Sawa’a is a verbal noun that is used in place of the verb, meaning the place of mushawa’a and musa’u, so sometimes it comes in place of the verb, and sometimes in place of the verbal noun. It may be said in sawa’a meaning justice: sawa and sawa as God the Most High said:
A place that is equal to and sawa

meaning: justice and fairness between us and you. It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that he used to read that up to the word justice between us and you.
And like what we said in the interpretation of His statement: to a word that is equal between us and you, that equality is justice, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O People of the Scripture
, come to a word that is equitable between us and you, justice between us and you,
h
that we worship none but God
, the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture
, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except God and not associate anything with Him,’ something similar.

x: Others said: It is saying: There is no god but God.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said, Abu Al-ʿAliyah said:
m: The word of equality is, there is no god but God. As for his saying:
h
That we worship none but God

, the that is in the accusative case, meaning: Come to worship none but God. We have previously explained the meaning of worship in the speech of the Arabs, and we have provided evidence for the correct meanings, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. As for his saying:
h
And let not some of us take others as lords

, then taking others as lords is not by obeying the leaders in what they commanded them to do of disobeying God, and leaving what they forbade them from obeying God, as God Almighty said: “They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were commanded not except to worship one God” (al-Tawbah 9:31). as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: h
And let not some of us take others as lords besides God
, meaning: let not some of us obey others in disobeying God. And it is said that this lordship is that people obey their masters and leaders in other than worship, even if they do not pray to them.

x: Others said: Taking each other as lords, prostrating to each other.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not some of us take others as lords besides God
, he said: Prostrating to one another. As for his saying:
h
But if they turn away

, then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims,’ it means: If those whom you are calling to the right word turn away from it and disbelieve, then you, O believers, say to them: Bear witness that we, with what you have turned away from, of the oneness of God, and the sincerity of servitude to Him, and that He is the God who has no partner, are Muslims, meaning: Submissive to God through it, humbled before Him by acknowledging that in our hearts and with our tongues. We have previously explained the meaning of Islam and provided evidence for it in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

evidence.text: It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that he used to read that up to the word justice between us and you.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying: O People of the Book, O People of the Torah and the Gospel, Why do you argue, why do you dispute, about Abraham and quarrel about him, meaning: about Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, may God’s prayers be upon him. Their argument for it was: the claim of each group of the people of these two books that he was one of them, and that he followed the religion of the people of his sect. So God, the Almighty, criticized them for their claim, and indicated their contradiction and claim, saying: How do you claim that he was of your faith and religion, while your religion is either Judaism or Christianity, and the Jew among you claims that his religion is to establish the Torah and act according to what is in it, and the Christian among you claims that his religion is to establish the Gospel and what is in it, and these two books were not revealed until some time after the destruction and death of Abraham?

So how can he be one of you? And what is the point of your dispute over him, and your claim that he was one of you, while the matter regarding him is as you have learned? It was said: This verse was revealed regarding the dispute between the Jews and Christians over Abraham, and each group claiming that he was one of them.

Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, who narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd bin Thabit narrated, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Christians of Najran and the Jewish rabbis gathered in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they disputed in his presence. The rabbis said: Abraham was nothing but a Jew! The Christians said: Abraham was nothing but a Christian! So God, the Almighty, revealed about them:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you dispute about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Will you not reason? The Christians said: He was a Christian! The Jews said: He was a Jew!

c: So God informed them that
m: the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him, and after him came Judaism and Christianity.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you argue about Abraham? He said: Why do you argue about Abraham? and you claim that he was a Jew or a Christian, and the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him, so Judaism came after the Torah, and Christianity came after the Gospel,
h
Do you not understand

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed regarding the Jews’ claim that Abraham was one of them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews of Medina to the word of truth, and they were the ones who argued about Abraham, and claimed that he died a Jew, so God Almighty denied them and denied him, saying:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you argue about Abraham? He said: The Jews and Christians, God Almighty cleared him of them, when every nation claimed that he was one of them, and He included with him the believers, whoever was from the people of the Hanifiyah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. As for his saying:
h
Do you not understand
?, he means:
h
Do you not understand
? Do you understand the error of your saying: Abraham was a Jew or a Christian, and you know that Judaism and Christianity occurred some time after his death? Surat Al Imran 3:65
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason?

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Here you are

, the people who [said about Abraham what they said, you have argued], you have disputed and argued, about that of which you have knowledge, of the matter of your religion which you found in your books, and which the Messengers of God brought to you from Him, and other than that which you were given and which you have established as being correct, so why do you argue, he says: why do you argue and quarrel, about that of which you have no knowledge, meaning: about that which you have no knowledge of regarding the matter of Abraham and his religion, and which you did not find in the books of God, nor did your Prophets bring it to you, nor did you witness it so that you could learn it? Like: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: “
h
Here you are
, arguing about that of which you have knowledge.

Why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge?” As for that of which they have knowledge, it is what was forbidden to them and what they were commanded to do. As for that of which they have no knowledge, it is the affair of Abraham.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Here you are

, arguing about that of which you have knowledge, meaning: about that which you witnessed, saw, and witnessed. So why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge, about that which you did not witness, did not see, and did not witness,
h
and God knows
and you do not know.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly. And His statement:
h
And God knows
, and you do not know, means:
h
And God knows

what is hidden from you, that you did not witness or see, and that His messengers did not bring to you, from the matter of Abraham and other matters and what you dispute about, because nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, and you do not know, of that except what you witnessed and witnessed, or you perceived His knowledge through reporting and hearing.

x: This is a denial from God Almighty of the claim of those who disputed about Abraham and his religion from the Jews and Christians, and claimed that he was of their religion, and a disavowal of them from him, and that they were opponents of his religion, and a judgment from Him Almighty for the people of Islam and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they are the people of his religion, and of his method and laws, without the rest of the people of other religions and faiths. God Almighty says: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, nor was he one of the polytheists, who worship idols and statues or a creature other than his Creator, who is the God of creation and their Maker. But he was a Hanif, meaning: following God’s command and obedience, upright on the path of guidance that He commanded us to adhere to, a Muslim, meaning: humble before God in his heart, submissive to Him with his limbs, and obedient to what He imposed upon him and obligated him of His rulings.

We have previously explained the differences among the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of Hanaf and we have provided evidence for the statement that is more correct than their statements, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen Al-Wasiti told me, he said, Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Amer, he said: The Jews said:
m: Abraham is of our religion. And the Christians said: He is of our religion. So God Almighty revealed: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian the verse, so God denied them and refuted their argument, meaning: the Jews who claimed that Abraham died a Jew.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A'la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ya'qub bin Abdul Rahman Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah - I do not think he narrated it except on the authority of his father -
m: that Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail went out to Ash-Sham asking about religion and following it. He met a Jewish scholar, so he asked him about his religion and said: I am determined to follow your religion, so tell me about your religion! The Jew said to him: You will not be of our religion until you take your share of God's wrath. Zaid said: I only flee from God's wrath, and I will never bear any of God's wrath while I am able. So can you guide me to a religion that does not include this? He said: I do not know anything except that it is Hanif! He said: What is Hanif? He said: The religion of Abraham. He was neither Jewish nor Christian, and he worshipped none but God. So he left him and met a Christian scholar, so he asked him about his religion. He said: I am determined to follow your religion, so tell me about your religion! He said: You will not be of our religion until you take your share of God's curse. He said: I will not tolerate any of God's curse or wrath ever while I am able to. Will you guide me to a religion that does not include this? He said to him something similar to what the Jew had said: I do not know of it except that it is a Hanif.

c: So he left him satisfied with what they had told him
m: and what they had agreed upon about the matter of Abraham. He kept raising his hands to God and saying: O God, I bear witness that I am of the religion of Abraham.
b.via: So he left him satisfied with what they had

m: Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Dawud bin Sulayman told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jarir al-Tabari told us.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: Indeed, the people most deserving of Abraham, is that the people most deserving of Abraham, his support and his guardianship, are those who followed him, meaning: those who followed his path and method, so they unified God, sincerely devoting their religion to Him, and established His Sunnah, and legislated His laws, and were monotheists and Muslims for God, not associating partners with Him. And this Prophet, meaning: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who believed, meaning: and those who believed in Muhammad and in what he brought to them from God. And God is the ally of the believers, meaning: God is the supporter of the believers in Muhammad, who believed in his prophethood and in what he brought to them from Him, against those who opposed them from the people of religions and faiths. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those of the people who have the closest claim to Abraham are those who followed him, meaning: those who followed him according to his religion, his Sunnah, his way, and his nature, and this Prophet, meaning the Prophet of God, Muhammad, and those who believed, with him, meaning the believers who believed in the Prophet of God and followed him. Muhammad was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those of the believers with him were the people who had the closest claim to Abraham.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Jabir ibn al-Kurdi, and al-Hasan ibn Abi Yahya al-Maqdisi told us:

c: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masʿud, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Every prophet has guardians from among the prophets, and my guardian among them is my father and the friend of my Lord.’ Then he recited: ‘Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this prophet and those who believe. And God is the ally of the believers.’”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Naim Al-Fadl Ibn Dukayn told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Abdullah - I think he
m: said: on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: God Almighty says: Indeed, the people who have the closest claim to Abraham are those who followed him, and they are the believers.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying: A group of the People of the Book would have wished, meaning a group, if they could mislead you, meaning the People of the Torah from the Jews, and the People of the Gospel from the Christians, if they could turn you away, meaning if they could turn you away, O believers, from Islam and return you from it to what they are upon of disbelief, and thereby destroy you. And misguidance in this context means destruction, from the words of God Almighty: And they say, ‘If we are lost in the earth, will we then be in a new creation?’ (al-Sajdah 32:10), meaning: if we are destroyed.

i: And from this is the saying of Al-Akhtal in satirizing Jarir:
x: I was the speck in a murky, foaming wave, the one who brought it threw it as a gift of misguidance.

Meaning: He perished completely. And the words of the genius of Banu Dhubyan: So his misguided ones returned with a clear eye, and Hazm and Nael were left in the Golan. Meaning: They destroyed him. They only mislead themselves. They do not destroy anyone but themselves, by what they do in trying to turn you away from your religion. By themselves, he means their followers and partisans of their faith and religions. Rather, they have destroyed themselves and their followers by what they have tried to do, because they have incurred God’s wrath by doing that, and have deserved His anger and curse, for their disbelief in God and their breaking of the covenant that God took from them in their Book, to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in him, and acknowledge his prophethood. Then He, the Most High, informed us about them, that they do what they do, of trying to turn the believers away from guidance to misguidance and ruin, out of ignorance of what God has in store for them in His punishment, and what He has stored up for them in His painful torment.
So He, the Most High, said:
h
And they do not perceive
that they are only misleading themselves, by trying to mislead you, O believers. The meaning of his saying:
h
And they do not perceive
, is that they do not know and do not understand. We have explained the interpretation of this with evidence in other places, so there is no need to repeat it.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: O People of the Book, from the Jews and Christians, Why do you disbelieve, meaning: Why do you deny, the signs of God, meaning: what is in the Book of God that He revealed to you on the tongues of your prophets, of its signs and evidence, while you bear witness that it is the truth from your Lord.

Rather, this is from God Almighty, a rebuke to the People of the Book for their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their denial of his prophethood, even though they find it in their books, while they testify that what is in their books is true and that it is from God, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while you bear witness, meaning: You bear witness that the description of Muhammad as the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in your book, then you disbelieve in it and deny it and do not believe in it, and you find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel: the unlettered prophet who believes in God and His words.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while you bear witness? He said: You bear witness that the description of Muhammad is in your book, then you disbelieve in it and do not believe in it, and you find him with you in the Torah and the Gospel: the unlettered prophet.

c: Muhammad told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while you bear witness, the verses of God are Muhammad, and as for bear witness, they bear witness that it is the truth, they find it written with them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while you bear witness that the religion with God is Islam, and God has no religion other than it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O people of the Torah and the Gospel, Why do you mix, meaning: Why do you mix, truth with falsehood? Their mixing of truth with falsehood was that they showed with their tongues their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, other than what was in their hearts of Judaism and Christianity. as: Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Sayf, ʿAdi ibn Zayd, and al-Harith ibn ʿAwf said to one another: Come, let us believe in what was revealed to Muhammad and his companions in the morning and disbelieve in it in the evening, so that we may confuse them about their religion, perhaps they will do as we do and turn away from their religion!
So God, the Almighty, revealed about them:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you mix truth with falsehood? until His saying: And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: O People of the Book, why do you mix truth with falsehood? He said: Why do you mix Judaism and Christianity with Islam, when you know that the religion of God, which He does not accept other than it, is Islam, and that no one is rewarded except with it?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly, except that he said: What is not accepted from anyone other than it is Islam, and he did not say: And he is not rewarded except with it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you mix truth with falsehood? Islam with Judaism and Christianity.

x: Others said about this, including:

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about the words of God Almighty: Why do you mix truth with falsehood? He said: Truth is the Torah that God revealed to Moses, and falsehood is what they wrote with their own hands.

x: We have already explained the meaning of confusion, so there is no need to repeat it.
By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Why do you, O People of the Book, conceal the truth?
The truth that they concealed: what is in their books about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his mission and his prophethood, such as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you conceal the truth while you know it
, they concealed the matter of Muhammad, although they found it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel, commanding them to do good and forbidding them from evil.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you conceal the truth while you know it

, meaning: They conceal the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though they find it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel: He commands them to do good and forbids them from evil.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And you conceal the truth, Islam, and the command of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
and you know
, that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that the religion is Islam. As for his saying:
h
And you know
, he means by it:
h
And you know

that what you are concealing of the truth is the truth, and that it is from God. This statement from God Almighty is report of the People of the Book’s deliberate disbelief in Him and their concealment of what they knew of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found in their books and brought to them by their prophets.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the meaning that this group was commanded to do: faith at the beginning of the day, and disbelief at the end of it.

Some of them said: This was an order from them to them to believe in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his prophethood and what he brought from God, and that it is true, in appearance, without believing in it with determination and belief in the hearts on that, and with disbelief in him and denial of all of that in the end.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Believe in that which has been revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end

, some of them said to each other: Give them contentment with their religion at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, for that is more likely to make them believe you, and to know that you have seen in them what you dislike, and that is more likely to make them turn back from their religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ma’la bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Believe in that which was revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end
, he said: The Jews said: Believe with them at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end,
h
perhaps they will return
with you.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And a party of the People of the Scripture said, ‘Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end that
h
perhaps they will return

.’ There were twelve rabbis from an Arab village, and they said to one another: Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day, and say: We bear witness that Muhammad is the truth and the truthful. Then when it is the end of the day, disbelieve and say: We returned to our scholars and rabbis and asked them, and they told us that Muhammad is a liar and that you are not upon anything. Now we have returned to our religion, and it is more pleasing to us than your religion. Perhaps they will doubt, and say: These people were with us at the beginning of the day, so what is wrong with them? So God, the Almighty, informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ghifari, who said: The Jews said to one another: Become Muslims at the beginning of the day and apostatize at the end of it, so that
h
perhaps they will return

. Then God revealed their secret, and God Almighty revealed: And a party of the People of the Scripture said, ‘Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end, so that
h
perhaps they will return

x: Others said: Rather, what I was commanded to do of faith is prayer, and attending it with them at the beginning of the day, and leaving it at the end of it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told me, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Believe in that which was revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day, the Jews say it. They prayed the dawn prayer with Muhammad, and they disbelieved at the end of the day, as a plot on their part, to show the people that he had shown them error, after they had followed him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a party of the People of the Scripture say

, ‘Believe in that which was revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day,’ 10:10. That is because a party of the Jews said: Surat Al Imran 3:72 And a party of the People of the Scripture said, "Believe in what was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end that
h
perhaps they will return

." When you meet the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the beginning of the day, then believe, and when it is the end of the day, then pray your prayers, perhaps they will say: These are the People of the Scripture, and they are more knowledgeable than us! Perhaps they will turn away from their religion. And do not believe except in one who follows your religion.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: And a group of the People of the Book said, meaning: of the Jews who read the Torah, They believed, they believed, in that which was revealed to those who believed, and that is what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them of the true religion, its laws and its traditions, at the beginning of the day, meaning: the beginning of the day. He called the first part of it his face, because it is the best part of it, and the first thing that the viewer sees of it, just as the first part of a garment is called its face, and as Rabi’ ibn Ziyad said: Whoever is happy about Malik's death, let him come to our women in broad daylight.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: the face of the day, the beginning of the day.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: The face of the day, the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, he said: the end of the day.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Believe in what was revealed to those who believe at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end, he said, he said: Pray with them at dawn, and do not pray with them at the end of the day, lest you cause them to slip by that. As for his saying: And disbelieve at the end of it, he means by that that they said: And deny what you believed in of their religion in the middle of the day, at the end of the day,
h
perhaps they will return
. He means by that:
h
perhaps they will return
from their religion with you and abandon it? Like: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
Perhaps they will return
, he said: Perhaps they will abandon their religion and return to what you are upon.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Perhaps they will return
, perhaps they will turn away from their religion.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Perhaps they will return
, perhaps they will doubt.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Perhaps they will return
, he said: They will return from their religion.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Do not believe anyone except someone who follows your religion and is Jewish. This is report from God about the statement of the group who said to their Jewish brothers: Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at daybreak. The lam in His statement: for those who follow your religion, is similar to the lam in His statement: Perhaps there will be a successor to you, meaning: a successor to you, some of that which you are hastening (al-Naml 27:72). And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And do not believe except in him who follows your religion
, this is what some of them said to each other.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And do not believe except in those who follow your religion. He said: Do not believe except in those who follow Judaism.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not believe except in him who follows your religion
, he said: Do not believe except in him who believes in your religion, and whoever opposes it, do not believe him.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: His statement, Say, ‘Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God,’ is an objection in the middle of the speech, as report from God that the explanation is His explanation and the guidance is His guidance. They said: The rest of the speech after that is connected to the first speech, as report of what the Jews said to each other. So the meaning of the speech according to them is: And do not believe except in the one who follows your religion, and do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given or that they will argue with you before your Lord, meaning: And do not believe that anyone will argue with you before your Lord. Then God the Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad: Indeed, grace is in God’s hand; He gives it to whom He wills, and Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: that someone should be given the like of what you have been given, out of envy on the part of the Jews that prophethood should be in someone other than them, and the desire that they should be followed in their religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: The interpretation of that is: Say, O Muhammad: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, that the explanation is the explanation of God, that someone is given, they said: And its meaning is: no one among the nations is given what you have been given, as He said:
God makes clear to you, lest you go astray
meaning: you do not go astray, and as He said:
Thus have We caused it to enter the hearts of the criminals, * They will not believe in it

meaning: that they will not believe, like what you have been given, he says: like what you, O Muhammad, and your nation have been given of Islam and guidance, or they argue with you before your Lord, they said: And the meaning of or is: except, that is: except that they argue with you, meaning: except that they argue with you before your Lord when your Lord did to them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Surat Al Imran 3:
m: h
And do not believe except in him who follows your religion

. Say, "Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God - that anyone should be given the like of what you have been given or that they should dispute with you before your Lord. Say, "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God. He grants it to whom He wills. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing." al-Suddi: God Almighty said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: ‘Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, that someone should be given the like of what you have been given,’” meaning: the like of what you have been given, O nation of Muhammad, or that they should argue with you before your Lord, the Jews say: God did such and such an honor to us, until He sent down manna and quails upon us. What I have given you is better, so say: “Indeed, the bounty is in God’s hand. He gives it to whom He wills,” the verse. According to this interpretation, all of this speech is a command from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the Jews, and it is interconnected with each other and there is no objection in it. The second guidance is a response to the first guidance, and that is in the nominative case as report of guidance.

x: Others said: Rather, this is a command from God to His Prophet to say it to the Jews. They said: Its interpretation is: Say, O Muhammad, Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, that anyone be given among the people the like of what you have been given, meaning: Like what you, O group of Jews, have been given of the Book of God, and like your Prophet, so do not envy the believers for what I have given them like what I have given you from My bounty, for the bounty is in My hand, and I give it to whomever I will.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God, that someone should be given the like of what you have been given,’ meaning: When God revealed a book like your book, and sent a prophet like your prophet, you envied them for that, Say, ‘Indeed, the bounty is in the hand of God,’ the verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: Say, O Muhammad: “Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God: that someone be given the like of what you have been given,” you, O group of Jews, from the Book of God. They said: This is the last statement that God commanded our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the Jews from this verse. They said: His statement, or they argue with you, is a response to His statement,
h
And do not believe except those who follow your religion
. The interpretation of the statement - according to the people of this article - is:
h
And do not believe except in him who follows your religion

, so you abandon the truth: that they argue with you about it before your Lord, the one whose religion you followed and chose: that he is right, and that you find his description in your book. Then his statement: or they argue with you is rejected as an answer to an abandoned prohibition, according to the statement of these people.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his saying: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God, that someone should be given the like of what you have been given, he said: This matter that you are upon: that someone should be given the like of what you have been given, or that they should argue with you before your Lord, he said: Some of them said to one another: Do not tell them what God has made clear to you in His Book, so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord, “Say: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God.”

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that his statement, Say, ‘Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God,’ is an objection to it, and the rest of the speech is consistent with one context. So its interpretation then would be:
h
And do not believe except in him who follows your religion

, and do not believe that anyone will be given what you have been given - meaning: no one will be given what you have been given - or that they will argue with you before your Lord, meaning: or that someone will argue with you before your Lord... about your faith, because you are more honorable to God because of what He has given you over them. So the entire speech is a report about the statement of the group about whom God Almighty said: And a party of the People of the Scripture said, ‘Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at daybreak’ except for His saying: Say, ‘Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God.’

Then the speech begins with their denial of their statement: Say, O Muhammad, to those who said what they said from the group whose statement I described to you to its followers from the Jews: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God. Indeed, success is God’s success and clarification is His clarification. Indeed, grace is in His hand, He gives it to whomever He wills, not what you, O group of Jews, wish for. We chose this from all the sayings we mentioned because it is the most correct in meaning, the best in consistency with the meaning of the Arabs’ speech, and the most consistent with the structure and context of the speech. Anything other than that is an abstraction that is far from correct, and is strongly discouraged by the speech.

By that, the Most High means: Say, O Muhammad, to these Jews whose words to their allies you described: The bounty is in the hand of God, that success in faith and guidance to Islam is in the hand of God and to Him, not to you or to the rest of His creation. He gives it to whomever He wills of His creation, meaning: He gives it to whomever He wills of His servants, as a refutation from God, the Most High, to them in their saying to their followers: No one is given what you have been given. So God, the Most High, said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: That is not up to you, rather it is up to God, in whose hand are all things, and to Him is the bounty and in whose hand He gives it to whomever He wills. And God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing, meaning: God is All-Encompassing in His bounty to whomever He wills to bestow it upon, All-Knowing, the All-Knowing of who among them is worthy of bounty.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: “Say, ‘Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills,’” he said: Islam.

x: What he means by his saying:
h
He singles out for His mercy whomever He wills
, is the verb yafʿala from the saying of the speaker: I singled out so-and-so with such-and-such, I singled him out with it.
As for his mercy, in this context, it is Islam and the Qur’an, along with prophethood, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He chooses for His mercy whomever He wills, he said: Prophethood, He chooses for it whomever He wills.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: He chooses for His mercy whomever He wills, he said: He chooses for prophethood whomever He wills.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: He chooses for His mercy whom He wills, he said: the Qur’an and Islam.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: the same. And God is the possessor of great bounty, meaning: He is the possessor of bounty with which He bestows it upon whomever He loves and wills of His creation. Then He described His bounty as great, saying: His bounty is great, because nothing is like Him in the greatness of His position among those whom He favors over Him [with bounty] from the favors of His creation, and nothing comes close to Him in the majesty of its importance or approaches it.

x: This is report from God Almighty: that among the People of the Book - and they are the Jews from the Children of Israel - are people of trust who fulfill their trust and do not betray it, and among them is the one who betrays his trust, is wicked in his oath, and considers it permissible.

What is the reason for God Almighty informing His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of this, when you know that people have always been like this: some of them fulfill their trusts and some of them betray them?

God Almighty intended, by informing the believers of their report - as He explained in His Book with these verses - to warn them against entrusting them with their money, and to frighten them from being deceived by them, because many of them consider the money of the believers permissible. The interpretation of the statement: Among the People of the Book is he who, O Muhammad, if you entrust him with a great deal of wealth, he will return it to you and will not deceive you concerning it. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, he will deceive you concerning it and will not return it to you unless you insist on litigation and demand it from him. The letter ba in his saying: with a dinar and ala alternate in this topic, as one says: I passed by him and I passed by him.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
Except as long as you are standing on it
Some of them said: Except as long as you are suing him.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except as long as you are standing upon it
, except what you seek and follow.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except as long as you are standing on it
, he said: It requires it of him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except as long as you are standing upon it
, he said: Persistent.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Except as long as you are standing over his head.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: Except as long as I am standing over him, meaning: He acknowledges his trust as long as I am standing over his head, but if you stand up and then come to seek him, you are a disbeliever - the one who fulfills and the one who denies.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the one that says: The meaning of this is: Except as long as I am standing up for it by demanding and exacting it. From their saying: So-and-so exacted my right from so-and-so until he extracted it for me, meaning he worked to free him and strove to extract it from him until he extracted it. Because God the Almighty described them as making the wealth of the illiterate permissible, and that among them are those who do not pay what they owe except by severe exacting and demanding. Standing up for the one who owes the debt does not require him to move from what he is doing by making permissible what is permissible for him, but it may be - along with his considering what he owes to the owner of the right permissible - to extracting it by exacting, litigating and litigating. So that exacting is the owner of the money taking his right from the one who owes it.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: that whoever among the Jews considers treachery permissible, and denies the rights of the Arab that are due to him, and does not pay what the Arab entrusted to him except as long as he is a claimant and demands it from him, for the sake of saying: There is no blame upon us for what we have taken from the Arabs’ money and no sin, because they are not on the right path, and they are polytheists. Surat Al Imran 3:75 And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, he will return it to you. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, he will not return it to you unless you remain standing over him. That is because they say, "
h
There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones
," and they speak a lie about God while they know.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we said about it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: That is because they said, ‘We have no claim against the unlettered people,’ the verse. The Jews said: We have no claim against the Arabs’ money that we have taken.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones
, he said: There is no blame upon us concerning the polytheists, meaning those who are not from the People of the Book.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: That is because they said, ‘We have no responsibility for the illiterate.’ He said: It will be said to him: Why do you not fulfill your trust? He will say: There is no blame on us for the money of the Arabs, God has made it lawful for us!!

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: When the verse was revealed: “And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you except as long as you stand over him. That is because they say, ‘We have no responsibility for the unlettered ones,’” the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The enemies of God have lied. There is nothing that existed in the Age of Ignorance but that it is under my feet, except for trusts, for they are returned to the righteous and the wicked.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hisham bin Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Yaʿqub al-Qummi, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr, he said:
m: When the Jews said: We have no right to take the money of the illiterate, meaning taking their money, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: Except that it is under these two feet of mine, except for the trust, for it is to be fulfilled, and he did not say more than that.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: That is because they said, ‘
h
There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones
,’ that is because the People of the Book used to say: There is no blame upon us concerning what we take from these people, because they are unlettered. So that is what He said:
h
There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones
, to the end of the verse.

x: Others said about that, what:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: “That is because they said: We have no right to deal with the unlettered ones.” He said: The Jews pledged allegiance to some Muslims during the pre-Islamic period, and when they converted to Islam, they demanded the price of their sales from them, and they said: You have no trust from us, and we have no right to judge you, because you have abandoned the religion that you were following! He said: And they claimed that they found that in their book, so God Almighty said: And they tell lies about God while they know.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa’sa’ah, he said:
m: I said to Ibn Abbas: Do we raid the People of the Book and take a share of their fruits? He said: And you say as the People of the Book said: We have no right to the unlettered!! Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, on the authority of Saʿsaʿah: A man asked Ibn Abbas and said: We take from the wealth of the People of the Book in the war - or: [the cluster], the doubt is from al-Hasan - a chicken and a sheep. Ibn Abbas said: What do you say? He said: We say: There is no problem with that! He said: This is like what the People of the Book said: We have no responsibility for the illiterate! If they pay the jizyah, their wealth is not permissible for you except with their willing consent.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Those among them who say: There is no blame upon us for the wealth of the illiterate Arabs if we betray them, they say - by saying that God has permitted that for us, so there is no blame upon us for betraying them and abandoning their judgment - lying about God, intentionally committing a sin by saying a lie about God, that He has permitted that for them.

i: And that is what the Almighty said:
x: and they know, as: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: He tells a lie about God, and He knows it.
He means the one among them who says - if it is said to him: Why do you not fulfill your trust? -: There is no blame on us regarding the money of the Arabs, God has made it permissible for us!

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And they tell lies about God while they know, meaning: their claim that they found in their book their saying: We have no authority over the unlettered.
