x: This is a statement from God, the Almighty, about what those who give their trust to those who entrusted it to fear God and are aware of Him, in His sight. So He, the Most High, said: The matter is not as those liars against God say from among the Jews, that there is no blame or sin upon them in the wealth of the illiterate. Then He said: Yes, but he who fulfills his covenant and fears God, meaning: but he who fulfills his covenant, and that is His command to them which He commanded them in the Torah, of believing in Muhammad and what he brought to them. The letter ha in His statement: whoever fulfills his covenant refers back to the name God in His statement: and they tell lies about God. He says: Yes, whoever fulfills the covenant of God which He made in His Book, so he believes in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believes in him and in what he brought from God, from returning the trust to the one who entrusted it to him, and other than that of God’s commands and prohibitions, and fears God, he says: and fears what God has forbidden him from, from disbelieving in Him, and all of His sins that He has forbidden him, so he avoids that out of awareness of God’s threat and fear of His punishment, for God loves the righteous, meaning: for God loves those who fear Him, so they fear His punishment and are wary of His torment, so they avoid what He has forbidden them and prohibited them from, and they obey Him in what He has commanded them to do.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to say: It is avoiding polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God meaning: fears polytheism then indeed, God loves the righteous, meaning: those who fear polytheism. We have explained the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding this and the correct statement regarding it, with evidence indicating it, in what has passed in our book, sufficiently so that we do not need to repeat it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Those who exchange - by abandoning the covenant of God that He entrusted to them, and His commandment that He commanded them in the books that God revealed to His prophets, for following Muhammad, believing in him, and acknowledging him and what he brought from God - and their false oaths by which they make lawful what God has forbidden them of the money of the people that they were entrusted with, for a price, meaning: a lowly exchange and substitute for the worldly goods and its debris, for them there is no portion in the Hereafter, meaning: for those who do that there is no share in the good things of the Hereafter, nor a portion of the bliss of Paradise and what God has prepared for its people in it, without others. We have previously explained the differences of the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of the Creator, and we have sufficiently demonstrated the first of their statements regarding that as being correct.
As for his saying:
h
And God will not speak to them

, it means: God will not speak to them in a way that pleases them. And He will not look at them, he says: He will not be kind to them with good, out of hatred from God for them, like the saying of one who says to another: Look at me as God looks at you, meaning: Be kind to me and God will be kind to you with good and mercy. And as it is said to a man: May God not hear your supplication, meaning: May God not answer you, and nothing is hidden from God.

i: And as the poet said:
x: I called upon God until I was afraid that God might not hear what I was saying.
And His statement:
h
And He will not purify them
, meaning: He will not cleanse them from the filth of their sins and disbelief. And for them is a painful punishment, meaning: And for them is a painful punishment.
The interpreters differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed, and who it meant.
Some of them said that it was revealed about some of the Jewish rabbis.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: This verse was revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price, about Abu Rafi’, Kinanah ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Al-Ash’ath bin Qais and his opponent.
Who said that?

c: Abu al-Sa’ib Salim ibn Junadah told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever swears an oath in which he is wicked in order to seize the wealth of a Muslim, will meet God while He is angry with him.’ Al-Ash’ath ibn Qays said: ‘By God, that was about me. There was a piece of land between me and a Jewish man, and he denied it. So I brought him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: ‘Do you have proof?’ I said: ‘No!’ So he said to the Jew: ‘Swear.’ I said: ‘O Messenger of God, then he will swear and my wealth will be lost!’ Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price…’” Mujahid bin Musa narrated that Yazid bin Harun narrated that Jarir bin Hazim narrated to us, on the authority of Adi bin Adi, on the authority of Raja bin Haywah and Al-Aras, that they both narrated to him, on the authority of his father Adi bin Umaira, who said: “There was a dispute between Imru’ al-Qais and a man from Hadhramaut. They went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to the Hadrami: ‘Your evidence, otherwise I swear.’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, if he swears, he will take my land!’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever swears a false oath in order to seize the right of his brother, will meet God while He is angry with him.’ Imru’ al-Qais said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the reward for one who abandons it, knowing that it is true?’ He said: ‘Paradise.’ He said: ‘Then I bear witness that I have abandoned it.’” Jarir said: I was with Ayoub al-Sakhtiyani when we heard this hadith from Adi, and Ayoub said: ‘Adi said in the hadith of Al-Aras bin Umaira: Then this verse was revealed. Those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price to the end of the verse. Jarir said: I did not remember that day from Adi.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Others said: Al-Ash'ath bin Qais and a man disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a piece of land that was in the possession of that man, who had taken it to strengthen him during the pre-Islamic period. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Present your evidence. The man said: No one will testify for me against Al-Ash'ath! He said: Then you may take his oath. So Al-Ash'ath stood up to swear, and God, the Almighty, revealed this verse. Al-Ash'ath declined and said: I call God and you to witness that my opponent is truthful. So he returned his land to him, and gave him a great deal of his own land, for fear that something of his right would remain in his possession, and it would be for that man's descendants after him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Whoever swears an oath to obtain money while he is wicked, will meet God while He is angry with him. Then God revealed confirmation of that: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price Al-An’am 2:17. Then Al-Ash'ath bin Qais came out to us and said: What did Abu Abd Al-Rahman tell you?

c: So we told him
m: what he said, and he said: He is right, for it was revealed! There was a dispute between me and a man over a well, so we brought the dispute to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your two witnesses or his oath. I said: Then he swears and does not care! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath by which he deserves money is a sinner, and he will meet God while He is angry with him. Then God Almighty revealed the confirmation of that: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price, the verse.

x: Others said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us:

c: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed me, on the authority of Aamer:
m: A man displayed his merchandise at the beginning of the day, and at the end of the day a man came to bargain with him, so he swore that he had prevented it at the beginning of the day for such and such, and if it had not been for the evening he would not have sold it for that. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price the verse, to: and for them is a painful punishment, God has placed them in the same position as the magicians.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Imran bin Husain used to say: Whoever swears a false oath to seize his brother’s wealth, let him take his seat in Hell. Someone said to him: Did you hear something from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said to them: You will surely find that. Then he recited this verse: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price Al-Baqarah 2:170.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said, Hussain bin Ali told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Hisham, he said,
m: Muhammad said, on the authority of Imran bin Husain: Whoever swears an oath that is not binding, let him face down his seat in the Fire. Then he recited this entire verse: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, who said:
m: A false oath is one of the major sins. Then he recited: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Abdullah bin Masoud used to say: We used to think, while we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and Surat Al Imran 3:77 Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price - those will have no portion in the Hereafter,
h
and God will not speak to them

, nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment. grant him peace, that among the sins that are not forgiven is the oath of patience, if its owner commits an immoral act in it.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price Al-Baqarah 2:170.
Then he recited this entire verse: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And among the People of the Book, who are the Jews who were around the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his time, are the Children of Israel. The ha and the mim in his saying: of them refer to the People of the Book whom he mentioned in his saying:
h
And among the People of the Book is he who

, if you entrust him with a great amount, he will return it to you. And His statement: For a party, meaning: a group, they distort, meaning: they distort, their tongues with the Book so that you may think it is from the Book, meaning: so that you may think that what they distort with their speech is from the Book of God and His revelation. God Almighty says: And what is that which they have distorted their tongues with, distorted it and innovated from the Book of God, and they claim that what they have distorted their tongues with of distortion, lies and falsehood and inserted into the Book of God, is from God, meaning: from what God has revealed to His prophets, and it is not from God, meaning: And what is that which they have distorted their tongues with, so that they innovated from what God has revealed to any of His prophets, but rather it is from what they have innovated from themselves, inventing against God.

God Almighty says: And they tell lies about God while they know. By that, He means that they intentionally lie about God, bear false witness against Him, and add to the Book of God things that are not from it, seeking leadership and the lowly debris of this world. And similar to what we said about the meaning of they distort the Book with their tongues, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And among them is a party who distort the Scripture with their tongues, he said: they distort it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them is a party who distort the Scripture with their tongues, until he reached: and they know, they are the enemies of God, the Jews, they distorted the Book of God, and innovated in it, and claimed that it was from God.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them is a party who distort the Scripture with their tongues, until he reached: and they know, they are the enemies of God, the Jews, they distorted the Book of God, and innovated in it, and claimed that it was from God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And among them is a party who distort the Scripture with their tongues so that you may think it is from the Scripture
, and they are the Jews, they used to add to the Book of God what God had not revealed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And among them is a party who distort the Scripture with their tongues, he said: A party of the People of the Book, distort their tongues, and that is their distortion of it from its place.

x: The origin of lay is twisting and turning. It is from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so twisted the hand of so-and-so, meaning he twisted it and turned it.

i: And from this is the saying of the poet:
x: God, who is victorious, twisted his hand.

It is said: He twisted his hand and tongue, twisting, and no one twisted someone’s back, if no one defeated him, and no one twisted his back, and he is very persistent, if he is very argumentative, patient with it, and is not defeated in it, the poet said: If Laila had any strength of enmity, I would have twisted the necks of her opponents.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: It is not appropriate for any human being. And the word humans is the plural of children of Adam and has no singular form, such as people and creation. It may be a name for one person. That God should give him the Book means that God should send down His Book to him, and wisdom means that He should teach him the details of wisdom, and prophethood means that He should give him prophethood, then he should say to the people, ‘Be servants to me instead of God’ means that he should call the people to worship himself instead of God, and God has given him what He has given him of the Book, wisdom, and prophethood. But if God gives him that, then he is calling them to knowledge of God, and urging them to know the laws of His religion, and to be leaders in knowledge of God’s commands and prohibitions, and leaders in obeying and worshipping Him, by being teachers of the Book to the people, and by being its students.

It was said that this verse was revealed about a group of people from the People of the Book who said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you call us to worship you? As: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi’ al-Qurazi said - when the Jewish and Christian rabbis from Najran gathered at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he called them to Islam -: Do you want, O Muhammad, for us to worship you, as the Christians worship Jesus, son of Mary? A Christian man from Najran called al-Rabis said: Is that what you want from us, O Muhammad, and to which you are calling us! Or something like that. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God forbid that we worship other than God, or command the worship of other than Him!
He did not send me for that, nor did He command me for that! Or something like that. Then God Almighty revealed regarding that from their statement:
h
It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood
, the verse up to His saying: After you have become Muslims.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Rafi’ al-Qurazi said, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood

, then he should say to the people, ‘Be my servants instead of God.’ He said: It is not befitting for a human being that God should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood, then he should command his servants to take him as a lord instead of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: There were some Jews who worshipped people instead of their Lord, by distorting the Book of God from its place. So God Almighty said:
h
It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood
, then he should say to the people, ‘Be servants to me instead of God,’ then he should command the people to do other than what God revealed in His Book.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: But He says to them: Be rabbis, so He left out the statement, sufficing with the indication of the speech on it. As for his saying: Be rabbis, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.
Some of them said: It means: Be wise and knowledgeable.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: Be rabbis, he said: wise scholars.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: Be rabbis, he said: wise scholars.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu Razin,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: h
But be rabbis
, wise scholars.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: Be rabbis, he said: Be jurists and scholars.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Be rabbis, he said: Jurists.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Qasim told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But be rabbis
, he said: jurists.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But be rabbis
, he said: Be jurists and scholars.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Mansur bin al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Abu Razin,
m: regarding his statement: Be scholars of God, he said: Scholars and wise men. Muammar said: Qatada said.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: Be rabbis, as for the rabbis, they are the wise jurists.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The rabbis are the learned jurists, and they are above the scholars.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But be rabbis
, meaning: Be wise and knowledgeable.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Munjab,
m: who said: Bishr bin Amara narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hamza Al-Thamali, on the authority of Yahya bin Aqil, regarding his statement: The rabbis and the scholars (al-Ma’idah 5:63), he said: The jurists and scholars.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Munjab,
m: who said: Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

c: Ibn Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me, he said, Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan Al-Ashqar told us, he said, Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Be rabbis, he said: Be wise and knowledgeable scholars.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Be rabbis, he said: Be jurists and scholars.

x: Others said: Rather, they are the pious wise men.
Who said that?

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Be pious people
, he said: Wise and pious people.

x: Others said: Rather, they are the people’s rulers and leaders.
Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His statement: Be rabbis, he said: The rabbis are those who educate the people, the rulers of this matter, educate them: they are in charge of them, and he recited: Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them? (al-Ma’idah 5:63), he said: The rabbis are the rulers, and the scholars are the scholars.

x: The most correct of the sayings in my opinion about the rabbis is that they are the plural of rabbi, and that the rabbi is related to the rabban, the one who raises people, and he is the one who corrects their affairs, raises them, and takes care of them.

i: From this is the saying of Alqamah ibn ʿAbdah:
x: I was a man to whom I entrusted my lute, and before you I was raised, and I was lost, lutes.
He means by his saying: You raised me: My guardian Surat Al Imran 3:79
h
It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood

and then he should say to the people, "Be my servants instead of God." But be devout scholars of the Scripture because you have been taught the Scripture and because you have been studying. and caretaker before you was someone who would raise and reform him, but they did not reform him, but they lost me, so I was lost. It is said: So-and-so is the Lord of my affair, so he is lord of it, and he is its rabb. If it is intended to exaggerate in praising him, it is said: he is a rabbān, just as it is said: he is na’sān, from their saying: na’sa yan’usu. Most of the nouns that come in the form fa’lān are the verbs whose past tense is fa’l, such as their saying: he is drunk, thirsty, and rayyān from sakāra yasakār, ‘atash ya’tash, and rawā yarrawā.

It may come from what has a past tense is fa’l, such as what we said about na’sa yan’usu and rabb yarwā. If the matter is as we have described, and the rabbi is as we have mentioned, and the rabbi is the one attributed to the one who has the description described, and the one who is knowledgeable in jurisprudence and wisdom from the reformers raises the affairs of the people, by teaching them good, and calling them to what is in their best interest, and likewise the wise one who is pious to God, and the governor who oversees the affairs of the people according to the method that the just reformers of the affairs of creation have been entrusted with, by doing for them what is good for their immediate and future lives, and what benefits them in their religion and their worldly life, then they all deserve to be among those included in the words of God Almighty:
h
But be rabbis
. So the Rabbaniyyun are the pillars of the people in jurisprudence, knowledge, and matters of religion and the world.

That is why Mujahid said: They are above the scholars, because the scholars are the scholars, and the Rabbani is the one who combines knowledge and jurisprudence, insight into politics, management, and taking care of the affairs of the subjects, and what is good for them in their worldly and religious affairs.

The reading of this differed. The majority of the reciters of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read: By what you know with the opening of the ta’ and the lightening of the lam, meaning: by your knowledge of the Book, your study of it, and your reading. They based their choice of reading it as such on the fact that the correct reading, as well, if the emphasis was on the lam and the ta’ was a damma, then the correct reading would be: tadrusun with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the ra’. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it as: By your teaching the Book with a damma on the ta’ of you teach and a shaddah on the lam, meaning: by your teaching people the Book and studying it. They based their choice on the fact that whoever described them as having taught, described them as having knowledge, since they do not know except after knowing what they know.

They said: There is no one described as having knowledge, except that he is described as having knowledge. They said: As for the one described as having knowledge, he is not described as having taught others.
They said: The first of the two readings is more correct and more eloquent in praising the people, and that is describing them as having taught people the Book, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid
m: that he read: Because you taught the Book and because you studied it, lightened by the accusative of the ta’, and Ibn Uyaynah said: They did not teach it until they taught it!

x: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads it with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam. Because God Almighty described the people as people who are a pillar for the people in their religion and their worldly affairs, and people who reform them and their affairs and educate them. God Almighty says:
h
But be rabbis
, based on what we explained before about the meaning of rabbi.

c: Then God Almighty informed us
m: about them that they became people who reformed and educated people by teaching them the Book of their Lord. And their study of it: its recitation. It has been said: Their study is jurisprudence. The most similar of the two interpretations to the study is what we said: from the recitation of the Book, because it is an appositive to his saying:
h
You learn the Book

, and the Book is the Qur’an, so the study should be intended to mean the study of the Qur’an, which is more appropriate than it being intended to mean the study of jurisprudence, which was not mentioned.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Yahya bin Adam said, Abu Zakariya said: Asim used to recite it: Because you taught the Book, he said: the Qur’an, And because you studied, he said: jurisprudence. The meaning of the verse is: But he says to them: Be, O people, masters of the people, and their leaders in the affairs of their religion and their worldly affairs, and be pious by teaching them the Book of God and what is in it of what is permissible and forbidden, what is obligatory and recommended, and all the rest of what it contains of meanings of the affairs of their religion, and by your recitation of it and your study of it.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.

The majority of the reciters of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read: By what you know with the opening of the ta’ and the lightening of the lam, meaning: by your knowledge of the Book, your study of it, and your reading.

They based their choice of reading it as such on the fact that the correct reading, as well, if the emphasis was on the lam and the ta’ was a damma, then the correct reading would be: tadrusun with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the ra’.

Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads it with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam.

The most similar of the two interpretations to the study is what we said: from the recitation of the Book, because it is an appositive to his saying: You learn the Book, and the Book is the Qur’an, so the study should be intended to mean the study of the Qur’an, which is more appropriate than it being intended to mean the study of jurisprudence, which was not mentioned.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam said, Abu Zakariya said: Asim used to recite it: Because you taught the Book, he said: the Qur’an, And because you studied, he said: jurisprudence.

x: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: nor does He command you. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Madinah read it as: And He does not command you, as a beginning from God with the report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He does not command you, O people, to take the angels and the prophets as lords. The reciters of that also cited a reading that they mentioned from Ibn Masoud that he used to recite, which is: And He does not command you, so they used the introduction of lan as evidence of the interruption of the speech from what preceded it, and the beginning of a new piece of report. They said: So when la was replaced in our recitation, it became obligatory to recite it in the nominative case.

Some of the Kufians and Basrans read it as: nor does He command you, with the ra’ in the accusative case, in apposition to His statement: Then He says to the people. Their interpretation was: It was not for a human being that God should give him the Book, then he should say to the people, nor that he should command you, meaning: Nor was it for him to command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords.

The more correct of the two readings in this regard is: nor does He command you, in the accusative case, in connection with what precedes it, with the interpretation: It is not for a human being that God should give him the Book, wisdom, and prophethood, then he should say to the people, Be my servants instead of God, nor that he should command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Because the verse was revealed regarding the people who said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you want us to worship you? So God, may He be glorified and exalted, informed them that it is not for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call the people to worship himself, nor to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Rather, what is for him is to call them to be lords. As for the one who claimed that he read it in the nominative case, that it is in the reading of Abdullah: And He will not command you as evidence for the correctness of his reading in the nominative case, then that is a report whose chain of transmission is not correct.

Rather, it is a report narrated by Hajjaj, on the authority of Harun al-A’war: that it is in the reading of Abdullah likewise. If that was a report whose chain of transmission was correct, then there would be no argument in it for the one who argues. Because what was correct in the reading of the Book that the Muslims came with as an inheritance from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is not permissible to abandon it for the sake of interpretation according to a reading attributed to some of the Companions, transmitted by someone in whose transmission errors and forgetfulness are permissible.

The interpretation of the verse is: It is not for the Prophet to command you, O people, to take the angels and the prophets as lords - meaning by that gods to be worshipped instead of God - just as it is not for him to say to them: Be my servants instead of God. Then He, the Most High, said - denying that His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would command His servants to do that - Would your Prophet command you to disbelieve, O people, by denying the Oneness of God, after you were Muslims, meaning: after you were submissive to Him in obedience, humbled before Him in worship: meaning that this would never happen from Him. And: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: “And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords.”

As for the one who claimed that he read it in the nominative case, that it is in the reading of Abdullah: And He will not command you as evidence for the correctness of his reading in the nominative case, then that is a report whose chain of transmission is not correct.
Rather, it is a report narrated by Hajjaj, on the authority of Harun al-A’war: that it is in the reading of Abdullah likewise.

Because what was correct in the reading of the Book that the Muslims came with as an inheritance from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is not permissible to abandon it for the sake of interpretation according to a reading attributed to some of the Companions, transmitted by someone in whose transmission errors and forgetfulness are permissible.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And remember, O People of the Book,
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

, meaning: when God took a covenant from the prophets, and their covenant, what they trusted upon themselves to obey God in what He commanded them and forbade them. We have explained the origin of the covenant, with the differences of the people of interpretation, sufficiently. When I have given you a Book and wisdom, and the reading of that differed. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as lama aatiyyatukum with the opening of the lam of lama, except that they differed in the reading: atayyatukum.
Some of them read it as: I have come to you in the singular form.
Others read it as: We have brought you in the plural. Then the Arabs differed about whether it was read in this way.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The lam that comes with ma at the beginning of a sentence is the lam of initiation, like when someone says: Zayd is better than you, because ma is a noun and what comes after it is a relative clause for it, and the lam in you will surely believe in him and you will surely support him is the lam of an oath, as if he said: By God, you will surely believe in him, it is emphasized at the beginning of the sentence and at the end of it, like one says: By God, if you had come to me, such and such would have happened, and one may dispense with it. So in you will surely believe in him, it is emphasized with the lam at the end of the sentence, and one may dispense with it, and the predicate of what I have given you of the Book and wisdom is made you will surely believe in it. Like: To Abdullah, by God, you will come to him. He said: If you wish, you can make the predicate of what “of the Book,” meaning: when I have given you, the Book and wisdom, and of is redundant.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa made a mistake in all of this and said: The lam that enters at the beginning of the conditional clause is answered with the answers of oaths. It is said: To whoever stands, I will give him and To whoever stands, I will do well. So if ma and la are in their answer, it is known that the lam is not an emphasis of the first, because ma and la are put in its place, so it is like the first, and it is an answer to the first. He said: As for his saying:
h
When I gave you from the Book and wisdom

, meaning omitting min, this is a mistake. Because min that enters and exits does not take the place of nouns. He said: Nor does it occur in the report either, it only occurs in denial, interrogation, and conditional clause.

The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this verse - according to the reading of those who read it with the opening of the lam - is that his saying: lama means lamhama, and that ma is a particle of reward to which the lam was inserted, and the verb was made with it into faʿl, then it was answered with what oaths are answered with, so the first lam became an oath, since it was met with the answer to the oath.
Others read it as: When I brought you with a kasra on the lam of lama. This is the reading of a group of the people of Kufa. Then the readers of that differed in their interpretation of it.
Some of them said: Its meaning, if read in this way, is:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
for what I gave you, so what is in this reading means what they have. The interpretation of the statement is:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

for what He gave them of the Book and wisdom, then a messenger came to you, meaning: Then if My messenger came to you, meaning: the mention of Muhammad in the Torah, you will believe in him, meaning: your belief in him will be for what you have in the Torah of his mention.
Others among them said: The interpretation of that, if it is read with a kasra on the lam of lama is:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, for that which He gave them of wisdom. Then He made His statement:
h
You shall believe in it from taking

, taking the covenant. Just as it is said in speech: I took your covenant that you shall do. Because taking the covenant is like taking an oath. So the interpretation of the speech according to the one who said this Surat Al Imran 3:81 And [mention] when God took a covenant from the prophets, “Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming that which is with you, you must believe in him and support him.” He said, “Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My covenant?” They said, “We have acknowledged.” He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.” statement was: And when God took an oath from the prophets for that which He gave them of the Book and wisdom, whenever there came to them a messenger confirming what was with them, that they would believe in him and support him.
The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

, ‘When I gave you’, with the lam open. This is because God, the Almighty, took a covenant from all the prophets to believe in every messenger He sent to His creation in what He sent him with, whether he was one of those to whom He gave a book or one to whom He did not give a book. This is because it is not permissible to describe any of the prophets and messengers of God, the Almighty, as being one of those who were permitted to disbelieve in any of His messengers. Since this is the case, and it is known that some of them were given the book and some of them were not given the book, it is clear that the reading of the one who reads it: When I gave you, with the lam closed, meaning: for the sake of what I gave you of the book, has no basis in understanding, except through a far-fetched interpretation and profound deduction.
Then the people of interpretation differed about the one who took his covenant to believe in the messengers of God who came to him, confirming what he had.

Some of them said: God only took a covenant from the People of the Book regarding this, not from their prophets. They cited as evidence for the validity of their statement the words: You shall believe in him and support him. They said: The nations to whom the messengers were sent were commanded to believe in the messengers of God and support them against those who opposed them. As for the messengers, there is no reason to command them to support anyone, because they are the ones who need help against those who oppose them from the disbelieving people of Adam. As for them, they do not help the disbelievers in their disbelief nor support them. They said: If there is no one other than them and the disbelieving nations, then who is the one who supports the prophet, so that a covenant is taken from him to support him?
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom,’ he said: It is a mistake by the writer, and in the reading of Ibn Masoud it is: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

, he said: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, and that is how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite it. Al-Rabi’ said: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, they are only the People of the Scripture. He said: And that is how Ubayy bin Ka’b used to recite it. Al-Rabi’ said: Do you not see that He says:
h
Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you
, that you must believe in him and support him? He says: You must believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and support him. He said: They are the People of the Scripture.

x: Others said: Rather, the one who took their covenant with that was the prophets, not their nations.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ahmad bin Hazim told me, they said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God only took a covenant from the prophets from their people.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, that some of them would believe in others.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you’ verse, he said: God took a covenant from the first of the prophets, to believe and have faith in what the last of them brought.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, he said:
m: God Almighty did not send a prophet - Adam and those after him - except that He took a covenant from him regarding Muhammad: If he is sent while he is alive, he will believe in him and support him, and he will command him to take a covenant from his people, so He said:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, ‘What I have given you of the Book and wisdom’, the verse.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book,’ the verse: This is a covenant that God took from the prophets that they would believe in each other and convey the Book of God and His messages. So the prophets conveyed the Book of God and His messages to their people, and He took a covenant from them - in what their messengers conveyed to them - that they would believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in him and support him.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets

, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom,’ the verse. He said: God, the Almighty, did not send a prophet since Noah except that He took a covenant from him that he would believe in Muhammad and support him if he emerged while he was alive, and if not, He took a covenant from his people that they would believe in him and support him if he emerged while they were alive.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abdul Kabir bin Abdul Majeed Abu Bakr Al Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansour told us, he said,
m: I asked Al Hassan about his saying:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, ‘What I have given you of the Book and wisdom,’ the entire verse, he said: God took a covenant from the prophets: The last of you will surely convey to the first of you, and do not differ.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that he took a covenant from the prophets and their nations, so he was satisfied with mentioning the prophets instead of mentioning their nations, because in mentioning taking a covenant from the one being followed, there is evidence of taking it from the one being followed, because nations follow the prophets.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Then he mentioned what he took from them - meaning from the People of the Book - and from their prophets of the covenant to believe in him - meaning to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace - when he came to them, and their acknowledgment of him for themselves. So he said:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, ‘What I have given you of the Book and wisdom’ to the end of the verse.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told us, he said, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is the report of God taking a covenant from His prophets to believe in one another, and the prophets taking a covenant from their nations and their followers in the same way that their Lord took from them to believe in God’s prophets and messengers in what they brought to them. Because the prophets, peace be upon them, were sent to their nations with that. And none of those who believed in the messengers claimed that a prophet was sent to a nation to deny one of God’s prophets and His proofs among His servants, rather all of them, even if some nations denied some of God’s prophets, by denying his prophethood, acknowledging that whoever’s prophethood is proven to be true, then they are to be judged for believing in him. So that is a covenant that all of them acknowledge. There is no meaning in the claim of those who claim that the covenant was taken from the nations and not from the prophets.

c: Because God Almighty has informed us that
m: He took that from the prophets. So whether someone says: Her Lord did not take that from her or he says: He did not command her to convey what she was sent for, and God Almighty has stated that He commanded her to convey it, because they are both two pieces of report from God about her: one of them is that He took that from her, and the other of them is that He commanded her. If doubt is permissible about one of them, it is permissible about the other. As for what Al-Rabi’ bin Anas cited as evidence that what is meant by that is the People of the Book, from his saying:
h
You will believe in him and support him

, that is not evidence of the correctness of what he said. Because the prophets were commanded to believe in each other, and to believe in each other, as support from each other. Then they differed about those meant by his saying:
h
Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you
, so you must believe in him and support him.

x: Some of them said: Those meant by that are the prophets, whose covenants were taken that they would believe each other and support him. We have mentioned the narration of that from the one who said it.

Others said: They are the People of the Book, who were commanded to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, if God sent him to support him, and He took a covenant from them in their books to that effect. We have also mentioned the narration of that from those who said it.
Others said, among those who said: Those meant by God taking His covenant from them in this verse are the prophets. His statement:
h
Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you
, means the People of the Book.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Ibn Tawus told us, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from the prophets
, ‘What I have given you of the Book and wisdom,’ he said, God took a covenant from the prophets that they would believe in one another, then He said:
h
Then there came to you a Messenger confirming what is with you

, you must believe in him and support him, he said: So this verse is for the Surat Al Imran 3:81 And [mention] when God took a covenant from the prophets, “Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming that which is with you, you must believe in him and support him.” He said, “Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My covenant?” They said, “We have acknowledged.” He said, “Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.” People of the Book, God took a covenant from them that they would believe in Muhammad and believe in him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told me, on the authority of his father, he said, Qatada said:
m: God took a covenant from the prophets: that they would believe in one another, and that they would convey God’s Book and His message to His servants. So the prophets conveyed God’s Book and His messages to their people, and they took covenants from the People of the Book - in their book, in what their messengers conveyed to them -: that they would believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in him and support him.

x: The most correct of the sayings in our view regarding the interpretation of this verse is that all of that is report from God Almighty about His prophets that He took their covenant with Him, and obligated them to call their nations to Him and acknowledge Him. Because the beginning of the verse is report from God Almighty about His prophets that He took their covenant, then He described that by which He took their covenant, saying: He is such and such and He is such and such.

c: We only said that what God informed us that
m: He took covenants from His prophets regarding that, the prophets took covenants from their nations regarding it, because they were sent to call the servants of God to the judgment with what they were commanded to judge in themselves, of believing in the messengers of God, as we explained before.
b.via: We only said that what God

x: The interpretation of the verse is: And remember, O people of the Book, when God took a covenant from the prophets, “Whatever I give you, O prophets, of the Book and wisdom, and then there comes to you a Messenger from Me confirming what is with you, you must believe in him - he says: you must believe him - and you must support him.”
Al-Saddī said about this:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: When I came to you, he says to the Jews: I took the covenant of the prophets through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is what is mentioned in the book that you have. The interpretation of this is according to what Al-Suddi mentioned: And remember, O people of the Book, when God took a covenant from the prophets, saying, What I have given you, O Jews, of the Book and wisdom. What Al-Suddi said was an interpretation that had a point, if the revelation had been: with what I have given you, but the revelation with the lam is when I have given you. It is not permissible in the language of any of the Arabs to say: God took a covenant from the prophets when I have given you, meaning: with what I have given you.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And when God took the covenant of the prophets with what was mentioned, He, may His praise be glorified, said to them: Have you acknowledged the covenant that you pledged to Me upon: that whenever a messenger comes to you from Me confirming what is with you,
h
you will believe in him and support him
, “and have you taken upon that My covenant”?

i: He says:
x: And you have taken, upon what you pledged to Me upon of believing in the messengers who come to you confirming what is with you from Me and undertaking to support them, My covenant.

Meaning My covenant and My testament, and you accepted that from Me and were pleased with it. Taking: is acceptance - in this context - and satisfaction, from their saying: the governor took the pledge of allegiance from him, meaning: he pledged allegiance to him and accepted his rule and was satisfied with it. We have explained the meaning of persistence according to the differences of those who differed about it, and the correct statement about it in what has passed before, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The letter fa was deleted from his statement: He said, ‘Did you acknowledge?’ because it is the beginning of a statement, as we have explained in similar examples previously. As for his saying: They said, ‘We acknowledge,’ he means by it: The prophets from whom God took a covenant with what was mentioned in this verse said: We acknowledge what you have obligated us to believe in your messengers whom you send, confirming what is with us of your books, and their support.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God said: So bear witness, O prophets, to what I took from you as a covenant of faith in believing in My messengers who come to you with confirmation of what is with you of the Book and wisdom, and their support over yourselves and over your followers from the nations if you take their covenant on that, and I am with you among the witnesses over you and over them in that, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib,
m: regarding his statement: He said, ‘Then bear witness,’ meaning: bear witness against your nations with that, and I am with you among the witnesses, against you and against them.

evidence.text: When I have given you a Book and wisdom, and the reading of that differed.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as lama aatiyyatukum with the opening of the lam of lama, except that they differed in the reading: atayyatukum.
Some of them read it as: I have come to you in the singular form.
Others read it as: We have brought you in the plural.
Then the Arabs differed about whether it was read in this way.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting this verse - according to the reading of those who read it with the opening of the lam - is that his saying: lama means lamhama, and that ma is a particle of reward to which the lam was inserted, and the verb was made with it into faʿl, then it was answered with what oaths are answered with, so the first lam became an oath, since it was met with the answer to the oath.
Others read it as: When I brought you with a kasra on the lam of lama.
This is the reading of a group of the people of Kufa.
Then the readers of that differed in their interpretation of it.
Some of them said: Its meaning, if read in this way, is: And when God took a covenant from the prophets for what I gave you, so what is in this reading means what they have.
Others among them said: The interpretation of that, if it is read with a kasra on the lam of lama is: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, for that which He gave them of wisdom.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘When I gave you’, with the lam open.

Since this is the case, and it is known that some of them were given the book and some of them were not given the book, it is clear that the reading of the one who reads it: When I gave you, with the lam closed, meaning: for the sake of what I gave you of the book, has no basis in understanding, except through a far-fetched interpretation and profound deduction.

Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom,’ he said: It is a mistake by the writer, and in the reading of Ibn Masoud it is: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding His statement: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, he said: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, and that is how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite it.
He said: And that is how Ubayy bin Ka’b used to recite it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: So whoever turns away from belief in My messengers whom I sent to confirm what was with My prophets of books and wisdom, and from supporting them, and turns away and does not believe in that, and does not support, and breaks his covenant and pact, after that, meaning after the covenant and pact that God took from him, they are the wicked, meaning by that: Those who turn away from belief in the messengers whose matter was described, and supporting them after the covenant and pact that God took from them, they are the wicked, meaning by that: those who have departed from the religion of God and the obedience of their Lord, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib:
m: Whoever turns away from you, O Muhammad, after this covenant from all nations, they are the wicked, they are the disobedient in disbelief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father - Abu Jaʿfar
m: said: meaning Al-Razi - But whoever turns away after that meaning after the covenant and pledge that was taken from them, then those are the wicked.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, [on the authority of his father], on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

x: And these two verses, even though the source of the report of them is from God Almighty, with what He informed that He bore witness and took a covenant from those who took a covenant with Him, from His prophets and messengers, then what is intended by it is to inform those who were around the migration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Jews of the Children of Israel during the days of his life, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what God had taken from them of the covenant and pacts in belief in the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the meaning [of it] is to remind them of what God had taken from their fathers and ancestors of covenants and pacts, and what the prophets of God had known and preceded them in believing in Him, following Him, and supporting Him against those who opposed Him and denied Him, and to inform them of what is in the books of God, which He sent down to His prophets whom He sent to them, of His description and His sign.
The readings differed in the reading of that: the majority of the readers of the Hijaz from Mecca and Medina, and the readers of Kufa read:
h
Do you seek other than the religion of God
, and to Him you will be returned, in the form of address.
Some of the people of Hijaz read it as
h
Do they seek other than the religion of God
? and And to Him they will return with both ya’s, as a report on the absent.
Some of the people of Basra read it as:
h
Do they seek other than the religion of God
? as a statement about the absent person, and to Him you will be returned, with the letter ta as a direct address.

The most correct of these is the reading of those who read: Do you then seek other than the religion of God? as a direct address, and to Him you will be returned, with the letter ta’. Because the verse before it is an address to them, so following the address with its counterpart is more appropriate than diverting the speech to something other than its counterpart. Even though the other interpretation is permissible, for what we have mentioned before: that the narration sometimes brings out the speech with it as a whole address, and sometimes as a report about the absent, and sometimes some of it as an address, and some of it as an absent, so his saying:
h
You seek and to Him you will be returned in this verse is from
that. The interpretation of the statement: O people of the Book,
h
do you seek other than the religion of God
? He says: Do you seek and desire other than the obedience of God?
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth
, He says:
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth

, so they submit to Him in worship, and acknowledge His uniqueness of Lordship, and submit to Him in sincerity of monotheism and divinity, willingly or by compulsion, He says whoever among them submits to Him by obedience, submits to God willingly, and that is like the angels, prophets, and messengers, for they submitted to God willingly, or by compulsion, whoever among them was by compulsion.
The interpreters differed about the meaning and description of the Islam of one who hates Islam.
Some of them said: His Islam is his acknowledgment that God is his Creator and Lord, even if he associates others with Him in worship.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth

. He said: It is like His saying: And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ (al-Zumar 39:38) Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth

, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned, he said: Every human being has acknowledged upon himself that God is my Lord and I am His servant. So whoever associates others with Him in worship, this is the one who has submitted unwillingly, and whoever sincerely worships Him, he is the one who has submitted willingly.

x: Others said: Rather, the conversion of the one who was reluctant among them to Islam was when the covenant was taken from him and he acknowledged it.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth
, willingly or by compulsion, he said: When the covenant was taken.

x: Others said: By the Islam of the one who hates them, he meant the prostration of his shadow.
Who said that?

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, he said, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth
, willingly or by compulsion, he said: The obedient one is the believer, and by compulsion is the shadow of the disbeliever.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: willingly or unwillingly, he said: The prostration of the believer is voluntary, and the prostration of the disbeliever is unwilling.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Unwillingly, he Surat Al Imran 3:83 Is it other than the religion of God that they seek, while to Him have submitted [all] those within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned? said: The prostration of the believer willingly, and the prostration of the shadow of the unbeliever while he is unwilling.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: His face prostrates willingly, and his shadow is unwillingly.

x: Others said: Rather, his Islam is in his heart in the will of God, and his submission to His command, even if he denies His divinity with his tongue.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer:
m: h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth
, he said: They all seek retribution for Him.

x: Others said: He meant by that the conversion of those who converted unwillingly, fearing the sword for themselves.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth
, willingly or by compulsion, the entire verse, he said: Some people were forced to Islam, and some people came willingly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah Al-Bahili told me, he said, Ruh bin Ata’ told us, on the authority of Matar Al-Warraq,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth
, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him they will be returned, he said: The angels willingly, the Ansar willingly, Banu Salim and Abd Al-Qais willingly, and all people unwillingly.

x: Others said that this means that the people of faith converted voluntarily, and that the unbeliever converted in a state of witnessing, when his conversion would not benefit him, out of force.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
Do you seek other than the religion of God

? The verse: As for the believer, he converted willingly, so that benefited him and was accepted from him. As for the disbeliever, he converted reluctantly when that did not benefit him, nor was it accepted from him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth

, willingly or by compulsion, he said: As for the believer, he submitted willingly, and as for the disbeliever, he submitted when he saw the wrath of God, But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our wrath
r
(Ghafir 40:85)

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: the worship of creation to God Almighty.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do they seek other than the religion of God

, while to Him have submitted [all] those within the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion? He said: Their worship of Me, all of them, willingly or by compulsion, and this is His statement:
h
And to God prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth
, willingly or by compulsion
r
(Al-Raʿd: 15)

. As for his statement: And to Him you will return, he means: And to Him, O group of those who seek a religion other than Islam, from the Jews, Christians, and all other people, you will return. He says: To Him you will go after your death, so He will reward you for your deeds, the good among you for his goodness, and the evildoer for his evil. This is from God Almighty, warning His creation that none of them should return to Him and become a follower of a religion other than Islam after his death.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The readings differed in the reading of that: the majority of the readers of the Hijaz from Mecca and Medina, and the readers of Kufa read: Do you seek other than the religion of God, and to Him you will be returned, in the form of address.
Some of the people of Hijaz read it as Do they seek other than the religion of God? and And to Him they will return with both ya’s, as a report on the absent.
Some of the people of Basra read it as: Do they seek other than the religion of God? as a statement about the absent person, and to Him you will be returned, with the letter ta as a direct address.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these is the reading of those who read: Do you then seek other than the religion of God? as a direct address, and to Him you will be returned, with the letter ta’.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: Do you seek other than the religion of God, O group of Jews, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and to Him you will be returned? So
h
if they seek other than the religion of God
, O Muhammad, then say to them: We believe in God. So He left out mentioning His statement: If they say: Yes, or He mentioned His statement:
h
If they seek other than the religion of God

, because of the evidence of what appeared in the speech on that. And His saying: “Say: We believe in God,” meaning: Say to them, O Muhammad: We believe in God that He is our Lord and our God, there is no god but Him, and we do not worship anyone other than Him, and what was revealed to us, meaning: And say: And we also believe in what was revealed to us of His revelation and sending down, so we acknowledged it, and what was revealed to Abraham, meaning: And we also believe in what was revealed to Abraham, the friend of God, and to his sons Ishmael and Isaac, and his grandson Jacob, and what was revealed to the tribes, who are the twelve children of Jacob, and we have explained their names in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, meaning: And we also believe with that in what God revealed to Moses and Jesus of the books and revelation, and in what was revealed to the prophets from Him.

And what God gave to Moses and Jesus, from what God Almighty commanded Muhammad to believe in and have faith in, is the Torah that He gave to Moses, and the Gospel that He gave to Jesus. We make no distinction between any of them, meaning: We do not believe some of them and disbelieve others, nor do we have faith in some of them and disbelieve in others, just as the Jews and Christians disbelieved in some of God’s prophets and believed in others. Rather, we believe in all of them and believe in them. And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him, meaning: We profess Islam to God and do not profess anything other than Him. Rather, we disavow to Him every religion other than Him, and every creed other than Him. What he means by his saying: And we are Muslims to Him, is that we are submissive to Him in obedience, humbled in servitude, acknowledging His divinity and lordship, and that there is no god but Him.
We have mentioned the narration with the meaning of what we said about that previously, and we dislike repeating it.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And whoever seeks a religion other than the religion of Islam to follow it, God will not accept it from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers, meaning: among those who deprive themselves of their share of God Almighty’s mercy. He mentioned that the people of every religion claimed that they were the Muslims, when this verse was revealed, so God commanded them to perform Hajj if they were truthful, because Hajj is part of the Sunnah of Islam, but they refused, so God thus refuted their argument.
The report mentioned that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said,
m: Ikrimah claimed: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion, so the religions said: We are the Muslims! So God Almighty revealed: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God - those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses. And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds.”
r
(Al Imran 3:97)
, so the Muslims performed Hajj, and the disbelievers stayed away.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Qa’nabi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him. The Jews said: So we are the Muslims! So God, the Almighty, revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, urging them to perform Hajj: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God - those who can afford the expenses for one’s journey. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds.”
r
(Al Imran 3:97)

Yunus told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: When the verse: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion to the end of the verse was revealed, the Jews said: So we are Muslims! God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell them that: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds.
r
(Al Imran 3:97)
Others said about this verse:

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh narrated to us, he said: Muawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews or Christians or Sabeans - those who believed in God and the Last Day to His statement: nor will they grieve (al-Baqarah 2:62). Then God Almighty revealed after this: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion - never will it be accepted from him.

x: The interpreters differed about who this verse refers to, and about whom it was revealed.
Some of them said: It was revealed about Al-Harith bin Suwaid Al-Ansari, who was a Muslim and then apostatized after his conversion to Islam.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzayʿ al-Basri told me, he said, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, he said, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: There was a man from the Ansar who had converted to Islam, then he apostatized and returned to polytheism. Then he regretted it and sent to his al-Nas 114:Send to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Is there any repentance for me? He said: Then the verse was revealed:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief
until His saying:
h
And clear proofs have come to them
? And God does not guide the wrongdoing people “Except those who repent after that and reform. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” So his people sent to him and he converted to Islam.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd Al-A’la told me, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: something similar, and he did not trace it back to Ibn Abbas, except that he said: So his people wrote to him, and he said: My people did not lie to me! So he returned.
