c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hakim bin Jami’ told us, on the authority of Ali bin Masaher, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: A man from the Ansar apostatized, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Jaʿfar bin Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Hamid al-Aʿraj narrated to us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Al-Harith bin Suwayd came and became Muslim with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Al-Harith disbelieved and returned to his people, so God, the Almighty, revealed the Qur’an concerning him:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief

? to Except those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He said: So a man from his people brought it to him and recited it to him, so Al-Harith said: By God, I do not know that you are truthful, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more truthful than you, and God, the Almighty, is more truthful than the three. He said: So Al-Harith returned and became Muslim, and his Islam was good.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief

and bore witness that the Messenger is true? He said: It was revealed about Al-Harith bin Suwaid Al-Ansari. He disbelieved after his belief, so God, the Almighty, revealed these verses about him, up to: Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. Then he repented and became Muslim, so God abrogated it for him, and said: Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief
and bore witness that the Messenger was true and clear proofs had come to them? He said: A man from Banu Amr bin Awf disbelieved after his belief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He is a man from Banu Amr ibn Awf, who disbelieved after his belief. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: He went to the land of the Romans and converted to Christianity, then he wrote to his al-Nas 114:Send, is there any repentance for me? He said: I thought that he had believed, then he returned. Ibn Jurayj said: Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Abu Amir the monk, Al-Harith ibn Suwayd ibn As-Samit, and Wahuh ibn Al-Aslat, and twelve men who turned away from Islam and went to Quraysh, then they wrote to their al-Nas 114:Is there any repentance for us? So this verse was revealed: Except for those who repent after that, and the verses.

x: Others said: This verse refers to the People of the Book, and it was revealed about them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief
? They are the People of the Book, they knew Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then they disbelieved in him.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief
, the entire verse, he said: The Jews and the Christians.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say regarding the verse:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief

? They are the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians. They saw the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their book and acknowledged it, and testified that it was true. But when he was sent from outside of them, they envied the Arabs for that and denied it, and disbelieved after their acknowledgment, out of envy for the Arabs when he was sent from outside of them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief
? He said: They are the People of the Book. They used to find Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their book, and they used to seek his help, but they disbelieved after their belief.

x: The two opinions that are most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation is what Al-Hasan said: that this verse is intended for the People of the Book according to what he said, except that the reports of the other opinion are more numerous, and those who say it are more knowledgeable in the interpretation of the Qur’an. It is possible that God, the Almighty, revealed these verses because of the people who He mentioned had apostatized from Islam, so He gathered their story and the story of those whose path was their path in apostasy from belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in these verses. Then He informed His servants of His way with them, so included in that is everyone who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, then disbelieved in him after he was sent, and everyone who was a disbeliever then became Muslim during his time, may God bless him and grant him peace, then apostatized from his Islam while he was alive, so the verse is intended for all of these two categories and others who are similar in meaning to them, and that is also the case, God willing.
The interpretation of the verse is:
h
How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief

? That is, how can God guide to the truth and guide to faith a people who denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after their belief, that is, after they believed in him and acknowledged what he brought them from his Lord, and bore witness that the Messenger is true, that is, after they acknowledged that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to His creation,
h
and clear proofs have come to them

, that is, and arguments from God and evidence of the truth of that have come to them? And God does not guide the wrongdoing people, that is, God does not guide to the truth and the right path the wrongdoing group, who are those who changed the truth to falsehood, so they chose disbelief over faith. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of injustice, which is putting something in the wrong place, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

evidence.text: He said: So a man from his people brought it to him and recited it to him, so Al-Harith said: By God, I do not know that you are truthful, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more truthful than you, and God, the Almighty, is more truthful than the three.

x: Their recompense - meaning: those who disbelieved after their belief, and after they had witnessed that the Messenger was true - their recompense, their reward for the work they did, is that upon them is the curse of God, meaning: that they will be ostracized and distanced from God, and that the angels and people will pray for a punishment that will harm them, all together, meaning: from all of them, not from some of those whom God, the Most High, named from the angels and people, but from all of them. And God, the Most High, made that the reward for their work, because their work was disbelief in God. We have explained the nature of the people’s curse on the infidel in other places, so there is no need to repeat it.

They will abide therein eternally means: they will remain there, meaning in God's punishment. The punishment will not be lightened for them, they will not be diminished in the least from the punishment under any circumstances, nor will they be relieved from it. Nor will they be reprieved, meaning: nor will they be reprieved for an excuse to apologize. All of this is the very definition of eternal punishment in the Hereafter.

Then He, the Most High, excepted those who repented, from those who disbelieved after their belief, so He, the Most High, said: Except for those who repent after that and reform, meaning: except for those who repented after their apostasy, so they reviewed the belief in God and His Messenger, and believed in what their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them from their Lord, and reformed, meaning: and did righteous deeds, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: for the one who does that after his disbelief, Forgiving, meaning: He conceals his sin that he committed of apostasy, so He leaves his punishment for it, and his disgrace for it on the Day of Resurrection, and does not hold him accountable for it if he dies repentant from it, Merciful, compassionate toward him with mercy.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: God Almighty meant by His saying: Indeed, those who disbelieved in some of His prophets who were sent before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after their belief and then increased in disbelief by their disbelief in Muhammad,
h
their repentance will not be accepted
, when death approaches and he himself is dying.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted,
h
and those are the ones who are astray
, he said: The Jews and Christians,
h
their repentance will not be accepted
at death.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief, those are the enemies of God, the Jews. They disbelieved in the Gospel and Jesus, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Criterion.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then they increased in disbelief
, he said: They increased in disbelief until death came to them, and their repentance was not accepted when death came to them. Muammar said: Ata al-Khurasani said something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted. And it is those who are the ones who are astray.” He said: They are the Jews, they disbelieved in the Gospel, then increased in disbelief when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they denied him and belied him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Those of the People of the Book who disbelieved in Muhammad, after believing in their prophets, then increased in disbelief, meaning: sins,
h
their repentance will not be accepted
for their sins, and they will remain in disbelief.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’:
m: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief, they increased in sins while they were disbelievers, their repentance will never be accepted from those sins, as long as they were in their disbelief and misguidance.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, he said:
m: I asked Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said, I said: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted? He said: They are only those Christians and Jews who disbelieved, then increased in disbelief due to sins they committed, so they repent from them in their disbelief.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, he said:
m: I asked Abu Al-Aaliyah about: those who believed and then disbelieved, and he mentioned something similar to it.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, he said:
m: I asked Abu Al-A’la about this verse: “Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted. And it is those who are astray.” He said: They are the Jews, Christians, and Magians. They committed sins in their disbelief, and they wanted to repent from them, but they will never repent from disbelief. Do you not see that He says: And it is those who are astray?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Their repentance will not be accepted
, he said: They repented from some of it, but they did not repent from the origin. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief, he said: They are the Jews and Christians, who commit sins and say: We repent, while they are polytheists. God Almighty said: Repentance will not be accepted in misguidance.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Those who disbelieved after their belief in their prophets, and then increased in disbelief, meaning: by their increasing disbelief: their completion of it, until they perished while they were still in it,
h
their repentance will not be accepted
, their first repentance and belief will not benefit them, because of their later disbelief and death.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then they increased in disbelief
, he said: They remained in their disbelief. Ibn Jurayj said:
h
Their repentance will not be accepted
, he said: Their faith the first time will not benefit them.

x: Others said: The meaning of his statement,
h
Then they increased in disbelief
, is that they died as disbelievers, so that was their increase in their disbelief. They said: The meaning of
h
Their repentance will not be accepted
, is that
h
their repentance will not be accepted
upon their death.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted. And it is those who are astray.” As for increased in disbelief, it means that they died as disbelievers. As for never will their repentance be accepted, it means at his death, if he repented, his repentance would not be accepted.

x: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting this verse is the saying of the one who said: It means the Jews, and that its interpretation is: Those Jews who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was sent, after their belief in him before his mission, then increased in disbelief because of the sins they committed in their disbelief and their persistence in their misguidance,
h
their repentance will not be accepted

for the sins they committed in their disbelief, until they repent from their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and return to repentance from it by believing in what came from God. We said: This is the most correct of the sayings about this verse, because the verses before and after it were revealed about them, so it is more likely that it is in the same meaning as what came before and after it, since they were in one context.
We said: The meaning of their increasing disbelief is the sins they committed in their disbelief, because God, the Most High, said:
h
Their repentance will not be accepted
. So it was known that the meaning of His statement:
h
Their repentance will not be accepted
is:
h
Their repentance will not be accepted

for what they increased in disbelief after their belief, not for their disbelief. Because God, the Most High, promised to accept repentance from His servants, saying: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants (al-Shura 42:25). So it is impossible for God, the Most High, to say: I accept and I do not accept in one thing. Since that is the case, and it is from God’s ruling regarding His servants that He accepts the repentance of every repentant person from every sin, and disbelief after belief is one of those sins for which He promised to accept repentance by saying: Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, it is known that the meaning for which He does not accept repentance is not the meaning for which He accepts repentance.

Since this is the case, then what is not accepted from him is the increase in disbelief after disbelief. God does not accept the repentance of his companion as long as he remains in his disbelief, because God does not accept any action from a polytheist as long as he remains in his polytheism and misguidance. But if he repents from his polytheism and disbelief and reforms, then God - as He described Himself - is Forgiving and Merciful.
Why do you deny that the meaning of this is as the one who said: His repentance from his disbelief will not be accepted when his time comes and his first repentance?

We deny that, because repentance from a servant does not occur except during his life, as for after his death there is no repentance. And God the Almighty has promised His servants to accept their repentance as long as their souls are in their bodies. And there is no disagreement among all the arguments that if a disbeliever converts to Islam before his soul departs by the blink of an eye, his ruling is the ruling of Muslims in praying over him, inheritance, and all other rulings besides them. So it was known from this that if his repentance in that state was not accepted, his ruling would not move from the ruling of the disbelievers to the ruling of the people of Islam, and there is no status between death and life. It is permissible to say: God does not accept the repentance of the disbeliever in it.

So if it is true that it is accepted during his life, and there is no way to it after death, then the statement of the one who claimed that it is not accepted when the appointed time comes is invalid. As for the statement of the one who claimed that the meaning of this is: the repentance that was before disbelief, then this statement has no meaning. Because God, the Almighty, did not describe the people with faith that came from them after disbelief, then disbelief after faith, but rather He described them with disbelief after faith. So that faith was not preceded by disbelief from which faith was a repentance for them, so the interpretation of that is according to what the speaker interpreted it. And the interpretation of the Qur’an according to what was present in the outward recitation - if there is no evidence indicating a specific inner meaning - is more appropriate than otherwise, even if it is possible to direct it to something else.
As for his saying:
h
And those are the ones who are astray

, he means by that: And those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief, they are the ones who went astray from the path of truth, so they erred in its path, and abandoned half the path and the guidance of the religion, out of confusion on their part, and blindness to it. Surat Al Imran 3:90 Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief - never will their repentance be accepted, and it is those who are the ones astray. We have previously explained the meaning of misguidance sufficiently.

evidence.text: And the interpretation of the Qur’an according to what was present in the outward recitation - if there is no evidence indicating a specific inner meaning - is more appropriate than otherwise, even if it is possible to direct it to something else.

x: By that, God the Most High means: Those who disbelieved, that is, denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and did not believe in him and what he brought from God, from the people of every religion, Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians, and others, died while they were disbelievers, that is, and died in that state of denying his prophethood and denying what he brought, the earth full of gold will not be accepted from any of them, even if he were to ransom himself with it, meaning: no reward or bribe will be accepted from someone who has this characteristic in the Hereafter for not punishing him for his disbelief, nor will he be given a reward for pardoning him, even if he had enough gold to fill the earth from east to west, as a reward and a reward for not punishing him and in pardoning him for his disbelief as compensation for what God has decreed for him of punishment. Because bribes are only accepted by someone who has a need for what he was bribed with.

As for the one who has this world and the hereafter, how can he accept the ransom, while he is the Creator of every ransom with which a person redeems himself or someone else? We have explained that the meaning of ransom is compensation and recompense from the one being ransomed, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Then the Almighty informed about what they will have with Him, saying: Those, meaning those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers, will have a painful punishment, meaning: they will have a painful punishment with God in the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers, meaning: they will have no relative, intimate friend, or friend to support him and rescue him from God and His punishment, as they used to support him in this world against those who tried to harm him and harm him. And: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said, Anas bin Malik told us: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: ‘The disbeliever will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: ‘Tell me, if you had the earth full of gold, would you ransom yourself with it?’

He will say: ‘Yes!’ It will be said: ‘You were asked something easier than that!’ That is what He said: ‘Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - never will an earth full of gold be accepted from one of them, even if he ransomed himself with it.’”

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: his saying: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - never will an earth full of gold be accepted from one of them, he said: It is every disbeliever. The accusative case of his saying: gold is to deviate from the amount that preceded it and to explain it, which is his saying: filling the earth, like the saying of the one who says: I have a skin’s worth of ghee and a pound’s worth of honey. So the honey is what is mentioned of the amount, and it is an indefinite noun in the accusative case to explain the amount and to deviate from it. As for the grammarians of Basra, they claimed that the word gold was placed in the accusative case because the word filling was occupied with the earth and that gold came after them, so its accusative case was similar to the accusative case of the state. This is because the state comes after a verb that is occupied with its subject, so it is placed in the accusative case like the object that comes after a verb that is occupied with its subject. They said: Similar to his saying, filling the earth with gold, in the accusative case of gold in speech: I have a man like you means: I have a man like you. They claimed that the accusative case of the man was due to the addition being occupied with the noun, so it was placed in the accusative case like the object is placed in the accusative case, because the verb is occupied with the subject. The letter waw was inserted in His statement,
h
And if he ransomed himself with it

, because of something omitted from the statement after it, which was indicated by the insertion of the waw. It is like the waw in His statement, And that he may be among the certain (al-An’am 6:75). The interpretation of the statement is: And that he may be among the certain, We will show him the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. Likewise in His statement,
h
And if he ransomed himself with it

. If there were no waw in the statement, the statement would be correct, and there would be no omission, and it would be: Then the earth full of gold would not be accepted from any of them if he ransomed himself with it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: You, O believers, will not attain righteousness, which is righteousness from God, which they seek from Him through their obedience to Him and their worship of Him, and which they hope for from Him. This is His favor upon them by admitting them into His Paradise and turning away His punishment from them. Therefore, many of the people of interpretation said that righteousness means Paradise, because the Lord’s righteousness towards His servant in the afterlife is His honoring him by admitting him into Paradise.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will not attain righteousness
, he said: Paradise.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will never attain righteousness
, he said: Righteousness is Paradise.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
You will not attain righteousness
. As for righteousness, it is Paradise.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: You, O believers, will not attain the Paradise of your Lord, until you spend from what you love, meaning: until you give in charity from what you love and desire to have, from your most precious wealth, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love
, meaning: You will not attain the righteousness of your Lord until you spend from that which pleases you and from that which you desire of your wealth.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will not attain righteousness until you spend from what you love
, he said: from money. As for his statement:
h
And whatever you spend
, indeed, God is Knowing of it, he means by it:
h
And whatever you spend

, and give in charity from your wealth, then God, the Most High, mentioned that which the charitable among you gives in charity, and spends from what he loves of his wealth in the way of God and other than that, is Knowing, meaning: He has knowledge of all of that, nothing of it is hidden from Him, until He rewards its owner for it with his reward in the Hereafter, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And whatever you spend

, God is Knowing of it, meaning: It is preserved for you, God is Knowing of it, and is grateful for it. In the same interpretation that we mentioned, a group of the Companions and Followers interpreted this verse.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
You will never attain righteousness

until you spend from that which you love, he said: Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash’ari to buy him a slave girl from Jalula on the day that Madain Kisra was conquered in the fight against Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas. Umar ibn al-Khattab called for her and said: God says:
h
You will never attain righteousness

until you spend from that which you love, so Umar freed her, and she is like the statement of God Almighty: And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive (al-Insan 76:8), and And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in privation (al-Hashr 59:9).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: “When this verse was revealed: ‘
h
You will never attain righteousness

until you spend from that which you love,’ or this verse: ‘Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan?’ (al-Baqarah 2:245, al-Hadid 57:11), Abu Talha said: O Messenger of God, my garden of such-and-such is charity, and if I could make it secret, I would not make it public! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give it to the poor of your family.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: “When this verse was revealed: ‘
h
You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love

,’ Abu Talha said: O Messenger of God, God will ask us about our wealth. I bear witness that I have given my land in Jericho to God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give it to your relatives. So he gave it to Hassan bin Thabit and Ubayy bin Ka’b.” Imran bin Musa narrated, Abdul Warith narrated, Laith narrated, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran: A man asked Abu Dharr: Which deeds are best? He said: Prayer is the pillar of Islam, jihad is the pinnacle of deeds, and charity is something amazing! He said: O Abu Dharr, you have left out something that is the most trustworthy deed in my heart, I do not see you mention it! He said: What is it? He said: Fasting! He said: An act of worship, but it is not there! And he recited this verse: By no means will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Dawud ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makki told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, who said:
m: “When this verse was revealed: ‘
h
You will never attain righteousness

until you spend out of that which you love,’ Zayd brought his horse called Sabl to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Give this in charity, O Messenger of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave it to his son Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Haritha, and he said: O Messenger of God, I only wanted to give it in charity! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have accepted your charity.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub and others:
m: “When the verse, ‘
h
You will not attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love

’ was revealed, Zaid bin Haritha came with a horse of his that he loved, and he said: O Messenger of God, this is for the sake of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mounted Usama bin Zaid on it, and it was as if Zaid felt something in his heart, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that from him, he said: Indeed, God has accepted it.”

evidence.text: And he recited this verse: By no means will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that nothing of the foods were forbidden to the Children of Israel - and they are the descendants of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful - before the Torah was revealed. Rather, all of that was permissible for them except what Jacob had forbidden for himself, for his descendants forbade it in imitation of their father Jacob, without God forbidding it to them in revelation or sending down, nor on the tongue of a messenger of His to them, before the Torah was revealed. Then the people of interpretation differed about the prohibition of that for them. Was it revealed in the Torah or not?
Some of them said: When God Almighty revealed the Torah, He forbade them from that which they had forbidden before it was revealed.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed

. Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.’” The Jews said: We only forbid what Israel had forbidden to himself. Israel only forbade the veins. He used to suffer from sciatica. He used to take it at night and leave it during the day. So he swore that if God spared him from it, he would never eat a vein again. So God forbade it to them. Then He said: Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.’ None has forbidden this to you except Me because of your transgression. That is what God said: But because of wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We prohibited for them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them
r
(An-Nisa’: 160)

x: The interpretation of the verse according to this statement is:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed

. For God forbade them from that what Israel had forbidden to himself in the Torah, because of their transgression and injustice towards themselves. Say, O Muhammad: So bring, O Jews, if you deny that, the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful, that God did not forbid that to you in the Torah, and that you only forbid it because Israel forbade it to himself.

Others said: None of that was forbidden to them, nor did God forbid it to them in the Torah. Rather, it was something they forbade themselves in following their father, then they attributed its prohibition to God. So God Almighty belied them in attributing that to Him. So God Almighty said to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muhammad: If you are truthful, then bring the Torah and recite it so that we may see whether that is in it or not. So their lie will be clear to those who are ignorant of their matter.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Except what Israel had forbidden to himself

, Israel is Jacob. He was afflicted with sciatica and would not sleep at night because of the pain, but it did not bother him during the day. So he swore that if God healed him he would never eat a plant again. This was before the Torah was revealed to Moses. So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the Jews: What is it that Israel had forbidden to himself? They said: The Torah was revealed with the prohibition of what Israel had forbidden. So God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful. ’” until His statement, For those are the wrongdoers. They lied and fabricated. The Torah was not revealed with that. The interpretation of the verse according to this statement is:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel

before the Torah was revealed and after it was revealed, except what Israel made unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed. Meaning: But Israel made some of that unlawful to himself before the Torah was revealed. It is as if Ad-Dahhak directed his statement: except what Israel made unlawful to himself to the exception that grammarians call the discontinuous exception.

x: Others said: The interpretation of that is: All food was permissible for the Children of Israel except what Israel forbade himself before the Torah was revealed, for that was forbidden to his son because Israel forbade it to his son, without God forbidding it to Israel or his son.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful to himself

, for he made the veins unlawful to himself, because he suffered from sciatica and would not sleep at night, so he said: By God, if God cures me of it, no child of mine will eat it. And it is not written in the Torah! Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, asked a group of the People of the Book, saying: Why is this unlawful? They said: It was unlawful to us from the Book. Then God Almighty said:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel
to if you are truthful.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: He - meaning Israel - suffered from sciatica, so he would not sleep at night because of the severity of the pain, and it did not bother him during the day, so he swore that if God healed him he would never eat sciatica again, and that was before the Torah was revealed. So the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The Torah was revealed prohibiting what Israel prohibited for himself. God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,” and they lied, it is not in the Torah.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: All food was permissible for the Children of Israel before the Torah was revealed, except for what Israel forbade for himself without God forbidding it to him, for it was forbidden to them because their father Israel forbade it to them, without God forbidding it to them in any revelation or revelation before the Torah, until the Torah was revealed, and God forbade them in it whatever He willed, and permitted them in it whatever He liked. This is a statement made by a group of interpreters, and it is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas that we mentioned before.
Some of those who said that said:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed
, and Israel is Jacob. Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,’ meaning:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel
before the Torah was revealed,
h
except what Israel had forbidden to himself
. Then when God revealed the Torah, He forbade them whatever He wanted and permitted them whatever He wanted.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, something similar.

x: The people of interpretation differed about what Israel forbade himself.
Some of them said: What Israel forbade himself was the veins.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mahak, who said:
m: A Bedouin came to Ibn Abbas and said that he had made his wife forbidden to him, so he said: She is not forbidden to you. The Bedouin said: Why, while God says in His Book:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel made unlawful to himself

? Ibn Abbas laughed and said: How do you know what Israel made unlawful to himself? He said: Then he turned to the people and told them, and said: Israel was exposed to women and they made him weak, so he made a vow to God that if God healed him from them he would not eat a vein. He said: That is why the Jews remove veins from meat.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said:
m: I heard Yusuf ibn Mahak narrating: A Bedouin came to Ibn ʿAbbas and mentioned a man who had forbidden his wife, so he said: She is not forbidden. The Bedouin said: What do you think of the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself
? He said: Israel had sciatica, so he swore that if God cured him he would not eat the veins of meat, and they are not forbidden to you.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding his statement:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself
, he said: Yaqub was afflicted with sciatica, so he made a vow to God - or he swore, or he made an oath - that he would not eat any animal. He said: And all the veins are subject to that vein.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that what Israel forbade himself was that women took him one night and kept him awake, so he swore that God had healed him that he would never eat women again, so his sons followed the veins after that, extracting them from the flesh.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, in a similar manner, and he added to it: He said: He swore that if God healed him, he would never eat a vein again. So his sons began to trace the veins after that and extract them from the meat. And what he had forbidden himself before the Torah was revealed was the veins.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except what Israel had forbidden to himself
, he said: Israel complained of sciatica and said: God has healed me, so I will forbid the veins! So he forbade them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us,
m: Surat Al Imran 3:93
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel
h
except what Israel had forbidden to himself
before the Torah was revealed. Say, “Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.”

c: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Israel was afflicted with sciatica, so he used to have a waterskin for himself every night. He made a vow to God that if he cured him, he would not eat the waterskin. Then God Almighty revealed:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel
h
except what Israel had forbidden to himself
. Sufyan said: It had a waterskin, meaning: a screaming sound.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except what Israel had forbidden to himself
, he said: He was suffering from sciatica, so he forbade the veins.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
All food was lawful for the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed
, he said: Israel was afflicted with sciatica, so he would sleep with a waterskin, so he forbade himself from eating sciatica.

x: Others said: Rather, the one who was Israel forbade himself the meat and milk of camels.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Kathir, who said:
m: We heard that he complained of a complaint, and they said: It is sciatica. So he said: O Lord, the food I love most is camel meat and milk, so if You cure me, then I forbid them to myself. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: The meat and milk of camels were forbidden to Israel.

c: Muhammad ibn Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel

, he said: Israel had forbidden himself camel meat, and they claimed that they would find in the Torah a prohibition of Israel from camel meat. But Israel had forbidden himself camel meat before the Torah was revealed, so God said: Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful, and He said: You will not find in the Torah a prohibition of Israel from himself, meaning camel meat.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Habib ibn Abi Thabit told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: That Israel was afflicted with sciatica, and he would spend the night crying out in the open - meaning: screaming - he said: So he vowed to himself that if God cured him of it, he would not eat it - meaning: camel meat - he said: So the Jews forbade it, and he recited this verse: “
h
All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed
. Say: ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful’” meaning: This was before the Torah.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding:
h
Except what Israel made unlawful for himself
, he said: He made unlawful the veins and the meat of camels. He said: He had sciatica, so he ate some of its meat and spent the night vomiting, so he swore that he would never eat it again.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except what Israel made unlawful for himself
. He said: He made unlawful the meat of livestock.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbas, which was narrated by Al-Aʿmash, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saʿid, on his authority: That is, the veins and the meat of camels, because the Jews are unanimously agreed to this day on their prohibition, just as they were in their early days.
And a report similar to this has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is: What:

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Bahram, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “A group of Jews attended the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Abu al-Qasim, tell us which food Israel forbade himself before the Torah was revealed? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I ask you by the One who revealed the Torah to Moses, do you know that Israel, Jacob, fell seriously ill and his illness lasted a long time, so he made a vow to God that if God cured him of his illness, he would forbid himself the most beloved food and drink to him, and the most beloved food to him was camel meat, and the most beloved drink to him was camel milk? They said: By God, yes.” As for his saying: “Say: ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,’” its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to those Jews who claim that God has forbidden them in the Torah the veins, meat, and milk of camels: Bring the Torah and recite it. He says: Say to them: Bring the Torah and recite it, so that it becomes clear to whoever is unaware of their lie and their false claim about God regarding their affair: that this is not what I revealed in the Torah, if you should be truthful. He says: If you are right in your claim that God revealed the prohibition of that in the Torah, then bring it to us and recite the prohibition of that to us from it. Rather, this is a report from God about their lie, because they never come with that in its correct form. So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their lie against Him, and made His informing him of that a proof for Him against them. Because that was hidden from many of the people of their religion, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was illiterate and not from their religion, had God not informed him of that through revelation from Him, it would have been more appropriate for him not to know it. So that was for him, one of the greatest proofs against them that he was a Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them. Because that was from the reports of their predecessors, it was from the hidden knowledge of theirs that no one knew except a select few of them, except for the one whom He informed, from whom nothing is hidden, of a prophet or messenger, or whomever God informed of His knowledge from among His creation He willed.

evidence.text: Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.’”
Then He said: Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.’

Say, O Muhammad: So bring, O Jews, if you deny that, the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful, that God did not forbid that to you in the Torah, and that you only forbid it because Israel forbade it to himself.

So God Almighty said to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muhammad: If you are truthful, then bring the Torah and recite it so that we may see whether that is in it or not.
So God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful. ’” until His statement, For those are the wrongdoers.
God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,” and they lied, it is not in the Torah.
Say, ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,’ meaning: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel before the Torah was revealed, except what Israel had forbidden to himself.
Say, “Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.”

But Israel had forbidden himself camel meat before the Torah was revealed, so God said: Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful, and He said: You will not find in the Torah a prohibition of Israel from himself, meaning camel meat.

Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Habib ibn Abi Thabit told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That Israel was afflicted with sciatica, and he would spend the night crying out in the open - meaning: screaming - he said: So he vowed to himself that if God cured him of it, he would not eat it - meaning: camel meat - he said: So the Jews forbade it, and he recited this verse: “All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed.
Say: ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful’” meaning: This was before the Torah.

As for his saying: “Say: ‘Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful,’” its meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to those Jews who claim that God has forbidden them in the Torah the veins, meat, and milk of camels: Bring the Torah and recite it.

He says: Say to them: Bring the Torah and recite it, so that it becomes clear to whoever is unaware of their lie and their false claim about God regarding their affair: that this is not what I revealed in the Torah, if you should be truthful.

x: By that, the Most High means: Whoever among us and among you lies about God, after you have brought the Torah and recited it, and you have not claimed that God has forbidden the veins, meat, and milk of camels in it.
Then those are the wrongdoers, meaning: whoever among them does that, they, meaning: those who do that, are the wrongdoers, meaning: they are the disbelievers, who say falsehood about God, like:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: Then it is those who are the wrongdoers, he said: It was revealed about the Jews.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, the Most High means: Whoever among us and among you lies about God, after you have brought the Torah and recited it, and you have not claimed that God has forbidden the veins, meat, and milk of camels in it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Say, O Muhammad, God has spoken the truth, in what He has informed us of in His saying: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel, and that God did not forbid Israel or his children the veins or the meat and milk of camels, and that this was only something that Israel forbade himself and his children without God forbidding it to them in the Torah—and in everything that He has informed His servants of, but not you. And you, O Jews, are the liars in your attribution of the prohibition of that to God upon you in the Torah, the slanderers against God falsely in your untrue claim against Him, So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth,
h
and he was not of the polytheists

, He says: If you, O Jews, are right in your claim that you are upon those whom God has chosen for His prophets and messengers, then follow the religion of Abraham, the friend of God, for you know that it is the truth which God has chosen for His creation as a religion, and with which He sent His prophets, that is the uprightness of Islam and its laws, not Judaism, Christianity, and polytheism.
And His statement:
h
And he was not of the polytheists

, meaning: He did not associate anyone of His creation with Him in His worship. So too you, O Jews, do not take one another as lords besides God, obeying them as Abraham obeyed his Lord. And you, O group of idol worshippers, do not take idols and statues as lords, and do not worship anything besides God, for Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, had the religion of sincere worship of his Lord alone, without associating anyone with Him in that. Likewise, you also, so devote your worship to Him and do not associate anyone with Him in worship, for all of you acknowledge that Abraham was on the right path and the straight path, so follow what you all agreed upon to be correct from his pure religion, and leave what you differed upon from all other religions, O parties, for they are innovations that you innovated for what you agreed upon to be the truth, for what you agreed upon to be correct and the truth from the religion of Abraham is the truth that I was pleased with and sent My prophets and messengers with, and the rest of that is falsehood that I will not accept from any of My creation who brings it to Me on the Day of Resurrection.
Rather, God the Most High said:
h
And he was not of the polytheists

, meaning: and he was not of their number and their allies. This is because the polytheists are from one another in their support of one another in their disbelief and their assistance to one another. So God cleared His friend Abraham from being one of them or [one of] their supporters and those who are their allies. Rather, God the Most High meant by the polytheists the Jews, Christians and all other religions other than the Hanifite religion. He said: Abraham was not one of the people of these polytheistic religions, but he was a Hanif Muslim.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: The first house established for people, in which God is worshipped, blessed and a guidance for the worlds, is the one in Bakkah. They said: It is not the first house established on earth, because there were many houses before it.
Who said that?

c: Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, he said:
m: A man stood up to Ali and said: Will you not tell me about the House? Was it the first House placed on Earth? He said: No, but it was the first House placed in the pool, the Station of Abraham, and whoever enters it is safe.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, who said:
m: I heard Khalid ibn Arʿarah say: I heard Ali, and it was said to him:
h
The first House established for mankind
was the one in Bakkah. Was it the first House on earth? He said: No! He said: Then where were the people of Noah? And where were the people of Hud? He said: But it was
h
the first House established for mankind
, blessed and a guidance.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said:
m: Hafs asked al-Hasan, and I was listening, about his saying: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah, full of blessing. He said: It is the first mosque in which God was worshipped on earth.

c: Abdul Jabbar bin Yahya Al-Ramli told us, he said, Damrah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Matar,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed,
h
the first House established for mankind
was that at Bakkah, he said: There were houses before it, but it was the first house established for worship.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: his saying:
h
The first House established for mankind
, in which God was worshipped, was that at Bakkah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
The first House established for mankind
was the one in Mecca, blessed. He said: It was established for worship.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the first house established for people. Then those who said that differed about the description of its first placement.
Some of them said: He was created before all the earths, then the earths were rolled out from beneath him.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told us, he said, Ubaid God bin Musa told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said:
m: God created the House two thousand years before the Earth, and it was - when His Throne was on the water - a white foam, then the Earth was spread out from beneath it.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told me, he said, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say: The first thing that God created was the Kaaba, then He spread out the earth from beneath it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind, like His statement: You are the best nation produced for mankind
r
(Al Imran 3:110)

c: Muhammad told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
The first House established for mankind

was that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds. As for the first House, it was when the earth was water, it was butter on the earth, so when God created the earth, He created the House with it, so it is the first House established on the earth.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed, he said: The first House that God Almighty established, so Adam and those after him circumambulated it.

x: Others said: The location of the Kaaba is the location of the first house that God placed on Earth. Surat Al Imran 3:96 Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was mentioned to us that the House descended with Adam when he descended. He said: My House descends with you, and it is circumambulated around it as one circumambulates around My Throne. So Adam and those who came after him of the believers circumambulated around it, until the time of the Flood came, the time when God drowned the people of Noah. God raised it and purified it from being afflicted with the punishment of the people of the Earth, so it became inhabited in the heavens. Then Abraham followed a trace of it after that, so he built it on an ancient foundation that had been before it.

x: The correct statement about this is what God Almighty said about it: The first blessed House and guidance established for mankind was the one in Makkah. The meaning of this is:
h
The first House established for mankind

, that is, for the worship of God in it, blessed and guidance, meaning by that: and a place of refuge for the worshippers and the circumambulations of those who circumambulate, in glorification and reverence of God, was the one in Makkah, due to the authenticity of the report about this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said, I said: O Messenger of God, which mosque was established first? He said: The Sacred Mosque.

He said: Then which? He said: Al-Aqsa Mosque. He said: How much time is between them? He said: Forty years. This report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has shown that the Sacred Mosque is the first mosque that God established on earth, according to what we have said. As for its location as a house, other than the meaning of a house for worship, guidance and blessing, there is a difference of opinion about it, some of which I have mentioned in this place, and some of which in Surat Al-Baqarah and other surahs of the Qur’an, and I have explained the correct statement about that, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. As for his saying:
h
For the one in Mecca

, blessed, he means: for the House in which people crowd for their circumambulation during their Hajj and Umrah. The root of baq is crowding. It is said: So-and-so crowded so-and-so if he jostled and bumped into him, so he wept over him, and they were crying in it, meaning: they were jostling and colliding in it.

So Bakkah is an action of so-and-so crowded so-and-so; the spot was named after the action of those crowding in it. If Mecca was as we have described, and it was a place of crowding of people around the House, and no circumambulation was permissible outside the mosque, then it was known from this that what was around the Kaaba was inside the mosque, and that what was outside the mosque was Mecca, not Mecca. Because there was no meaning outside it that would require people to weep in it. Since that was the case, then it was clear from this that the statement of those who said: Mecca is the name of the valley of Mecca and Mecca is the name of the sanctuary is false.
Mention of those who said what we said about that: that Mecca is a place crowded with people for circumambulation:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ghifari,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah, he said: Bakkah is the location of the House, and Mecca is everything else.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, he said:
m: A woman passed in front of a man while he was praying and she was circumambulating the House, so he pushed her.

x: It is Mecca, some parts of it weeping over others.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-Samad told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It was called Bakkah because people wept in it, men and women.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Saeed, he said:
m: I said: Why is it called Mecca? He said: Because they weep in it. He said: Meaning: They crowd together.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Al-Zubayr, he said:
m: It was called Bakkah because they came to it as pilgrims.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed, for God has blessed all people in it, so women pray in front of men, and it is not appropriate in any other city.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Mecca, people are in Mecca, some of them are in Mecca, men and women, some of them pray in front of others, this is not appropriate except in Mecca.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi, he said:
m: Bakkah is the location of the House, and Mecca is what is around it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yahya bin Azhar told me, on the authority of Ghalib bin Ubaid God:
m: that he asked Ibn Shihab about Bakkah, he said: Bakkah is the House and the Mosque. And he asked him about Mecca, Ibn Shihab said: Mecca is the entire Sanctuary.

c: Al-Husayn told us, Hisham told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid, who said:
m: Mecca, in Mecca there are men and women.

c: Abdul Jabbar bin Yahya Al-Ramli told me: Damrah bin Rabi’ah said:
m: Bakkah is the mosque, and Mecca is the houses.

x: Some of them said: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah, he said: It is Mecca. It was said: Blessed, because circumambulating it is a forgiveness of sins. As for the accusative of his saying: blessed, it is to depart from his saying: placed, because in placed there is a mention of the house with which he is occupied, and it is definite, and blessed is indefinite, and it is not appropriate for it to follow it in parsing. As for the saying of those who said: It is
h
the first House established for mankind
, according to what we mentioned in that, the saying of those we mentioned, then it is in the accusative case as a state of his saying:
h
for the one in Mecca
. Because the meaning of the speech according to their saying:
h
The first House established for mankind
is the House in Mecca, blessed.

So the House, according to them, is described as the one in Mecca, and the one connected to it is definite, and blessed is indefinite, so it is in the accusative case as a separation from it, according to the saying of some of them, and as a state according to the saying of some of them, and guidance is in the accusative case as a conjunction to his saying: blessed.
The readings differed in the reading of that. So he read it as the people of the regions read:
h
In it are clear signs
, in the plural of ayat, meaning:
h
in it are clear signs
. Ibn Abbas read it: There is a clear sign in it, meaning the Station of Abraham, meaning one sign. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying:
h
In it are clear signs
, and what are those signs?
Some of them said: The Station of Abraham, the Sacred Monument, and the like.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
In it are clear signs
, the Station of Abraham and the Mash’ar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Mujahid:
m: h
In it are clear signs
, the Station of Abraham, he said: The Station of Abraham, is one of the clear signs.

x: Others said: The clear signs, the station of Abraham.
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
In it are clear signs
, he said: Abraham stood up, and whoever entered it was safe.

x: Others said: The clear signs are the Station of Abraham.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
In it are clear signs
, the Station of Abraham. As for the clear signs, they are the Station of Abraham.

x: As for those who read that: There is a clear sign in it for monotheism, they meant by the clear sign the Station of Abraham.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: In it is a clear sign. He said: His feet in the station are a clear sign. He says:
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe
. He said: This is something else.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: In it is a clear sign, the Station of Abraham. He said: The trace of his feet in the Station is a clear sign.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is that of those who say: The clear signs, among them is the Station of Abraham. This is the opinion of Qatada and Mujahid, which was narrated by Muʿmar from them. So the speech would mean that it is among them, so he left out mentioning it because the speech indicates it.
This position is one of the clear signs, so what are the other signs for which it was said: clear signs?
Some of them are the Maqam, some are the Stone, and some are the Hatim. The most correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads it:
h
In it are clear signs

regarding sexual intercourse, because the readers of the Muslim countries agree that this is the correct reading and no other. As for the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the interpretation of the station of Abraham, we have mentioned it in Surat Al-Baqarah, and we have explained the most correct of the sayings there, and that in our view it is the station known by it. The interpretation of the verse is: The first House established for mankind, blessed and a guidance for the worlds, was that at Bakkah. In it were clear signs of God’s power and traces of His friend Abraham, including the trace of the foot of His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, in the stone on which he stood.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: Its interpretation is: The report that whoever committed a crime in the pre-Islamic era and then sought refuge in the House, will not be held accountable for it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe

. This was in the pre-Islamic era. If a man committed every crime against himself, then sought refuge in the sanctuary of God, he would not take it or seek it. But in Islam, he is not prevented from the limits of God. Whoever steals therein will have his hand cut off, whoever commits adultery therein will have the prescribed punishment carried out on him, and whoever kills therein will be killed. Qatada reported that Al-Hasan used to say: The sanctuary does not prevent from the limits of God. If he committed a crime outside the sanctuary, then sought refuge in the sanctuary, that would not prevent him from having the prescribed punishment carried out on him. Qatada saw what Al-Hasan said.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever enters it is safe
, he said: That was during the pre-Islamic era. As for today, if someone steals, his hand is cut off, if he kills, he is killed, and if he is able to defeat the polytheists, they are killed.

c: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, he said, Abdul Salam bin Harb told us, he said, Khasif told us, on the authority of Mujahid -
m: regarding a man who kills and then enters the Sacred Sanctuary - he said: He is taken, taken out of the Sacred Sanctuary, then the prescribed punishment is carried out on him. He says: killing.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Hammad,
m: similar to what Mujahid said.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of al-Hasan and Ata’ -
m: regarding a man who commits the prescribed punishment and takes refuge in the sanctuary - he leaves the sanctuary, and the prescribed punishment is carried out on him.

x: The interpretation of the verse, according to what these people say, is: It contains clear signs, the Station of Abraham, and whoever entered it from the people was safe in it during the pre-Islamic era.

Others said: The meaning of this is: And whoever enters it will be safe therein, in the sense of reward, like the saying of someone: Whoever stands up for me, I will honor him, meaning: Whoever stands up for me, I will honor him. They said: This was a matter that existed in the pre-Islamic era, the sanctuary was a refuge for every frightened person, and a shelter for every jinn, because no one who committed a crime was attacked there, and no man would expose the killer of his father or son to harm therein. They said: And it is the same in Islam, because Islam increased its glorification and honor.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib told me, he said, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said, Mujahid told us, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: If a man is subject to the prescribed punishment, whether he kills or steals, and enters the Sacred Sanctuary, he should not pledge allegiance or give shelter until he becomes fed up and leaves the Sacred Sanctuary, and the prescribed punishment should be carried out on him. I said to Ibn Abbas: But I do not see that! I see that he should be taken in his entirety, then taken out of the Sacred Sanctuary, and the prescribed punishment should be carried out on him, because the Sacred Sanctuary only increases his severity. Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated, they said: Ibn Idris narrated, he said: Abdul Malik narrated, on the authority of Ata' who said: Ibn al-Zubayr took Sa'd, the freed slave of Mu'awiyah - who was in a castle in Taif - and sent someone to Ibn Abbas to consult him about them: They are our enemy. Ibn Abbas sent him: If I found the killer of my father, I would not attack him. Ibn al-Zubayr sent him: Shall we not expel them from the sanctuary? Ibn Abbas sent him: Why not before you bring them into the sanctuary? Abu al-Sa'ib added in his hadith: So he expelled them and crucified them, and did not pay attention to what Ibn Abbas said.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Whoever commits an act of ritual impurity outside the Haram, then takes refuge in the Haram, he should not be approached, pledged allegiance to, spoken to, or given shelter until he leaves the Haram. When he leaves the Haram, he should be seized and the prescribed punishment should be carried out on him. He said: Whoever commits an act of ritual impurity in the Haram, the punishment should be carried out on him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said,
m: Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Nasr Surat Al Imran 3:97
h
In it are clear signs
[the station of Abraham].
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses (for one's journey).
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds.

c: Al-Salami told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Habeeba, on the authority of Dawud bin Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said:
m: Whoever commits an act of evil and then seeks protection in the House, he is safe, and the Muslims have no right to punish him for anything until he leaves. Then if he leaves, they will carry out the prescribed punishment on him.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: If I found the killer of Umar in the sanctuary, I would not attack him.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Laith told us, on the authority of Ata’:
m: Al-Walid ibn Utbah wanted to carry out the punishment in the sanctuary, so Ubayd ibn Umair said to him: Do not carry out the punishment on him in the sanctuary, unless he committed it in it.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: Mutraf told us, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: If he commits the prescribed punishment and then flees to the sanctuary, then he is safe. But if he commits it in the sanctuary, then the prescribed punishment is carried out on him in the sanctuary.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Firas, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: Whoever commits a prescribed punishment in the Sacred Sanctuary, the punishment will be carried out against him in the Sacred Sanctuary.
