And whoever commits it outside the Sacred Sanctuary and then enters the Sacred Sanctuary, he will not be spoken to or pledge allegiance to until he leaves the Sacred Sanctuary, and the punishment will be carried out against him.

c: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, he said, Abdul Salam bin Harb told us, he said, Ata bin Al-Saib told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair.
m: And on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah - regarding a man who kills and then enters the Sacred Sanctuary - he said: The people of Mecca do not sell him or buy from him, nor give him water or food or shelter - he listed many things - until he leaves the Sacred Sanctuary, then he is punished for his sin.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn al-Saʿib, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If a man commits a sin and then enters the Sacred Sanctuary, he is not to be given food, drink, shelter, spoken to, married, or sold. Then, when he leaves it, the prescribed punishment is carried out on him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If a man commits an act of ritual impurity and then enters the Sacred Sanctuary, he should not be given shelter, nor should he sit with others, nor should he pledge allegiance, nor should he be given food or drink, until he leaves the Sacred Sanctuary.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for his saying:
h
And whoever enters it is safe
, if a man kills a man, then comes to the Kaaba and seeks refuge in it, then the brother of the murdered man meets him, it is never permissible for him to kill him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever enters it will be safe from the Fire.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Muslim told us, Abu Asim told us, Zuraiq bin Muslim Al-Makhzumi told us, Ziyad bin Abi Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe
, he said: Safe from the Fire.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter in our view is the saying of Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and al-Hasan, and those who said: The meaning of that is: And whoever enters it from someone other than him who has taken refuge in it, seeking protection from it, is safe as long as he is in it, but he leaves it and the punishment is carried out on him, if he committed what he deserves in another place and then took refuge in it. And if he committed it in it, it is carried out on him in it. The interpretation of the verse is:
h
In it are clear signs
, the Station of Abraham, and whoever enters it among the people seeking refuge in it will be safe from that from which he sought refuge, until he leaves it.
What prevented you from carrying out the punishment on him?

Because all the predecessors agreed that whoever committed a crime in another place and then sought refuge in it, he will not be held accountable for his crime in it. They only differed about the manner of removing him from it in order to hold him accountable for it.
Some of them said: Its description is: preventing meanings that, when prevented and lost, one is forced to leave.

Others said: There is no description for that other than removing it from what is possible to remove from the meanings that lead to the implementation of God’s punishment on it with it. Therefore, we said: It is not permissible to carry out the punishment on him in it except after he is expelled from it. As for the one who is subject to the punishment in it, there is no disagreement among all that the punishment is carried out on him in it. Both issues are a principle agreed upon in their ruling as we have described.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is your proof that expelling the one who seeks refuge in the House - if he comes to it seeking protection from a crime he committed or from a punishment he suffered - from the Sacred Sanctuary is permissible in order to carry out the punishment on him and take him for the crime, while you have acknowledged that God Almighty has made whoever enters it safe, and the meaning of safe is not the meaning of fearful? So how do they differ?

We said that, because of the consensus of all the scholars of the nation, both early and late, that expelling the one who seeks refuge in Him - from a crime he committed or an abomination he committed for which he was required to be punished - with some meanings of expulsion to take what is required of him, is obligatory upon the leader of the Muslims and the people of Islam with him. They only differed on the reason for which he leaves it.

Some of them said: The reason for which it is permissible to expel him from it is that all Muslims did not pledge allegiance to him, feed him, give him water, shelter him, speak to him, and other similar meanings in which the one seeking refuge with him has no stability with some of them, so how about with all of them?

Others among them said: Rather, his removal to carry out the punishment that is required of him is obligatory in all meanings of removal. Since there was consensus among all that the ruling of God - regarding someone who sought refuge in the House from a punishment that had befallen him or a crime that he committed - was to expel him from it, in order to carry out what God had obligated the believers to carry out upon it, then they differed about the reason by which it was permissible to expel him from it. It was necessary for them and their Imam to expel him from it in any sense in which they could expel him from it, so that they could carry out upon him the punishment that was incumbent upon him outside it if he had sought refuge in it from outside, as we have explained before. Moreover, God Almighty did not set any of His limits for any of His creation because of a spot or location that someone who was obliged to do so went to.

The report has been reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I have made Medina sacred just as Abraham made Mecca sacred. There is no disagreement among the entire Ummah that if someone seeks refuge from a punishment imposed on him in the sanctuary of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he will be held accountable for the punishment therein. Were it not for what I mentioned about the consensus of the predecessors that the sanctuary of Abraham is not to be carried out on someone who seeks refuge in it from a punishment imposed on him until he has done what he was obligated to do, then the most deserving of places in which the obligations of God that He has imposed on His servants, whether killing or otherwise, should be performed would be the greatest of places to God, like the sanctuary of God and the sanctuary of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.

But we were commanded to expel from the sanctuary of God whoever we were commanded to expel in order to carry out the prescribed punishment, because of what we mentioned about the Ummah doing that by inheritance. The meaning of the statement - since the matter is as we have described - is: whoever enters it is safe as long as he is in it. So since that is the case, whoever seeks refuge in it from the punishment that is upon him, seeking protection in it, is safe as long as he is in it until he leaves it. And he only becomes fearful after leaving or being removed from it, so at that time he is neither entering it nor in it.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: It is an obligation that is incumbent upon God - upon those of those who are obligated to perform the Hajj - to perform the Hajj to His Sacred House. We have previously explained the meaning of Hajj, and we have demonstrated the correctness of what we have said about its meaning, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Whoever can afford a way to it, and what is the way that requires the obligation of Hajj if one is able to do so?
Some of them said: It is the provisions and the mount.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said,
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said:
h
Whoever can find a way to it
, he said: provisions and a mount.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Amr ibn Dinar said:
m: The provisions and the mount.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Abu Janab, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whoever can find a way to it
, he said: provisions and a camel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses, and the expenses are for the servant’s body to be healthy, and for him to have the price of provisions and a mount without being overburdened by it.

c: Khallad bin Aslam told us, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Bajali, who said:
m: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about his statement:
h
Whoever can afford it
, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever has three hundred dirhams, then that is Surat Al Imran 3:97
h
In it are clear signs
[the station of Abraham].
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses (for one's journey).
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds. the way to it.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ishaq bin Othman, he said:
m: I heard Ata’ say: The path is the provisions and the mount.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for
h
whoever can find a way to it
, Ibn Abbas said: The way is a mount and provisions.

c: Al-Muthanna and Ahmad bin Hazim told me, they said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Suqah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
Whoever can find a way to it
, he said: provisions and a mount.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: The provisions and the mount.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses of making the journey to it.’ A man said: O Messenger of God, what is the expenses of making the journey? He said: ‘Provisions and a mount.’”

x: Those who said this article based their argument on reports narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner similar to what they said about it.
Mentioning the narration on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibrahim bin Yazid al-Khawzi told us, he said:
m: I heard Muhammad bin Abbad bin Jaʿfar narrating, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, he said: “A man stood up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What is the way? He said: Provisions and a mount.”

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Khawzi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God Almighty: ‘Whoever can afford the expenses’, he said: The expenses to Hajj are provisions and a mount.”

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Yunus told us, and Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses of the journey to it.’ They said: O Messenger of God, what is the expenses of the journey? He said: ‘Provisions and a mount.’”

c: Abu Uthman al-Muqaddami and al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us,
m: Hilal ibn Abdullah, the client of Rabia ibn Amr ibn Muslim al-Bahili told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever has provisions and a mount to take him to the House of God and does not perform Hajj, then it does not matter if he dies a Jew or a Christian. This is because God Almighty says in His Book:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses for one’s own expenses.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: It has reached us that a speaker or a man said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of God, what is the way to it? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever finds provisions and a mount.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Tirmidhi told us, Shadh ibn Fayyad al-Basri told us, Hilal Abu Hashim told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has provisions and a mount but does not perform Hajj dies a Jew or a Christian. This is because God says in His Book: ‘
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses’” the verse.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatada and Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: “A man said: O Messenger of God, what is the way to it? He said: The provisions and the mount.”

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly.

x: Others said: The way that if a person is able to do Hajj, he must do it: the ability to reach it. They said: This may be by walking or riding, and it may be with both of them the inability to reach it: due to the road being blocked by an enemy, or the scarcity of water, and the like. They said: There is no clearer explanation of that than what God Almighty explained, that he is able to do it, and that is: reaching it without any obstacle or barrier between him and it, and this may be by walking alone even if he lacks a vehicle, and it may be by vehicle or otherwise.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Karima, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses, he said: According to one’s ability.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whoever can find a way to it

, he said: Provisions and a mount. If he is a healthy young man who has no money, then he must hire himself out for his food and nap until he completes his Hajj with it. Someone said to him: Did God command people to walk to the House? He said: If some of them had an inheritance in Mecca, would they abandon it? By God, he would set out even if he had to crawl!! Hajj is also obligatory upon him.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ata’ said:
m: Whoever finds something to attain, has found a way, as God Almighty said:
h
Whoever can find a way to it

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Abu Hani told us,
m: Amer was asked about this verse:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses. He said: The expenses are what God makes easy.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: Whoever finds something to convey, has found a way to it.

x: Others said: The way to do that is health.
Who said that?
Muhammad bin Hamid, Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam and Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told us, they said:

c: Abu Abdul-Rahman Al-Muqri told us, he said: Haywah bin Shureih and Ibn Lahi’ah told us, they said: Shurahbil bin Sharik Al-Ma’afari told us:
m: that he heard Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, say about this verse:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses. He said: The expenses are health.

x: Others said: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God

, those who can afford the expenses, he said: Whoever finds the strength to spend, the body, and the means to carry it. He said: And if he has enough in his body to make it impossible for him to make Hajj, then Hajj is not obligatory upon him, even if he has the strength in money, as if he is healthy in body but does not find money or strength, they say: He is not required to walk.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of those who said the words of Ibn al-Zubayr and Ata’: That it is according to one’s ability. Because the path in the speech of the Arabs means the road. So whoever has a path to Hajj that is not prevented from it by time, or inability, or an enemy, or lack of water on his way, or excess, or weakness from walking, then he must perform the obligatory Hajj, and nothing will suffice him except performing it. But if he does not have a path - I mean by that: if he is not able to perform Hajj, because some of the meanings that we have described are difficult for him - then he is one of those who does not find a path to it and is not able to do it. Because the ability to do that is the capacity to do it. And whoever is unable to do it for some of the reasons that we have mentioned or otherwise, then he is not able and has no path to it.

We said: This statement is more correct than what contradicts it, because God Almighty did not specify, when He made the obligation of Hajj obligatory for people, some of those who are able to do it by dropping the obligation from them, so it is for everyone who is able to do it by the generality of the verse. As for the reports that were narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this as: provisions and a mount, they are reports whose chains of transmission are questionable, and it is not permissible to use such reports as evidence in religion.
The recitation differed in the recitation of Hajj.
A group of the people of Medina and Iraq read it with a kasra:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
Another group of them read it with the fat-ha:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
. They are two languages known to the Arabs. The kasr is the language of the people of Najd, and the fathah is the language of the people of Aliyah.
We have not seen anyone from the Arabs claim a difference between them in meaning or anything else, other than what we mentioned about the difference between the two languages, except for what:

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rifai told us, he said,
m: Hussein Al-Ja’fi said, Hajj is open, a noun, and Hajj is closed, a verb. This is a statement that I have not seen people with knowledge of the languages of the Arabs and the meanings of their speech know. Rather, I have seen them agree on what I have described, that they are two languages with one meaning. What we say about reading this is that the two readings - since they are widespread in the reading of the people of Islam, and there is no difference between them in meaning or anything else - then they are two readings that have come as proof. So whichever of the two readings - I mean: with the kasra or fatha of the ha’ of al-Hajj - the reader reads, then he is correct in his reading. As for min which is with his saying: whoever is able, it is in the accusative case as a replacement for al-nas, because the meaning of the statement is: And God has obligated whoever among the people is able to find a way to perform Hajj to the House, His Hajj. So when the mention of al-nas came before min, He explained with his saying: whoever is able to find a way to it, who among them is obligated to do that. Because that is obligatory on some of the people and not all of them.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, Surat Al Imran 3:97
h
In it are clear signs
[the station of Abraham].
h
And whoever enters it shall be safe
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses (for one's journey).
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds.

He means: Whoever denies what God has obligated him to do of the obligation of Hajj to His House, and rejects it and disbelieves in it, then God is independent of him and of his Hajj and his deeds, and of all of His creation from the jinn and mankind, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi al-Mujalid, he said:
m: I heard Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves
, he said: Whoever claims that it is not obligatory upon him.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is independent of the worlds, they said: Whoever denies the Hajj and disbelieves in it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Whoever denies it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Imran al-Qattan told us, he said:
m: Whoever claims that Hajj is not obligatory upon him.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is independent of the worlds, he said: Whoever denies it and does not see that it is a right upon him, then that is disbelief.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves
, he said: whoever disbelieves in Hajj.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is independent of the worlds, he said: Whoever disbelieves in Hajj, disbelieves in God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Yaʿla bin Asad told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
, those who can afford the expenses for one’s own expenses. He said: Whoever does not see it as obligatory upon him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves
, he said: in the Hajj.

x: Others said: This means that he should not believe that he will be rewarded for his Hajj, nor that he will be sinful or punished for abandoning it.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Abdullah bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is independent of the worlds, he said: It is what if he performs Hajj he does not see as righteousness, and if he sits he does not see as sin.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It is what if he performs Hajj he does not see as righteousness, and if he sits he does not see as sinful.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Fitr told us, on the authority of Abu Dawud Nafi’, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by people, whoever is able to make the journey.
h
And whoever disbelieves

, then indeed, God is independent of the worlds.’ A man from Hudhayl stood up and said: O Messenger of God, whoever abandons it has disbelieved? He said: Whoever abandons it and does not fear its punishment, and whoever performs the pilgrimage and does not hope for its reward, then that is he.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is independent of the worlds, meaning: whoever disbelieves in Hajj, and does not see his Hajj as righteousness, nor does his abandonment of it as sin.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
And whoever disbelieves
in God and the Last Day.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: I asked him about his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is independent of the worlds. What is this disbelief? He said: Whoever disbelieves in God and the Last Day.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And whoever disbelieves
, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God and the Last Day.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God

, those who can afford the expenses, he said: “When the verse of Hajj was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered the people of all religions and said: O people, God, the Almighty, has prescribed Hajj for you, so perform Hajj. One religion believed in it, and it is those who believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believed in him. Five religions disbelieved in it, and they said: We do not believe in it, nor do we pray to it, nor do we face it. So God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds.’”

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Abu Hani told us, he said,
m: Amer was asked about his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves
, he said: Whoever among creation disbelieves, then God is independent of him.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding God’s statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves
, he said: Whoever disbelieves in God and the Last Day.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And whoever desires other than Islam as religion
r
(Al Imran 3:85)
, the religions said: We are Muslims! So God Almighty revealed: “
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
- those who can afford the expenses for one's expenses to it.
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds.” So the believers performed Hajj, and the disbelievers stayed away.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
And whoever disbelieves
in these verses in the Station of Abraham.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds, so he recited: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed, so he recited until he reached: “And
h
whoever can find a way to it
h
And whoever disbelieves

,” he said: Whoever disbelieves in these verses, then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds, it is not as they say: If he does not perform Hajj and he is rich and has the strength, then he has disbelieved in them. And some of the polytheists said: We disbelieve in them but we do not do them! So God, the Almighty, said: then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds.

x: Others said: Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Muslim told me, he said, Abu Omar Al-Dharee’ told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Baqiyah, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - then indeed
, God is free from need of the worlds, he said: Whoever disbelieves in the House.
Others said: His disbelief in him means that he left him until he died.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for whoever disbelieves, whoever finds what he can use to perform Hajj but does not perform Hajj, he is a disbeliever.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of
h
and whoever disbelieves
is that whoever denies the obligation of this and rejects its necessity, then God is independent of him, his argument, and all the worlds. We said that this is more appropriate because his statement,
h
And whoever disbelieves
, following his statement,
h
And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God

, those who can afford the expenses, is more appropriate for it to be report about the disbelievers in Hajj than it is for it to be report about someone else, even though the one who disbelieves in the obligation of Hajj on the one upon whom God imposed it, is a disbeliever in God, and disbelief is originally denial, and whoever denies Him and His obligation, then there is no doubt that if he performs Hajj, he does not hope to be righteous by his Hajj, because he who left it and did not perform Hajj did not see it as a sin.
These interpretations, even if the wording differs, are similar in meaning.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
So he read it as the people of the regions read: In it are clear signs, in the plural of ayat, meaning: in it are clear signs.
Ibn Abbas read it: There is a clear sign in it, meaning the Station of Abraham, meaning one sign.
Abu Jaafar said: As for those who read that: There is a clear sign in it for monotheism, they meant by the clear sign the Station of Abraham.

The most correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads it: In it are clear signs regarding sexual intercourse, because the readers of the Muslim countries agree that this is the correct reading and no other.

Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: ‘And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses of making the journey to it.’
Abu Jaafar said: The recitation differed in the recitation of Hajj.
A group of the people of Medina and Iraq read it with a kasra: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God.
Another group of them read it with the fat-ha: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God.

What we say about reading this is that the two readings - since they are widespread in the reading of the people of Islam, and there is no difference between them in meaning or anything else - then they are two readings that have come as proof.
So whichever of the two readings - I mean: with the kasra or fatha of the ha’ of al-Hajj - the reader reads, then he is correct in his reading.

x: By that he means: O group of Jews of the Children of Israel and others from all those who claim to follow the religion of what God the Almighty has revealed from His books, from those who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and rejected his prophethood: Why do you disbelieve in the signs of God? He says: Why do you deny the proofs of God that He gave to Muhammad in your books and other than them, which have been established for you with his truthfulness, prophethood, and proof, and you know. He says: Why do you deny that from his command, and you know his truthfulness?
So God, the Most High, informed about them that they deliberately disbelieved in God and His Messenger, knowingly and knowingly, and they disbelieved, and:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O People of the Book, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God? As for the verses of God, it is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while God is Witness over what you do? He said: They are the Jews and Christians.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: O group of Jews of the Children of Israel and others who claim to believe in the Books of God: Why do you turn away from the path of God? He says: Why do you go astray from the path of God and His way that He has prescribed for His prophets, His saints, and the people of faith? He who believes, He says: He who believes in God and His Messenger and what he brought from God, seek to make it crooked, meaning: seek to make it crooked. The ha and the alif in his saying: you seek it refer to the path, and he made it feminine because of the feminization of the path. The meaning of his saying:
h
You seek to make it crooked

, is from the saying of the poet, who is Sahim Abd Bani Al-Hashas: He wanted you, and you did not want him until you found him, as if you had made an appointment with him yesterday Meaning: your request and what you are asking for.

It is said: Abghni khudan meaning seek it for me. So if they want to help me seek it and seek it with me, they say: Abghni with the alif open. Likewise, it is said: Ahlbni meaning: Keep me from milking, and Ahlbni meaning help me with it. And so is everything that has been mentioned of this type, so on this basis. As for crookedness, it is deviation and inclination. What is meant by that is: straying from guidance. God Almighty says: Why do you turn away from the religion of God those who have believed in God and His Messenger, seeking to distort the religion of God from its laws and straightness? The speech went astray, and the meaning is for its people. It is as if the meaning is: You seek for the people of God’s religion, and for those who are on the path of truth, a deviation. He says: a deviation from the truth, and a deviation from the right path and guidance. Al-Awj, with a kasra on the first letter, means a sway in religion and speech.
Al-Awj, with a fatha on the first letter, means a tilt in a wall, canal, or anything that is upright and straight. As for His statement:
h
And you are witnesses

, it means: witnesses that what you are turning away from of the path is the truth, that you know it and find it in your books. And God is not unaware of what you do, meaning: God is not unaware of the deeds that you do that He does not approve of for His servants and other deeds of yours, so that He hastens to punish you for them immediately, or delays that for you until you meet Him and He recompenses you for them. It has been mentioned that these two verses, from His saying:
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God? and the verses after them until His saying: And
h
for those is a great punishment
, were revealed about a Jewish man who tried to incite discord between the two tribes of Aws and Khazraj after Islam, to return to what they had been upon in their ignorance of enmity and hatred.

So God rebuked him for that action, and condemned what he did and rebuked him for it. He also preached to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and forbade them from division and disagreement, and commanded them to unite and come together. The novel mentioned that: Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said, a trustworthy man narrated, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: Shas ibn Qays, who was an old man who had been oppressed in the pre-Islamic era, a great disbeliever, who bore a grudge against the Muslims and was extremely envious of them, passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from the Aws and Khazraj, in a gathering where he had gathered them to talk. He was angered by what he saw of their gathering, their harmony, and their reconciliation with Islam, after the enmity that had existed between them in the pre-Islamic era.

He said: The leaders of Banu Qaylah have gathered in this country! By God, we have no place with them when their leaders gather in it! So he ordered a young Jewish man who was with him, saying: Go to them, sit with them, and remind them of the Day of Bu’ath and what had happened before it, and recite to them some of the poems they had exchanged on that day - and the Day of Bu’ath was a day when the Aws and Khazraj fought, and the Aws were victorious over the Khazraj - and he did so. Then the people spoke, argued and boasted, until two men from the two tribes jumped on the camel: Aws ibn Qayzi, one of Banu Haritha ibn al-Harith from the Aws, and Jabbar ibn Sakhr, one of Banu Salamah from the Khazraj. They argued, then one of them said to the other: If you wish, by God, we will return it now as a young camel! Both groups became angry and said: We have done so, weapons, weapons! Your meeting place is al-Zahira - and al-Zahira means al-Harra - so they went out to it.
The people turned aside. The Aws joined together, and the Khazraj joined together, on their claim that Surat Al Imran 3:99 Say, "
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you avert from the way of God those who believe, seeking to make it crooked while you are witnesses? And God is not unaware of what you do." they had in the pre-Islamic era. report of that reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he went out to them with those of his companions who were with him from the emigrants until he came to them and said: O group of Muslims, by God, is it the claim of the pre-Islamic era while I am among you, after God has guided you to Islam and honored you with it, and cut off from you the matter of the pre-Islamic era, and saved you from disbelief, and united you with it, that you will return to what you were upon as disbelievers? The people realized that it was a temptation from Satan and a plot from their enemy, so they threw down their weapons and wept, and the men of Aws and Khazraj embraced each other, then they left with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, listening and obeying, God had extinguished from them the plot of God’s enemy, Sha’s bin Qays, and what he had done.
God revealed about Sha’s bin Qays and what he had done: “Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while God is Witness to what you do? Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you avert from the way of God those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?’” 10:10. God the Almighty revealed about Aws bin Qayzi and Jabbar bin Sakhr and those who were with them from their people who had done what they had done, because of what Sha’s bin Qays had brought upon them of the affairs of the Age of Ignorance: O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your belief, to disbelief, until His saying:
h
For those is a great punishment
. It was said that what he meant by his saying: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you avert [people] from the way of God?’ was the group of Jews, the Children of Israel, who were in the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when these verses were revealed, and the Christians.

And that their averting people from the way of God was because they informed those who asked them about the Prophet of God, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do they find mention of him in their books? That they did not find his description in their books.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture

, why do you avert from the way of God those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?’ When someone asked them, Do you find Muhammad? they would say, No! So they averted people from him, and sought to make Muhammad crooked and destroyed.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you avert from the way of God?’ He says: Why do you avert from Islam and from the Prophet of God, those who believe in God,
h
and you are witnesses

to what you read from the Book of God: that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that Islam is the religion of God, which does not accept anything other than it and does not reward anything other than it, you find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘
h
O People of the Scripture
, why do you avert [people] from the way of God?’ He said: They are the Jews and Christians. He forbade them from averting the Muslims from the way of God, and they wanted to lead people astray.

x: The interpretation of the verse, according to what al-Suddi said, is: O group of Jews, why do you turn away from Muhammad and prevent those who believe in him from following him, by concealing his description that you find in your books? And Muhammad, according to this statement, is the path,
h
You seek to make it crooked

, you seek Muhammad’s destruction. As for the rest of the narrations other than it and the sayings about it, it is similar to the interpretation that we explained before: that the meaning of the path that he mentioned in this place is: Islam, and what Muhammad brought of the truth from God.
The people of interpretation differed about who was meant by that.
Some of them said: What he meant by his saying:
h
O you who believe
, is the Aws and the Khazraj, and by those who were given the Scripture, is Shas bin Qais the Jew, based on what we mentioned before about his story on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam.

Others said about those who believed, like the statement of Zaid bin Aslam, except that they said: The one who spoke between him and others from the Ansar until they wanted to fight, and the Jew found fault with him in them: Tha’laba bin Anma Al-Ansari.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed

, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your belief, to disbelief. He said: It was revealed about Tha’laba ibn ‘Anmah al-Ansari. There was a discussion between him and some of the Ansar, and a Jew from Qaynuqa’ walked between them, and some of them attacked each other, until the two groups of the Aws and the Khazraj wanted to take up arms and fight, so God Almighty revealed: If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your belief, to disbelievers. He said: If you take up arms and fight, you have disbelieved. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated, he said: Jaafar bin Sulaiman narrated, on the authority of Hamid Al-Araj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed

, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, he said: The tribes of the Ansar were grouped into two clans: Aws and Khazraj, and there was war, bloodshed and hatred between them in the pre-Islamic period, until God bestowed upon them Islam and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God extinguished the war that had been between them and united them through Islam. He said: While a man from Aws and a man from Khazraj were sitting and talking, and with them was a Jew sitting, he kept reminding them of their days and the enmity that had been between them, until they quarreled and then fought. He said: So this one called out to his people and this one to his people, so they went out with weapons and lined up in rows with one another. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was present that day in Medina, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and continued to walk among them to these and to those to calm them down, until they returned and laid down their weapons, so God Almighty revealed the Qur’an regarding that:
h
O you who have believed
, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture until His saying: a great punishment.

x: The interpretation of the verse is:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger, and have acknowledged what their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them from God, if you obey a group of those who claim to be from the Book, from the People of the Torah and the Gospel, and accept from them what they command you, they will mislead you and turn you back, after your belief in the Messenger of your Lord, and after your acknowledgment of what he brought from your Lord, into disbelievers. He says: denying what you have believed in and confirmed of the truth that came to you from your Lord.
So God, the Most High, forbade them from seeking their advice or accepting their opinion or counsel, and He, the Most High, informs them that they are full of rancor, deceit, envy and hatred, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you back after your belief to disbelief, God has already spoken to you about them as you hear, and has warned you and informed you of their misguidance, so do not trust them with your religion, and do not seek their advice regarding yourselves, for they are the enemies, envious and misguided. How can you trust a people who disbelieved in their Book, killed their messengers, were confused about their religion, and were helpless against themselves? By God, they are the people of suspicion and enmity!

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

x: By that, the Most High means: And how can you disbelieve, O believers, after your belief in God and His Messenger, then turn back on your heels, while the verses of God are recited to you, meaning the proofs of God upon you that He sent down in His Book to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among you is His Messenger, another proof against you from God, along with the verses of His Book, calling you to the truth, showing you guidance and righteousness, and forbidding you from error and misguidance? The Most High says to them: What is your excuse before your Lord for your denial of the prophethood of your Prophet, your turning back on your heels, and your return to the matter of your ignorance, if you return to that and disbelieve, and in it are these clear proofs and clear signs on the error of your action if you do it? Like: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you
, the verse, two clear signs: the conscience of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Book of God.

As for the Prophet of God, he has passed away, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for the Book of God, God has kept it among you as a mercy from God and a blessing, in it is what He has made lawful and unlawful, obedience to Him and disobedience to Him. As for his saying:
h
And whoever holds fast to God has certainly been guided to a straight path

, he means: And whoever clings to the causes of God and adheres to His religion and obedience, has certainly been guided, meaning: He has been guided to a clear path and a straight, uncrooked path, through which he will be guided to the pleasure of God, and to salvation from the punishment of God and to winning His Paradise, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever holds fast to God has been guided

, he said: He believes in God. The root of the word ‘asm’ is prevention. So, anyone who prevents something is its protector, and the one who is protected by it is protected by it. From this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: I am the son of the two capitals, Banu Tamim. When the two events are great, we will be afflicted. That is why the rope is called Issam, and the reason that causes a man to achieve his need is called Issam. From this is the saying of Al-A’sha: To the man Qais, I extend my journey and take protection from every living being By protection, he means the reasons, the reasons of covenant and security. It is said: I held fast to a rope from so-and-so. I held fast to a rope from him, I held fast to him, and I held fast to him. The most eloquent of the two languages is to insert the letter ba, as God Almighty said: And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of God
r
(Al Imran 3:103)

. It has also been said: I held fast to him, as the poet said: If you reward brotherhood with the same and console me, then you hold fast to your ropes He said: I held fast to the ropes, and he did not add the letter ba. This is similar to their saying: I took hold of the reins, and I took hold of the reins, and I clung to them, and I clung to them, as the poet said: India was adorned with a young apron, and you, having committed a sin, did not know what a dream was. I have explained the meaning of guidance and the path, and that it refers to Islam, in what has passed before with its evidence, so we disliked repeating it in this place. It was mentioned that what was revealed regarding the reason for the two tribes’ transgression: Aws and Khazraj, was His saying:
h
And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hasan bin Atiyah told us, he said, Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Al-Aghar bin Al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifa bin Husain, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: There was a war between the Aws and the Khazraj during the pre-Islamic era every month. While they were sitting, they mentioned what had happened between them until they became angry, so some of them rose up against each other with weapons, and this verse was revealed:
h
And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you
and among you is His Messenger to the end of the two verses, And remember the favor of God upon you when you were enemies to the end of the verse.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O group of those who have believed in God and His Messenger, fear God, fear God and observe Him by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience, the right fear of Him, the right fear of Him, which is to obey Him and not disobey Him, to thank Him and not be ungrateful, to remember Him and not forget, and do not die, O believers in God and His Messenger, except as Muslims to your Lord, submitting to Him in obedience, sincerely devoting divinity and worship to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
Fear God as He should be feared
, he said: That He be obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not ungrateful.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Murrah al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Kuraib and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Laith, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra bin Shurahil Al-Bakili, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Masoudi, on the authority of Zubayd Al-Ayami, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun:
m: h
Fear God as He should be feared
. He said: That He should be obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not ungrateful, and remembered and not forgotten.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Shu’bah told us, Amr bin Murrah told us, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim, who said:
m: To be obeyed and not disobeyed, to be thanked and not ungrateful, and to be remembered and not forgotten.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, he said,
m: I heard Murrah Al-Hamdani narrating, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim, regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
Fear God as He should be feared
, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Tawus:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
, that is, to obey Him and not disobey Him.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
, he said, As He should be feared, that is, to be obeyed and not disobeyed.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, he said, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Then he went forward to them - meaning to the believers from the Ansar - and said:
h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
h
and do not die except as Muslims
. As for as He should be feared, He is obeyed and not disobeyed, remembered and not forgotten, and thanked and not denied.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
, that is, obey Him and not disobey Him. He said:
h
And do not die except as Muslims

x: Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is as follows:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Fear God as He should be feared

, he said: As He should be feared, that is, they strive in God’s cause as He should be striven in, and they are not deterred by the blame of any blamer in God’s cause, and they stand up for God with justice even if it is against themselves, their fathers, and their children. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding this verse: Is it abrogated or not?

x: Some of them said: It is a binding and not abrogated ruling.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his saying:
h
Fear God as He should be feared
, that it was not abrogated, but as He should be feared, is that you strive in God’s cause as He should be striven for. Then he mentioned the interpretation of it that we mentioned from him earlier.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays ibn Saʿd, on the authority of Tawus:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
. If you do not do so and are not able to, then do not die except as Muslims.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Tawus said, regarding his statement:
h
And do not die except as Muslims
, he says: If you do not fear Him, then do not die except as Muslims.

x: Others said: It is abrogated, abrogated by His statement:
h
So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
h
and do not die except as Muslims
. Then He revealed relief and ease, and returned with His reward and mercy for what He knows of the weakness of His creation, saying:
h
So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64
:16), so this verse came, in which there is relief, well-being, and ease.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal Al-Anmati told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
h
and do not die except as Muslims

. He said: This verse in At-Taghabun abrogated it: So fear God as much as you are able, and listen and obey (al-Taghabun 64:16), and upon it the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to hearing and obeying as much as they were able.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, he said:
m: When the verse,
h
Fear God as He should be feared
, was revealed, then after it was revealed,
h
So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64
:16), this verse in Al-ʿImran was abrogated.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared
h
and do not die except as Muslims
. But the people could not bear this, so God abrogated it for them and said: So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun: 16).

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
fear God as He should be feared

, he said: A severe matter has come! They said: Who knows the extent of this or can attain it? So when he knew that this had become difficult for them, he abrogated it for them and brought this other one and said:
h
So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64
:16), so he abrogated it. As for his saying:
h
And do not die except as Muslims
, its interpretation is as follows:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Tawus:
m: h
And do not die except as Muslims
, he said: On Islam, and on the sanctity of Islam.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And cling to all of God’s causes. By that, may His praise be glorified, He means:
h
And hold fast

to the religion of God which He has commanded you with, and His covenant which He has entrusted to you in His Book to you, of harmony and unity upon the word of truth, and submission to God’s command. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of adherence. As for the rope, it is the means by which one reaches the goal and need. That is why safety is called a rope, because it is a means by which one reaches the elimination of fear and salvation from panic and terror. From this is the saying of A’sha of Banu Tha’labah: If the ropes of a tribe cross it, it will take its ropes from the other tribe to you. And from it is the saying of God Almighty: Except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
r
(Al Imran 3:112)
. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, that he said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God, he said: the group.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God, he said: The rope of God is the group.

x: Others said: He meant by that the Qur’an and the covenant in which he made the covenant.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God, the strong rope of God that he commanded us to hold fast to: this is the Qur’an.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God, he said: to the covenant of God and His command.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: The path is full of devils, they call out: O servant of God, come this way! To turn people away from the path of God, so hold fast to the rope of God, for the rope of God is the Book of God.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God. As for the rope of God, it is the Book of God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: By the rope of God, by the covenant of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’:
m: By the rope of God, he said: the covenant.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: h
And hold fast
to the rope of God, he said: The rope of God, the Qur’an.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God, he said: The Qur’an.

c: Saeed bin Yahya told us: Asbat bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman Al-Arzami, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Book of God is the rope of God extended from heaven to earth.”

x: Others said: Rather, it is the sincerity of monotheism to God.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And hold fast
, Surat Al Imran 3:103
h
And hold fast
to the rope of God all together
h
and do not be divided
h
And remember the favor of God upon you
h
when you were enemies
and He united your hearts
h
and you became
, by His favor, brothers.
h
And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire
and He saved you from it. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be guided. all together, to the rope of God, he said: Hold fast to sincerity to God alone.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And hold fast
, all together, to the rope of God, he said: The rope is Islam. And he recited:
h
And do not be divided

x: He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
And do not be divided
h
and do not be divided

from the religion of God and His covenant that He entrusted to you in His Book, of unity and gathering in obedience to Him and to obedience to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and adhering to his command, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And do not be divided
h
and remember the favor of God upon you

, for God, the Almighty, has hated division for you, and has presented it to you, and warned you against it, and has forbidden you from it, and has approved for you obedience, harmony, and community, so be satisfied for yourselves with what God has approved for you if you are able, and there is no power except with God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abi Al-Aaliyah:
m: h
And do not be divided
, do not be hostile to him, he says: on sincerity to God, and be brothers in him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me: Al-Awza’i told him, Yazid Al-Raqashi told him that
m: he heard Anas bin Malik say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, and my nation will split into seventy-two sects, all of them in Hell except one. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is this one? He said: He closed his hand and said: The group, “
h
And hold fast
to the rope of God all together and do not become divided.”

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said,
m: I heard Al-Awza’i narrating, on the authority of Yazid Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Thabit bin Qutbah Al-Madani, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said:
m: O people, adhere to obedience and congregation, for it is the rope of God that He has commanded, and what you dislike in congregation and obedience is better than what you like in division.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari told us, he said, Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Thabit bin Qataba, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Masoud while he was giving a sermon and he was saying: O people, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Ismail bin Hafs Al-Abli told us, he said, Abdullah bin Numayr Abu Hisham told us, he said, Mujalid bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Thabit bin Qataba Al-Madani, he said: Abdullah said:
m: You must obey and adhere to the group, for it is the rope of God that He commanded, then he mentioned something similar.

x: What he meant by the words of God Almighty:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you
, is remember what God has bestowed upon you of harmony and unity in Islam. The Arab scholars differed regarding his saying:
h
When you were enemies
, He brought your hearts together.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said about this: The speech stopped at his saying:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you

, then he explained it by saying: And He brought your hearts together, and he informed of what they were in before the bringing together, just as you say: He held the wall from leaning. Some grammarians of Kufa said that his statement,
h
When you were enemies
, He brought your hearts together, followed his statement,
h
And remember the favor of God upon you
, without being interrupted by it.
The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that his statement,
h
When you were enemies
, He brought your hearts together, is connected to his statement,
h
And remember the favor of God upon you
, and is not disconnected from it. The interpretation of this is: And remember, O believers, the blessing of God upon you which He bestowed upon you,
h
when you were enemies
in your polytheism, killing one another out of tribalism, not in obedience to God or to His Messenger.

Then God united your hearts through Islam, making some of you brothers to others after you had been enemies, communicating with one another through the love of Islam and the unification of your word upon it, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together

, you were slaughtering one another therein, the strong among you eating the weak, until God brought Islam and made brotherhood between you through it, and brought you together through it. By God, there is no god but Him, love is indeed mercy, and separation is indeed torment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you when you were enemies
, some of you killed others, and your strong consumed your weak, until God brought Islam and united you through it, and united your people upon it, and made you brothers upon it.

x: The blessing that God bestowed upon the Ansar, which He, the Most High, commanded them to mention in this verse, is the unity of Islam, and their unification upon it, and the enmity that was between them, of which God, the Most High, the Most Great, said:
h
When you were enemies
, for it is the enmity of the wars that were between the two tribes of Aws and Khazraj in the pre-Islamic era.
The scholars of the days of the Arabs claim that it lasted between them for twenty and one hundred years, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said:
m: The war between the Aws and the Khazraj lasted one hundred and twenty years, until Islam came while they were still like that. Their war was between them, and they were brothers from the same father and mother. It has never been heard of a people who had such enmity and war between them as they had. Then God Almighty extinguished that with Islam, and united them through His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So He, the Most High, mentioned to them when He admonished them, the greatness of what they had been through in their ignorance of affliction and misery due to their hostility towards one another, their killing of one another, and their fear of one another, and what they had come to through Islam and following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in him and in what he brought, of unity and gathering, and their security from one another, and their becoming brothers to one another. The reason for that was what:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said: Asim bin Umar bin Qatada Al-Madani narrated to us, on the authority of elders from his people, they said:
m: Suwaid bin Samit, the brother of Banu Amr bin Auf, came to Mecca for Hajj or Umrah. He said: Suwaid was called by his people among themselves: Al-Kamil, for his skin, his hair, his lineage and his honor. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about him, he approached him and called him to God Almighty and to Islam. Suwaid said to him: Perhaps what you have is like what I have! He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What do you have with you? He said: The Journal of Luqman - meaning: The Wisdom of Luqman - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Show it to me. So he showed it to him, and he said: This is good speech, but I have something better than this, a Qur’an that God revealed to me, guidance and light. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an to him and called him to Islam. He did not turn away from him and said: This is indeed a good statement! Then he turned away from him and went to Medina. It was not long before the Khazraj killed him. His people would say: He was killed while he was a Muslim. He was killed before the day of Bu’ath. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said, Al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, one of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, narrated to me: Mahmud ibn Labid, one of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, said: When Abu al-Haysir Anas ibn Rafiʿ came to Mecca, accompanied by young men from Banu Abd al-Ashhal, among whom was Iyas ibn Muʿadh, seeking an alliance from Quraysh against their people from the Khazraj, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of them. He came to them and sat with them and said: Do you have something better than what you have come for? They said: What is that? He said: I am the Messenger of God. He sent me to the servants to call them to God, to worship God and not to associate anything with Him, and the Book was revealed to me. Then he mentioned Islam to them and recited the Qur’an to them. Iyas ibn Muʿadh, who was a young boy, said: O people, this, by God, is better than what you have come for! He said: Abu Al-Haysir Anas bin Rafi took a handful of sand from the plain and hit Iyas bin Muadh with it and said: Leave me alone, by God we came for something other than this! Iyas bin Muadh remained silent, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) stood up and left them, and they returned to Madinah. Then the Battle of Buath took place between the Aws and the Khazraj. He said: Then Iyas bin Muadh died shortly after. He said: When God willed to make His religion prevail, to honor His Prophet (peace be upon him), and to fulfill His promise to him, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) went out during the season in which he met the group of the Ansar, introducing himself to the tribes of the Arabs, as he did every season. While he was at Al-Aqabah, he met a group of the Khazraj for whom God wanted good. Ibn Humayd said, Salamah said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada told me on the authority of elders from his people who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met them, he said to them: Who are you? They said: A group of Khazraj. He said: Are you from the clients of the Jews? They said: Yes. He said: Will you not sit down so that I may speak to you? They said: Yes! He said: So they sat down with him, and he called them to God, and presented Islam to them, and recited the Qur’an to them. He said: Among the things that God did for them in Islam was that the Jews were with them in their land, and they were people of the Book and knowledge, and they were polytheists who worshipped idols, and they had invaded their land. So whenever something happened between them, they would say to them: A prophet has just been sent, and his time has come, so we will follow him and kill you with him as the people of ‘Aad and Iram were killed! So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke to those men and called them to God, the Almighty, some of them said to one another: O my people, by God, you know that he is the prophet that the Jews promised you, so do not let him get to him before you! They responded to what he called them to, by believing him and accepting what he offered them of Islam, and they said to him: We have left our people and there is no people among them as much enmity and evil as among them, and perhaps God will unite them with you, and we will go to them and call them to your command, and we will offer them Surat Al Imran 3:103
h
And hold fast
to the rope of God all together
h
and do not be divided
h
And remember the favor of God upon you
h
when you were enemies
and He united your hearts
h
and you became
, by His favor, brothers.
h
And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire

and He saved you from it. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be guided. what we responded to you to of this religion, and if God unites them upon it, then no man is more honorable than you. Then they turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returning to their country, having believed and believed, and they were, as I was told, six men.
