He said: When they came to Medina to their people, they mentioned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, and called them to Islam until it spread among them, and there was not a house of the Ansar except that there was mention of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in it. Then, when the next year came, twelve men from the Ansar arrived at the season, and they met him at Al-Aqabah, which is the first Aqabah. They pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the pledge of allegiance of women, and that was before war was made obligatory upon them. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated that Abd al-Razzaq narrated that Muammar narrated from Ayoub from Ikrimah that six men from the Ansar met the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and they believed in him and confirmed his truthfulness. He wanted to go with them, but they said: O Messenger of God, there is war between our people, and we fear that if you come in this state, what you want will not be achieved. So they promised him the following year and said: O Messenger of God, let us go, perhaps God will put this war right! He said: So they went and did so, and God the Almighty put this war right, and they thought that it would not be put right, and that was the day of Buath. So they met him the following year with seventy men who had believed, so he took twelve leaders over them, and that is when He says:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for
h
when you were enemies

, it was in the war of Ibn Sameer, He brought your hearts together, with Islam. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Abu Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah, in a similar manner, and he added to it: When what happened to Aisha happened, the two tribes clashed, and some of them said to others: Your meeting place is Al-Harrah! So they went out to her, and this verse was revealed:
h
And remember the favor of God upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together

so that by His favor you became brethren, the verse. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them and continued reciting it to them until some of them embraced one another, and they even started to cry. Samir, about whom al-Suddi claimed that his saying:
h
When you were enemies meant his war

, is Samir bin Zaid bin Malik, one of the sons of Amr bin Awf, whom Malik bin al-Ajlan mentioned in his saying: Sameer, I see that his clan has turned away from him and has become arrogant. If my suspicions are true about the Banu Najjar, they did not covet what they had been fed.

x: The scholars of the Ansar mentioned: The beginning of the enmity that sparked the wars that took place between the two tribes, Aws and Khazraj, was due to the killing of a client of Malik bin Al-Ajlan Al-Khazraji called Al-Har bin Sameer from Muzaynah, who was an ally of Malik bin Al-Ajlan. Then that enmity continued between them until God extinguished it through His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the meaning of Al-Suddi’s statement: The war of Ibn Sameer.
As for his saying:
h
And by His grace you have become brothers

, he means: “And by God Almighty’s bringing you together through Islam and the word of truth, and cooperation in supporting the people of faith, and supporting one another against those who oppose you from among the people of disbelief, you have become sincere brothers, with no grudges between you and no envy, as:

c: Bishr told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And you became
, by His grace, brothers.” And he mentioned to us that a man said to Ibn Masoud: How did you become? He said: We became, by the grace of God, brothers.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire

, is that you, O group of believers, from the Aws and Khazraj, were on the edge of a pit of Fire. This is an example of their disbelief that they were upon before God guided them to Islam. God, the Most High, says: And you were on the edge of Hell because of your disbelief that you were upon before God bestowed His favor upon you with Islam,
h
and you became

brothers through your unity upon it, and there was nothing between you and falling into it except that you died upon that of your disbelief, and you would be among those who would abide therein eternally. But God saved you from it through the faith to which He guided you. The edge of a hole is its edge and its edge, like the edge of a pond or a well. From this comes the saying of the rajaz poet: We dug for the pilgrims a record of it growing above her lips with a herb Meaning: above its edge.

It is said: this is the lip of this well, shortened, and they are its lips. He said: Then He saved you from it, meaning He saved you from the pit. He returned the report to the pit, and he began the report about the cure, because the cure comes from the pit. So that was permissible, since the report about the cure, in the way that he mentioned it in this verse, was report about the pit, as Jarir ibn Atiyah said: She saw the years passing by, they took from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon. He mentioned: The years passed, then he returned to the report about the years, as Al-Ajjaj said: All the nights I hastened to spend my whole life The reason for which this was said was also explained previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire

, and He saved you from it. Thus does God make clear to you His signs.” This tribe of Arabs was the most humiliated of people, the most miserable in life, the most clearly astray, the most naked in skin, and the hungriest in stomachs, they were on a rocky peak between the two lions, Persia and Rome. By God, there was nothing in their land that day for which they could be envied. Whoever of them lived lived miserably, and whoever died was thrown into the Fire. They were eaten but did not eat. By God, we do not know of any tribe on that day from the inhabitants of the earth who had lesser fortune and lesser status than them, until God, the Almighty, brought Islam, and made the Book your inheritor, and made the abode of jihad lawful for you, and provided for you provisions, and made you kings over the necks of people. And through Islam God gave what you have seen, so be grateful for His blessings, for your Lord is a benefactor who loves the grateful, and the grateful are in God’s abundance, so exalted is our Lord and blessed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were on the brink of a pit of fire
, meaning: you were disbelieving in God, and He saved you from it, from that, and guided you to Islam.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And you were on the brink of a pit of fire

, and He saved you from it, through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: You were on the edge of the fire, whoever among you died would be cast into the fire, so God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He saved you through him from that pit.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Hassan bin Hayy told us:
m: h
And you were on the brink of a pit of fire
, and He saved you from it. He said: Partisanship.

x: By His saying, Likewise, He, the Most High, means that just as your Lord has made clear to you in these verses, O believers from the Aws and Khazraj, the rancor of the Jews that they hold for you, and their deception of you, and His command to you with what He commanded you to do therein, and His prohibition of you from what He prohibited you from, and the state that you were in during your ignorance, and the state that you have reached in your Islam, He made you aware in all of that of the places of His blessings before you and His favors upon you, so likewise He makes clear the rest of His proofs to you in His revelation and on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that you may be guided, meaning: that you may be guided to the path of righteousness and follow it, and not go astray from it.

By that, the Most High means: And let there be from you, O believers, a nation, meaning a group, calling people to goodness, meaning to Islam and its laws that God has legislated for His servants, and enjoining what is right, meaning: they command people to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion that he brought from God, and forbidding what is wrong, meaning: and forbidding disbelief in God and denial of Muhammad and what he brought from God, by striving with their hands and limbs until they submit to you in obedience. His saying: And those are the successful ones, means those who are successful with God and remain in His gardens and bliss. We have demonstrated the meaning of success in other places, so there is no need to repeat it here.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Issa bin Omar Al-Qari told us, on the authority of Abu Awn Al-Thaqafi:
m: that he heard Subaih say: I heard Uthman recite: And let there arise out of you a group inviting to good, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and seeking help from God against what has befallen them.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he said:
m: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr reciting, and he mentioned the same recitation as Uthman that we mentioned before, exactly the same.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And let there arise from you a group inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, he said: They are the special companions of the Messenger of God, and they are the special narrators.

evidence.text: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr reciting, and he mentioned the same recitation as Uthman that we mentioned before, exactly the same.

x: By that, the Most High means: And do not be, O group of believers, like those who were divided, from the People of the Book, and differed in the religion of God and His commands and prohibitions, after the clear proofs had come to them, from the proofs of God in what they differed about, and they knew the truth about it, but they deliberately opposed it, and disobeyed the command of God, and broke His covenant and pact out of boldness towards God, and for those, meaning: and for those who were divided and differed from the People of the Book after what had come to them, is a punishment from God, great.

The Most High says: So do not be divided, O group of believers, in your religion as these were divided in their religion, and do not do what they did, and follow their example in your religion, so that you will have from the great punishment of God like what they had, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And be not like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them

, he said: They are the People of the Book. God forbade the people of Islam from becoming divided and differing as the People of the Book became divided and differed. God Almighty said: And for those is a great punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not be like those who became divided and differed

, and something similar to this in the Qur’an. God, may He be glorified and praised, commanded the believers to remain united, so He forbade them from differing and being divided, and He informed them that those who came before them were destroyed only by arguments and disputes in the religion of God.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And do not be like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them
. And those will have a great punishment,” he said: They are the Jews and Christians.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Those will have a great punishment on a day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black. As for his statement:
h
As for those whose faces will be black
h
did you disbelieve after your belief
?, its meaning is:
h
As for those whose faces will be black
, it will be said to them:
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief

? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. As for as, it must have an answer with fa, so when the answer was dropped, the fa was dropped with it. It is permissible to omit mentioning it, so it is said, because what was mentioned in the speech indicates it. As for the meaning of His Most High’s saying:
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief
?, the people of interpretation differed as to who was meant by it.
Some of them said: He meant the Muslims who face our Qiblah.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black

, the verse, some people disbelieved after their belief, as you hear. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, some people from among my companions will come to me at the Cistern, and when they are brought up to me and I see them, they will be kept away from me, so I will say: ‘O Lord! My companions! My companions!’ And it will be said: ‘You do not know what they innovated after you!’” And his statement:
h
As for those whose faces will turn white
, they will be in the mercy of God, these are the people of obedience to God and loyalty to the covenant of God. God, the Almighty, said: So in the mercy of God, they will abide therein eternally.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black
. As for those whose faces will turn black, it will be said:
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief
? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.” This is from those who disbelieved from the people of the Qiblah when they fought.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah and Al-Rabi’ bin Subaih, on the authority of Abu Mujalid, on the authority of Abu Umamah:
m: As for those whose faces will be blackened,
h
did you disbelieve after your belief
? He said: They are the Khawarij.

x: Others said: What is meant by that is: everyone who disbelieved in God after the faith he had, when God took from the loins of Adam his offspring and made them testify against themselves what was stated in His Book.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ali bin Al-Haitham told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abi Al-ʿAliyah, on the authority of Abi bin Kaʿb,
m: regarding His statement:
h
On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black
, he said: On the Day of Resurrection, they will be divided into two groups. Then He will say to those whose faces will turn black, and He will reproach them:
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief

? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. He said: It is the faith that existed before the differences in the time of Adam, when He took their covenant and pledge from them, and they all acknowledged servitude, and He created them upon Islam, so they were one Muslim nation. He says:
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief

? He means: after that which existed in the time of Adam. And He said about the others: those who remained steadfast in their belief, so they devoted religion and deeds to Him, so God made their faces white, and admitted them into His pleasure and Paradise.

x: Others said: Rather, those meant by his saying,
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief
, are the hypocrites.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black
, the verse, he said: They are the hypocrites, they gave the word of faith with their tongues, but denied it with their hearts and actions.

x: The most correct of the statements we mentioned is the statement we mentioned on the authority of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, that he meant all the infidels, and that the faith from which they are rebuked for their apostasy is the faith that they acknowledged on the day it was said to them: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we bear witness.
r
(Al-Aʿraf: 172)
This is because God, the Most High, has made all the people of the Hereafter into two groups: one with black Surat Al Imran 3:106
h
On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black
. As for those whose faces will turn black, [it will be said], "
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief

? Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve." faces, and the other with white faces. It is known - since there are only these two groups - that all the disbelievers are included in the group of those with black faces, and that all the believers are included in the group of those with white faces.
So there is no reason for the speaker to say:
h
Did you disbelieve after your belief

? He meant some of the disbelievers and not others, while God, the Most High, has made the report general about all of them. And if all of them are included in that, and then all of them did not have a state in which they believed and then apostatized as disbelievers after that except one state, it is known that this is what is meant by that. The interpretation of the verse is: Those will have a great punishment on a day when the faces of some people will turn white and the faces of others will turn black. As for those whose faces will turn black, it will be said: Did you deny the Oneness of God, His covenant and His pledge which you made with Him, that you would not associate anything with Him, and that you would devote worship to Him alone - after your belief, meaning: after your belief in Him? - Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve, meaning: for what you used to deny in this world, what God had taken from you to acknowledge and believe in.

And as for those whose faces have turned white, those who have remained steadfast in God’s covenant and pledge, and have not changed their religion, nor turned back after acknowledging monotheism, and bearing witness to the divinity of their Lord, and that there is no god but Him, they are in the mercy of God, meaning: in His Paradise and its bliss and what God has prepared for its people in it, they will abide therein eternally, meaning: they will remain therein forever without end or limit.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
These are the signs of God
, is that
h
these are the signs of God

. We have already explained how the Arabs put that and that in place of this and that, in other places in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. His saying: The verses of God, meaning God’s sermons, lessons, and arguments, We recite them to you, we read them to you and we narrate them, in truth, meaning with honesty and certainty. What he means by his saying:
h
These are the signs of God are these verses in which he mentioned the affairs of the believers from the supporters of the Messenger of God

, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the affairs of the Jews of the Children of Israel and the People of the Book, and what he will do with the people who are faithful to his covenant, and with those who change his religion, and those who break his covenant after acknowledging it.

Then the Almighty informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would recite that to him in truth, and informed him that whoever punishes among His creation with what He informed him He would punish him with: by blackening his face, and immortalizing him in His painful torment and great punishment, and whoever rewards him from among them with what He rewards him with: by whitening his face, honoring him, and ennobling his status with Him, by immortalizing him in His eternal bliss, then it is not through injustice from Him to a group of them, but rather because of the right they deserved, and deeds of theirs that He rewarded them for, so the Almighty said: And God does not desire injustice for the worlds, meaning by that: And God, O Muhammad, is not by blackening the faces of these and making them taste the great torment, and whitening the faces of those and making them enjoy His Paradise, seeking to place something of what He did of that in a place other than its place, informing His servants with that that He will not amend in His wisdom for His creation other than what He promised the people of His obedience and faith in Him, and other than what He threatened the people of His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and as a warning from Him to these, and as a good tiding from Him to those.

evidence.text: His saying: The verses of God, meaning God’s sermons, lessons, and arguments, We recite them to you, we read them to you and we narrate them, in truth, meaning with honesty and certainty.

Then the Almighty informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would recite that to him in truth, and informed him that whoever punishes among His creation with what He informed him He would punish him with: by blackening his face, and immortalizing him in His painful torment and great punishment, and whoever rewards him from among them with what He rewards him with: by whitening his face, honoring him, and ennobling his status with Him, by immortalizing him in His eternal bliss, then it is not through injustice from Him to a group of them, but rather because of the right they deserved, and deeds of theirs that He rewarded them for, so the Almighty said: And God does not desire injustice for the worlds, meaning by that: And God, O Muhammad, is not by blackening the faces of these and making them taste the great torment, and whitening the faces of those and making them enjoy His Paradise, seeking to place something of what He did of that in a place other than its place, informing His servants with that that He will not amend in His wisdom for His creation other than what He promised the people of His obedience and faith in Him, and other than what He threatened the people of His disobedience and disbelief in Him, and as a warning from Him to these, and as a good tiding from Him to those.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that He punishes those who disbelieved after their belief with what He mentioned that He will punish them with of great torment and blackening of faces, and He rewards the people of faith in Him who were steadfast in belief and fulfillment of their covenants that they made with what He described as His reward for them of eternity in His Paradise, without wronging either party in what he did, because He has no need for wrongdoing. This is because the wrongdoer only wrongs another in order to increase his own glory by wronging him, or to increase his authority, or to decrease some of his causes by which he completes the wrongdoing of another in what was lacking in its causes from completion. As for He who has everything between the regions of the East and the West, and what is in this world and the Hereafter, there is no point in him wronging anyone, so it is permissible for him to wrong something, because none of His causes is lacking and needs completion, so that is completed by wronging another, God is exalted, greatly exalted.
Therefore, God Almighty said after His statement: And God does not intend injustice for the worlds, “
h
And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
, and to God all matters are returned.” The Arabists differed about the reason for God Almighty repeating His name with His statement:
h
And to God all matters return
, apparently, and His name was mentioned before with His statement:
h
And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth

. Some Arabists from Basra said: This is similar to the Arabs’ saying: As for Zaid, Zaid has gone, and as the poet said: I do not see death preceded by anything that made death bitter to the rich and the poor So it appears in the place of concealment. Some grammarians of Kufa said: This is not similar to this verse, because the second place of death in the verse is a place of metaphor, because it is a single word, and this is not the case in the verse, because his saying:
h
And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a predicate
, not from his saying:
h
And to God all matters return in any way
This is because each of the two stories is separate in meaning from the other, each of them is sufficient on its own, not in need of the other.

i: And what the poet said:
x: I do not see death, is in need of a complete predicate about it.

This second statement is more correct in our view, because the meanings of the Book of God Almighty and what is in it of explanation are not directed to the oddities of speech and meanings, and it has a correct and existing aspect in eloquent logic and apparent understood meanings. As for His statement:
h
And to God all matters return

, He, the Most High, means: To God is the final destination of the matter of all His creation, the righteous among them and the wicked, the doer of good and the wrongdoer, so He rewards each according to the degree to which they deserve reward from Him, without wronging any of them.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind

Some of them said: They are those who migrated with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to Medina in particular, from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said
m: regarding
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, he said: They are those who left with him from Mecca.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, he said: They are those who migrated from Mecca to Medina.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
h
You enjoin what is right

and forbid what is wrong.” Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If God had willed, He would have said: You, so we were all. But He said: You were in particular from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who did as they did. They were the best nation produced for mankind. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Ibn Masoud, Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, and Muadh ibn Jabal.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Musʿab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of someone who told him: Umar said:
m: h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
. He said: It will be for the first of us and not for the last of us.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, he said: They are those who migrated with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Medina.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that Omar bin Al-Khattab said during a Hajj he performed and he saw bad behavior from the people, so he recited this:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, the verse. Then he said: O people, whoever is pleased to be from that nation, let him fulfill the condition of God regarding it.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind

, he said: They are the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in particular, meaning: And they were the narrators and preachers whom God commanded the Muslims to obey.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: You are the best nation brought forth for mankind, if you have these conditions that God Almighty described you with. So the interpretation of this according to them was: You are the best nation, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong and believing in God, brought forth for mankind in your time.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, he says: on this condition: that
h
you enjoin what is right
, forbid what is wrong, and believe in God, he says: for those among whom you are, like His statement:
h
And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds (al-Dukhan 44

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, he said, he says: You are the best people for mankind on this condition: that
h
you enjoin what is right
, forbid what is wrong, and believe in God, he says: for those who are behind him, like his statement:
h
And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds (al-Dukhan 44

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah:
m: h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
. He said: You were the best people for mankind, you brought them in chains, you brought them into Islam.

c: Ubaid bin Asbat told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, he said: The best people for mankind.

x: Others said: It was said,
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
, because they were the nations most responsive to Islam.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his saying: “
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
h
You enjoin what is right
and forbid what is wrong.” He said: There was no nation more responsive to Islam than this nation, so he said:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind

x: Some of them said: He meant by that that they were the best nation brought forth for mankind.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
h
You enjoin what is right
and forbid what is wrong,” he said: What you hear of goodness has been in this nation.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: We are the last of them and the most honorable of them to God.

x: The most appropriate of these sayings to interpret the verse is what Al-Hasan said, which is that:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Bahz bin Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Behold, you have succeeded seventy nations, and you are the last of them and the most honored of them in the sight of God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us,
m: “On the authority of Bahz bin Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather: that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say regarding his statement: ‘
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
,’ he said: You complete seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honored of them in the sight of God.”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day while he was leaning his back against the Kaaba: We will complete seventy nations on the Day of Resurrection, we are the last of them and the best of them.” As for his saying:
h
You enjoin what is right

, it means: You enjoin belief in God and His Messenger, and working according to His laws, and you forbid what is wrong, meaning: You forbid associating partners with God, denying His Messenger, and working according to what He forbade, as:

c: Ali bin Dawud told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind

, meaning: You command them to do what is right: to testify that there is no god but God, and to acknowledge what God has revealed, and you fight them for it, and there is no god but God, is the greatest good, and you forbid them from evil, and evil is denial, and it is the worst evil. The origin of the known is everything that is known to be done, beautiful and approved, and not considered ugly by people of faith in God. Rather, obedience to God is called known because it is something that people of faith know and do not find objectionable. The root of munkar is what God disapproved of and considered ugly to do. That is why disobeying God is called munkar, because those who believe in God disapprove of doing it and consider it too great to do it. His saying:
h
And you believe in God
, means: You believe in God, so you devote monotheism and worship to Him.

x: If someone asks, “How is it said, ‘You were the best nation,’ when you have claimed that the interpretation of the verse is that this nation is the best of the nations that have passed, and it is only said, ‘You were the best nation,’ about a people who were good and then changed from what they were?” It was said: The meaning of this is contrary to what you have gone to, and rather its meaning is: You are the best nation, as it was said: And remember when you were few (al-Anfal 8:26), and He said in another place: And remember when you were few and He made you many (al-A’raf 7:86), so the inclusion of kan in such a case and its omission have the same meaning, because the meaning of the speech is known. If someone also said about this: You were, meaning completeness, its interpretation would be: You were created the best nation, or: You found the best nation, which would be a correct meaning.

Some Arabists have claimed that the meaning of this is: You were the best nation in the sight of God in the Preserved Tablet, brought forth for mankind. The first two statements that we mentioned are more similar in meaning to the report that we narrated Surat Al Imran 3:110
h
You are the best nation produced for mankind
h
You enjoin what is right

and forbid what is wrong and believe in God. And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient. before.
Others said: The meaning of this is: You were the best people of the path. He said: The nation, the path.

By this, the Most High means: If the people of the Torah and the Gospel, the Jews and Christians, had believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought to them from God, it would have been better for them with God in this world and the hereafter. Among them are the believers, meaning: among the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, the believers who believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he brought to them from God, and they are: ʿAbdullah bin Salam and his brother, and Thaʿlaba bin Saʿiyah and his brother, and those like them who believed in God and believed in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and followed what he brought to them from God, but most of them are wicked, meaning: those who have deviated from their religion. That is because the religion of the Jews is to follow what is in the Torah and believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the religion of the Christians is to follow what is in the Gospel and believe in him and what is in the Torah, and in both books there is a description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his attributes, his mission, and that he is a prophet of God.
Both groups - I mean the Jews and Christians - are liars. This is their immorality and their departure from the religion that they claim to follow, which God Almighty said: Most of them are immoral.

i: Qatada said:
x: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Among them are believers, but most of them are wicked. God condemned most people. Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O people of faith in God and His Messenger, these wicked people of the Book will not harm you in any way, with their disbelief and denial of your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except harm.

He means by that: But they harm you with their polytheism, and making you hear their disbelief, and what they say about Jesus, his mother, and Ezra, and their calling you to misguidance, and they will not harm you with that. This is an isolated exception that contradicts the meaning of what precedes it, as it is said: He did not complain about anything except good, and this is a word that is transmitted from the Arabs by hearing. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They will not harm you except with harm
, he said: They will not harm you, except with harm that you hear from them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
They will not harm you except with harm
, he said: Harm that you hear from them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: They will not harm you except with an annoyance, he said: Their associating partners with Ezra, Jesus, and the cross.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: They will not harm you except with annoyance the verse, he said: You hear from them lies about God, calling you to misguidance.

evidence.text: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that Omar bin Al-Khattab said during a Hajj he performed and he saw bad behavior from the people, so he recited this: You are the best nation produced for mankind, the verse.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And if the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, fight you, they will be defeated and turn their backs to you in defeat. His saying:
h
They turn their backs to you

, is a metaphor for their defeat, because the defeated person turns his back to the pursuer, fleeing to a refuge and shelter to which he can resort, fearing for himself, while the pursuer is following him. So the back of the pursued person then is parallel to the face of the defeated pursuer.
h
Then they will not be helped

, meaning: Then God will not help them, O believers, against you, because of their disbelief in God and His Messenger, and your belief in what your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave you. Because God Almighty has cast terror into their hearts, so He has supported you, O believers, with your victory. This is a promise from God Almighty mentioned by His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of faith, that He will grant them victory over the disbelievers among the People of the Book.
Rather, He raised His statement,
h
Then they will not be helped
, and made His statement,
h
They will turn their backs to you

, in the affirmative, as a response to the condition, to resume the speech, because the beginnings of the verses before it were with the letter nun, so He attached this to it, just as He said, And they will not be given permission to make excuses (al-Mursalat 77:36), raising it, and He said in another place, They will not be given a decree to die
r
(Fatir 35:36)
, since it was not the beginning of a verse.

By His Most High’s words, humiliation was imposed upon them, He meant that they were forced into humiliation. Humiliation is the verb from humiliation, and we have explained that with its evidence in other places.
h
Wherever they are found
means:
h
wherever they are found

God Almighty says: The Jews who denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were forced to be humiliated wherever they were on earth, and wherever they were in its regions, in the lands of Muslims and polytheists,
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
, as:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
. They incurred the wrath of God, and poverty was imposed upon them,” he said: This nation overtook them, and the Magians were collecting the jizya from them.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people

, he said: God humiliated them so that they have no protection, and God placed them under the feet of the Muslims. As for the rope that God mentioned in this place, it is the reason by which they are safe from the believers, and their money and children, from a covenant and security that was made for them before they settled in the lands of Islam, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: except by a rope from God, he said: by a covenant, and a rope from the people, he said: by their covenant.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found
, except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, meaning: except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Ghayath, he said,
m: Ikrimah says: Except with a rope from God and a rope from the people, he said: with a covenant from God and a covenant from the people.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Except with a rope from God and a rope from the people, meaning: Except with a covenant from God and a covenant from the people.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
Except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
, meaning: Except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Wherever they are found

, except by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, so it is a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, just as a man says: the covenant of God and the covenant of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it is the covenant.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: h
Wherever they are found

, they are bound by a covenant from God and a covenant from the people. He said: By a covenant from God and a covenant from the people to them. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ata’ said: The covenant is the covenant from God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
Wherever they are found
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people

, he said: Except by a covenant, and they are the Jews. He said: A rope is a covenant. He said: And that is the statement of Abu Al-Haitham Ibn Al-Taihan to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Ansar came to him at Al-Aqabah: O man, we will cut a rope between us and the people about you, he said: Covenants, he said: And the Jews will not feel safe in any land of God’s land except by this rope that God the Almighty said: And he recited: And He will make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection
r
(Al Imran 3:55)

, he said: There is no country in which there are any Christians except that they are superior to the Jews in the East or the West, they are humiliated in all countries, God said: And We dispersed them throughout the earth into nations (al-A’raf 7:68), Jews.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
Except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
, saying: By a covenant from God and a covenant from the people.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: similarly.

x: The Arabists differed about the meaning of the preposition ba in his statement:
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The preposition ba in his statement: by a rope is an implied verb that was not mentioned. He said: The meaning of the statement is:
h
Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found
, except that they hold fast to a rope from God.

i: So he implied that, and he cited as evidence for his statement the words of the poet:
h
She saw me
with my ropes on, so she turned away in fear, and in the rope there are differences in the heart’s fear He said:
x: He meant: She came with her two ropes, and in the words of the other: The benevolence of time has bent me so much that I feel as if I am a hunter approaching to hunt.

I walk quickly, and whoever sees me thinks that I am not in chains. He wants: bound by a shackle. So he made it obligatory to use a deleted verb and to show its connection, which is abandoned. This is weak in the schools of Arabic, and far from the speech of the Arabs. As for the verses he cited as evidence for his statement, they do not indicate the validity of his claim, because in the poet’s statement:
h
She saw me

with her ropes, there is clear evidence that she saw him holding the rope. So in his informing her that she saw him with her ropes, there is informing him that she saw him holding the ropes. So, in what appeared from the speech, there was no need to mention holding, and the ba’ was a connection to his statement:
h
She saw me

, like the statement of the speaker: I am with God, sufficient for myself, and the listener’s knowledge of its meaning, that the ba’ is in need of speech that would bring it something other than what appeared, and that the meaning is: I am with God for help.
Some Basra grammarians said that his statement: except by a rope from God is an exception that comes out from the beginning of the statement. He said: This is not more severe than his statement:
“They will not hear therein any ill speech, but [only], ‘Peace’”
Other grammarians of Kufa said: It is a connected exception, and the meaning is:
h
Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found

, meaning: in every place, except in a place of a rope from God, just as you say: Humiliation was imposed upon them in all places except in this place. This is also a request for the truth, but he made a mistake in the explanation. That is because he claimed that it is a connected exception. If it were connected as he claimed, then it would be necessary that if the people are found with a rope from God and a rope from the people, then poverty would not be imposed upon them. And that is not the description of the Jews, because whenever they are found with a rope from God and a rope from the people, or without a rope from God the Almighty and without a rope from the people, then humiliation is imposed upon them, according to what we mentioned about the people of interpretation before.

So if his statement, except with a rope from God and a rope from the people, was a connected exception, then it would be necessary that if the people are found with a covenant and protection, then humiliation would not be imposed upon them. This is contrary to what God described them with in their description, and contrary to what they have in their description. Thus, the corruption of the statement of this speaker has also become clear.

But our opinion is that the preposition ba in His statement: except by a rope from God was inserted because the statement before the exception requires the preposition ba in meaning. That is because the meaning of His statement:
h
humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found
is
h
humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found
. Then He said:
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
is not connected to the first, but rather it is disconnected from it. Its meaning is: but they are found by a rope from God and a rope from the people, as it was said:
And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake

So, even though mistake is the object of what it did in what preceded the exception, His statement with the exception is not connected to the first in the sense of: except by mistake, for he has the right to kill him in the same way, but its meaning is: but he may kill him by mistake.
Likewise, his statement:
h
Wherever they are found
, except by a rope from God, even though what brought the ba after except was the verb that required it before except, so the exception is not the Surat Al Imran 3:112
h
Humiliation has been imposed upon them wherever they are found
h
except by a rope from God and a rope from the people
. And they incurred wrath from God, and poverty has been imposed upon them.
h
That is because they disbelieved in the signs of God

and killed the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and were transgressors. exception connected to the one before it, meaning: that if the people meet, humiliation will be removed from them, rather humiliation is fixed in every case. But its meaning is what we explained earlier.

God Almighty means: And they incurred the wrath of God, and they bore the wrath of God and turned away with it those who deserved it. We have explained the origin of that with its evidence, and the meaning of poverty is that it is the humiliation of want and poverty and their submission, and the meaning of: the wrath of God in the past, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His saying:
h
That is because they disbelieved in the signs of God

, He, the Most High, means by His saying: That, that is: the affliction that they incurred from the wrath of God and the humiliation that was imposed upon them, instead of what they disbelieved in the signs of God, He says: because they denied the signs of God and His evidence of the truthfulness of His prophets, and what He imposed upon them of His obligations, and killed the prophets without right, He says: and because they killed their prophets and God’s messengers to them, as an aggression against God and audacity towards Him with falsehood, and without right, they deserved to be killed by them.

The interpretation of the statement is: They were forced to be humiliated wherever they found themselves, except with a covenant from God and a covenant from the people, and they turned away with the wrath of God, bearing it, and they were forced to be humiliated by want and humbled by poverty, instead of what they were denying of God’s signs, evidence, and proofs, and killing His prophets unjustly, unjustly, and aggressively.

God Almighty says: We did that to them because of their disbelief, their killing of the prophets, their disobedience to their Lord, and their transgression against the command of their Lord. We have explained the meaning of aggression in more than one place in our book, sufficiently enough to need to repeat it. So our Lord, may His praise be glorified, informed His servants of what He did to these people of the People of the Book, of bringing humiliation and disgrace upon them in this worldly life, along with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter of punishment, chastisement, and painful torment, since they transgressed the limits of God and made permissible what He has forbidden.

This is a reminder from Him, may He be glorified, to them, and an alert to the place of the affliction from which they came so that they might repent and remember, and a lesson from Him to our nation that they should not follow their example and adopt their methods, lest they follow their paths and be afflicted with the punishments and examples of God that He has afflicted them, such as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: That is because they disobeyed and were transgressors. Avoid disobedience and transgression, for because of them, those who came before you were destroyed among the people.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
They are not equal
, is that there is no group of the People of the Book, the believers and the disbelievers among them: equal. What He means by that is: that
h
they are not equal
. He says:
h
they are not equal
, but they differ in righteousness and corruption, goodness and evil. It was said:
h
They are not equal
, because it mentions the two groups of the People of the Book that God mentioned in His statement:
h
And if the People of the Scripture had believed
, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are wicked.”
then God, the Most High, informed about the state of the two groups before Him, the believers and the disbelievers, and said:
h
They are not equal

, meaning: these are not equal, the believers and the disbelievers. Then God, the Most High, began the report about the description of the believing group among the People of the Book, and praised them and spoke highly of them, after describing the wicked group among them with what He described them with of panic, the elite of Paradise, the alliance of humiliation and lowliness, the constant poverty and destitution, and bearing the shame of this world and the disgrace of the Hereafter, so He said: Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting
h
the verses of God
during the hours of the night and prostrating, the three verses up to His statement:
h
And God is Knowing of the righteous
His saying:
h
A nation that stands
is raised by his saying: Of the People of the Book.

A group of grammarians from Kufa and Basra, and the most prominent among them in their profession, imagined that what comes after sawaa in this place in His statement: an established nation, is a translation of sawaa and an explanation of it, meaning: There is no equal among the People of the Book a nation that is established and recites
h
the verses of God

during the hours of the night and another that is disbelieving. They claimed that mentioning the other group was omitted, sufficing with mentioning one of the two groups, which is the established nation, and they gave an example of this with the statement of Abu Dhu’ayb: I disobeyed her heart: I hear her command, so I do not know how to guide her seekers? He did not say: Or is it not right? He was satisfied with saying: More right than the one mentioned, or is it not right? and with the saying of the other: I see you, but I do not know what his ambition is?
And the one with ambition is humble and diminished.

It is, however, in their view a mistake to say that the speaker who wants to say: Whether you stay or sit: Whether you stay, so that he says: Or sit. They only permit the deletion of the second letter in the speech that is sufficient with one, not in what is lacking from that, such as: I do not care or I do not know, so they permit in that: I do not care I stayed, and they mean: I do not care whether I stayed or sat, because I do not care is sufficient with one, and likewise in I do not know. And they refused to permit in whether, because of its deficiency, and that it is not sufficient with one, so they overlooked - in their interpretation of his statement:
h
They are not all alike among the People of the Scripture

, a community standing, according to what we have related from them, to what they have directed it to - their schools of thought in Arabic, since they permitted in it the deletion that is not permissible according to them in speech with whether, and they made a mistake in interpreting the verse.
So whether in this place means completion and sufficiency, not in the meaning interpreted by the one whose statement we have related. It was mentioned that his saying:
h
Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing - the three verses - was revealed about a group of Jews who converted to Islam
and their conversion was good.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When Abdullah ibn Salam, Tha’laba ibn Sa’iyah, Asid ibn Sa’iyah, Asad ibn Ubayd, and those Jews who had converted with them, and believed and were truthful and desired Islam and were firmly established in it, the rabbis of the Jews and the unbelievers among them said: None believed in Muhammad and followed him except the worst of us! If they had been among the best of us, they would not have abandoned the religion of their fathers and gone to another one. So God, the Almighty, revealed regarding that from their statement: “They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing [in prayer], reciting
h
the verses of God
” until His saying:
h
And those are among the righteous

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said,
m: Ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “They are not all the same. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing” the verse, he says: Not all of the people perished, God had a remnant among them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: A standing nation, Abdullah bin Salam, and Tha’laba bin Salam his brother, and Sa’iyya, and Mubashar, and Asid and Asad, the sons of Ka’b. Others said: The meaning of this is: The People of the Book and the nation of Muhammad who uphold the right of God are not equal before God.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Yazid Al-Ajli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud
m: that he used to say regarding his statement:
h
They are not equal among the People of the Scripture - a community standing
, he said: The People of the Scripture and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are not equal.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing,” the verse, meaning: These Jews are not like this nation that is standing.

x: We have shown that the more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: The story was completed when he said:
h
They are not equal
, about God informing us about the matter of the believers among the People of the Book and the disbelievers among them, and that his saying:
h
Among the People of the Book is a community standing

, is a new statement about praising their believers and describing them according to their characteristics, according to what Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, and Ibn Jurayj said. By His saying, a standing nation, He, the Most High, means a group steadfast on the truth. We have already demonstrated the meaning of the nation in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. As for the list, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.
Some of them said: It means: fair.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
A nation that stands
up, he said: Just.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that it is based on the Book of God and what He commanded in it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A nation that stands
firm, he said: Standing firm on the Book of God, His obligations, and His limits.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
A nation that stands
, meaning: standing on the Book of God, His limits, and His obligations.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Among the People of the Book is
h
a nation that stands
, he says: a nation that is guided, standing by the command of God, not turning away from it and abandoning it as others abandoned it and wasted it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of standing is obedient.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: A nation standing, the verse, he says: These Jews are not like this nation that is obedient to God. And obedient, obedient.

x: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting this is what was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah, and those who said the same as them, according to what we have narrated from them, even though all the other sayings are close in meaning to what Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said about this. This is because the meaning of his saying, standing, is upright on guidance, the Book of God, His obligations, Surat Al Imran 3:113 They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing [in prayer], reciting
h
the verses of God

during periods of the night, and they prostrate. the laws of His religion, justice, obedience, and other causes of goodness, from the description of the people of uprightness on the Book of God and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Similar to this is the report narrated by An-Nuʿman ibn Bashir, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The example of the one who upholds the limits of God and the one who transgresses them is like the example of a people who boarded a ship.
Then he gave them an example. The one who adheres to the limits of God is the one who is steadfast in adhering to what God has commanded him to do and avoiding what God has forbidden him to do.

The interpretation of the statement is: Among the People of the Book is a group that adheres to the Book of God, clings to it, and is steadfast in acting in accordance with what is in it and what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, has prescribed for them.
What he means by his saying, “
h
They recite the verses of God
,” is that they read the Book of God during the hours of the night. What he means by his saying,
h
The verses of God

, is what God has revealed in His Book of lessons and admonitions. He says, They recite that during the hours of the night, meaning: during the hours of the night, they contemplate it and reflect upon it.

i: As for the hours of the night, they are the hours of the night, the singular of which is ani, as the poet said:
x: Sweet and bitter, like the affection of the cup, its bitterness is in every place where I walk, the night is next to it It has been said that one vessel is a small vessel, just as one intestine is a small intestine.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: Its interpretation is: the hours of the night, as we said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night
, meaning: the hours of the night.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said: The hours of the night means the hours of the night.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah bin Katheer said: We heard the Arabs say: the hours of the night, the hours of the night.

x: Others said: Ana’ al-Layl means the middle of the night.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night
. As for the hours of the night, it means the middle of the night.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that people who used to pray the last evening prayer.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Yazid Al-Ajli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night
, the Isha prayer, they pray it, and those other than them from the People of the Book do not pray it.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Zahr, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masʿud, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was detained from us one night. He was with some of his family and wives, and he did not come to us for the ʿIsha prayer until night had passed. Then he came, and some of us were praying and some of us were lying down. He gave us good report and said: No one from the People of the Book prays this prayer! Then God revealed: ‘They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting
h
the verses of God
during periods of the night and prostrating.’”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ali bin Ma'bad told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya al-Khurasani, on the authority of Nasr bin Tarif, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, who said:
m: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us while we were waiting for the evening prayer - meaning: the night prayer - and he said to us: There is no one on earth from the people of religions waiting for this prayer at this time except you! He said: Then this verse was revealed: 'They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting
h
the verses of God
during periods of the night, and they prostrate themselves.'"

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that people who used to pray between sunset and evening prayers.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said:
m: It reached me that the verse was revealed: “They are not all the same. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting
h
the verses of God
during periods of the night and prostrating themselves,” between sunset and night prayers.

x: These statements that I have mentioned, despite their differences, are close in meaning. That is because God, the Most High, described these people as reciting
h
the verses of God

during the hours of the night, which are its hours. The one who recites them in the ʿIsha prayer may be reciting them during the hours of the night, and likewise the one who recites them between Maghrib and ʿIsha, and the one who recites them in the middle of the night, so everyone who recites them has hours of the night. However, the first statement in the interpretation of the verse is the statement of the one who said: He meant by that the recitation of the Qur’an in the ʿIsha prayer, because it is a prayer that none of the People of the Book pray, so God described the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as praying it, unlike the People of the Book who disbelieved in God and His Messenger.

As for his saying: and they prostrate, some Arabists claimed that the meaning of prostration in this context is the name for prayer, not prostration, because recitation does not occur in prostration or bowing. So the meaning of the statement, according to him, was:
h
they recite the verses of God during the hours of the night
while they pray. The meaning is not as he went to, but rather the meaning of the speech is: Among the People of the Book is a nation who stands and recites
h
the verses of God
during the hours of the night in their prayers, and they also prostrate in them. So prostration is the well-known prostration in prayer.

evidence.text: He says, They recite that during the hours of the night, meaning: during the hours of the night, they contemplate it and reflect upon it.

The one who recites them in the ʿIsha prayer may be reciting them during the hours of the night, and likewise the one who recites them between Maghrib and ʿIsha, and the one who recites them in the middle of the night, so everyone who recites them has hours of the night.

However, the first statement in the interpretation of the verse is the statement of the one who said: He meant by that the recitation of the Qur’an in the ʿIsha prayer, because it is a prayer that none of the People of the Book pray, so God described the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as praying it, unlike the People of the Book who disbelieved in God and His Messenger.

x: What is meant by His Most High’s saying: They believe in God and the Last Day, is that they believe in God and in the resurrection after death, and they know that God will reward them for their deeds. They are not like the polytheists who deny the oneness of God, worship others besides Him, deny the resurrection after death, and deny the reward and punishment for deeds. And His statement: And they enjoin what is right, meaning: they enjoin people to believe in God and His Messengers, and to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought to them. And they forbid what is wrong, meaning: they forbid people from disbelieving in God, and denying Muhammad and what he brought to them from God. By that, He means: that they are not like the Jews and Christians who enjoin people to disbelieve and deny Muhammad in what he brought to them, and they forbid them from doing good deeds, which is believing in Muhammad in what he brought to them from God.

And they hasten to do good deeds, meaning: and they hasten to do good deeds for fear that they will miss out on that before they deal with their deaths. Then He, the Most High, informed us that those of the People of the Book who have this description are among the righteous, because whoever among them is a sinner has incurred the wrath of God for his disbelief in God and His signs, and his killing of the prophets without right, and his disobedience to his Lord and his transgression of His limits.

The readings differed in the reading of that. The majority of the Kufan readers read it as: And whatever good they do, they will not be denied it, with the letter ya in both letters, in response to the description of the people whom God Almighty described as enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. The majority of the readers of Medina and Hijaz and some of the readers of Kufa read it with the letter ta’ in both letters: And whatever good you do, you will not be denied it, meaning: And whatever good you do, you believers, your Lord will not deny it to you.
Some of the Basra reciters considered both readings permissible with the letter ya and the letter ta in both letters.

The correct reading of this in our view is: And whatever good they do, they will not be denied it, with the letter ya in both letters, meaning by that the report about the established nation following the verses of God. We chose this because the verses before this verse are report about them. So attaching this verse, since there is no indication in it that indicates a departure from their description, to the meanings of the verses before it is more appropriate than diverting it from the meanings of what came before it. And what we chose from the reading was what Ibn Abbas used to read.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf al-Taghlabi told me, he said, al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Abu Amr bin al-Ala’, he said: It was reported to me on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to read them both with the letter ya’.

x: The interpretation of the verse, according to what we have chosen from the reading, is: Whatever good this nation does, and whatever work it does for the sake of God, God will not deny them that. What he means by that is: God will not invalidate the reward for their work, nor will He leave them without a reward from Him for it, but He will reward them abundantly for it, and will grant them honor and recompense. We have demonstrated the meaning of disbelief previously with its evidence, and that its origin is covering something. Likewise, in His statement: They will not deny Him, He will not cover up the good they did and leave them without reward, but they will be thanked for what they did, and He will give them a great reward for it. In the same way as we said about that interpretation, those who interpreted that interpreted it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And whatever good you do, you will never be denied it, meaning: it will never go astray from you.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly. As for His statement:
h
And God is All-Knowing of the righteous

, God Almighty says: God is All-Knowing of those who fear Him, by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience, and He preserves their righteous deeds until He rewards them for them and recompenses them for them, as good report from Him, may He be glorified, for them in this worldly life, and as an urging for them to adhere to the good morals that He has chosen for them.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.

The majority of the Kufan readers read it as: And whatever good they do, they will not be denied it, with the letter ya in both letters, in response to the description of the people whom God Almighty described as enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Hijaz and some of the readers of Kufa read it with the letter ta’ in both letters: And whatever good you do, you will not be denied it, meaning: And whatever good you do, you believers, your Lord will not deny it to you.
Some of the Basra reciters considered both readings permissible with the letter ya and the letter ta in both letters.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading of this in our view is: And whatever good they do, they will not be denied it, with the letter ya in both letters, meaning by that the report about the established nation following the verses of God.
And what we chose from the reading was what Ibn Abbas used to read.

Ahmad bin Yusuf al-Taghlabi told me, he said, al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Abu Amr bin al-Ala’, he said: It was reported to me on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read them both with the letter ya’.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The interpretation of the verse, according to what we have chosen from the reading, is: Whatever good this nation does, and whatever work it does for the sake of God, God will not deny them that.
