x: This is a threat from God Almighty to the other wicked nation of the People of the Book, about whom He has informed us that they are wicked and that they have incurred His wrath, and to those who are like them among the people of disbelief in God and His Messenger and what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought from God. God Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve, meaning: those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied him and what he brought to them from God, neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God, meaning: his wealth that he accumulated in this world, and his children whom he raised in it, will not ward off anything from God’s punishment on the Day of Resurrection if He delays it for them until the Day of Resurrection, nor in this world if He hastens it for them in it.

He specifically mentioned his children and his wealth because a man’s children are his closest relatives, and he has more power over his wealth than he does over the wealth of others, and his command over it is more permissible than his command over the wealth of others. So if his children, his own bloodline, and his wealth, over which he has authority, are of no use to him, then his relatives and all his relatives and their wealth are even less likely to be of any use to him before God. Then He, the Most High, informed us that they are the people of the Fire, who are its people, by His saying: And those are the companions of the Fire. He made them its companions because they are its people who will not leave it or depart from it, like a man’s companion who does not leave him, and his companion who does not leave him. Then He confirmed that by informing us about them that they will abide therein eternally, that their companionship with it is a companionship that has no end, since there are things that leave their companion in some cases, and leave him in some times.

This is not the case with the companionship of those who disbelieved in the Fire that they entered, but it is a permanent companionship that has no end or end. We seek refuge in God from it and from what brings one closer to it in word and deed.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: a likeness of what those who disbelieve spend, i.e. a likeness of what the disbeliever gives in charity from his money, to give it to someone who gives it as a way of drawing closer to his Lord, while he denies the Oneness of God and denies Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that it is of no benefit to him despite his disbelief, and that it is wasted when he needs it, and gone after what he had hoped for from the return of its benefit to him, like a wind with intense cold, this wind with intense cold struck, the tillage of a people, meaning: the crops of a people who had hoped for its harvest, and hoped for its yield and the return of its benefit, they wronged themselves, meaning: the owners of the crops, they disobeyed God and transgressed His limits, so it destroyed it, meaning: the wind with the cold destroyed their crops, after what they had hoped for from hope and the return of its benefit to them. God Almighty says: Likewise, what God does with the spending and charity of the unbeliever during his life, when he meets Him, its reward is nullified and his hope in it is disappointed.
The parable was used for spending, and what is meant by parable is God’s action with spending. This is explained by His statement:
h
Like a wind in which there is a chill
, so it is as we have explained in its parable His statement:
h
Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire (al-Baqarah 2
:17), and what is similar to that.

The interpretation of the statement is: The example of God nullifying the reward for what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind in which there is a cold snap. It is permissible to omit mentioning God nullifying the reward for that because the last part of the statement indicates it, which is His statement: like a wind in which there is a cold snap, and because the listener knows its meaning.
The interpreters differed about the meaning of the expenditure mentioned in this verse.
Some of them said: It is the known expenditure among people.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Like what they spend in this worldly life, he said: The spending of the unbeliever in this world.

x: Others said: Rather, it is what he says with his tongue, which he does not believe in his heart.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told me, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like that of a cold wind which strikes the crops of a people who have wronged themselves and destroys them. He said: The example of what he says but is not accepted from him is like this crop, when the wrongdoing people have planted it and a cold wind strikes it and destroys it. So they spent, and their polytheism destroyed them. We have explained the first of these correctly before. We have already explained the interpretation of the life of this world, and it is sufficient to repeat it in this place. As for the cold, it is severe cold, and that is due to a storm from the north in a hurricane of dew and rain, on a dark morning following a clear night, as:

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Yazid ibn Zuraiʿ told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn Ghiyath, who said,
m: I heard ʿIkrimah say:
h
A wind in which there is cold
, he said: severe cold.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said:
h
A wind in which there is cold
, he said: severe cold and freezing cold.

c: Ali bin Dawud told us, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A wind in which there is cold
, meaning: cold.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Al-Sarr means cold.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like a wind in which there is a chill
, meaning: intense cold.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the cold, meaning severe cold.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Like
h
a wind in which there is cold
, he said:
h
a wind in which there is cold

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: A wind in which there is a cold wind, he said: Cold wind, a cold wind that destroyed their crops. He said: The Arabs call it the dharīb. The wind comes cold and becomes a dharīb that has burned the crops. They say: He blew last night, he was struck by the dharīb of that dharīb that struck him.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
A wind in which there is cold
, he said:
h
A wind in which there is cold

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And what God did to these infidels what He did to them, of nullifying the reward of their deeds and invalidating their wages, out of injustice from Him to them, meaning: He placed what He did to them in the wrong place and with those who were not worthy of it. Rather, He placed His action in its right place and did to them what they were worthy of. Because the work that they did was not for God, and they were loyal to Him in His Oneness, and followed His command, and believed in His messengers. Rather, that was from them, and they were polytheists in it, and opposed His command, and denied His messengers, after He had previously told them that He does not accept any work from a worker except with sincerity in monotheism for Him, and acknowledgment of the prophethood of His prophets, and belief in what they brought them, and His confirmation of the arguments against them with that.

So, by doing what he did to those who disbelieved in him and disobeyed his command in that - after he had been excused, by nullifying and wasting his work, he was not unjust to him. Rather, the disbeliever is the unjust himself, by causing him to commit disobedience to God and disobey His command, which led him to the fire of Hell and burned him in the blazing fire of Saqar.
By this, the Most High means:
h
O you who have believed
in God and His Messenger, and have acknowledged what their Prophet brought to them from their Lord,
h
Do not take as intimates those other than yourselves

, meaning: Do not take as allies and friends for yourselves, other than yourselves, meaning: other than the people of your religion and your nation, meaning from among the non-believers. He made the inner circle an example of a man’s intimate friend, so he likened it to what is around his stomach, which is his clothes, because it takes the place of what is around his body, which is his clothes, in his knowledge of his secrets and what he conceals from his relatives and many of his relatives. God forbade the believers in Him from taking the disbelievers as friends and companions. Then He made them aware of what they are like to them, in terms of deceit and treachery, and their desire to cause them calamities.
So He warned them about them and their friendship with them. God Almighty said: They will not spare you any harm, meaning: they will not be able to harm you.

i: From alut to spare, it is said: Ma ala so-and-so is such-and-such, meaning: he was not able, as the poet said:
x: She is loud and clear, if she shows her sight, or the means to suffice me.

Meaning: You cannot see at noon. Rather, what He, the Most High, means by His saying: They will spare no effort in ruining you, is the inner circle that He forbade the believers from taking with them. He said: This inner circle will not let you go as far as it can, meaning it will not spare any effort in what will cause you to go astray. The root of the word khabal and khabal is corruption, and it is then used in many meanings, as indicated by the hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Someone who is afflicted with madness - or: injury. As for his saying:
h
They wish you would suffer

, he means: They wish you to suffer. He says: They wish you to suffer and evil in your religion and that which will upset you and not please you. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of Muslims who used to mix with their Jewish allies and hypocrites among them, and they showed them affection for the reasons that existed between them in their ignorance before Islam.
So God forbade them from doing that and from seeking their advice in any of their affairs.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad said, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Some of the Muslims used to maintain close relations with some of the Jews, because of the neighbourliness and alliance between them in the pre-Islamic era. So God Almighty revealed about them, forbidding them from keeping close relations with them, fearing that they would cause them discord:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, until His saying: and believe in the entire Book.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, for they will not spare you any ruin, regarding the hypocrites from the people of Medina. God Almighty forbade the believers from taking them as allies.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, for they will not spare you any ruin.
h
They wish you would suffer
.” God Almighty forbade the believers from bringing in the hypocrites, or befriending them, or taking them as allies instead of the believers.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, they are the hypocrites.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, for they will not spare you any ruin, meaning do not bring in the hypocrites, befriending them instead of the believers.

c: Abu Kuraib and Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated to us, they said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Al-Awam bin Hawshab informed us, on the authority of Al-Azhar bin Rashid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and
h
do not engrave Arabic on your rings
.” He said: We did not know what that meant, until they came to Al-Hasan and asked him. He said: Yes, as for his saying:
h
Do not engrave Arabic on your rings

, he means: Do not engrave Muhammad on your rings. As for his saying: And do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, he means the polytheists, he says: Do not consult them in any of your affairs. Al-Hasan said: And the confirmation of that is in the Book of God. Then he recited this verse:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
. As for the intimates, they are the hypocrites.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, the verse, he said: The believer does not take the hypocrite as intimates to the exclusion of his brother.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
, the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites. And he recited His statement:
h
Hatred has already appeared from their mouths
, the verse.

x: They differed in the interpretation of his saying:
h
They wish you had suffered
Some of them said: It means: They wish you had not strayed from your religion.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They wish you had suffered
, meaning: you had not gone astray.

x: Others said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: They wish you would be stubborn, meaning: in your religion, meaning: they wish you would be stubborn in your religion.

If someone were to say to us: How was it said: They wished you had suffered, and the report came from the inner circle, in the past tense in the place of the state, and the cut-off after the completion of the report, and the states are only in the form of future nouns and verbs and not past ones? It was said: The matter is not as you thought, that his saying:
h
And they wish that you would suffer

, is a state of the inner circle, but rather it is a second piece of report about them, separate from the first and not connected to it. Rather, the interpretation of the statement is: O you who believe, do not take as inner circles their description is such and such, their description is such and such. So the report about the second quality is not connected to the first quality, even if they are both from the description of one person. Some Arabists have claimed that his saying,
h
They wish you had suffered

, is a connection to the inner circle, and it was connected to his saying, They spare no effort to ruin you, so there is no reason for another connection after the inner circle is complete with his connection.

But the statement on that is as we explained before, that his saying: And they wished that you had suffered, is a predicate of the subject of the entourage, not the first predicate, and not a state of the entourage nor a separation from it.

By that, the Most High means: The hatred of those whom I have forbidden you, O believers, from taking as intimates for you from among yourselves has become apparent from their mouths, meaning: with their tongues. And what became apparent to them from them with their tongues was their persistence in their disbelief, and their enmity towards whoever differs from what they are persisting upon of misguidance. So that is one of the most important reasons for their enmity towards the people of faith, because that is enmity against religion, and enmity against religion is enmity that cannot be removed except by one of the two enemies moving to the religion of the other of them, and that is moving from guidance to misguidance that was previously misguidance for the one to whom it was moved. So in their showing that to the believers, and their persistence upon it, was the clearest evidence for the people of faith of what they are upon of hatred and enmity towards them.

Some of them said: The meaning of his statement: Hatred has already appeared from their mouths is that their hatred for the people of faith has already appeared to their allies from among the hypocrites and Surat Al Imran 3:118
h
O you who have believed
h
do not take as intimates those other than yourselves
. They will not spare you any ruin. They desire what you suffer.
h
Hatred has already appeared from their mouths
h
and what their hearts conceal is greater

. We have made clear to you the verses, if you would only use reason. the unbelievers, by informing one another of that. The proponents of this statement claimed that those meant by this verse are the hypocrites, not those who openly declare their unbelief from among the Jews and the polytheists.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Hatred has already appeared from their mouths
, meaning: Hatred has already appeared from the mouths of the hypocrites towards their brothers among the infidels, due to their deceit of Islam and its people, and their hatred of them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ: Hatred has appeared from their mouths, meaning: from the mouths of the hypocrites. This statement that we have mentioned from Qatada is a statement that has no meaning. That is because God, the Most High, mentioned it, only forbade the believers from taking as intimates those whom they knew to be deceitful towards Islam and its people and to be hostile, either through clear evidence indicating that this is part of their description, or through the enmity, hatred and rivalry shown by those described in this manner. As for those whom they did not establish with knowledge that they were the one whom God, the Most High, forbade them from being intimate with or intimate with, it is not permissible that they forbade them from being intimate with or befriending them, except after they had made them known, either by their persons and names, or by the descriptions by which they knew them. Since this is the case, and the hypocrites express with their tongues what is in their hearts of the hatred of the believers towards their disbelieving brothers, without the believers realizing what they are towards them, while they show faith to them with their tongues and are friendly to them, it is clear that the ones whom God forbade the believers from taking as intimates to themselves, are those whose hatred has become apparent to them with their tongues, as God the Almighty described them with, so the believers recognized them by the description with which God described them, and that they are the ones whom God the Almighty described as the companions of the Fire, abiding therein, from those who had a covenant and a pact with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from the People of the Book. Because if they were the hypocrites, the matter concerning them would be as we have explained. Even if the infidels were among those who had waged war against the believers, the believers would not have taken them as confidants for themselves, rather than the believers, despite the differences in their countries and the separation of their cities. Rather, they were those who were among the believers from the People of the Book during the days of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among those who had a covenant and agreement with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Jews of the Children of Israel. And hatred is a verbal noun. It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: Hatred has appeared from their mouths in the masculine form. This is permissible in the masculine form and in the feminine form because the feminine of verbal nouns is not necessarily feminine, so it is permissible to make what comes out of them masculine in the feminine form and make it feminine, as the Almighty said: And the shriek seized those who did wrong
r
, and as He said: There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord
r
(Al-An'am: 157)
, and in another place: And the shriek seized those who did wrong
r

There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord (Al-A'raf: 73, 85). He said: From their mouths, and the hatred that appeared appeared from their tongues, because what is meant by it is the speech that appeared to the believers from their mouths, so he said: The hatred has appeared from their mouths, from their tongues.

x: God Almighty means by that: And what their hearts conceal, meaning: the hearts of those whom He forbade them from taking as intimates, so they conceal it from you, O believers, is greater, meaning: greater than what has appeared to you with their tongues from their mouths of hatred and greater, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And what their hearts conceal is greater
, he said:
h
And what their hearts conceal is greater
than what they have revealed with their tongues.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what their hearts conceal is greater
, meaning: What their hearts conceal is greater than what they have revealed with their tongues.

x: By that, the Most High means: We have made clear to you, O believers, the signs, meaning by signs the lessons. We have made clear to you the affair of these Jews whom We forbade you from taking as intimates instead of the believers, what you may consider and learn from their affair, if you were to reason, meaning: if you were to understand from God His admonitions, His commands, and His prohibitions, and you know the places where that benefits you, and the extent of its return to you.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves.
It has been mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: Hatred has appeared from their mouths in the masculine form.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means:
h
Here you are
, O believers, whom you love, He says: You love these infidels whom I forbade you from taking as intimates instead of the believers, so
h
you love them
and maintain relations with them while they do not love you, rather they conceal enmity and deceit towards you,
h
and you believe in the entire Book
. The meaning of book in this context is the meaning of the collective, as it is said: The dirhams increased in people’s hands, meaning dirhams. Likewise, his statement:
h
And you believe in the entire Book

, means: in all the books, your book that God revealed to you, their book that He revealed to them, and other books that God revealed to His servants. God Almighty says: So you, O believers, believe in all the books, and you know that those whom I forbade you from taking as intimates from among yourselves are disbelievers in all of that, because of their denial of all of God’s covenants to them, and their changing what is in it of God’s command and prohibition, and they are more deserving of your enmity towards them, their hatred and their deception, than your enmity and hatred, along with their denial of some of the books and their rejection of some of them, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: You believe in the entire Book, meaning: in your Book and their Book and in the books that came before that, and they disbelieve in your Book, so you are more deserving of hatred for them than they are for you.

x: He said:
h
Here you are

, these you, and he did not say these are you, so he differentiated between ha and thala by the pronoun of the name of the addressees, because the Arabs do this in this way if they want to approximate it and the method of deficiency that needs the completion of the report, and this is like when it is said to some of them: Where are you, and the one to whom it is said responds: Here I am, so they differentiate between the warning and this by the pronoun of his own name, and they hardly say: This is me, then it is dualized and pluralized on that. And they may repeat the letter of warning with: dha and say: Here I am this. And they do not do that except in what is approximate, but if it is not approximate and deficiency, they say: This is him and this is you. And they do the same with the apparent names, they say: This is Amr standing, if this is an approximation.
And they only do that in the pronoun with approximation, to differentiate between this if it means the deficient that needs completion, and it if it means the correct name. His saying:
h
You love them
, is a predicate of approximation.

In this verse there is a clarification from God Almighty about the state of the two groups - I mean the believers and the disbelievers - and the mercy and compassion of the people of faith towards those who disagree with them, and the hardness of the hearts of the people of disbelief and their harshness towards the people of faith, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Here you are
, loving them but they do not love you,
h
and you believe in the entire Book
. By God, the believer loves the hypocrite and shelters him and has mercy on him. If the hypocrite had the power to do what the believer has the power to do to him, he would destroy its greenery.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: The believer is better for the hypocrite than the hypocrite is for the believer, may God have mercy on him. If the hypocrite were able to do to the believer what the believer is able to do to him, he would destroy his greenery. Mujahid used to say: This verse was revealed about the hypocrites.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me that.
m: He said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.

x: By this, the Most High means: That those whom God forbade the believers to take as intimates from those other than themselves, and described them by their description, if they meet the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they will give them with their tongues a precaution, out of fear for themselves from them, and they will say to them: We have believed and confirmed what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. But if they are alone and are in a secluded place where the believers cannot see them, they will bite their fingers - despite what they see of the Surat Al Imran 3:119
h
Here you are
h
you love them
but they do not love you, and you believe in the Book, all of it,
h
and when they meet you
they say, "We believe," but when they are alone they bite their fingertips at you out of rage. Say, "Die in your rage.

Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts." believers’ unity, their word being united, and their relationship being in good terms - their fingertips, out of anger at the resentment they have towards them, and grief over the backs they lean on to confront their enmity and fight them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when they meet you

, they say, ‘We believe,’ but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage. When they meet the believers, they say, We believe. They only fear for their blood and wealth, so treat them that way. And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage. He says: Because of the rage and hatred they find in their hearts for what they are doing. If they could smell it, they would be against the believers, so they are as God, the Almighty, has described them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly, except that he said: Out of anger for their hatred of what they are doing, and he did not say: If they find a smell, and what follows it.

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told us, Muslim told us, Yahya bin Amr bin Malik Al-Nakri told me, my father told us:
m: When Abu Al-Juza’ recited this verse:
h
And when they meet you

, they say, ‘We believe,’ but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage, he said: They are the Ibadis. Fingers is the plural of anmlah, and it is also said anmlah, and it may be the plural of anmlan. The poet said: I would like you both, as long as my saliva moistens my throat and my fingers can hold ten fingers They are the fingertips, such as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The fingers, the tips of the fingers.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you, the fingers.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They bit their fingertips out of rage
, he said: They bit their fingers.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Say, O Muhammad, to these Jews whose characteristics I have described to you, and I have informed you that when they meet your companions they say: We believe, and when they are alone they bite their fingertips at you in rage: Die in your rage that you have against the believers because of their unified word and the unity of their group. This statement came out as a command, and it is a supplication from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he should supplicate against them that God destroy them, out of grief for the anger they have toward the believers, before they see in them what they wish for them of hardship in their religion, and misguidance after their guidance. So He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad: Destroy yourselves with your anger, Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts, meaning by that: God is All-Knowing of what is in the breasts of those who, when they meet the believers, say: We believe, and what they conceal of rancor and sorrow for them, and what they believe of enmity and hatred for them, and what is in the breasts of all His creation, He preserves for all of them what is concealed of good and evil, until He rewards all of them for what they have presented of good and evil, and what they believed of faith and disbelief, and what they concealed for His Messenger and the believers of advice, or rancor and anger.

evidence.text: Abbas bin Muhammad told us, Muslim told us, Yahya bin Amr bin Malik Al-Nakri told me, my father told us: When Abu Al-Juza’ recited this verse: And when they meet you, they say, ‘We believe,’ but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage, he said: They are the Ibadis.

x: What is meant by the words of God Almighty:
h
If good befalls you

, it distresses them, is that if you, O believers, attain joy through your victory over your enemy, and people follow one another in entering your religion, believing in your prophet, and assisting you against your enemies, it distresses them.
And if harm befalls you through the failure of a military expedition, or the injury of an enemy among you, or a disagreement that occurs among your group, they rejoice over it, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If good befalls you

, it grieves them, but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. So when they see unity, unity, and victory over their enemy among the people of Islam, that angers and upsets them. And when they see division and disagreement among the people of Islam, or a party of the Muslims is afflicted, that pleases them, amazes them, and rejoices at it. So whenever a generation emerges from among them, God belies their story, tramples their position, invalidates their argument, and exposes their shame. So that is the judgment of God regarding those of them who have passed away and those who remain until the Day of Resurrection.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
If good befalls you

, it grieves them, but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. He said: They are the hypocrites, when they saw among the people of Islam a unity and victory over their enemy, that angered them greatly and made them sad. And when they saw among the people of Islam division and disagreement, or a party of the Muslims was afflicted, that pleased them and they were amazed by it. God the Almighty said: “But if you are patient and fear God, not will their plot harm you at all. Indeed, God encompasses what they do.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If good befalls you
, it distresses them, he said: If they see a group and harmony among the believers, that distresses them, and if they see division and disagreement among them, they rejoice. As for His statement:
h
And if you are patient and fear God
h
their plot will not harm you at all

, He, the Most High, means by that: And if you are patient, O believers, in obeying God and following His command in what He has commanded you to do, and avoiding what He has forbidden you from: taking as intimates for yourselves those Jews whose description God has described, apart from the believers, and other than that from all the rest of what He has forbidden you, and fear God, your Lord, so that you fear going before Him in what He has obligated you and made obligatory upon you of His right and the right of His Messenger,
h
their plot will not harm you at all

, meaning: the plot of those whose description He has described. By their plot, he means the evils they seek for the Muslims, and their deceit against them, to turn them away from guidance and the path of truth.

x: There are different readings of the verse:
h
It will not harm you

A group of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as la yadhurkum with a kasra on the letter Ḍād, from the saying of the one who says: So-and-so harmed me, so he is harming me with harm. It has been reported that it was heard from the Arabs: it does not benefit me nor does it harm me. If it had been read in this language, it would have been said:
h
their plot will not harm you at all
, but I do not know of anyone who read it like that.
A group of the people of Medina read it, and most of the people of Kufa read it:
h
Their plot will not harm you at all
, with a damma on the letter Ḍād and a shaddah on the letter rā’, from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so harmed me, so he will harm me greatly. As for the nominative case in his saying:
h
It will not harm you

, it is from two aspects: One of them: to follow the letter ra in its movement - since its origin is the jussive, and it could not be jussive because of its emphasis - the closest movement of the letters before it, and that is the movement of the letter dad which is the damma, so the movement of the letter ra was added to it because of its proximity to it, as they said: Madd ya hada. The other aspect of the two aspects of raising in this: that it is raised on the correctness, and la means not, and the fa which is the answer to the conditional clause is left to the listener’s knowledge of its position.
If that is what it means, then the interpretation of the statement is:
h
And if you are patient and fear God
, then
h
their plot will not harm you at all

i: Then the fa was left out of his statement:
h
Their plot will not harm you at all
, and la was directed to the meaning of not, as the poet said:
x: If it does not satisfy you until you return me to my country, I do not think you will be satisfied.

If the letter ra was moved to the accusative and genitive cases, it would be permissible, as it was said: Madd ya hada and Madd. And His statement: Indeed, God encompasses what they do, the Most High says: Indeed, God encompasses what these infidels do to His servants and His lands of corruption, turning people away from His path, enmity towards the people of His religion, and other acts of disobedience to God. He encompasses all of it, preserving it, and nothing of it escapes Him until He pays them their recompense for all of it and makes them taste His punishment for it.

evidence.text: A group of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as la yadhurkum with a kasra on the letter Ḍād, from the saying of the one who says: So-and-so harmed me, so he is harming me with harm.
If it had been read in this language, it would have been said: their plot will not harm you at all, but I do not know of anyone who read it like that.

A group of the people of Medina read it, and most of the people of Kufa read it: Their plot will not harm you at all, with a damma on the letter Ḍād and a shaddah on the letter rā’, from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so harmed me, so he will harm me greatly.

x: What God, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And when you went forth from your family to place the believers in their homes is that if you are patient and fear God

, the plot of these infidel Jews will not harm you at all, O believers, but God will grant you victory over them if you are patient in obeying Me and following the command of My Messenger, just as I granted you victory at Badr when you were weak. But if you, O believers, disobey My command and are not patient in what I have charged you with of My obligations, and do not fear what I have forbidden you and disobey My command and the command of My Messenger, then what happened to you will happen to you as happened to anyone else. Remember that day, when your Prophet went forth to place the believers in their homes. He left out mentioning the report about the matter of the people if they were not patient in the matter of their Lord and did not fear Him, being content with the indication of what appeared from the speech on its meaning, since he mentioned what He would do to them of turning away the plot of their enemies from them if they were patient in the matter of His and feared His prohibitions, and he followed that by reminding them of the calamity that befell them at Uhud, since some of them disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they disputed over opinion among themselves.
He brought out the address in his saying:
h
And when you left your family

, as an address to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by its meaning: those whom he forbade from taking the infidel Jews as confidants instead of the believers. So he made clear that his saying: And when, only included it in the meaning of the speech as I have explained and clarified.
The people of interpretation differed about the day that God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And when you left your family
in the morning, you assigned the believers positions for battle.
Some of them said: He meant the day of Uhud.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the words of God:
h
And when you went forth from your family
, to appoint the believers to their stations for battle, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked on his feet that day, appointing the believers to their stations.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when you went forth from your family to assign the believers to positions for battle
, that was on the day of Uhud. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went forth from his family to Uhud to assign the believers to positions for battle.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said:
m: h
And when you went forth from your family

to assign the believers to Surat Al Imran 3:121 And when you went out in the morning from your family to station the believers in stations for battle. And God is Hearing and Knowing. positions for battle. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went forth from his family to Uhud to assign the believers to positions for battle.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when you went forth from your family
, to appoint the believers to their stations for battle, it was the Day of Uhud.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And when you went out in the morning from your family to meet the believers, he said: This was the day of Uhud.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Among what was revealed on the Day of UHud 11:
h
And when you went forth from your family
to rest with the believers.

x: Others said: He meant the Day of the Confederates.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when you went forth from your family to assign the believers to their positions for battle
, he said: He meant Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who went forth to assign the believers to their positions for battle on the Day of the Confederates.

x: The more correct of these two statements is the statement of the one who said: He meant the Day of Uhud. Because God Almighty says in the verse that follows it: When two parties among you were about to lose heart, and there is no disagreement among the people of interpretation that He meant by the two parties: Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha, and there is no disagreement among the people of biography and knowledge of the campaigns of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that what God mentioned about their affair was only the Day of Uhud, not the Day of the Confederates.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How could that be on the day of Uhud, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only went to one of his family to fight on Friday after he had prayed the Friday prayer with his family in Medina with the people, like the one who told you: Ibn Hamid said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said, Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and other scholars of ours told me: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to Uhud after the Friday prayer. He entered and put on his garments for his nation. That was on Friday when he had finished the prayer, and a man from the Ansar had died on that day. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, then he went out to them and said: It is not appropriate for a prophet, when he has put on his garments for his nation, to take them off until he fights?”

Even though the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to the people in the evening, he did not assign the believers their places to fight when he went out, but rather that was before he went out to fight his enemy. That is because the polytheists came to their place in Uhud - as far as we have been informed - on Wednesday, and they stayed there that day, Thursday, and Friday, until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to them on Friday, after he had prayed the Friday prayer with his companions, and he was in the valley of Uhud on Saturday, the middle of Shawwal.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, Asim ibn Amr ibn Qatada, al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, and others told me.

x: How did he assign the believers positions to fight in the morning before he went out, and you know that assigning positions means taking a place?

He appointed them to that position before confronting his enemy, when he consulted his companions about the opinion he saw for them, a day or two ago. That is because when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about the descent of the polytheists from Quraysh and their followers at Uhud, he said - among other things:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein narrated to us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi - on his companions:
m: Advise me what I should do? They said: O Messenger of God, go out to these dogs! The Ansar said: O Messenger of God, no enemy has ever defeated us when he came to our land, so how about when you are among us!! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and he had never called him before, and consulted him, and he said: O Messenger of God, go out with us to these dogs! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, liked it when they entered the city and fought in the alleys, so An-Nu'man bin Malik Al-Ansari came to him and said: O Messenger of God, do not deprive me of Paradise, for by He who sent you with the truth, I will enter Paradise! He said to him: Why? He said: Because I bear witness that there is no god but God, and that you are the Messenger of God, and that I do not flee from battle! He said: You have spoken the truth. So he was killed that day. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for his armor and put it on. When they saw him wearing his armor, they regretted it and said: What a bad thing we have done! We are advising the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while the revelation is coming to him!! So they stood up and apologized to him and said: Do what you have seen. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not appropriate for a prophet to wear armor for his nation and then put it down until he fights.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri narrated to me,
m: and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, and Asim ibn Amr ibn Qatadah, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and other scholars of ours, they said: When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and the Muslims heard that the polytheists had descended to their camp at Uhud, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: I saw cows, so I interpreted it as good. I saw a dent in the fly of my sword, and I saw that I put my hand into a strong shield, so I interpreted it as Medina. If you see fit to stay in Medina and leave them where they have descended, then if they stay, then they will stay in a bad place, and if they enter upon us, then we will fight them there. The opinion of ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was with the opinion of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), he shared the opinion of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) in that: that he should not go out to them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) hated to leave the city.

x: Some of the Muslims whom God had honored with martyrdom on the day of Uhud, and others who had missed Badr and its presence, said: O Messenger of God, let us go out to our enemies, so that they will not see that we are cowards and weak before them! Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul said: O Messenger of God, stay in the city and do not go out to them, for by God, we have never gone out to an enemy of ours without him killing us, and no one has ever entered upon us without us killing him. So leave them, O Messenger of God, for if they stay, they will stay in a prison cell, and if they enter, the men will fight them in their faces, and the women and children will throw stones at them from above, and if they return, they will return disappointed as they came. The people, who were in a state of love to meet the people, kept on following the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered and put on his clothes for his nation.

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, assigned the believers positions for fighting, as we mentioned of his consultation with his companions with the opinion we mentioned, according to what those whose words we have narrated described. It is said: I provided a home for the people, and I provided it for them. So I provide them with a home, and I provide them with a home.

i: It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud:
h
And when you went forth from your family
to prepare for the believers stations for battle, and that is permissible, just as it is said: He rode behind you and He rode behind you, and I paid her dowry and I paid her, as the poet said:
x: I ask forgiveness from God for a sin that I cannot count.
To Him belongs the face and the work. The words: I ask God for forgiveness for my sin.

c: It was narrated from the Arabs by hearing:
m: I have returned the people to a place of rest, so I will return them to a place of rest. It is also said: I have returned the camels to their resting place. The resting place is the place where they spend the night. Seats is the plural of seat, which is the council.

x: The interpretation of the statement is: And remember when you, O Muhammad, went out from your family to take for the believers a camp and a place to fight their enemy. And His saying:
h
And God is All-Hearing
, All-Knowing, means by that, the Most High,
h
And God is All-Hearing

, of what the believers say to you regarding what you consulted them about, regarding the place of your meeting and their meeting with your enemy and their enemy, from the saying of the one who said: Go out with us to them until we meet them outside the city, and the saying of the one who said to you: Do not go out to them and stay in the city until they enter it upon us, as we have explained before - and what you advise them with, O Muhammad, All-Knowing, of the best of those opinions for you and for them, and what the hearts of those who advise you to go out to your enemy conceal, and the hearts of those who advise you to stay in the city, and other than that of your affair and their affair, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God is All-Hearing
, All-Knowing, meaning: He hears what they say, and He knows what they conceal.

evidence.text: It was mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: And when you went forth from your family to prepare for the believers stations for battle, and that is permissible, just as it is said: He rode behind you and He rode behind you, and I paid her dowry and I paid her, as the poet said: I ask forgiveness from God for a sin that I cannot count.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, when two groups of you were about to lose heart. The two groups that were about to fail, he told us, were Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart
, he said: Banu Haritha were towards Uhud, and Banu Salamah were towards Sal’, and that was on the day of the Trench.

x: We have proven that this happened on the day of Uhud in the past, sufficiently enough to not repeat it.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart

, the verse, and that was on the day of Uhud, and the two parties were Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha, two tribes of the Ansar, they were about to do something but God protected them from that. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed they said: It would not please us that we did not intend to do what we intended to do, and God has informed us that He is our protector.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
When two parties among you were about to attack

, the verse, and that was on the day of Uhud. The two parties were Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha, two tribes of the Ansar. Then he mentioned something similar to what Qatada said. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Uhud with a thousand men, and he promised them victory if they were patient. When Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul returned with three hundred, Abu Jabir al-Sulami followed them, calling them. When they defeated him and said to him: We do not know how to fight, and if you obey us, you will return with us. And God Almighty said:
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart

, and they were Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha. They were about to return when Abdullah ibn Ubayy returned, but God protected them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained with seven hundred.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ikrimah said:
m: It was revealed about Banu Salamah from the Khazraj, and Banu Haritha from the Aws, and their leader was Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart
, they were Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart
, and the two parties were: Banu Salamah from Jushm ibn al-Khazraj, and Banu Haritha from al-Nabi’t from al-Aws, and they are the two wings.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart
, the verse, he said: They were two parties from the Ansar who were about to lose heart, but God protected them and defeated their enemy.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he said,
m: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say:
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart
, he said: They were Banu Salamah and Banu Haritha, and we would not have liked it if we had not been about to lose heart, because God Almighty said: And God is their protector.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, he said:
m: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: When two groups of you were about to lose heart, he said: This was the day of Uhud. As for his saying: that they fail, he means that they become weak and turn away from meeting their enemy. It is said: So-and-so failed to meet his enemy, he failed Surat Al Imran 3:122
h
When two parties among you were about to lose heart
, but God was their protector. And upon God let the believers rely. miserably, like:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Failure is cowardice.

x: Their concern, which they were about to do in terms of failure, was to turn away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers when ʿAbdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and those with him turned away from them, out of cowardice on their part, without any doubt in Islam or hypocrisy. So God protected them from what they were about to do, and they went with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the purpose for which he had gone, and they left ʿAbdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and the hypocrites with him. So God, the Almighty, praised them for their steadfastness in the truth, and informed us that He was their guardian and supporter against their enemies among the infidels, as: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And God is their Guardian, meaning He is the Defender of them in whatever they intended to do of their failure.

This was because of their weakness and frailty that had afflicted them, without a doubt afflicting them in their religion. So He took care of that for them through His mercy and favor until they were saved from their frailty and frailty, and joined their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning: Whoever among the believers has weakness or frailty, let him put his trust in Me and seek My help, so that I may help him in his matter and defend him until I reach him and strengthen him in his intention.

It was mentioned that Ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, used to recite: And God is their protector. It was only permissible to recite it in this way because the two groups, even though they are in the wording of two, are in the meaning of a group, like the two opponents and the two parties.

evidence.text: It was only permissible to recite it in this way because the two groups, even though they are in the wording of two, are in the meaning of a group, like the two opponents and the two parties.

x: By that, the Most High means: If you are patient and fear God, their plot will not harm you at all, and your Lord will support you. And God had already supported you at Badr, over your enemies, and you were on that day were weak, meaning: few, without protection from the people, until God made you victorious over your enemy, despite their great number and your small number, and you are more numerous today than you were then. So if you are patient for the sake of God’s command, He will support you as He supported you that day.

So fear God, the Most High says: So fear your Lord by obeying Him and avoiding His prohibitions, that you may be grateful, meaning: to thank Him for what He has bestowed upon you of victory over your enemies and the manifestation of your religion, and for what He has guided you to of the truth from which your opponents have strayed, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God gave you victory at Badr when you were weak, meaning: and you were fewer in number and weaker in strength,
h
so fear God that you may be grateful
, meaning: so fear God, for it is gratitude for My blessings. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning for which Badr was called Badr.

x: Some of them said: It was named thus because it was the water of a man called Badr, so it was named after its owner.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Badr belonged to a man called Badr, and it was named after him.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Zakariya told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, that he said:
m: And God gave you victory at Badr, he said: Badr was a well belonging to a man called Badr, so it was named after him.

x: Others denied this and said: This is the name given to the spot, just as all other countries are named after it.

Who said that? Al-Harith bin Muhammad narrated, Ibn Saad narrated, Muhammad bin Umar al-Waqidi narrated, Mansur narrated, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: It was called Badr because it was a water source for a man from Juhayna called Badr. Al-Harith said, Ibn Saad said, al-Waqidi said: So I mentioned that to Abdullah bin Ja’far and Muhammad bin Salih, and they denied it and said: Why was it called al-Safra’? Why was it called al-Hamra’? Why was it called Rabigh? This is nothing, it is just the name of a place. He said: I mentioned that to Yahya bin al-Nu’man al-Ghifari, and he said: I heard our elders from Banu Ghaffar say: It is our water source and our home, and no one has ever owned it and it is called Badr, and it is not from the lands of Juhayna, rather it is the lands of Ghaffar. Al-Waqidi said: This is what is well-known among us.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Badr is a body of water to the right of the road to Mecca, between Mecca and Medina. As for his saying: humiliated, it is the plural of humiliated, just as a’zza is the plural of aziz and al-albah is the plural of labib.

x: God Almighty called them humiliated because of their small number, as they were three hundred souls and a dozen, and their number was between nine hundred and a thousand - as we have explained previously - so He made them humiliated because of their small number. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “
h
And God had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak
h
So fear God that you may be grateful

.” Badr is a body of water between Mecca and Medina, where the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists met. It was the first battle that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought. It was mentioned to us that he said to his companions on that day: You are today like the companions of Saul on the day he met Goliath. They were three hundred and some men, and the polytheists on that day were a thousand, or nearly that.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And God certainly gave you victory at Badr when you were weak
h
So fear God that you may be grateful
,” he said, he says: and you were weak, few, and they were on that day a dozen or three hundred.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similar to the statement of Qatada.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us,
m: on the Surat Al Imran 3:123
h
And God had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak
h
So fear God that you may be grateful
. authority of Ibn Ishaq: And God gave you victory at Badr when you were weak, fewer in number and weaker in strength.

x: As for his saying:
h
So fear God that you may be grateful
, its interpretation is like that which I have explained, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So fear God that you may be grateful
, meaning: So fear Me, for it is gratitude for My blessings.

x: God Almighty means: And God gave you victory at Badr when you were weak, when you said to the believers among your companions: Is it not enough for you that your Lord should support you with three thousand angels sent down? That was on the day of Badr. Then the people of interpretation differed about the presence of the angels on the day of Badr, their war. On which day did they promise that?

Some of them said: God Almighty had promised the believers on the day of Badr that He would support them with His angels if the enemy came to them suddenly, but they did not come to them and did not support them.
Who said that?

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told me, saying, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying, Dawud told us, on the authority of ʿAmir,
m: saying: The Muslims were told that Karz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi was supplying the polytheists. He said: This was difficult for the Muslims, so they were told: “Is it not enough for you that your Lord should supply you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once, your Lord will supply you with five thousand angels marked.” Karz was defeated, so he returned, and did not supply them with the five.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd Al-A'la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, he said:
m: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed, then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: And they will come to you in a fit of this - meaning Kurz and his companions - Your Lord will reinforce you
h
with five thousand marked angels

. He said: Then Kurz and his companions were informed of the defeat, but he did not reinforce them, and the five did not come down, and they were reinforced after that with a thousand, so they were four thousand angels with the Muslims.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: When you said to the believers, ‘Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels?’ the entire verse, he said: This was on the day of Badr.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: The Muslims were told that Kurz bin Jabir Al-Muharibi wanted to reinforce the polytheists at Badr. He said: This was difficult for the Muslims, so God Almighty revealed: Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you? until His saying:
h
From the angels marked
. He said: Then the defeat of the polytheists reached him, so he did not reinforce his companions, and they did not reinforce the five.

x: Others said: This was a promise from God to them on the day of Badr, so the believers were patient and feared God, so He supported them with His angels as He promised them.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr told me, on the authority of some of Banu Sa’idah, he said:
m: I heard Abu Asid Malik bin Rabi’ah, after his eyesight was damaged, say: If I were with you at Badr now and I had my eyesight, I would tell you about the valley from which the angels came out, I would not doubt or dispute.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said,
m: Ibn Ishaq said, and Abdullah bin Abi Bakr told me, on the authority of some of Banu Sa’idah, on the authority of Abu Asid Malik bin Rabi’ah, who had witnessed Badr, that he said after he lost his sight: If I were with you today at Badr and had my sight, I would show you the valley from which the angels came out, I would not doubt or dispute. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who narrated, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who narrated, Ibn Abbas said, a man from Banu Ghafar narrated to me, saying: My cousin and I set out until we climbed a mountain overlooking Badr, and we were polytheists, waiting for the battle to be fought, to see who would be defeated so that we could plunder with whoever plundered. He said: While we were on the mountain, a cloud approached us, and we heard the neighing of horses in it, and I heard a voice saying: Advance, Haizum. He said: As for my cousin, the veil of his heart was lifted and he died on the spot, but as for me, I almost perished, then I pulled myself together.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said, and Al-Hasan ibn Ammarah told me, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Muqsim,
m: the freed slave of Abdullah ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, he said: The angels did not fight on any day except the day of Badr, and on other days they were in number and reinforcements and did not strike. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, my father Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated, on the authority of men from Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Mazini, who had witnessed Badr, who said: I was following a polytheist on the day of Badr to strike him, when his head fell before my sword could reach it. I knew that someone else had killed him. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Muhammad narrated, Husayn ibn Abdullah ibn Ubaydullah ibn Abbas narrated, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Rafi, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was a slave of al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, and Islam had entered us, the people of the household. Al-Abbas converted to Islam, and Umm al-Fadl converted to Islam, and I converted to Islam. Al-Abbas feared his people and hated to oppose them, and he concealed his conversion to Islam. He had much wealth that was distributed among his people. Abu Lahab, the enemy of God, had stayed behind from Badr and sent in his place al-Asi ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira. And so they did, no man stayed behind except that he sent another man in his place. So when the report came of the disaster of the companions of Badr from Quraysh, God subdued and humiliated him, and we found strength and honor in ourselves. He said: I was a weak man, and I was making arrows, carving them in the room of Zamzam. By God, I was sitting there carving arrows, and Umm al-Fadl was sitting with me, and we were pleased with what had come to us of the report, when the wicked Abu Lahab came, dragging his feet in evil, until he sat on the rope of the room, and his back was to my back. While he was sitting, the people said: This is Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib who has arrived! He said: Abu Lahab said: Come to me, O son of my brother, for you have the report! He said: So he sat down with him while the people were standing around him, and he said: O son of my brother, tell me, how was the situation of the people? He said: Nothing, by God, it was only that we met them and turned our shoulders to them, and they killed us and took us prisoner as they wished! By God, I did not blame the people for that. We met white men on piebald horses between the sky and the earth. They were not worthy of anything, and nothing could stand up to them. Abu Rafi said: So I lifted the rope of the room with my hand and said: Those are the angels! Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: Al-Hasan ibn Ammarah narrated, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The one who took Al-Abbas prisoner was Abu Al-Yusr Kaab ibn Amr, the brother of Banu Salamah. Abu Al-Yusr was a strong man, and Al-Abbas was a large man. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Al-Yusr: How did you take Al-Abbas, Abu Al-Yusr, prisoner? He said: O Messenger of God, a man helped me against him whom I had never seen before or after, his appearance was such and such! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A noble angel helped you against him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Will it not suffice for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down
? They were reinforced with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand, Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you suddenly,
h
your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks
. That was on the day of Badr, God reinforced them with five thousand angels.

c: I was told by Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks
, that they came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with marks.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Hisham, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The angels did not fight except on the day of Badr.

x: Others said: God Almighty promised them on the day of Badr that He would support them if they were patient in obeying Him and fighting His enemies, and feared Him by avoiding His prohibitions, that He would support them in all their wars. But they were not patient and did not fear Him except on the day of the Confederates, so He supported them when they besieged Qurayza.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Ammarah Al-Asadi narrated to me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa narrated to us, he said: Sulayman bin Zaid Abu Idam Al-Muharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, he said:
m: We were besieging Qurayzah and An-Nadir for as long as God willed that we besiege them, but He did not grant us victory. So we returned, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for water and washed his head, when Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: O Muhammad, you have laid down your weapons but the angels have not laid down their burdens! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for a rag and wrapped it around his head but did not wash it. Then he called to us, and we stood up, exhausted and not caring about the journey at all, until we reached Qurayzah and An-Nadir. On that day, God, the Almighty, supported us with three thousand angels, and God granted us an easy victory, so we returned with a blessing from God, the Bounty.

x: Others said something similar to this meaning, but they said: The people were not patient, did not fear God, and did not provide anything for anyone.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Amr ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: who heard him say: Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come to you at once, he said: On the day of Badr. He said: So they were not patient and did not fear God, so they did not advance on the day of Uhud, and if they had advanced, they would not have been defeated that day.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, he said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say: They were not supported on the day of Uhud, not even by a single king, or he said: except by a single king, Abu Jaʿfar is doubtful.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: I heard Ubayd ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
Will it not suffice you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand to five thousand angels with marks

. This was a promise from God on the Day of Uhud that He presented to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: that if the believers feared Surat Al Imran 3:125 Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you in haste,
h
your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks
. God and were patient, He would reinforce them with five thousand angels with marks. So the Muslims fled on the Day of Uhud and turned their backs, but God did not reinforce them.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once

the entire verse. They said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they were looking at the polytheists: O Messenger of God, will God not support us as He supported us on the day of Badr? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will it not suffice for you that your Lord supports you with three thousand angels sent down?
