And He only supported you on the day of Badr with a thousand? He said: So the increase came from God on the condition that they be patient and fear God. He said: On the condition that they come upon you at once, your Lord will support you, the entire verse.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is to say: God informed us about His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said to the believers: Will it not suffice you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? So God promised them three thousand angels as reinforcements for them, then He promised them five thousand after the three thousand if they were patient with their enemies and feared God. There is no indication in the verse that they were reinforced with the three thousand or the five thousand, nor that they were not reinforced with them. It may be possible that God, the Almighty, reinforced them, in the manner narrated by those who confirmed that He reinforced them, and it may be possible that He did not reinforce them in the manner mentioned by those who denied that. We do not have any authentic report from the source that proves that they were reinforced with the three thousand or the five thousand.

It is not permissible to say anything about that except with a report that establishes evidence. And there is no report of that kind, so we accept the statement of one of the two groups. However, there is evidence in the Qur’an that they were reinforced on the day of Badr with a thousand angels, as He says: When you called upon your Lord, He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another’ (al-Anfal 8:9). As for the day of Uhud, the evidence that they were not reinforced is clearer than that they were reinforced. This is because if they had been reinforced, they would not have been defeated, nor would they have suffered what they suffered. So the correct thing to say about it is as God Almighty said. We have previously explained the meaning of supply, and the support, and the meaning of patience and piety. As for his saying:
h
They will come to you all at once
, the people of interpretation differed about it.
Some of them said: The meaning of his saying: from their place is from their place.
Who said that?

c: Humaid bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said,
m: And they will come to you from this place of theirs, he said: from this place of theirs.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: From their face, he said: From their face.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they will come to you all at once
, from this direction of theirs.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they will come to you all at once
, meaning: from this direction.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they will come to you all at once
, meaning: from this direction.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And they will come to you in this state of theirs, he said: from this state of theirs, and it is said - meaning on the authority of someone other than Ibn Abbas - rather it is: from this state of theirs.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: From this place of theirs, from this place of theirs.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: because of their anger.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they will come to you all at once
, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, he said: That was their all at once, it was on the day of Uhud, they were angry on the day of Badr because of what they encountered.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said, Sahl bin Amer told us, he said, Malik bin Mughol told us, he said:
m: I heard Abu Salih, the freed slave of Umm Hani’, say: From their anger, he said: From their anger.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And they will come upon you at this moment, he said: He became angry for them, meaning the infidels, so he did not fight them at that moment, and that was on the day of Uhud.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: From their anger, he said: From their anger.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And they will come to you in their immediate presence, meaning: in their faces and anger.

x: The root of the word for is to begin something and then connect it to something else. It is said: The pot boiled and furan if what was in it began to boil and then continued. I went to so-and-so immediately, meaning: from the direction I began. The one who said about this verse: The meaning of his saying: from this place of theirs, from this place of theirs, intended that its interpretation is: And Karz bin Jaber and his companions will come to you on the day of Badr from the beginning of their exit from which they came out to support their companions from the polytheists. As for those who said: The meaning of that is: from their anger - they meant that the interpretation of that is: And the infidels of Quraysh will come to you and follow you on the day of Uhud from the beginning of their anger that they were angry for their dead who were killed on the day of Badr, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand.
Therefore, due to the difference in their interpretation of the meaning of His statement:
h
And they will come to you all at once
, the people of interpretation differed regarding God’s provision of the believers with one of His angels.

Some of them said: They did not provide them with reinforcements because the believers did not have patience with their enemies and did not fear God, the Almighty, by abandoning the archers who abandoned the obedience of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in remaining in the place where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to remain. Rather, they permitted it to be done in order to seek spoils, so those Muslims who were killed were killed and the polytheists took from them what they took. God, the Almighty, had promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would provide them with reinforcements if they were patient and feared God. As for those who said: That was on the day of Badr because of Karz bin Jabir, some of them said: Karz and his companions did not come to their brothers from the polytheists to reinforce them at Badr, and God did not reinforce the believers with His angels.

Because God Almighty only promised them that He would reinforce them with His angels if Karz came to them and reinforced the polytheists immediately, and the reinforcements did not come to them. As for those who said: God Almighty supported the Muslims with angels on the day of Badr, they based their argument on the words of God Almighty: When you called upon your Lord, and He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another’ (al-Anfal 8:9). He said: So the thousand of them came to them as reinforcement. The promise was in which there were conditions, so what was more than a thousand, as for the thousand, they were supported by it, because God Almighty had promised them that, and God will not break His promise.
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: marked. The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: Masumin, with the opening of the waw, meaning that God has poisoned it.
Some of the people of Kufa and Basra read it as masmoomin with a kasra on the waw, meaning that the angels samt for themselves.

The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads with a kasra on the waw, because the reports from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of interpretation among them and the followers after them are clear: that the angels are the ones who branded themselves, without attributing their branding to God Almighty, or to anyone else among His creation. There is no meaning in the statement of those who said: He would have chosen the kasra in his saying marked, if it were for humans, but as for the angels, he described them differently, thinking that it is not possible for angels to mark themselves as humans can. This is because it is not impossible that God, the Almighty, enabled them to mark themselves in the same way that He enabled humans to mark themselves, so they marked themselves in the same way that humans were marked, seeking from them thereby the obedience of their Lord, so their marking themselves was attributed to them, even if that was due to God causing them to have causes.

And if it was described as marking itself out of its approach to its Lord, it would have been more eloquent in praising it, for choosing to obey God, than for it to be described as being done to. Mentioning the report with what we mentioned: from the addition of those who added marking to the angels, without adding that to others, in the manner we said about it.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Umair ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: The first time wool was on that day - meaning the day of Badr - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bid on it, for the angels have bid on it.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Mukhtar ibn Ghassan told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil told us, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn al-Mundhir, on the authority of his grandfather Abu Asid - and he was a Badri - he used to say:
m: If my eyesight were to improve, and you went with me to Uhud, I would tell you about the valley from which the angels emerged in yellow turbans which they had thrown between their shoulders.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Surat Al Imran 3:
m: 125 Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you in haste,
h
your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks
. Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
With five thousand marked angels
, he said: Marked, with the tails and forelocks of their horses cut off - in which there is wool or wool. And that is the marking.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
With five thousand marked angels
, he said, their tails are cut off, and their manes contain wool or wool, so that is the marking.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Marked, he told us that their mark on that day would be wool on the forelocks and tails of their horses, and that they would be on piebald horses.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: marked, he said: Its mark was wool on its forelocks.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that he used to say: Marked. He said: Their horses had their manes trimmed, and their forelocks and tails were marked with wool and wool.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: They were on piebald horses that day.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak and some of our sheikhs, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: similar to the hadith of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Marked, meaning taught.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
With five thousand angels marked
, for they came to Muhammad, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, marked with wool, so Muhammad and his companions marked themselves and their horses with wool according to their mark.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Hamza, he said:
m: The angels descended in the guise of Al-Zubayr, wearing yellow turbans. And Al-Zubayr’s turban was yellow.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: marked, he said: with wool on their forelocks and tails.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, he said:
m: The angels descended on the day of Badr on piebald horses, wearing yellow turbans. Al-Zubayr was wearing a yellow turban that day.

c: Ahmad bin Yahya al-Sufi told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Sharik told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of Urwa, on the authority of Abdullah bin al-Zubayr:
m: Al-Zubayr was wearing a yellow sheet on the day of Badr, so he wrapped himself in it, so the angels descended on the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, wrapping himself in yellow turbans.

x: These narrations, some of which we have mentioned, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to his companions: ‘Mark, for the angels have marked,’” and the statement of Abu Usaid: The angels came out in yellow turbans that they had thrown between their shoulders, and the statement of those among them who said: Marked, marking, all of that indicates the correctness of what we have chosen from the reading in that, and that the marking was from the angels themselves, in the manner that we said about that previously.
As for those who read it: poisoned, I think they interpreted it as:

c: Humayd bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
With five thousand marked angels
, he said: They have the mark of battle on them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
With five thousand marked angels
, he says: They have the mark of battle, and that was on the day of Badr, God supported them
h
with five thousand marked angels

. He says: They have the mark of battle. They said: The mark of the battle was upon them, not that they were branded with a mark, so branding is attributed to them. For that reason, they read them as branded, meaning that God Almighty attributed branding to those who branded them with that mark. The mark is the sign. It is said: It is a beautiful mark, or a beautiful appearance, as the poet said: A young man whom God has blessed with beauty, with a features that are not difficult for the eye to see. He means by this: a sign of goodness. So if a man is informed of a sign by which he is known in war or otherwise, it is said: He has marked himself, so he marks himself with a mark.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: marked.
The majority of the people of Medina and Kufa read it as: Masumin, with the opening of the waw, meaning that God has poisoned it.
Some of the people of Kufa and Basra read it as masmoomin with a kasra on the waw, meaning that the angels samt for themselves.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads with a kasra on the waw, because the reports from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of interpretation among them and the followers after them are clear: that the angels are the ones who branded themselves, without attributing their branding to God Almighty, or to anyone else among His creation.

Abu Jaʿfar said: These narrations, some of which we have mentioned, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to his companions: ‘Mark, for the angels have marked,’” and the statement of Abu Usaid: The angels came out in yellow turbans that they had thrown between their shoulders, and the statement of those among them who said: Marked, marking, all of that indicates the correctness of what we have chosen from the reading in that, and that the marking was from the angels themselves, in the manner that we said about that previously.
As for those who read it: poisoned, I think they interpreted it as:
For that reason, they read them as branded, meaning that God Almighty attributed branding to those who branded them with that mark.

x: He, the Most High, means: And God did not make His promise to you what He promised you of His support for you with the angels whose number He mentioned, except as good tidings for you, meaning good tidings, with which He gives you good tidings, and that your hearts may be reassured thereby, meaning: And so that your hearts may be reassured by His promise that He promised you, so that they may be at peace with Him, and not be alarmed by the great number of your enemy or the small number of you, and victory is only from God, meaning: And your victory, if you are victorious over your enemy, is only by the help of God, not by the support that comes to you from the angels. He says: So put your trust in God, and seek help from Him, not by the multitudes and the great number, for if your victory is only by God and His help, and with you from His angels five thousand, then it is more likely that it will be by the help of God and His strengthening you against your enemy, because there are large multitudes of people with you.
So fear God and be patient in the struggle against your enemy, for God will support you against them, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And God did not make them except as good tidings for you, meaning that He only made them so that you would be glad of them and feel reassured by them, and they did not fight with them on that day - meaning the day of Uhud - Mujahid said: And they did not fight with them on that day, nor before it, nor after it, except on the day of Badr.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God did not make it except as good tidings for you and that your hearts might be reassured thereby, because I know of your weakness, and victory is only from Me by My authority and power, and that is because glory and judgment belong to Me, not to any of My creation.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And victory comes only from God, if He had wanted to help you with other than the angels, He would have done so, the Almighty, the Wise. As for the meaning of His statement: The Mighty, the Wise, He, may His praise be glorified, is: The Mighty in His vengeance against the disbelievers through the hands of His allies from among the people of His obedience, the Wise in His management of you, O believers, against your enemies from among the people of disbelief, and other than that of His affairs. He says: So be glad, O believers, with My management of you against your enemies and My victory for you over them, if you obey Me in what I have commanded you, and are patient in the struggle against My enemy and your enemy.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant: And God gave you victory at Badr
h
to cut off a portion of those who disbelieved

, and by a portion He meant the group or the individuals. God Almighty says: And God had already given you victory at Badr, in order to destroy a group of those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger, and denied the Oneness of their Lord, and the prophethood of their Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved
, so God cut off a portion of the disbelievers on the day of Badr, and killed their leaders, chiefs, and leaders in evil.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved
, the entire verse, he said: This was the day of Badr, God cut off a group of them and a group remained.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved
, meaning: To cut off a portion of the polytheists by killing them in order to take revenge on them.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Victory comes only from God,
h
to cut off a portion of those who disbelieved
. He said: He only meant by that those who were killed at Uhud.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: God mentioned the dead polytheists - meaning at Uhud - and they were eighteen men, and He said:
h
To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved
. Then He mentioned the martyrs and said: And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead
r
(Al Imran 3:169)

. As for His statement: or He subdues them, He means by that: or He disgraces them with disappointment in what they had hoped for of victory over you. It has been said that the meaning of his saying: or He suppresses them is or He knocks them down on their faces.

x: Some of them mentioned that he heard the Arabs say: God suppressed him on his face, meaning God knocked him down.

The interpretation of the statement: “And indeed God gave you victory at Badr to destroy a group of the infidels with the sword, and to disgrace them with their disappointment in what they had hoped for of victory, ‘so they would return disappointed,’” means: so they would return from you disappointed, having not attained from you anything that they had hoped to attain from you, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Or He suppresses them and they return disappointed, or He returns them disappointed, meaning: whoever remains of them returns disappointed, they did not attain anything of what they had hoped for.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Or He will subdue them, meaning: He will disgrace them, so they will return disappointed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

x: By that, the Most High means: To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved, or to suppress them, or to accept their repentance, or to punish them, for they are wrongdoers. You have no say in the matter. So His statement, And accept your repentance, is in the accusative case, in apposition to His statement, or to suppress them. It may be possible that its interpretation is: You have no say in the matter until He forgives them, so the accusative of repents is in the sense of or which is in the sense of until.

The first statement is more correct, because nothing of the creation’s affairs is up to anyone except their Creator, before the repentance of the infidels and their punishment and after that. The interpretation of his saying:
h
You have no part in the matter

, is that you, O Muhammad, have no part in the matter of My creation except that you carry out My command in them, and that you obey Me in them. Their matter is only in My hands, and the judgment in them is in My hand, and no one else’s.

I judge and rule in them as I will, from repentance for whoever disbelieved in Me, disobeyed Me, and opposed My command, or punishment, either in this worldly life with killing and devastating punishments, or in the Hereafter with what I have prepared for the people of disbelief in Me, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then he said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “You have no control over My servants, except what I have commanded you to do with them, or I will turn to them with My mercy, so if you wish I will do so, or I will punish them for their sins, “for they are wrongdoers,” meaning they deserved that by disobeying Me. He mentioned that God Almighty revealed this verse to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because when he was afflicted with what the polytheists afflicted him with, he said, as if they had lost hope of guidance or of turning to the truth: How can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet!!

x: Who said that?

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Humayd told us, Anas said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Uhud, and his front tooth was broken and he was wounded, so he began wiping the blood from his face and saying: How can a people succeed when they have stained their Prophet with blood while he is calling them to their Lord! Then the verse was revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Yaqoub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hamid al-Tawil, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Hamid Al-Tawil, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he was wounded in the forehead and his front tooth was broken: A people who did this to their Prophet will not succeed!! So God revealed to him:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: Yaqub told me, on the authority of Ibn Ulayyah, who said: Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of UHud 11:How can a people succeed when they have caused blood to flow from the face of their Prophet while he was calling them to God Almighty! Then this verse was revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: Yaqub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar to that.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You have no part in the matter

, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. He mentioned to us that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded in the face and some of his front teeth were injured. Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, was washing the blood from his face and said: How can a people succeed when they have stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he is calling them to their Lord! So God Almighty revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was injured on the day of Uhud, and his front tooth was broken and his eyebrow was parted. He fell down wearing two coats of mail, and blood was flowing. Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, passed by him, sat him down, and wiped his face. He regained consciousness and said: What about people who did this to their Prophet while he was calling them to God? Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement:
h
You have no part in the matter

the verse. Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been wounded in the face and his front tooth had been injured. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to supplicate against them, but he said: “How can a people succeed when they have blackened the face of their best friend while he calls them to God and they call him to Satan, and he calls them to guidance and they call him to misguidance, and he calls them to Paradise and they call him to Hellfire.” He wanted to supplicate against them, but God Almighty revealed: “
h
You have no part in the matter
. Either He turns to them in forgiveness or He punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refrained from supplicating against them.

c: Muhammad ibn Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You have no part in the matter

, or He may forgive them, the entire verse, he said: Abu Sufyan came from the year angry at what he had done to his companions on the day of Badr, so he fought the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud fiercely, until he killed as many of them as were captured on the day of Badr, “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said a word that God knew was mixed with anger: How can a people succeed who have stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he was calling them to Islam?” Then God Almighty said:
h
You have no part in the matter
, or He may forgive them or punish them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Prophet’s front tooth was injured on the day of Uhud. It was injured by Utbah bin Abi Waqqas, and he cut it in the face. Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, was washing the blood from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was saying: How can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “
h
You have no part in the matter
. Whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri and on the authority of Uthman al-Jazari,
m: on Surat Al Imran 3:128 You have no control over the matter. Either He forgives them or punishes them, for indeed, they are wrongdoers. the authority of Muqsim: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against Utbah bin Abi Waqqas on the day of Uhud, when his front tooth was broken and his face was wounded, and he said: O God, do not let a year pass over him until he dies as an unbeliever! He said: So a year did not pass over him until he died as an unbeliever.
b.via: al-Zuhri and on the authority of Uthman al-Jazari

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was wounded in the parting of his eyebrow and his front tooth was broken. Ibn Jurayj said: It was mentioned to us that when he was wounded, Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifa, began to wash the blood from his face, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “was saying: How can a people succeed when they have stained the face of their Prophet with blood while he is calling them to God!” Then God Almighty revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he called down curses on a people, so God Almighty revealed: The matter is not up to you regarding them.
The novel mentioned that:

c: Yahya bin Habib bin Arabi told me, he said, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ajlan told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying against four men, so God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. He said: And God guided them to Islam.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib Salim bin Junadah told me, he said, Ahmad bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Umar bin Hamza, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, curse Abu Sufyan! O God, curse Al-Harith bin Hisham! O God, curse Safwan bin Umayya.” So the following was revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.

c: Mujahid bin Musa narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Abd God bin Ayyash bin Abi Rabia, on the authority of Abd God bin Kaab, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Hisham, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, and when he raised his head from the second rak’ah, he said: O God, save Ayyash bin Abi Rabia, Salamah bin Hisham, and al-Walid bin al-Walid! O God, save the weak among the Muslims! O God, intensify your oppression on Mudar! O God, years like the years of the family of Joseph! Then God revealed:
h
You have no part in the matter
, or He will forgive them al-Baqarah 2:17.
b.via: Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Hisham

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus ibn Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab,
m: he told him, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman: that they heard Abu Hurayrah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when he finished reciting the Fajr prayer, and he would say, ‘God hears those who praise Him, our Lord, to You is praise.’ Then he would say while standing: ‘O God, save al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, and the oppressed among the believers! O God, intensify Your punishment upon Mudar, and make it like the years of Joseph upon them! O God, curse Lihyan, Raʿl, Dhakwan, and ʿAsiyah who disobeyed God and His Messenger.’ Then we were informed that he stopped doing that when the verse was revealed: ‘
h
You have no part in the matter
, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.’”

x: By that, the Most High means: You, O Muhammad, have no control over the matter, and God owns everything between the regions of the heavens and the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting, apart from you and them. He rules over them as He wills, and decrees over them as He loves. He accepts the repentance of whomever He loves from among His creation who disobeys His command and prohibition, then forgives him, and punishes whomever He wills from among them for his crime and takes revenge on him. He is the Forgiving One who conceals the sins of whomever He loves to conceal from among His creation his sins by His grace upon them through pardon and forgiveness, and the Merciful One with them in leaving their punishment immediately despite the greatness of what they will do from the Qa’im, as Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning He forgives sins and has mercy on the servants, regardless of what is in them.
By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: O you who believe in God and His Messenger,
h
do not consume usury

in your Islam after He has guided you to it, as you used to consume it in your ignorance. And their eating of that in their ignorance was: a man among them would have money owed to another man until a term came, and when the term came he would ask his friend for it, and the one who owed the money would say to him: Delay your debt from me and I will give you more of your money, and they would do that: and that is usury, multiplied and multiplied, so God Almighty forbade them from it in their Islam, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Sinan told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Thaqif used to borrow from Banu al-Mughira in the pre-Islamic era, and when the due date came, they would say: Shall we give you more and you delay? So the verse was revealed: And
h
do not consume usury
, doubled and multiplied.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: O you who have believed,
h
do not consume usury
, doubled and multiplied, meaning: Do not eat in Islam, since God has guided you to it, what you used to eat when you were not upon it, which is not permissible for you in your religion.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: O you who have believed,
h
do not consume usury
, doubled and multiplied, he said: The usury of the Age of Ignorance.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say about His statement,
h
Do not consume usury

, doubled and multiplied, he said: My father used to say, “Usury in the pre-Islamic era was only in doubling and in age. A man would have an extra debt, so when the due date came, he would come to him and say, ‘Will you pay me or give me more?’ If he had something to pay it, he would pay it, otherwise he would transfer it to the next year. If it was a young female camel, he would make it a two-year-old female camel, then a one-year-old female camel, then a three-year-old female camel, then a four-year-old female camel, then so on up. And in the ‘ayn, he would come to him. If he did not have anything, he would double it the following year. If he did not have anything, he would add it still, so it would be one hundred, and he would make it two hundred the following year. If he did not have anything, he would make it four hundred, doubling it for him every year or paying it off. He said: So this is His statement, “
h
Do not consume usury

, doubled and multiplied.” As for His statement: And fear God that you may be successful, it means: And fear God, O believers, in the matter of usury, so do not eat it, and in other matters that He has commanded you to do or forbidden you from, and obey Him in them, that you may be successful, meaning: so that you may succeed and be saved from His punishment, and attain what He has desired of you of His reward and eternity in His Paradise, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And fear God that you may succeed, meaning: Obey God that you may be saved from what He has warned you of of His punishment, and attain what He has desired of you of His reward.

x: God Almighty says to the believers: And fear, O believers, the Fire that you may enter by consuming usury after I have forbidden you from it, which I have prepared for those who disbelieve in Me, so that you enter their place after your belief in Me, by disobeying My command and abandoning My obedience, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers, which has been made a home for those who disbelieve in Me.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Obey God, O believers, in what He has forbidden you from, such as eating usury and other things, and in what the Messenger has commanded you to do. He says: And obey the Messenger also in this way, that you may receive mercy, meaning: so that you may receive mercy and not be punished. It has been said that this was a rebuke from God Almighty to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who disobeyed his command on the day of Uhud, and thus neglected the positions they were ordered to remain in.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And obey God and the Messenger that you may receive mercy, as a rebuke to those who disobeyed His Messenger when he ordered them to do what he ordered them to do on that day and on other days - meaning: on the day of Uhud.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying: And hasten, and hasten and race, to forgiveness from your Lord, meaning: to what conceals your sins from His mercy, and what covers them from His pardon for your punishment for them,
h
and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth

, meaning: And hasten also to a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth. It was mentioned that the meaning of this is: A paradise whose width is like the width of the seven heavens and the seven earths, if some of them are combined with others.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And a Paradise whose width is that of the heavens and the earth, he said: Ibn Abbas said: The seven heavens and the seven earths are joined together, just as clothes are joined together, so that is the width of Paradise. Rather, it was said: And a garden as wide as the heavens and the earth, so its width was described as the heavens and the earths, and the meaning is what we described: describing its width as the width of the heavens and the earth, likening it to it in spaciousness and greatness, as it was said: He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul
r
(Luqman 31:28)

, meaning: except as the resurrection of a single soul, and as the poet said: As if their excuse is in the south of the ostrich's nest in a barren land Meaning: an ostrich’s excuse, and as the other said: I thought my camel's embrace was an embrace! But it is not an embrace, except for you Wants: Hug sound.

x: It was mentioned that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: ‘This Paradise is as wide as the heavens and the earth, so where is Hell?’ He said: ‘This is the day when it comes, where is the night?’”
Mentioning the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muslim bin Khalid told me, on the authority of Ibn Khathim, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Yaʿla bin Murrah, he said:
m: I met Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Homs, an old man who had been refuted. He said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, and he handed the paper to a man on his left. I said: Who is your companion who is reading? They said: Muʿawiyah. Then my companion’s letter was: You have written inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth,
h
prepared for the righteous
. So where is the Fire? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! So where is the night when the day comes?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab:
m: Some Jews asked Umar bin al-Khattab about Paradise, the width of which is the heavens and the earth. Where is Hell? He said: Have you seen when night comes, where is the day? They said: O God, you have taken something like it from the Torah!

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab:
m: Three men from Najran came to ʿUmar and asked him while his companions were with him. They said: What do you think of His statement:
h
And a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth

, so where is the fire? The people hesitated, so ʿUmar said: What do you think, when night comes, where is the day? And when day comes, where is the night? They said: Something similar was taken from the Torah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim Ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Tariq Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Umar,
m: something similar to it regarding the three men who came to Umar and asked him: About a Paradise whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, similar to the hadith of Qays Ibn Muslim. Mujahid bin Musa narrated, Jaafar bin Awn narrated, Al-A'mash narrated, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: A Jewish man came to Umar and said: You say, Paradise is as wide as the heavens and the earth. Where is Hell? Umar said to him: Have you seen when the day comes, where is the night? Have you seen when the night comes, where is the day? He said: It is like it in the Torah. His companion said to him: Why did you tell him? His companion said to him: Leave him, for he is certain of everything.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Jaafar bin Burqan told us, he said, Yazid bin Al-Asamm told us:
m: A man from the People of the Book Surat Al Imran 3:133 And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth,
h
prepared for the righteous

. came to Ibn Abbas and said: You say, Paradise is as wide as the heavens and the earth, but where is Hell? Ibn Abbas said: Have you seen when the night comes, where is the day? And when the day comes, where is the night?

x: As for his saying:
h
Prepared for the righteous
, it means: Paradise, whose width is like the width of the seven heavens and earths, God has
h
prepared for the righteous
, those who feared God and obeyed Him in what He commanded and forbade them, so they did not transgress His limits, and did not fall short in the duty of His right upon them, so as to waste it, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth,
h
prepared for the righteous
, meaning: a home for whoever obeys me and obeys my Messenger.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying:
h
Those who spend in prosperity and adversity

, is that Paradise, the width of which is the heavens and the earth, has been prepared for the righteous, and they are those who spend their wealth in the way of God, either by spending it on someone in need, or by strengthening someone who is weak to rise up for his jihad in the way of God. As for his saying: in prosperity, he means: in a state of happiness, with abundant money and comfortable living. Siraa is a noun derived from the word Siraa which means: This matter pleased me greatly. "Ad-Daraa" is a noun derived from the saying: "So-and-so has been harmed, so he is harming", if harm befalls him, and that is if he is afflicted with distress and difficulty in his life.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who spend in prosperity and adversity

, meaning: in hardship and ease. So He, the Most High, informed us that the Paradise whose description He described is for those who fear Him and spend their money in His cause, in times of ease and abundance, and in times of hardship and difficulty. His saying:
h
And those who restrain anger

, means: And those who suppress anger when their souls are filled with it. It is said: So-and-so swallowed his anger, meaning he swallowed it, and preserved himself from doing what he was capable of doing, by empowering himself against the one who angered him, and by taking revenge against the one who wronged him. The origin of this comes from the word kazum al-qurbah, which means to fill the water skin with water. Someone is kazeem or makzoom, meaning he is filled with grief and sadness. From this comes the saying of God the Almighty: And his eyes became white from grief, so he was kazeem
r
(Yusuf 12:84)

, meaning: filled with grief. From this comes the word kaza’im, meaning filled with grief, for the watercourses are called kaza’im, because they are filled with water. From this comes the word took hold of his hold, meaning: the watercourses of his soul. Anger is a noun derived from the saying: So-and-so angered me, so he angers me with anger, meaning that he made him angry and upset him. As for his saying:
h
And those who pardon people
, he means:
h
And those who pardon people
, the punishment of their sins is upon them, and they are able to take revenge on them, so they leave it to them. As for his saying:
h
And God loves the doers of good

, it means: God loves the one who does these things for which He described that He has prepared for those who do them Paradise, the breadth of which is the heavens and the earth, and the ones who do them are the doers of good, and their goodness is their doing them, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
Those who spend in prosperity and adversity
the verse, and pardon the people -
h
and God loves the doers of good
, meaning: and that is goodness, and I love whoever does it.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Those who spend in ease and hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people -
h
and God loves the doers of good

. People who spent in hardship and ease, in difficulty and in prosperity. So whoever is able to overcome evil with good, let him do so, and there is no power except with God. So, by God, O son of Adam, you are drinking a sip of patience while you are angry and you are wronged.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman told me, he said, Muhammad bin Bishr told us, he said, Mahraz Abu Raja told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It will be said on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Let whoever has a reward from God stand. No one will stand except a person who has pardoned. Then he recited this verse: And those who pardon the people -
h
and God loves the doers of good

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Dawud bin Qais told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of a man from the people of Ash-Sham called Abd al-Jalil, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who restrain anger
: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever restrains anger when he is able to give vent to it, God will fill him with security and faith.”

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who restrain anger to And God loves the doers of good
. So those who restrain anger is like His statement: And when they become angry, they forgive (al-Shura Surat Al Imran 3:134
h
Those who spend in prosperity and adversity
, who restrain anger and pardon the people -
h
and God loves the doers of good

. 42:37). They become angry about a matter that if they had committed it, it would have been forbidden, so they forgive and pardon, seeking thereby the face of God. And those who pardon the people is like His statement: And let not those among you who are endowed with bounty and wealth swear to Do you not love that God should forgive you? (al-Nur 24:22). He says: Do not swear that you will not give them anything from the expenses, but pardon and overlook.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: And those who pardon the people - and God loves the doers of good.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And those who
, when they commit an immorality, is that the Paradise whose description He described is prepared for the righteous, those who spend in prosperity and adversity,
h
and those who
, when they commit an immorality.
And all of these attributes are from the description of the righteous, about whom the Most High said: And a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous, as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Jaʿfar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, he said:
m: I heard al-Hasan recite this verse: Those who spend during ease and hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people - and God loves the doers of good. Then he recited:
h
And those who
, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins to the reward of the workers. He said: These two descriptions describe one man.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And those who

, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, he said: These are two sins, immorality is a sin, and wronging themselves is a sin. As for indecency, it is a description of something abandoned, and the meaning of the words is:
h
And those who

, when they commit an indecency act. The meaning of obscenity is an ugly act that goes beyond what God Almighty has permitted. The root of obscenity is ugliness and going beyond the limit and measure in everything. From this, it is said of a tall person who is excessively tall: he is obscenely tall, meaning: ugly in height, going beyond the acceptable measure. From this, it is said of ugly speech that is not intended: obscene speech, and it is said of the speaker: he is obscene in his speech, if he utters obscenities. It was said: The obscenity in this context means adultery.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Abbas bin Abdul-Azim told us, he said, Habban told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Jabir:
m: h
And those who
, when they commit an immorality, he said: The people commit adultery, by the Lord of the Kaaba.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And those who

, when they commit an immorality, as for immorality, it is adultery. His statement: or wronged themselves, means: they did to themselves something other than what they should have done to them. What they did of that was committing a sin against God that made them incur His punishment, such as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who
, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, he said: Injustice comes from immorality, and immorality comes from injustice. And His saying:
h
They remembered God
, meaning by that:
h
They remembered God
’s threat for what they had committed of disobeying Him, and sought forgiveness for their sins, meaning: They asked their Lord to cover their sins by pardoning them from punishment for them,
h
and who forgives sins except God

, meaning: Who forgives sins - that is, pardons the one who commits them and covers them for him - except God, and they did not persist in what they had done, meaning: They did not persist in their sins that they had committed, and their disobedience that they had committed, while they knew, meaning: They did not persist in their sins, intending to persist in them, while they knew that God had previously prohibited them and threatened punishment for those who committed them. He mentioned that this verse was revealed specifically for our nation, in order to make it easy and light, because of the great affliction that the Children of Israel were being tested with due to their sins.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: “On the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah: They said: O Prophet of God, the Children of Israel are more honorable to God than us! Whenever one of them sinned, the expiation for his sin would be written on the threshold of his door: Cut off your ear, cut off your nose, do it! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, then this verse was revealed: “And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous” until His saying:
h
And those who

, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you of something better than that? So he recited these verses.” Surat Al Imran 3:135
h
And those who

, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except God - and do not persist in what they have done while they know.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Omar bin Abi Khalifa Al-Abdi told us, Ali bin Zaid bin Jadaan told us: Ibn Masoud said:
m: When the Children of Israel sinned, the sin and its expiation were written on its door in the morning, so we were given something better than that, this verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Jaafar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, who said:
m: When the verse, And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, was revealed, Iblis wept in fear of this verse.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Jaʿfar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, he said:
m: It has reached me that when this verse was revealed:
h
And those who
, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, Iblis wept.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard ʿUthman, the client of the family of Abu ʿAqil al-Thaqafi, he said: I heard ʿAli ibn Rabiʿah narrating, on the authority of a man from Fazarah called Asmaʿ - and: Ibn Asmaʿ - on the authority of ʿAli, he said: Whenever I heard something from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with whatever He willed to benefit me [from it].

c: Abu Bakr narrated to me
m: - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no servant - Shuʿbah said: and I think he said: a Muslim - who commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays two rakʿahs, then seeks God’s forgiveness for that sin [but that He will forgive him].” Shuʿbah said: And he recited one of these two verses: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it
r
(An-Nisaʿ: 123)
h
And those who

, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, my father narrated, and Al-Fadl ibn Ishaq narrated, Wakee’ narrated, on the authority of Misa’ar and Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn Al-Mughirah Al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi’ah Al-Walibi, on the authority of Asma’ ibn Al-Hakam Al-Fazari, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: Whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me from it as He willed.

c: And if someone else narrated it to me,
m: I would make him swear, and if he swore to me, I would believe him.

c: Abu Bakr narrated to me,
m: and Abu Bakr spoke the truth, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no man who commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays - one of them said: two rak’ahs, and the other said: then prays - and seeks God’s forgiveness, but that He will forgive him. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated, Saʿd ibn Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿid al-Maqburi narrated, on the authority of his brother, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, who said:

c: No one narrated to me from the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, except that I asked him to swear to me by God that he had heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except Abu Bakr, for he never lied. ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, said:

c: Abu Bakr narrated to me that
m: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no servant who commits a sin, then stands up when his sin is mentioned, performs ablution, then prays two rakʿahs, and seeks God’s forgiveness for that sin, except that God forgives him. As for his saying:
h
They remembered God and sought forgiveness for their sins
, its interpretation is as we have explained. In a similar way, the interpreters used to say:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us:
m: h
And those who

, when they commit an immorality, meaning: if they commit an immorality, or wrong themselves, by disobeying God, remember God’s prohibition of it, and what God has forbidden them, so they seek forgiveness for it,
h
and they know
that no one forgives sins except Him. As for his statement:
h
And who forgives sins except God

?, the name God is raised and there is no negation before it. Rather, what comes after except is raised by following what comes before it if it is indefinite and accompanied by a negation, like the saying of the one who says: There is no one in the house except your brother.

x: But if it is said: The people stood up except your father, then the way of speaking about the father is the accusative. And from its connection in his statement:
h
And who forgives sins except God

, it is definite. For that came in the nominative case because the meaning of the statement is: Does anyone forgive sins? Or: No one forgives sins except God. So what comes after except of [the name] God is raised based on the interpretation of the statement, not based on its wording. As for his saying:
h
And they did not persist in what they did while they knew
, the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of persistence and the meaning of this word.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: They did not persist in the sins they committed and did not persist in them, but they repented and sought forgiveness, as God described them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they did not persist in what they did while they knew

, so beware of persistence, for only those who persist are destroyed, those who go forward, not being prevented by the fear of God from doing something forbidden by God, and not repenting from a sin they committed, until death comes to them while they are still doing that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they did not persist in what they did while they knew
, he said: They went on and on in disobeying God!! The fear of God did not stop them, until God’s command came to them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And they did not persist in what they did while they knew
, meaning: they did not persist in disobeying Me, as one who associates partners with Me does, in what they did of disbelief in Me.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They did not commit the sin if they intended to do so.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they did not persist in what they did
, he said: The servant committing a sin is persistence, until he repents.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And they did not persist in what they did
, he said: They did not have intercourse.

x: Others said: The meaning of persistence is to remain silent about the sin and not seek forgiveness.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they did not persist in what they did while they knew
. As for persist, they are silent and do not seek forgiveness.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in our view, is the saying of those who say: Persistence is intentionally continuing in the sin and not repenting from it. There is no meaning to the saying of those who say: Persistence in the sin is committing it, because God the Almighty praised the perpetrators of the sin for not persisting in the sin, as He said: “
h
And those who

, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except God - and do not persist in what they have done while they know.” If the perpetrator of the sin persisted in committing it, then there would be no clear reason for seeking forgiveness, because seeking forgiveness for a sin is only repentance from it and regret, and there is no known reason for seeking forgiveness for a sin that its perpetrator has not committed.
It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he does it seventy times a day.

c: Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Sabi’i told me that, he said: Abdul Hamid Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Waqid, on the authority of Abu Nasirah, on the authority of a freed slave of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace. If the one who commits the sin was persistent, then his statement,
h
He who seeks forgiveness is not persistent

, even if he returns seventy times a day, would have no meaning. Because if committing the sin is persistence, then the name that is attached to it does not remove the meaning of another one, just as the name fornicator is not removed from the adulterer and the name killer from the murderer, his repentance from it, nor any other meaning. This report has shown that the one who seeks forgiveness for his sin is not persistent in it, so it is known from this that persistence is not committing, and that it is the persistence in it, as we said before. The commentators differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
And they know

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
And they know
that they have sinned.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for
h
and they know
, they know that they have sinned, then they stood up and did not seek forgiveness.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They know that what they did was a sin against God.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And they know
, he said: They know what I have forbidden them of worshipping other than Me.

x: Our explanation has already been presented, which is more correct.

evidence.text: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Jaʿfar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, he said: I heard al-Hasan recite this verse: Those who spend during ease and hardship, and who restrain anger and pardon the people - and God loves the doers of good.
So he recited these verses.”

x: God Almighty means by His saying: Those, those for whom He mentioned that He has prepared Paradise, the width of which is the heavens and the earth, from among the righteous, and He described them with what He described them with. Then He said: Those who have this description, their reward, meaning: their reward for their deeds that God Almighty described them to have done, is forgiveness from their Lord, meaning: pardon for them from God for their punishment for their past sins, and for them for what they obeyed God in of their good deeds, gardens, meaning orchards, underneath which rivers flow, meaning: rivers flow through its trees and in its lower parts, as a reward for them for their good deeds, abiding therein meaning: permanent residence in these gardens that He described, and excellent is the reward of the workers, meaning: excellent is the reward of the workers for God, the gardens that He described, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And excellent is the reward of the workers,” meaning the reward of the obedient.

x: What is meant by the words of God Almighty:
h
There have already been precedents before you

, is that they have passed and preceded from Me with those who were before you, O group of companions of Muhammad and people of faith in him, such as the people of ʿAd and Thamud and the people of Hud and the people of Lot, and others from the ancestors of the nations before you. Reflectives means: examples that I followed with them and with those who denied Him from among their prophets who were sent to them, by giving respite to those who denied them, and by My leading them on, until the Book reached its term that I had set for the victory of their prophets and people of faith in them over them. Then I brought down My punishment upon them, and sent down My vengeance upon their courtyards, and left them as examples and lessons for those after them. So travel through the land and see how was the end of the deniers, meaning: So travel - O you who think - that My leading on those I led from among the polytheists on the day of Uhud over Muhammad and his companions was not due to My leading on those who associated partners with Me and disbelieved in My messengers.

And My command was disobeyed - in the lands of the nations who were before you, from those who were like those who denied My Messenger and rejected My Oneness. So look at what was the end of their disbelief in My Prophets, and what happened to them after their disobedience to My command and their denial of My Oneness. Then learn from that that My victory over those I gave victory to from the polytheists over My Prophet Muhammad and his companions with Uhud, is only a luring and a respite so that the Book may reach its appointed time which I have set for them. Then either their condition will end up like that which happened to the nations who came before them: of the punishment being hastened upon them, or they will turn to My obedience and following My Messenger. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
There have already been precedents before you

, so travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied, he said: Did you not travel through the land and see how God punished the people of Noah, the people of Lot, the people of Salih, and the nations that God Almighty punished?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There have already been precedents before you
, he said: regarding the infidels and the believers, and the good and the evil.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: There have been precedents before you, concerning the believers and the unbelievers.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: He addressed the mention of the calamity that befell them - meaning the Muslims on the day of Uhud - and the affliction that had befallen them, and the examination of what was in them, and His taking of martyrs from among them, and said, as a consolation to them and informing them of what they had done and what He would do to them:
h
There have already been precedents before you

, so travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied. That is, events have already occurred from Me as punishment for the people who denied My messengers and associated partners with Me: Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the people of Midian. So travel through the land and you will see examples that have occurred in them, and for whoever was like them in that from Me, and if I grant them respite, that is, so that you do not think that My punishment has ceased from your enemy and My enemy, for the state that I have shown you, I will test you with that, so that I may know what is in you.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There have already been precedents before you
, so travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied, meaning: He gave them enjoyment in this world for a little while, then sent them to the Fire.

x: As for the Sunnah, it is the plural of Sunnah, and Sunnah is the example that is followed and the imam that is followed. It is said: So-and-so established a good tradition among us, and established a bad tradition, if he did an action that was followed for, whether good or bad. From this is the saying of Labid bin Rabiʿah: From a group whose fathers have set a precedent for them, and every people has a precedent and its leader And the saying of Sulayman bin Qatta: The Hashemites who were in Karbala felt sorry for each other, so it is a good example for the noble to feel sorry for each other.
Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: There have already been examples before you, he said: Examples.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning indicated by this.
Some of them said: What he meant by his saying, this, is the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
This is an explanation for the people and guidance and instruction for the righteous
, he said: This is the Qur’an.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
This is an explanation for the people
, which is this Qur’an. God made it an explanation for the people in general, and guidance and advice for the righteous in particular.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said,
m: in his statement:
h
This is a statement for the people and guidance and instruction for the righteous
, in particular.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
This is a statement for the people and guidance and instruction for the righteous
, in particular.

x: Others said: What he referred to by his saying: This is his saying: There have already been precedents before you, so travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied. Then he said: This that I have made known to you, O group of companions of Muhammad, is a clarification for the people.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: that.

x: The more correct of the two opinions in this regard, in my opinion, is the opinion of those who say: His statement, this, is an allusion to what preceded this verse of God’s reminder to the believers, His informing them of His limits, and His urging them to adhere to His obedience and to be patient in the struggle against His enemies and their enemies. Because His statement, this, is an allusion to something present: either seen or heard, and in this instance it is referring to something present and heard from the previous verses. The meaning of the statement: This which I have explained to you and made known to you is an explanation for the people.
By explanation, I mean explanation and interpretation, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: h
This is an explanation for the people
, meaning: This is an interpretation for the people if they accept it.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim and Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: This is a statement for the people, he said: from blindness.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: similarly. As for his saying: and guidance and admonition, he means by guidance, the indication of the path of truth and the method of religion, and by admonition, the reminder of what is right and correct, as:

c: Ahmad bin Hazim and Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Naim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: And guidance, he said: from misguidance, and admonition, from ignorance.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: similarly.
