c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: For the righteous, meaning: for those who obey me and know my command.

x: This is from God Almighty, as a consolation to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the wounds and killing they suffered at Uhud. He said: Do not weaken and do not grieve, O companions of Muhammad, meaning, do not be weakened by what your enemy has done to you, whether by killing or wounds, from jihad and war against your enemy. From the saying: So-and-so is weak in this matter, so he will be weak and feeble. And do not grieve, and do not feel sad or anxious about the calamity that befalls you on that day, for you will be the superior ones, meaning: the ones who are victorious over them, and you will have the final victory and triumph over them, if you are believers, meaning: if you believe in my Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he promises you, and in what he informs you of the report about what will happen to you and their situation, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said:
m: Killing and wounding increased among the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, until every man among them was affected by the pain. Then God Almighty revealed the Qur’an, in which He comforted the believers in the best way He comforted a group of Muslims who were before them from the past nations, saying:
h
And do not weaken and do not grieve
, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers, until His saying: Those upon whom death was decreed will come forth to their deathbeds.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not weaken and do not grieve

, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers, he consoles the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as you hear, and urges them to fight their enemy, and forbids them from weakness and infirmity in pursuing their enemy in the way of God.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not weaken and do not grieve
, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers, he said: He commands Muhammad, saying: And do not weaken, to proceed in the way of God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty: And do not weaken, and do not become weak.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not weaken and do not grieve
, he said: And do not become weak.

c: Al-Qasim told me, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And do not weaken, Ibn Jurayj said: And do not be weak in the matter of your enemy, And do not grieve while you are superior, he said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were defeated in the ravine, and they said: What happened to so-and-so? What happened to so-and-so? So they mourned each other, and said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed, and they were in a state of worry and grief. While they were like that, Khalid bin Al-Walid climbed the mountain with the cavalry of the polytheists above them, while they were lower in the ravine. When they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they rejoiced, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, we have no strength except through You, and none worship You in this town except these people! He said: A group of Muslim archers jumped up, climbed up and shot at the cavalry of the polytheists until God defeated them, and the Muslims climbed the mountain. That is what He said: And you are superior if you are believers.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And do not weaken, meaning: do not become weak, and do not grieve, and do not feel sorry for what has befallen you, and you will be the highest, meaning: you will have the final outcome and victory, if you are believers, if you have believed in my Prophet in what he brought you from me.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Khalid bin Al-Walid came wanting to climb the mountain over them, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, do not let them climb over us. So God Almighty revealed:
h
And do not weaken and do not grieve
, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers. Surat Al Imran 3:139
h
And do not weaken and do not grieve
, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers.

x: The readings differed in the reading of that. The people of Hijaz, Medina, and Basra generally read it as:
h
If a wound should touch you

, then a wound similar to it has touched the people. Both of them are with the opening of the qaf, meaning: If killing and wounding should touch you, O group of companions of Muhammad, then a wound - killing and wounding - similar to it has touched the people from your enemies among the polytheists. The majority of Kufa reciters read this:
h
If a wound should touch you
, a wound similar to it has already touched the people [both with a damma on the qaf].
The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads:
h
If a wound should touch you

, there has already touched the people a wound similar to it, with the qaf open in both letters, because the people of interpretation agree that its meaning is killing and wounds, so that indicates that the reading is the fathah. Some Arabists claimed that al-Qarh and al-Qarh are two words with the same meaning. What we have said is well-known among scholars of Arabic speech. It was mentioned that ulcers are wounds and killing.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If a wound should touch you
, there has already touched the [other] people a wound similar to it, he said: Wounds and killing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If a wound should touch you
, there has already touched the people a wound similar to it, he said: If some of you are killed on the day of Uhud, then you killed some of them on the day of Badr.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
If a wound should touch you

, a wound similar to it has already touched the people. Wounds are wounds, and that was on the day of Uhud. Killing and wounding spread among the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day, so God Almighty informed them that the people had been afflicted with something similar to what had afflicted you, and that what had afflicted you was a punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If a wound should touch you
, then a wound like it has touched the people, he said: That was on the day of Uhud, when wounds spread among the Muslims, and killing spread among them, so that is what his statement:
h
If a wound should touch you

, then a wound like it has touched the people, is saying: If a wound has touched you, then a wound like it has touched your enemy, offering condolences to the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and urging them to fight.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
If a wound should touch you
, a similar wound has already touched the people. Wounds are injuries.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
If a wound should touch you
, meaning: a wound, a wound similar to it has already touched the people, meaning: a wound similar to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Umar told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Muslims slept with wounds on them - meaning the day of Uhud - Ikrimah said: And regarding them was revealed: “
h
If a wound should touch you

, there has already touched the [other] people a wound similar to it. And such days We alternate among the people,” and regarding them was revealed: “If you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering. And you hope from God that which they do not hope for”
r
(An-Nisa’: 104)
. As for the interpretation of his saying:
h
If a wound should touch you
, it is: If it should afflict you, as:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: If it touches you, if it befalls you.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And those days We alternate among the people
, the days of Badr and Uhud. What he means by his saying:
h
We circulate it among the people is that we make it circulate among the people and be spent

. By people he means Muslims and polytheists. God Almighty gave victory to the Muslims over the polytheists at Badr, killing seventy of them and capturing seventy. He gave victory to the polytheists over the Muslims at Uhud, killing seventy of them, in addition to those who were wounded. It is said: God gave someone victory over someone else, meaning that He defeated him and took revenge on him for what the one who was defeated had suffered. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And those days We alternate among the people
, he said, God made the days alternate, and the infidels prevailed on the day of Uhud among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those days We alternate among the people

, that by God, if it were not for the alternations, the believers would not have been harmed. However, the disbeliever may be favored by the believer, and the believer may be tested by the disbeliever, so that God may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him, and know the truthful from the liar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those days We alternate among the people

, so God, the Almighty, made His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions victorious over the polytheists on the day of Badr, and made their enemy victorious over them on the day of Uhud. And the disbeliever may prevail over the believer, and the believer may be tested by the disbeliever, so that God may know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him, and know the truthful from the liar. As for those of them who were tested - from the Muslims - on the day of Uhud, it was a punishment for their disobedience to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And those days We alternate among the people
, one day for you and one day against you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: We alternate it among the people. He said: He defeated the polytheists against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those days We alternate among the people

, for the day of Uhud was like the day of Badr. The believers were killed on the day of Uhud, and God took martyrs from among them. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated the polytheists on the day of Badr, so He gave him the rule over them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Umar told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “When the Battle of Uhud took place and the Muslims suffered what they suffered, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, climbed the mountain, and Abu Sufyan came and said: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! Won’t you go out? Won’t you go out? War is a contest: one day for us and one day for you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Answer him. They said: They are not equal, they are not equal. Our dead are in Paradise and your dead are in Hell! So Abu Sufyan said: We have Uzza and you have no Uzza! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say: God is our protector and you have no protector. So Abu Sufyan said: Hubal is superior! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say: God is higher and more majestic! So Abu Sufyan said: Your meeting place and our meeting place is Badr Al-Sughra.” Ikrimah said: And it was revealed about them:
h
And those days We alternate among the people

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those days We alternate among the people
, that he gave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the day of Uhud.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And those days We alternate among the people
, meaning We assign them to the people, for trial and testing.

c: Ibrahim bin Abdullah told me, he said, Abdullah bin Abdul Wahhab Al-Hajabi told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn,
m: on the Surat Al Imran 3:140
h
If a wound should touch you

, there has already touched the [other] people a wound similar to it. And these days We alternate among the people so that God may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs. And God does not like the wrongdoers. authority of Muhammad, regarding the statement of God:
h
And those days We alternate among the people
, he said: He means the princes.

x: By that, the Almighty means: And that God may know those who believe and take from among you witnesses, we will alternate it among the people. If there were no waw in the sentence, his saying,
h
So that he may know
, would have been connected to what preceded it, and
h
And those days We alternate among the people

would have been So that God may know those who believe. But when the waw entered it, it indicated that the sentence was connected to what preceded it, and that after it was a required piece of report, and the lam in his saying,
h
So that he may know
, is related to it.

How is it said: And that God may know those who believe, as a definite noun, and you do not permit the statement: I asked and I knew Abdullah, and you mean: I knew his person, unless you mean: I knew his description and what he is?

This is only permissible with alladhina because alladhina has an interpretation of min and ay, and the same is permissible with the definite article, as God Almighty said: Then God will surely make evident those who are truthful and He will surely make evident the liars (al-Ankabut 29:3), because in alladhina there is an interpretation of ay and ay, like alladhi. And if a definite noun is used with a noun that indicates ay, it is permissible, as one says: I asked to know Abdullah from Amr, and what is meant by that is: so that I may know this from this.

The interpretation of the statement is: And that God may know those among you who believe, O people, from those among you who are hypocrites. We alternate among the people. So, by saying: And that God may know those among you who believe, there is no need to mention His statement: from those who are hypocrites, because the statement indicates it. Since there was an interpretation in His statement: those who believe, that is, as we have described. So it is as if it was said: And that God may know which of you is the believer, as He, the Most High, said: That We may know which of the two parties has the best counting (al-Kahf 18:12). However, when the definite article, which, and from are placed with a proper noun in the place of any, they are in the accusative case because the proper noun falls upon it, as it is said: And that He may know the liars. As for any, it is in the nominative case.
As for his statement:
h
And He takes from among you witnesses
, it means: And that God may know those who believe, and And that He may take from among you witnesses, meaning: to honor from among you with martyrdom whoever He wants to honor with it.
Martyrs is the plural of martyr, as in:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And that God may know those who believe and take from among you witnesses, meaning: to distinguish between the believers and the hypocrites, and to honor those of the people of faith who are honored with martyrdom.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us,
m: reading on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement:
h
And that God may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs

, he said: The Muslims used to ask their Lord: Our Lord, show us a day like the day of Badr in which we will fight the polytheists, and test You with good in it, and seek martyrdom in it! So they met the polytheists on the day of Uhud, and He took martyrs from among them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And that God may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs
, so God honored His friends with martyrdom at the hands of their enemy, then the outcome and consequences of matters will be for the people of God’s obedience.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And that God may know those who believe and take from among you witnesses, he said: Ibn Abbas said: They were asking for martyrdom, so they met the polytheists on the day of Uhud, so He took from among them witnesses.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And that God may know those who believe and take from among you martyrs

, that the Muslims used to ask their Lord to show them a day like the day of Badr, in which they would be tested with goodness, and be granted martyrdom, and be granted Paradise, life, and sustenance. Then they encountered the polytheists on the day of Uhud, and God took from among them martyrs, and they are the ones mentioned by God the Almighty, who said: And do not say of those who are killed in the way of God, ‘They are dead,’ (al-Baqarah 2:154).

x: As for his saying:
h
And God does not love the wrongdoers
, he means by it: those who wronged themselves by disobeying their Lord, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And God does not love the wrongdoers
, meaning: the hypocrites who show obedience with their tongues, but their hearts are determined to disobey.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
The people of Hijaz, Medina, and Basra generally read it as: If a wound should touch you, then a wound similar to it has touched the people.
The majority of Kufa reciters read this: If a wound should touch you, a wound similar to it has already touched the people [both with a damma on the qaf].

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads: If a wound should touch you, there has already touched the people a wound similar to it, with the qaf open in both letters, because the people of interpretation agree that its meaning is killing and wounds, so that indicates that the reading is the fathah.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And that God may purify those who believe

, and that God may test those who believed in God and His Messenger, so He tests them by giving victory to the polytheists among them, until the sincere and true believer among them is distinguished from the hypocrite, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And that God may test those who believe
, he said: To test.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And that God may purify those who believe
, he said: God may purify the believer until he is truthful.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And that God may test those who believe
, meaning: He tests the believers.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And that God may test those who believe
, he said: He tests them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers
, so it was a purification of the believers and a destruction of the disbelievers.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: h
And that God may test those who believe
, meaning: He tests those who believe, until He delivers them from the affliction that befell them, and how patient and certain they were.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers
, he said: He destroys those who are destroyed in this world, and the rest of those who are destroyed in the Hereafter will be in the Fire. As for his saying:
h
And He will destroy the disbelievers

, he means by that: He will diminish them and annihilate them. It is said: So-and-so destroyed this food, if he diminished it or destroyed it, he destroyed it, and from this it is said of the new moon: new moon, and that is its diminishment and destruction, like:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And He will destroy the disbelievers
, he said: He will diminish them.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He will destroy the disbelievers
, he said: He will destroy the disbeliever until he belies him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And He will destroy the disbelievers
, meaning: He will invalidate the hypocrites’ saying with their tongues what is not in their hearts, until their disbelief that they conceal from you becomes apparent.

x: By that, the Most High means: Or did you think, O group of companions of Muhammad, and you thought, that you would enter Paradise, and attain the honor of your Lord, and the honor of stations with Him, while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive, meaning: And it has not yet become clear to My believing servants who among you strives in the way of God in accordance with what He has commanded him to do. I have explained the meaning of his saying:
h
And God knows
h
And God knows
,” and what is similar to that, with his evidence in what has passed, so that there is no need to repeat it.
And His saying: And He knows the patient ones, meaning: those who are patient when faced with hardship, despite the wound, pain, and misfortune that befalls them for the sake of God, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise, and attain from My reward the honor, and that I will not test you with hardship, and afflict you with hardships, until I know the truth of that from you through faith in Me, and patience with what befalls you in Me. The accusative of and He knows the patient is in the morphological sense. In the morphological sense, two verbs come together with some of the letters of the conjunction, and at the beginning of it there is something that it is not appropriate to repeat with the letter of the conjunction, so the one after the letter of conjunction is in the accusative case because it is diverted from the meaning of the first, but it is with a denial or a question or a prohibition at the beginning of the speech. This is like their saying: Nothing can suffice me and it is difficult for you, because the la that is with suffices me is not appropriate to repeat it with his saying: and it is difficult for you, so that is why it is in the accusative case. The reading of this letter is in the accusative case.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: that he used to recite: And He knows the patient, breaking the mim of knows, because he intended to make it jussive in conjunction with his saying: And when God knows.

evidence.text: The reading of this letter is in the accusative case.

x: What he meant by his saying, may his praise be glorified: And you were wishing for death, and you were, O group of companions of Muhammad, You wish for death, meaning the causes of death, which are: fighting. You have seen it, meaning you have seen what you were wishing for - and the ha in his statement:
h
You have seen it refers back to death

, and the meaning is: [fighting], and you are watching, meaning: you have seen it in your sight and view, meaning close to you. Some Arab scholars claim that it was said: And you are watching, to emphasize the statement, just as it is said: I saw it with my own eyes, I saw it with my own eyes, and I heard it with my own ears.

“It was said, ‘And you used to wish for death before you met it,’ because some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had not witnessed Badr, used to wish before Uhud for a day like the day of Badr, so that God might test them with goodness and attain the reward like that which the people of Badr attained. When the day of Uhud came, some of them fled, and some of them were patient until they fulfilled what they had pledged to God before that. So God rebuked those of them who fled, saying, ‘And you used to wish for death before you met it,’ and He praised those of them who were patient and fulfilled their pledge.”
Mentioning the report of what we mentioned of that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: “
h
And you were wishing for death before you met it

. But now you have seen it while you are looking on,” he said: Some men were absent from Badr, and they were wishing to meet it on the day of Badr, so that they might attain goodness and reward like what the people of Badr attained. Then, on the day of Uhud, those of them who had turned away turned away, so God rebuked them - or: He found fault with them, or: He found fault with them - for that. Abu Asim was not sure.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar to it - except that he said: So God rebuked them for that, and he did not doubt.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And you were wishing for death before you met it

. But you have seen it while you were looking on.” They were people from the believers who did not witness the day of Badr. And what God gave the people of Badr of virtue, honor, and reward, they wished to be granted fighting so they could fight. So the fighting was led to them until it was in the outskirts of Medina on the day of Uhud. Then God Almighty said as you hear: And you were wishing for death, until He reached the grateful.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you were wishing for death before you met it
, he said: They were wishing to meet the polytheists and fight them, but when they met them on the day of Uhud, they turned back.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: Some of the believers did not witness the day of Badr, and what God had given them of grace, so they wished to see fighting so that they could fight. So the fighting was brought to them until it was in the vicinity of Medina on the day of Uhud, so God Almighty revealed: And you had been wishing for death before you met it, the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It reached me that some men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: If we meet with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, we will do this and that, so they were tested with that, but by God, not all of them spoke the truth about God, so God Almighty revealed: “And you had certainly wished for death before you met it. But now you have seen it while you were looking on.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: There were some companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had not witnessed Badr. When they saw the virtue of the people of Badr, they Surat Al Imran 3:143 And you had wished for death before you met it. But now you have seen it while you are looking on. said: O God, we ask You to show us a day like the day of Badr, in which We will test You with goodness! So they saw Uhud, and he said to them: You were wishing for death before you met it, but now you have seen it while you are looking on.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And you were wishing for death before you met it

. But you have seen it while you were looking.” That is, you were wishing to bear witness to the truth that you were upon before you met your enemy. He meant those who urged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go out with them to their enemy, because they had missed being present on the day before at Badr, desiring the martyrdom that had passed them by. He said: But you have seen it while you were looking. That is, death by swords in the hands of men, had left you alone with them, and you were looking at them, so you turned away from them.

x: God Almighty means by that: Muhammad is only a messenger like some of the messengers of God whom He sent to His creation, calling to God and to His obedience, who died when their appointed times came and God took them to Himself. God Almighty says: So Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only in what God will do with him when He takes him to Himself when his appointed time comes to an end, like all of His messengers to His creation who passed before him and died when their appointed times came to an end. Then he said to the companions of Muhammad, rebuking them for the panic and fear they had felt when they were told at Uhud that Muhammad had been killed, and finding it ugly that those who had turned away from their enemy had fled from them: Has Muhammad died, O people, because his term had expired or an enemy had killed him, ‘have you turned back on your heels?’
That is,
h
you have turned back
from your religion to which God sent Muhammad and
h
you have turned back

from it as disbelievers in God after believing in it, and after the truth of what Muhammad had called you to had been made clear to you, and the reality of what he had brought to you from his Lord, And whoever turns back on his heels, meaning by that: whoever among you turns back from his religion and returns as a disbeliever after his belief, will never harm God at all, that is, that will not weaken God’s glory or authority, nor will that cause any deficiency in His kingdom, rather his apostasy will harm himself, and his own fortune will be diminished by his disbelief,
h
and God will reward the grateful
, that is, God will reward whoever thanks Him for His success and guidance to His religion by making him steadfast on it.
What Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought, if he died or was killed, and his steadfastness on his path, and his adherence to his religion and faith after him, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, he said, Saif bin Omar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God will reward the grateful

, those who are steadfast in their religion, Abu Bakr and his companions. So Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to say: Abu Bakr was the trustworthy of the grateful, and the trustworthy of the beloved of God, and he was the most grateful of them and the most beloved of them to God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Badr, he said:
m: Abu Bakr is the trustworthy of the grateful. And he recited this verse:
h
And God will reward the grateful

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And God will reward the grateful

, meaning: those who obey Him and act according to His command. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding one of his companions who fled from him in one of the battles. Mentioning the report reported about this:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; other messengers have passed away before him, until His statement:
h
And God will reward the grateful
, that was on the day of Uhud, when they were afflicted with wounds and killing, then they disputed about the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that.

x: Some people said: If he had been a prophet, he would not have been killed!

Some of the elite companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fight for what your Prophet Muhammad fought for until God grants you victory or you join him! Then God, the Almighty, said: “
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; other messengers have passed away before him.
h
If he dies
or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?” He said: If your Prophet dies or is killed, will you turn back as disbelievers after your belief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly, and he added to it. Al-Rabiʿ said: And it was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that a man from the Muhajirun passed by a man from the Ansar who was wallowing in his blood, and he said: O so-and-so, do you know that Muhammad has been killed? The Ansari said: If Muhammad has been killed, then he has conveyed the message, so fight for your religion. Then God Almighty revealed: “And
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; other messengers have passed away before him. So
h
if he dies
or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?” He said: Will you turn back as disbelievers after your belief.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to them on the day of Uhud - meaning: to the polytheists - he ordered the archers to stand at the foot of the mountain in front of the polytheists’ cavalry and he said: Do not move from your place if you see that we have defeated them, for we will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your place. And he appointed Abdullah ibn Jubayr, the brother of Khawwat ibn Jubayr, over them. Then Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad attacked the polytheists and defeated them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions attacked and defeated Abu Sufyan. When Khalid ibn Al-Walid, who was leading the polytheists’ cavalry, saw this, he charged. The archers shot at him but he retreated. When the archers saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions in the midst of the polytheists’ camp, plundering it, they rushed to seize the spoils.

x: Some of them said: We will not abandon the command of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Most of them set out and joined the camp. When Khalid saw the small number of archers, he shouted to his cavalry and charged, killed the archers and attacked the Prophet’s companions. When the polytheists saw that their cavalry was fighting, they called out to each other, and they charged the Muslims, defeated them and killed them. Then Ibn Qumay'ah al-Harithi - one of the sons of al-Harith ibn Abd Manat ibn Kinanah - came and threw a stone at the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), breaking his nose and front teeth and wounding his face, making him heavy. His companions dispersed from him, some of them entered the city, and some of them went up the mountain to the rock and stood on it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) began calling the al-Nas 114:Come to the servants of God!

Come to the servants of God! Thirty men gathered around him and began walking in front of him, but no one stopped except Talhah and Sahl ibn Hunaif. Talhah protected him, and an arrow was shot at his hand, which dried up. Abi bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi came - he had sworn to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, I will kill him - so he said: O liar, where are you running to? So he charged at him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stabbed him in the pocket of his armor, and he was slightly wounded, and he fell down bellowing like a bull. They carried him and said: You have no wound! [What makes you so upset]? He said: Didn't he say: I will kill you? If it had been for all of Rabi'ah and Mudar, I would have killed them! He did not live more than a day and part of a day until he died from that wound.
It spread among the people that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed.

Some of the companions of the rock said: If only we had a messenger to Abdullah bin Ubayy so he could take us safe from Abu Sufyan! O my people, Muhammad has been killed, so go back to your people before they come and kill you. Anas bin An-Nadr said: “O my people, if Muhammad has been killed, then the Lord of Muhammad has not been killed, so fight for the same reason that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought for. O God, I apologize to You for what these people say, and I disavow before You what these people have brought!” Then he took up his sword and fought until he was killed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out calling the people until he reached the Companions of the Rock. When they saw him, a man put an arrow in his bow and wanted to shoot him, but he said: I am the Messenger of God! They were happy when they found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, alive, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was happy when he saw that among his Companions there were those who could protect him.

When they gathered and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among them, their sadness left them, and they began to remember the conquest and what they had missed of it, and to remember their Companions who had been killed. Then God Almighty said to those who said: Surat Al Imran 3:144 And
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; messengers have passed away before him. So
h
if he dies
or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels - never will he harm God at all.
h
And God will reward the grateful
. Muhammad has been killed, so return to your al-Nas 114:“
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; other messengers have passed away before him.
h
If he dies
or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? But whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all,
h
and God will reward the grateful

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And whoever turns back on his heels, he said: He apostatizes.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of his father, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of his father:
m: A man from the Muhajireen passed by a man from the Ansar who was wallowing in his blood, and he said: O so-and-so, do you know that Muhammad has been killed! The Ansari said: If Muhammad has been killed, then he has conveyed the message! So fight for your religion.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me,
m: Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Rafi’, the brother of Banu Adi ibn al-Najjar, told me: Anas ibn al-Nasr - the uncle of Anas ibn Malik - went to Umar and Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, with some men from the Muhajireen and Ansar who had thrown down their hands, and he said: What makes you sit here? They said: Muhammad, the Messenger of God, was killed! He said: What will you do with life after him? Rise and die upon what the Messenger of God died upon! He confronted the people and fought until he was killed, and Anas ibn Malik was named after him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: A crier called out on the day of Uhud when the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were defeated: Behold, Muhammad has been killed, so return to your former religion! So God Almighty revealed: And
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; and there were messengers before him, the verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It was put in the mouths of the Muslims on the day of Uhud that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed, so this verse was revealed: And
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; and there were messengers before him, the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group with him withdrew to a hill that day, and the people were fleeing, and a man was standing on the road asking them: What did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do? And whenever they passed by him, he would ask them, and they would say: By God, we do not know what he did! So he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed, we will surely give them our own hands, for they are our tribesmen and brothers! And they said: If Muhammad were alive, he would not have been defeated, but he was killed! So they were permitted to flee at that time. Then God, the Almighty, revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; other messengers have passed away before him, the entire verse.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger

; many messengers have passed away before him, the verse, some people of doubt, sickness and hypocrisy said on the day the people fled from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was wounded above his eyebrow and his front tooth was broken: Muhammad has been killed, so return to your first religion! That is what His statement means:
h
If he dies
or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then if he dies or is killed

, will you turn back on your heels? He said: What stands between you and abandoning Islam and turning back on your heels is that Muhammad dies or is killed! So one of these two things will happen: he will die, or he will be killed.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger
; many messengers have passed away before him, until His saying:
h
And God will reward the grateful

, that is, because of the people’s saying: Muhammad has been killed, and their defeat at that time and their turning away from their enemy, that is: If your Prophet dies or is killed, will you turn back from your religion as disbelievers as you were, and abandon jihad against your enemy and the Book of God and what His Prophet left behind of his religion with you and with you, and He has made clear to you in what has come to you from me that he is dead and will leave you? And whoever turns back on his heels, that is: turns back from his religion, will never harm God at all, that is: that will not diminish the glory of God, His kingdom, or His authority.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: The people of sickness, doubt, and hypocrisy said, when the people fled from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Muhammad has been killed, so return to your first religion! Then this verse was revealed.

x: The meaning of the statement is:
h
Muhammad is no more than a messenger

, and messengers have passed away before him. Will you then turn back on your heels if Muhammad dies or is killed? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all. So the question was made in the letter of the recompense, and its meaning is that it is in its answer. Likewise, every question that enters into a recompense, its meaning is that it is in its answer.

i: Because the answer is a piece of report that stands on its own, and the recompense is a condition for that piece of report, then its answer is made jussive, and it is like that, and its meaning is the nominative, because it comes after the recompense, as the poet said:
x: I swore to him: If night falls, one of my houses will still be in front of you.
The meaning of la yazl is to raise, but it is a crime because it comes after the recompense, so it becomes like an answer. Similar to it is: Then if I die, will they be immortals?
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 34)
, and How will you be saved if you disbelieve? (al-Muzzammil 73:17). If the place of they will be immortals
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 34)
had been they will be immortals, and it was said: Then if I die, will they be immortals, it would have been permissible to raise and subdivide it. Likewise, if the place of
h
you have turned back
had been
h
you have turned back
, it would have been permissible to raise and subdivide it, because of what was described before. And the repetition of the question was left out a second time with His saying:
h
You have turned back
, being satisfied with the question at the beginning of the speech, and that the question at the beginning indicates its position and location.

Some of the reciters chose in His statement: When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected? [al-Isra’ 17:82- al-Saffat 37:16- al-Waqi’ah 56:47], to leave out repeating the question with when, and to be content with the question in His statement: When we have become dust. The correctness of this is proven by the consensus of the reciters in leaving out repeating the question with His statement:
h
You have turned back
, and to be content with the question in His statement:
h
If he dies

, since it indicates the meaning of the speech and the place of the question in it. He did the same throughout the Qur’an. We will come to the correct statement about that, God willing, when we reach it.

evidence.text: And he recited this verse: And God will reward the grateful.
Some of the reciters chose in His statement: When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?

The correctness of this is proven by the consensus of the reciters in leaving out repeating the question with His statement: You have turned back, and to be content with the question in His statement: If he dies, since it indicates the meaning of the speech and the place of the question in it.

x: By that, the Most High means: Muhammad and no other of God’s creation will die except after reaching the term that God has made the end of his life and survival. So when he reaches that term that God has written for him, and He gives him permission to die, then he dies.
But before that, he will not die by the plot of a plotter or the trick of a deceiver, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And no soul can die except by God’s permission at a predetermined time, meaning: Muhammad has a term that he will reach, if God permits him to do so, it will happen. It has been said that the meaning of this is: No soul can die except by God’s permission. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of the accusative in his saying: a deferred book.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is an emphasis, and its accusative is: God wrote a deferred book. He said: And likewise everything in the Qur’an from His saying: truly is: The most true of that is truly. And likewise: The promise of God [An-Nisa’: 122- Yunus 10:4- Luqman 31:9] and A mercy from your Lord [al-Kahf 18:82- al-Qasas 28:46- al-Dukhan 44:6] and The work of God who perfected all things (al-Naml 27:88), and The Book of God upon you
r
(An-Nisa’: 24)
, is: God made thus a work. So this is the interpretation of everything in the Qur’an similar to this, for it is abundant.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said about his statement:
h
And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of God
, that it means: God has written the terms of the souls. Then it was said: A deferred book, so his statement: A deferred book was removed from the meaning in the speech, since his statement:
h
And it is not for a soul to die except by the permission of God
, had conveyed the meaning: written. He said: And so is the rest of what is in the Qur’an of similar examples, so it is of this type.

Others among them said: The saying of the speaker: Zaid is standing truly, means: I say Zaid is standing truly, because every speech is a statement, so the statement is conveyed by the statement, then what comes after it is excluded from it, just as you say: I say a true statement, and likewise in supposition and certainty, and likewise: God’s promise, and what is similar to it.

The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that all of that is accusative as a source of meaning from the speech that precedes it, because in everything that precedes the sources, whose wording is different from the words of the speech that precedes it, the meanings of the words of the sources are the same even if they differ from them in wording, so it is accusative from the meanings of what precedes it, not its words.

By that, the Most High means: And whoever among you, O believers, desires, through his work, some of the worldly goods as a reward, without what is with God of honor for whoever seeks through his work what is with Him, We will give him from it, meaning: We will give him from it, meaning from this world, meaning that He will give him from it what He has allotted him in it of provision during the days of his life, then he will have no share in the honor of God that He has prepared for whoever obeys Him and seeks what is with Him in the Hereafter. And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, meaning: And whoever among you desires through his work, a reward from it, meaning: what is with God of His honor that He has prepared for those who work for Him in the Hereafter, We will give him from it, meaning: We will give him from it, meaning from the Hereafter. The meaning is: from the honor of God with which He has distinguished the people of His obedience in the Hereafter.
So the speech is applied to this world and the Hereafter, and the meaning is what is in them, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof. And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof.” That is, whoever among you desires this world, but has no desire for the Hereafter, We will give him what has been allotted to us of provision, and he will have no share in the Hereafter. And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof what He promised him, along with what he receives of provision in this world. As for his saying:
h
And We will reward the grateful

, he says: And I will reward the one who is grateful to Me for the good I have bestowed upon him, by obeying Me, adhering to My command, and avoiding My prohibitions, in the Hereafter, with the same honor that I promised My friends for their gratitude to Me. Ibn Ishaq said about this:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And We will reward the grateful
, meaning: That is the reward of the grateful, meaning by that: God will give him what He promised him in the Hereafter, along with the provision that will flow to him in this world.

x: The readings differed in the reading of that: Some of them read it as: Wa-ka-ayn, with a hamza on the alif and a shaddah on the ya.

Others read it with an extended alif and a light ya. They are two well-known readings in the reading of Muslims, and two well-known languages, with no difference in their meaning. So whichever reading a reader reads it with, he is correct. Because the meaning is the same, and they are well-known in the speech of the Arabs. Its meaning is: How many prophets.
There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Two thousand men were killed with him.
A group of the readers of Hijaz and Basra read it as: killed, with a damma on the qaf.
Another group read it with the qaf open and with the alif. This is the reading of a group of the readers of Hijaz and Kufa.
As for the one who read killed, he chose that, because he said: If they had been killed, there would not have been a known meaning for his saying:
h
They did not weaken

, because it is impossible for them to be described as not weakening or becoming weak after they were killed. As for those who read it as: killed, they said: What he meant by killing was the Prophet and some of the rabbis who were with him, not all of them, and he only denied weakness and frailty from those who remained from the rabbis who were not killed.

The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of the one who reads with the qaf with a damma: Many ribān were killed with him, because God Almighty only rebuked in this verse and the verses before it, in His saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who fought, those who fled on the day of Uhud and abandoned the fighting, or heard the voice calling out: Muhammad has been killed. So God Almighty rebuked them for fleeing and abandoning the fighting, saying: If Muhammad dies or is killed, O believers, will you turn back from your religion and turn back on your heels?

c: Then he told them
m: about what many of the followers of the prophets before them had done, and said to them: Why did you not do as the people of virtue and knowledge among the followers of the prophets before you did when their prophet was killed, by continuing on the path of their prophet and fighting for his religion against the enemies of the religion of God, in the same way that they fought with their prophet, and you did not weaken or become weak, just as those who were before you from the people of knowledge and insight among the followers of the prophets did not become weak when their prophet was killed, but they were patient with their enemies until God judged between them and them? And with this interpretation came the interpretation of the interpreters. As for the ribāyīn, they are raised by His saying: with him, not by His saying: he was killed. Rather, the interpretation of the speech is: How many a prophet was killed, and with him were many ribāyīn, but
h
they did not weaken

for what befell them in the way of God. And in the speech there is an implied waw, because it is waw that indicates the meaning of the state of the killing of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. However, what was mentioned in the speech was sufficient to indicate it by mentioning it, and that is like the saying of the speaker in the speech: the prince was killed with a great army, meaning: he was killed and with him a great army. As for the riba, the Arabs differed about its meaning.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: They are those who worship the Lord, and one of them is my Lord. Some grammarians of Kufa said: If they were attributed to the worship of God, they would have been rabbiyyun with the opening of the ra’, but it is: the scholars and the thousands. And the rabbis among us are the many groups, one of them is rabbi, and they are the group.
The interpreters differed about its meaning.
Some of them said the same as we said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: The ribun are the thousands.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said:
m: Abd al-Razzaq Surat Al Imran 3:146 And how many a prophet fought with him many pious men, but they never lost heart because of what befell them in the cause of God, nor did they weaken, nor did they humble themselves. And God loves the patient. told us, he said:

c: Al-Thawri and Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Zur bin Habish, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: many thousands, he said: many multitudes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Many thousands fought with him
, he said: crowds.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah told me, he said, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: And how many a prophet was killed with many thousands, he said: Thousands.

x: Others said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, he said:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us, he said: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And how many a prophet was killed with many devout men
, he said: Many scholars.

c: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And how many a prophet was killed with him many devout men
, he said: Jurists and scholars.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And how many a prophet was killed with him many devout men
? He said: The great multitudes. Yaqub said: And this is how Ishmael read it?
h
Many devout men were killed with him

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And how many a prophet was killed with many devout people, he said: large crowds.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
Many devout men were killed with him
, he said: Many scholars, and Qatada said: Large crowds.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: many thousands, he said: many multitudes.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid Al-Amili told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Many thousands were killed with him, he said: Many multitudes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
Many rabbis were killed with him
, meaning: large groups.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
How many a prophet was killed with him many devout men
, he said: large crowds, their prophet was killed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Habban and Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And how many a prophet fought with whom were many pious men
, Jaʿfar said: Scholars who were patient, and Ibn Al-Mubarak said: Pious and patient.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement:
h
Many rabbis were killed with him
, meaning the great multitudes, their prophet was killed.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Many rabbis fought with him, meaning: large groups.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: his saying:
h
And how many a prophet was killed with many devout men
, he said: And how many a prophet was killed, and with him were groups.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And how many a prophet was killed with whom were many devout men. The devout are the large crowds.

x: Others said: The rabbis, the followers.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And how many a prophet was killed along with whom were many devout people

, he said: The devout people are the followers, the devout people are the rulers, and the devout people are the subjects. And with this God rebuked them when they fled from him, when Satan cried out: Muhammad has been killed. He said: The defeat was when he cried out in [Saha shouted]: O people, Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has been killed, so return to your tribes so that they may believe in you!

x: What is meant by the words of God Almighty: And
h
they did not weaken

because of what befell them in the cause of God, is that they were not helpless, because of the pain of the wounds that befell them in the cause of God, nor because of the killing of those who were killed from among them, from fighting the enemies of God, nor did they shrink from their struggle. And
h
they did not weaken

, meaning: their strength did not weaken because of the killing of their Prophet, nor did they submit, meaning: they were not humiliated so that they would humble themselves before their enemy by entering into their religion and flattering them in it out of fear of them, but they moved forward with their insights and the path of their Prophet, patiently following the command of God and the command of their Prophet, and obedience to God and following His revelation and inspiration. And God loves the patient, meaning: God loves these people and their likes from those who are patient with His command and obedience and obedience to His Messenger in the struggle against His enemy, not those who failed and fled from their enemy, nor those who turned on their heels and were humiliated before their enemy because their Prophet was killed or died, nor those who entered it and were weak before their enemy and weak because of the loss of their Prophet.
Nabeel And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They did not lose heart for what befell them in the cause of God, nor did they weaken, nor did they submit, meaning: they did not become helpless, nor did they weaken because of the killing of their Prophet. And they did not submit, meaning: they did not turn away from their insight or their religion, but rather they fought for what the Prophet of God fought for until they joined God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they did not lose heart for what befell them in the cause of God

, nor did they weaken, he says: they did not fail, nor did they weaken because of the killing of their Prophet, nor did they submit, he says: they did not turn away from their insight, they fought for what the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought for until they joined God.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And
h
they did not weaken
, so the usurers did not weaken, for what befell them in the cause of God, of the killing of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And
h
they did not weaken
, he says:
h
they did not weaken

in the cause of God because of the killing of the Prophet. And they did not submit, he says: they did not humiliate themselves when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, they have no right to prevail over us - and And do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers
r
(Al Imran 3:139)

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
They did not weaken

due to the loss of their prophet, nor did they weaken due to their enemy, nor did they submit due to what happened to them in the struggle for God and their religion, and that is patience, and God loves the patient.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: And they did not humble themselves, he said: They were humble.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And they did not submit, he said: They did not submit to their enemy, and God loves the patient.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that: Some of them read it as: Wa-ka-ayn, with a hamza on the alif and a shaddah on the ya.
Others read it with an extended alif and a light ya.
They are two well-known readings in the reading of Muslims, and two well-known languages, with no difference in their meaning.
So whichever reading a reader reads it with, he is correct.
Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: Two thousand men were killed with him.
A group of the readers of Hijaz and Basra read it as: killed, with a damma on the qaf.
Another group read it with the qaf open and with the alif.
This is the reading of a group of the readers of Hijaz and Kufa.

As for those who read it as: killed, they said: What he meant by killing was the Prophet and some of the rabbis who were with him, not all of them, and he only denied weakness and frailty from those who remained from the rabbis who were not killed.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of the one who reads with the qaf with a damma: Many ribān were killed with him, because God Almighty only rebuked in this verse and the verses before it, in His saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who fought, those who fled on the day of Uhud and abandoned the fighting, or heard the voice calling out: Muhammad has been killed.
Yaqub said: And this is how Ishmael read it?

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And their saying was not

, and the saying of the two rabbis - and the ha and mim are from the mention of the names of the two rabbis - except that they said, meaning: They had no saying other than this saying, when their prophet was killed, and His statement: Our Lord, forgive us our sins, meaning: They did not hold fast, when their prophet was killed, except to be patient with what befell them, and to struggle against their enemy, and to ask their Lord for forgiveness and victory over their enemy. The meaning of the statement is: Their saying was not except that they said, Our Lord, forgive us our sins. As for extravagance, it is excess in something. It is said: So-and-so was excessive in this matter, if he exceeded its amount and went to extremes. Its meaning here is: Forgive us our sins: the minor ones, and those in which we have been excessive and have gone beyond the major ones.
The meaning of the words was: Forgive us our sins, the minor ones and the major ones, as in:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And our extravagance in our affair
, he said: Our sins.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And our extravagance in our affair
, our sins and our injustice to ourselves.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
And our extravagance in our affair
, meaning major sins.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Ubaid bin Sulayman, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, he said:
m: The major sins.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And our extravagance in our affair
, he said: Our sins.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And our extravagance in our affair

, he said: our sins. As for his saying: And make our feet firm, he is saying: Make us among those who are steadfast in the war against Your enemy and in fighting them, and do not make us among those who are defeated and flee from them and do not establish their feet in one place to fight them. And give us victory over the disbelieving people, he is saying: And give us victory over those who denied Your Oneness and the prophethood of Your Prophet.

x: This is a reprimand from God the Almighty to His servants who fled from the enemy on the day of Uhud and abandoned fighting them, and a discipline for them. God the Almighty says: Why did you not do, when it was said to you: Your Prophet has been killed, as these rabbis who were followers of the prophets did when their prophets were killed? Why did you not be patient with your enemy as they were patient, and not weaken and submit to your enemy and try to turn back on your heels, as these rabbis did not weaken and submit to their enemy, and you asked your Lord for victory and triumph as they asked, so that God would grant you victory over them as they were victorious, for God loves those who are patient in their matter and in the struggle against their enemy, so He gives them victory and triumph over their enemy?
Like: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said:

c: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “And their only statement was that they said: ‘Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our conduct and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.’” That is: So say as they said, and know that this is only because of sins on your part, and seek forgiveness as they sought forgiveness, and continue in your religion as they continued in their religion, and do not turn back on your heels, and ask Him as they asked Him to plant firmly your feet, and seek His aid as they sought His aid against the disbelieving people. All of this is from their statement, and it happened when their prophet was killed, so they did not do as you did.

x: The reading that is the reading in His statement:
h
And their saying was not

is the accusative, due to the consensus of the readers of the regions on that, transmitted widely and inherited from the proof. The accusative was chosen for the saying, because an can only be definite, so it was more appropriate for it to be the noun, rather than the nouns that may be definite sometimes and indefinite sometimes. Therefore, the accusative was chosen for every noun that followed kan if it was followed by the light an: like His statement:
h
So the answer of his people was only that they said
, ‘Kill him or burn him’
r
(Al-ʿAnkabut: 24)

, and His Surat Al Imran 3:147 And their only statement was that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our conduct and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people." statement: Then their trial was only that they said
r
(Al-Anʿam: 23)

But if what follows kan is a definite noun, and what follows it is like it, then the nominative and accusative are the same in what follows kan. If you make what follows kan the noun, you raise it and put what follows it in the accusative. If you make the one who follows it the predicate, you put it in the accusative case and raise what comes after it, as in the statement of God Almighty: Then the worst was the end of those who did evil (ar-Rum 30:10). If you make the consequence the noun, you put it in the nominative case, and make the worst the predicate in the accusative case.

i: If you make the consequence the predicate, you put it in the accusative case and say: Then the worst was the end of those who did evil (ar-Rum 30:10), and make the worst the noun, so it is in the nominative case, as the poet said:
x: The people knew that the only disease of Thahlan was the disgrace of those who led it.

It was also narrated: Her illness in Thalan was nothing but disgrace, in the accusative and nominative cases, as I have explained. If he had done something like that, even though it was permissible, the most eloquent speech among the Arabs would be what I have described.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that is the reading in His statement: And their saying was not is the accusative, due to the consensus of the readers of the regions on that, transmitted widely and inherited from the proof.

x: By that, the Most High means: So God gave those whom He described with what He described them, of patience in obeying God after the killing of their prophets, and in fighting their enemy, and seeking help from God in their affairs, and following the paths of their leader for what they did in God - the reward of this world, meaning: a reward in this world, and that is: victory over their enemy and the enemy of God, and triumph, and conquest over them, and empowerment for them in the lands, and the good reward of the Hereafter, meaning: and the best reward of the Hereafter for what they did in the world of their righteous deeds, and that is: Paradise and its delights, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: And their only saying was that they said, ‘Our Lord, forgive us our sins,’ and he recited until he reached
h
And God loves the doers of good

, yes, by God, God would have given them victory, supremacy, empowerment, and triumph over their enemy in this world, and the best reward of the Hereafter, he says: the best reward in the Hereafter, which is Paradise.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: his saying: And what was their saying, then he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So God gave them the reward of this world
