, he said: victory and spoils, and the good reward of the Hereafter, he said: God’s pleasure and mercy.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So God gave them the reward of this world
, victory over their enemy, and the good reward of the Hereafter, Paradise and what is prepared in it. And His statement,
h
And God loves the doers of good

, God Almighty says: God did that to them because of their goodness, for He loves the doers of good, and they are the ones who do what God Almighty described about them that they did when their prophet was killed.

x: By that, the Most High means:
h
O you who have believed

in God and His Messenger in God’s promise and threat, His command and His prohibition, If you obey those who disbelieve, meaning: those who denied the prophethood of your Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, from the Jews and Christians - in what they command you to do and what they prohibit you from doing - and you accept their opinion in that and advise them in what they claim that they are advising you in, they will turn you back on your heels, meaning: they will make you apostatize after believing, and disbelieve in God and His verses and His Messenger after Islam, and you will turn back as losers, meaning: you will turn back from your faith and religion to which God has guided you, losers, meaning: doomed, you have lost yourselves, and you have gone astray from your religion, and your worldly life and your afterlife are gone.
This prohibits those who believe in God from obeying the disbelievers in their opinions and seeking their advice in their religions, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
O you who have believed
, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers, meaning: from your religion, so your worldly life and your afterlife will be lost.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, if you obey those who disbelieve, Ibn Jurayj said: He says: Do not seek advice from the Jews and Christians regarding your religion, and do not believe them in anything regarding your religion.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers. He says: If you obey Abu Sufyan, he will turn you back as disbelievers.

x: By this, the Most High means: God is your guide, O believers, and He will save you from obeying those who disbelieve. It was said: Rather, God is your Master, because in His statement: If you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, there is a prohibition against obeying them. It is as if He said: O you who have believed, do not obey those who disbelieve, lest they turn you back on your heels. Then He began the statement and said: Rather, God is your Master, so obey Him, not those who disbelieve, for that is better than victory. Therefore, He raised the name God, and if it had been in the accusative case meaning: Rather, obey God, your Master, not those who disbelieve, it would have been a correct interpretation. What he means by his saying: Rather, God is your protector, is your guardian and supporter against your enemies who disbelieve, and He is the best of helpers, not from those to whom you fled from the Jews and the disbelievers in God.
So hold fast to God, who is your protector and protector, and seek His help, not from anyone else who seeks to harm you and lies in wait for you with misfortunes, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Rather, God is your protector, if what you say with your tongues is true in your hearts, and He is the best of helpers, meaning: So hold fast to Him and do not seek help from anyone other than Him, and do not turn back on your heels, apostatizing from your religion.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God will cast, O believers, into the hearts of those who disbelieved, in their Lord, and denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from those who fought you at Uhud, terror, which is panic and fear, because they associated partners with God, meaning: because of their association with God, their worship of idols, and their obedience to Satan, for which I have not given them any proof, and it is the authority, which the Almighty informed that He did not send down because of their disbelief and association. This is a promise from God, the Most High, to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of victory over their enemies and their success, as long as they adhere to His covenant and adhere to His obedience.

c: Then He informed them
m: of what He will do to their enemies after their fate is Him, so He, the Most High, said: And their refuge is the Fire, meaning: And their return to which they will return on the Day of Resurrection is the Fire, And evil is the residence of the wrongdoers, meaning: And evil is the residence of the wrongdoers - those who wronged themselves by acquiring what necessitated God’s punishment - the Fire, as: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: “We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they have associated with God that for which He has not sent down any authority. And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.” Indeed, I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, by which I used to support you against them, because they associated with Me that for which I have not given them any proof. That is, do not think that they will have a final victory or supremacy over you, as long as you hold fast and follow My command, because of the calamity that has befallen you from them due to sins that you have committed against yourselves, in which you disobeyed My command and disobeyed the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Husayn told me, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When Abu Sufyan and the polytheists set out on the day of Uhud, heading towards Mecca, Abu Sufyan set out until he reached part of the road. Then they regretted it and said: What a bad thing you have done! You killed them, and when none remained but the fugitives, you left them! Go back and exterminate them! So God, the Almighty, cast terror into their hearts and they fled. Then they met a Bedouin, and they promised him a reward and said to him: If you meet Muhammad, tell him what we have gathered for them. So God, the Almighty, informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he pursued them until he reached Hamra’ Al-Asad, and God, the Almighty, revealed about that, and mentioned Abu Sufyan when he wanted to go back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what terror He had cast into his heart, so He said: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with God.

x: By the words of God Almighty: And God has fulfilled for you, O believers among the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He means His promise that He promised them through the tongue of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The promise that he made to them on his tongue at Uhud was his saying to the archers: Stay where you are and do not move, and if you see that we have defeated them, then we will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain where you are.
And the promise of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them was victory on that day if they obeyed his command, like the one who:

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) went out to fight the polytheists at Uhud, he ordered the archers to stand at the foot of the mountain in front of the polytheists’ horses and said: Do not move from your place if you see that we have defeated them, for we will continue to be victorious as long as you remain in your place. He appointed Abdullah ibn Jubayr, the brother of Khawat ibn Jubayr, over them. Then Talhah ibn Uthman, the standard-bearer of the polytheists, stood up and said: O company of the companions of Muhammad, you claim that God will hasten us to the Fire with your swords, and hasten you to Paradise with our swords! Is there anyone among you whom God will hasten to Paradise with my sword, or hasten me to the Fire with his sword? Ali ibn Abi Talib stood up and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will not leave you until God hastens you to the Fire with my sword, or hastens me to Paradise with your sword! Ali struck him and cut off his leg, so he fell and his private parts were exposed. He said: I ask you by God and by kinship, cousin! So he left him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is great, and Ali said to his companions: What prevented you from finishing him off? He said: My cousin asked me to do so when his private parts were exposed, and I was shy of him. Then Az-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad attacked the polytheists and defeated them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions attacked and defeated Abu Sufyan. When Khalid ibn Al-Walid saw that while he was riding the polytheists’ cavalry, he attacked and the archers shot him, so he retreated. When the archers saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions in the middle of the polytheists’ camp, plundering it, they rushed to the spoils.

x: Some of them said: We will not abandon the command of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So most of them set out and joined the camp. When Khalid saw the small number of archers, he shouted to his cavalry, then charged and killed the archers, then charged the Prophet’s companions. When the polytheists saw that their cavalry was fighting, they called out to each other and attacked the Muslims, defeated them and killed them. Harun ibn Ishaq narrated, Musʿab ibn al-Miqdam narrated, Israʿil narrated, Abu Ishaq narrated, on the authority of al-Baraʿ who said: When the day of Uhud came and we met the polytheists, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) seated some men opposite the archers and put Abdullah ibn Jubayr, the brother of Khawwat ibn Jubayr, in command of them. He said to them: Do not move from your place. If you see us prevailing over them, do not move, and if you see them prevailing over us, do not help us.

When the people met, the polytheists were defeated until I saw the women lifted from their shins and their anklets exposed. They began to say: The spoils, the spoils! Abdullah said: Wait! Do you not know what the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) has entrusted you with! But they refused and set out. When they reached them, God turned their faces away, and seventy Muslims were killed.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission

, that Abu Sufyan came three nights before the end of Shawwal until he reached Uhud, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and announced to the people, so they gathered, and he put Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam in charge of the cavalry, and with him that day was Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad Al-Kindi. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave the banner to a man from Quraysh called Mus'ab ibn Umair. Hamza ibn Abdul Muttalib went out with Al-Hasr, and Hamza was sent ahead of him. Khalid ibn Al-Walid approached the cavalry of the polytheists, with Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Az-Zubayr and said: Face Khalid ibn Al-Walid and stand opposite him until I give you notice. He put other cavalry in charge, so they were on the other side, and he said: Do not move until I give you notice. Abu Sufyan came carrying Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Al-Zubayr to charge, so he charged Khalid bin Al-Walid and defeated him and those with him, as he said:
h
And God has fulfilled His promise to you

when you were killing them with His permission until you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love, and God promised the believers that He would support them and that He is with them.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd God al-Zuhri told me,
m: and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and others from our scholars - in a story he mentioned on the authority of Uhud - he mentioned that all of them had narrated some of it, and that their hadiths were combined in what he presented of the hadith, so what he mentioned in that was: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended from the ravine of Uhud, on the opposite side of the valley to the mountain, so he turned his back and his army towards Uhud and said: No one should fight until we order him to fight. And the Quraysh had let their backs and forelegs go out to graze crops that were in al-Samghah from Qanat, and a man from the Ansar said when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade fighting: Are you grazing the crops of Bani Qaylah while we have not yet fought?! The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) mobilized for battle with seven hundred men, and the Quraysh mobilized with three thousand men, and with them were two hundred horses which they had set aside. They put Khalid bin Al-Walid on the right flank of the cavalry, and Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl on the left flank. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) appointed Abdullah bin Jubair, the brother of Banu Amr bin Awf, who was a scholar in white clothes at that time, as the archers, and the archers were fifty men. He said: Spray the cavalry with arrows, lest they come to us from behind! Whether they are for us or against us, then stand where you are, lest we be attacked from your side. When the people met, they drew near to each other and fought until the battle became fierce. Abu Dujana fought until he had engulfed the people, and Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib and Ali bin Abi Talib, with men from the Muslims. Then God, the Almighty, revealed His victory and fulfilled His promise, so they struck them with swords until they were routed, and there was no doubt about the defeat. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ibad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: Al-Zubayr said: By God, I saw myself looking at the servants of Hind bint Utbah and her companions, with their sleeves rolled up and running away, with neither of them being few nor many, when the archers turned towards the camp when the people had fled from it, wanting to plunder, and they left our backs to the horses, so we were attacked from behind. A crier cried out: Muhammad has been killed! So we retreated, and the people retreated upon us after we had killed the standard-bearers, until no one of the people could come near it.
b.via: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Ubayd God al-Zuhri

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God has fulfilled His promise to you
, meaning: I have fulfilled what I promised you of victory over your enemy.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his saying:
h
And God has fulfilled His promise to you

, and that was on the day of Uhud. He said to them: You will prevail, so do not let me know what you have taken of their spoils until you are done! So they abandoned the command of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disobeyed, and fell into the spoils, and forgot the covenant he had made with them, and disobeyed and did something other than what he had ordered them to do.

x: God Almighty means by that: And God has fulfilled for you, O believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what He promised you of victory over your enemy at Uhud, when you kill them, meaning: when you kill them.
It is said: He killed him, if he killed him, like:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Saeed al-Wasiti told me,
m: Surat Al Imran 3:152 And God has already fulfilled His promise to you when you were oppressing them by His permission until you lost heart and disputed in the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love -
h
among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter
h
Then He turned you away from them to test you

; and He has certainly pardoned you, and God is full of bounty to the believers. he said, Yaqub ibn Isa told us, he said, Abdul Aziz ibn Imran ibn Abdul Aziz ibn Umar ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Awf told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abdul Aziz, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Awf regarding his statement:
h
When you were killing them by His permission
, he said: Killing means killing.
b.via: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Saeed al-Wasiti

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I heard Ubaidullah Ibn Abdullah say regarding the statement of God Almighty: When you were killing them, he said: killing.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
When you were killing them by His permission
, he said: You were killing them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them
, meaning: killing them with His permission.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: When you kill them, he said: When you kill them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: h
When you were killing them by His permission
, and killing means killing.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And God fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them
with His permission, meaning: you were killing them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When you kill them, with swords, meaning: killing.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
When you were killing them by His permission
, meaning: killing.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
When you were killing them by His permission
, meaning: you were killing them. As for his saying: With His permission, he means: With My judgment and decree for you regarding that, and My giving you authority over them, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When you are killing them with My permission, and I have given you control over them, and I have restrained their hands from you.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: Until you failed, until you became cowardly and weak, and disputed over the matter, meaning: and you differed over the matter of God, meaning: and you disobeyed and opposed your Prophet, so you abandoned his command and what he entrusted to you. And what He means by that is the archers whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ordered to remain in their position and seat at the mouth of the ravine at Uhud, opposite Khalid ibn al-Walid and those of the polytheist horsemen who were with him, whose command we mentioned before. As for his saying:
h
After He showed you what you love

, he means by that: after what God showed you, O believers in Muhammad, of victory and triumph over the polytheists, and that is the defeat in which they had defeated them from their women and their money before the archers left their positions in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had seated them, and before the polytheists’ cavalry came out against the believers from behind them.

In a similar manner to what we have said, the report of the people of interpretation has become clear. Some of those who said this have already been mentioned, and we will mention the words of some of those whose words were not mentioned previously.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until you became weak and disputed about the matter, meaning you differed about the matter, and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love, and that was on the day of Uhud. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a covenant with them and ordered them to do something, but they forgot the covenant, transgressed, and disobeyed what the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ordered them to do, so their enemy threw them down, after He had shown them from their enemy what they love.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent some people - meaning on the day of Uhud - and they were behind them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Stay here, and turn back the faces of those who fled from us, and be our guards from behind us. And when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated the people, he and his companions, those who had been behind them said to one another, when they saw the women ascending the mountain and the spoils, they said: Go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and seize the spoils before you are beaten to them! And another group said: Rather, we will obey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and remain where we are! So that is what His statement,
h
Among you are those who desire this world

, is for those who desired the spoils, And among you are those who desire the Hereafter, is for those who said: We will obey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and remain where we are. So they came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he failed when they disputed among themselves. He said: And you disobeyed
h
after He showed you what you love
. They had seen the victory and the spoils.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: Until you failed, meaning: you became cowardly before your enemy, and disputed about the matter, meaning: you differed, and disobeyed
h
after He showed you what you love

, and that was on the day of Uhud. He said to them: You will prevail, so do not let me know what you have taken from their spoils until you are done, so they abandoned the command of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and disobeyed, and fell into the spoils, and forgot his covenant that he had made with them, and disobeyed to something other than what he had ordered them to do, so their enemy attacked them, after He showed them in them what they love.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Until you become weak, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: Failure is cowardice.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Until you become weak and dispute over the matter and disobey after He has shown you what you love, from Al-Fath.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Until you failed, meaning: you were weak, and disputed about the matter, meaning: you differed about my matter, and disobeyed, meaning: you abandoned the matter of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he entrusted to you, meaning the archers,
h
after He showed you what you love
, meaning: the victory, there is no doubt about it, and the defeat of the people from their women and their money.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: After I showed you what you love, meaning: the conquest.

x: It was said that the meaning of his statement:
h
Until when you lost heart and disputed over the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love is until when you disputed over the

matter and lost heart and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love, and that it is from the introduction which means delay, and that the waw entered into that and its meaning is falling, as it is said, So when they both submitted and he prostrated himself upon his forehead, * And We called to him (37:103-104) meaning: We called to him. This is said in until when and in So when [it did not come in other than these two]. And from it is the statement of God the Almighty: Until when Gog and Magog are let loose (38:96-97). Then He said: And the true promise has drawn near (37:96-97).

i: It means: come close, as the poet said:
x: Even if your stomachs are lice-ridden and you see your children grow up You turned your back on us, you are the mean, weak, and cunning one.
By His saying,
h
Among you are those who desire this world

, He, the Most High, means those who left their seat in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had seated them in the valley of Uhud for the horses of the polytheists, and joined the Muslim army seeking plunder when they saw the defeat of the polytheists.

And among you are those who desire the Hereafter, meaning by that: those archers who remained in their seats in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had seated them, and followed his command, preserving the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and seeking what is with God of reward for their actions and the Hereafter, as:

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Some of you want this world and some of you want the Hereafter. So those who set out seeking the spoils were the people of this world, and those who remained and said: We will not disobey the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted the Hereafter.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly. Al-Husayn narrated, he said, I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter

, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered a group of Muslims on the day of Uhud, saying: Be armed for the people, in the same way as he ordered them to remain in it, and he ordered them not to leave their place until he gave them permission. So when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met Abu Sufyan and the polytheists who were with him on the day of Uhud, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated them. So when the armed men saw that God, the Almighty, had defeated the polytheists, some of them set off calling out: The spoils! The spoils! Do not let them go! And some of them remained in their place, and said: We will not leave our place until the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gives us Surat Al Imran 3:152 And God has already fulfilled His promise to you when you were oppressing them by His permission until you lost heart and disputed in the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love -
h
among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter
h
Then He turned you away from them to test you
; and He has certainly pardoned you, and God is full of bounty to the believers. permission! So it was revealed:
h
Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter
. Ibn Masʿud used to say: I did not feel that any of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted this world and its glory, until the day of Uhud.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: When God defeated the polytheists on the Day of Uhud, the archers said: Catch up with the people and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do not let them precede you to the spoils, so that they will be theirs and not you! And some of them said: We will not shoot until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gives us permission. So this verse was revealed:
h
Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter
, Ibn Jurayj said. Ibn Masʿud said: We did not know that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted this world and its glory, until that day.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Among you are those who desire this world
, those who seek spoils, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter, those who follow them and kill them.

c: Al-Husayn bin Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abd Al-Khair, who said: Abdullah said:
m: I did not see any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanting the world until the following verse was revealed about us on the day of UHud 11:Among you are those who want the world and among you are those who want the Hereafter.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abd Al-Khair, who said: Ibn Masoud said:
m: I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day wanted the world, until God said what He said.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said:
m: Abdullah ibn Masʿud said when he saw them falling into the spoils: I did not think that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted the world until today.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Ibn Masoud used to say: I did not feel that any of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted the world and its glory, until that day.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Among you are those who desire the world, meaning: those who wanted to plunder out of desire for the world and to abandon what they were commanded to do of obedience for which there is a reward in the Hereafter, And among you are those who desire the Hereafter, meaning: those who strove in the cause of God and did not disobey what they were forbidden to do for the sake of worldly gain out of desire for it, hoping for what is with God of good reward in the Hereafter.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Then He turned you away, O believers, from the polytheists
h
after He showed you what you love
in them and in yourselves, of your defeating them and your victory over them.

He turned your faces away from them because you disobeyed the command of My Messenger and opposed his obedience, because you preferred this world over the Hereafter, as a punishment for what you did, to test you, meaning: to test you, so that the hypocrite among you may be distinguished from the sincere and honest in his faith among you, as:

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then he mentioned when Khalid bin Al-Walid turned against them:
h
Then He turned you away from them to test you

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Then He turned you away from them

, he said: He turned the people away from them, and killed a number of the Muslims who were taken prisoner on the day of Badr, and the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, and his front tooth was broken, and his face was wounded, and he was wiping the blood from his face and saying: How can a people succeed who did this to their Prophet while he was calling them to their Lord? Then the verse was revealed: You have no part in the matter
r
(Al Imran 3:128)
. They said: Did not the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, promise us victory? Then God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
And God has fulfilled His promise to you
until His statement:
h
Then He turned you away from them to test you
, and He has forgiven you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
Then He turned you away from them to test you
, meaning: He turned you away from them to test you, and that was with some of your sins.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And He has pardoned you

, is that God has pardoned you, O you who disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and abandoned his obedience in what he brought to you regarding staying in the place he ordered you to stay in, from you.

He has pardoned you from the punishment of your sin that you committed, for what is greater than what He punished you with, of defeating your enemies and turning your faces away from them, since He did not uproot your group, as:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He has pardoned you

, he said: Al-Hasan said, and clapped his hands: How did He pardon them, when seventy of them were killed, and the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, and his front tooth was broken, and his face was wounded? He said: Then he says: God, the Almighty, said: I have pardoned you when you disobeyed Me, lest I should have exterminated you. He said: Then Al-Hasan says: These are with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the way of God, wrathful for God, fighting the enemies of God, they were forbidden from something and they did it, and by God they did not leave until they were distressed by this distress, so the most wicked of the wicked today commits every major sin, commits every calamity, and drags his clothes over them, and claims that there is nothing wrong with him!! So he will know.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He has pardoned you
, he said: He did not eradicate you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And He has pardoned you
, and God has pardoned the enormity of that. He did not destroy you because of the disobedience you committed against your Prophet, but I returned with My favor upon you. As for his saying:
h
And God is full of bounty toward the believers

, it means: God is full of bounty toward the people of faith in Him and in His Messenger, by forgiving them of many of the sins for which they deserve punishment from Him. If He punishes them for some of that, then He is being kind to them through His good deeds toward them, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God has pardoned you, and God is full of bounty to the believers, meaning: And likewise God has been gracious to the believers, if He punishes them for some sins in this world as a lesson and admonition, then He does not eradicate all that is in them of the right that He has over them for what they committed of disobeying Him, as mercy for them and a reward for them, for what is in them of faith.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And He has pardoned you, O believers, since He did not uproot you in order to destroy you and gather you together because of your sins and your flight, when you ascended and did not turn back to anyone. There are different readings of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Iraq and the Levant, except for Al-Hasan Al-Basri, read it as idh ta’as’dun with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ‘ayn. This is the reading according to us, because the majority of the reciters have agreed on reading it with this reading, and they have denounced anything that contradicts it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri
m: that he used to read it: When you ascend, with the opening of the ta’ and the ‘ayn.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me that, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan.
m: As for those who read tas’adun with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ‘ayn, they directed the meaning of that to the fact that when the people were defeated by their enemy, they took to the valley, fleeing. They mentioned that this is in Abu’s reading: When you ascend in the valley.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us
m: [that], he said, Abu Ubaid told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun. They said: Fleeing at ground level, in valleys and ravines is an ascent, not an ascent. They said: Ascending is only on mountains, ladders and stairs, because the meaning of ascending is rising and rising above something. They said: As for taking the ground level and descending, it is an ascent, just as it is said: We ascended from Mecca, if you began traveling from it and leaving, and we ascended from Kufa to Khorasan, meaning: We left it traveling to it, and we began leaving from it to it. They said: The interpretation of most of the interpreters is that the people were taken by their enemy in the valley when they were defeated.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And do not turn back to anyone, that was on the day of Uhud. They went up into the valley fleeing, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was calling them at the back: To the servants of God, to the servants of God!

x: As for Al-Hasan, I think that he went in his reading: When you ascend with the opening of the ta’ and the ‘ayn, to the point that when the people were defeated by the polytheists, they ascended the mountain. A number of the people of interpretation have said that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: “When the polytheists rose up against the Muslims at Uhud and defeated them, some of them entered the city, and some of them set out on the mountain to the rock and stood on it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began calling the al-Nas 114:‘To the servants of God, to the servants of God.’ God mentioned their ascent to the mountain, then He mentioned the supplication of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, and He said: ‘When you ascended and did not turn back to anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you.’”

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They withdrew to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they began to turn away on the mountain, and the Messenger was calling them from behind them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement:
h
When you were ascending and did not look back at anyone
, he said, they ascended to Uhud fleeing.

x: We have mentioned that the first of the two readings is correct, the reading of those who read: When you ascend, with a damma on the ta’ and Surat Al Imran 3:153
h
When you were ascending and did not look back at anyone
, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you.
h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you or what had befallen you. And God is Acquainted with what you do. a kasra on the ‘ayn, meaning: racing and fleeing at ground level or in the descents, because the hujjah has agreed that this is the correct reading. In their consensus on this, there is clear evidence that the first of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of those who said: They ascended into the valley and proceeded in it, rather than the saying of those who said: They turned back on the mountain.
As for his saying:
h
And do not turn to anyone
, he means: Do not turn to anyone among you, and do not turn to one another, fleeing from your enemy ascending into the valley. What he means by his saying:
h
And the Messenger calls you to your rear

, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls you, O believers in him from among his companions, to your rear, meaning: He calls you from behind you: To the servants of God, to the servants of God! Just as: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said: And the Messenger calls you in your afterlife, to the servants of God, return, to the servants of God, return!

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the Messenger calls you to your rear
, they saw the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling them: To me, servants of God!

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: God warned them to flee from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was calling them, and they did not show sympathy for him because of his calling them, so He said: When you were ascending and did not turn back to anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the Messenger calls you to your rear
, this was on the day of Uhud when the people turned away from him.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief
, is: So He rewarded you for fleeing from your Prophet, failing to confront your enemy, and disobeying your Lord, grief for grief, meaning:
h
grief upon grief

. And he called the punishment with which he inflicted upon them, by giving their enemy power over them until he gained from them what he gained a reward, since it was a compensation for their work that angered him and was not pleased with them. Thus, may His praise be glorified, he indicated that every compensation that was given to someone for something of work, whether good or bad, or the compensation that a man gave to a man, or a hand that he extended to him, then it is deserving of the name reward, whether that compensation was an honor or a punishment.

i: Similar to that is the saying of the poet:
x: I fear that Ziyad's gift may have been given to them black or brown.
So he made giving restrictions. This is like what someone says to another who has done something unpleasant to him: I will reward you for your action and give you your reward. As for his saying:
h
Grief upon grief
, it was said:
h
Grief upon grief
, meaning:
h
grief upon grief
, just as it was said: And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees
r
, meaning: And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. This is permissible because the meaning of the speaker’s saying: May God reward you
h
grief upon grief
, is May God reward you grief after grief that preceded it. So the meaning of: So He rewarded you
h
grief upon grief

, because its meaning is: May God reward you grief after grief that preceded it. It is similar to the speaker’s saying: I descended upon the Banu so-and-so, and I descended upon the Banu so-and-so, and I struck him with the sword and on the sword.
The people of interpretation differed about the grief that the people were rewarded for their grief, and what was their first and second grief?

Some of them said: As for the first sorrow, it was what the people were saying, that their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed. As for the other gossip, it was what had befallen them of killing and wounds.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, they were talking on that day that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been wounded, and the other grief was the killing of their companions and the wounds that had befallen them. He said: And it was mentioned to us that seventy men of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were killed on that day, sixty-six men from the Ansar and four from the Muhajireen. And His saying,
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you
, means what you have missed of the spoils of the people, nor what has befallen you, in yourselves of killing and wounds.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So He rewarded you with grief after grief

, he said: One panic after another: the first when they heard the voice that Muhammad had been killed, and the second when the infidels returned, so they struck them as they fled, until they killed seventy men of them, then they withdrew to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they began to climb the mountain, and the Messenger was calling them at the back of them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And others said: Rather, their first grief was because of the killing of those among them who were killed and the wounding of those among them who were wounded. And the second grief was from hearing the voice of the one who said: Muhammad has been killed, because he was bitten by them.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: grief for grief, he said: The first grief was the wounds and killing, and the second grief was when they heard that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed. So the second grief made them forget what had befallen them of wounds and killing, and what they had hoped for of the spoils, and that was when He said:
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you
or over what has befallen you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, he said: The first grief was the wounds and killing, and the second grief was when they heard that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been killed. So the second grief made them forget what had befallen them of wounds and killing, and what they had hoped for of the spoils, and that was when God said:
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you
or over what has befallen you.

x: Others said: Rather, the first grief was the conquest and spoils they had missed, and the second was Abu Sufyan’s supervision of them in the ravine. This is because Abu Sufyan - according to what some of the biographers claim - when he inflicted on the Muslims what he inflicted, and the Muslims fled, he came until he supervised them and among them was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the ravine of Uhud, to which they had fled when they were defeated, and they feared that Abu Sufyan and his companions would crush them. The report mentioned that: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out that day calling the people until he reached the Companions of the Rock. When they saw him, a man put an arrow in his bow and wanted to shoot it, but he said: I am the Messenger of God!

They were happy when they found the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) alive, and the Messenger of God was happy when he saw that there were those among his Companions who could resist. When they gathered and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was among them, and their sorrow had subsided, they began to mention the conquest and what they had missed of it, and to mention their Companions who had been killed. Abu Sufyan approached until he looked down upon them, and when they looked at him, they forgot what they had been doing, and Abu Sufyan was worried. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: They have no right to prevail over us. O God, if you kill this group, you will not be worshipped! Then he called upon his Companions and they threw stones at them until they brought them down. Abu Sufyan said that day: Subdue Hubal!

Hanzala for Hanzala, and one day for another in Badr! And they killed that day Hanzala bin Al-Rahib, who was in a state of ritual impurity, so the angels washed him. And Hanzala bin Abi Sufyan was killed on the day of Badr, and Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar: Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master! Abu Sufyan said: Is Muhammad among you? They said: Yes! He said: Indeed, there was a mutilation among you, which I did not command or forbid, and it did not please me nor did it displease me! Then God mentioned Abu Sufyan’s supervision of them, saying:
h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, that you might not grieve over what escaped you or what befell you. The first grief was what they missed of the spoils and conquest, and the second grief was the enemy’s supervision of them, that you might not grieve over what escaped you, of the spoils, or what befell you, of killing when you remembered.
So Abu Sufyan distracted them.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri narrated to me,
m: and Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and others from our scholars, in what they mentioned from the hadith of Uhud, they said: The Muslims on that day - because of the severe calamity that befell them - were in thirds: a third killed, a third wounded, and a third defeated. The war had reached them until they did not know what to do, until the enemy reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he threw stones until he fell on his side, and his front tooth was injured, and his face was cut, and his lip was wounded. The one who was wounded was Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, and Musʿab ibn Umair fought in defense of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had his standard with him until he was killed. The one who was wounded was Ibn Qumayʿah al-Laythi, and he thought that he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he returned to the Quraysh and said: I have killed Muhammad. Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: The first one to recognize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the defeat and the people saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been killed - as Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said:

c: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri narrated to me
m: - was Kaʿb ibn Malik, the brother of Banu Salamah, he said: I recognized his eyes shining under the helmet, so I called out at the top of my voice: O group of Muslims, be glad, this is the Messenger of Surat Al Imran 3:153
h
When you were ascending and did not look back at anyone
, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you.
h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you or what had befallen you. And God is Acquainted with what you do. God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God motioned to me to be quiet. When the Muslims recognized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they rose up with him, and he rose up towards the ravine, with him were Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafah, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam, and al-Harith ibn al-Summah, with a group of Muslims. He said: While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in the valley with those men from his companions, a high mountain of Quraysh climbed the mountain. “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O God, it is not right for them to climb us!” So Umar ibn al-Khattab and a group of the Muhajireen fought with him until they were forced down from the mountain. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to a rock on the mountain to climb it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had become fat, so he appeared between two coats of mail. When he went to climb but could not, Talha ibn Ubaydullah sat beneath him, so he climbed until he was on top of it. Then, when Abu Sufyan wanted to leave, he looked out over the mountain and shouted at the top of his voice: “Well done! War is a contest, one day for another. Make Hubal victorious.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar: “Get up and answer him, and say: ‘God is higher and more sublime! They are not equal! Our dead are in Paradise and your dead are in Hellfire!’” When Umar, may God be pleased with him, answered Abu Sufyan, Abu Sufyan said to him: Come to me, Umar! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Go to him and see what is wrong with him. So he came to him, and Abu Sufyan said to him: I ask you by God, Umar, did we kill Muhammad? Umar said: By God, no, and he was listening. You are more truthful to me than Ibn Qami’ah and more pious.

c: Ibn Qami’ah told them:
m: I killed Muhammad. Then Abu Sufyan called out and said: There has been an example of your dead, and by God, I am neither pleased nor angry, nor have I forbidden nor commanded.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me:
m: h
So He rewarded you with grief after grief

, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you or what had befallen you, meaning: distress after distress, the killing of those of your brothers who were killed, the dominance of your enemy over you, and what had occurred to you from the saying of those who said: Your Prophet was killed, so that was what had happened to you, grief after grief, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you, of your victory over your enemy after you had seen him with your own eyes, or what had befallen you, of the killing of your brothers, until that distress was relieved from you, and God is Acquainted with what you do, and what relieved them of the distress and grief that had befallen them was that God Almighty repelled from them the lie of Satan by killing their Prophet. When they saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, alive among them, they felt light-hearted about what they had missed from the people after their victory over them, and the calamity that had befallen them in their brothers, when God had averted the killing of their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: The people were afflicted with grief and sorrow over what had befallen them in their companions who had been killed. So when they entered the ravine and they were afflicted, Abu Sufyan and his companions stopped at the gate of the ravine, and the believers thought that they would attack them and kill them as well, so they were afflicted with grief over that as well, which made them forget their grief over their companions. That is what His statement:
h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief that you might not grieve over what had escaped you
, Ibn Jurayj said, His statement: for what had escaped you, means: for what you had missed of the spoils of the people, nor for what had befallen you, in yourselves.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said:
m: Abu Sufyan bin Harb and those with him came and stopped at the ravine, then he called out: Is Ibn Abi Kabsha among the people? They were silent. Abu Sufyan said: He was killed, by the Lord of the Kaaba! Then he said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? They were silent. Then he said: He was killed, by the Lord of the Kaaba! Then he said: Is Umar bin Al-Khattab among the people? They were silent. Then he said: He was killed, by the Lord of the Kaaba! Then Abu Sufyan said: Hubal is exalted, one day for the day of Badr, and Hanzala for Hanzala, and you will find a proverb among the people, it was not according to the opinion of our leaders and best, and we did not dislike it when we saw it! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar bin Al-Khattab: Get up and call out and say: God is Most High and Most Majestic! Yes, this is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is Abu Bakr, and here I am! The companions of Hellfire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the winners. Our dead are in Paradise, and your dead are in Hellfire!

x: Others said about this, including:

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: When you were ascending and not turning back to anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you, so they returned and said: By God, we will come to them and kill them! They have been wounded by us! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Wait, for what has befallen you has only befallen you because you disobeyed me! While they were like that, the people came to them, fully armed and having drawn their swords. So there was the grief of defeat, and their grief when they came to them, so that you would not grieve for what escaped you, of killing, nor for what befell you, of wounds,
h
so He rewarded you with grief for grief
, so that you would not grieve, the verse, and it was the day of Uhud.

x: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting the verse is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of His statement,
h
So He rewarded you with grief for grief

, is, O believers, by God depriving you of the spoils of the polytheists and the victory and triumph over them, and what befell you of killing and wounding on that day - after He had shown you in all of that what you loved - because of your disobedience to your Lord and your opposition to the command of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the grief of your thinking that your Prophet was killed, and the enemy’s turning against you after your remnants from them. What indicates that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse than what contradicts it is His statement:
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you or what has befallen you
. And what has escaped is undoubtedly what they hoped to attain from others, either from victory over them by defeating them, or from spoils that they would seize.

And His statement: nor what has befallen you, is what has befallen them: either in their bodies or in their brothers. If that is the case, then it is known that the second grief has a meaning other than these two. Because God Almighty informed His believing servants from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He rewarded them grief for grief so that they would not be saddened by what befell them of grief arising from what they missed from others, nor by what had befallen them before that in themselves, which is the first grief, as we have explained before. As for his saying:
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you or what has befallen you
, its interpretation is as I have explained, that it is:
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you

, for you did not attain what you were hoping to attain from your enemy by defeating them and prevailing, and taking possession of their spoils, nor what has befallen you, in yourselves, of the wounding of those who were wounded and the killing of those who were killed from among your brothers.
We have mentioned the differences of the people of interpretation regarding it before, regarding the way in which they differed, as:

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you or what has befallen you

, he said: Over what you have missed of the spoils that you were hoping for, and do not grieve over what has befallen you, of defeat. As for His statement: And God is All-Knowing of what you do, He, the Most High, means: God, with regard to what you do, O believers - from your ascent into the valley fleeing from your enemy, your defeat by them, your abandonment of your Prophet while he was calling you in your rear, and your grief over what you have missed from your enemy and what has befallen you in yourselves - is All-Knowing and All-Aware, and He is recording all of that for you, until He rewards you for it: the good among you for his good, and the evildoer for his evil, or He pardons him.

evidence.text: The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Iraq and the Levant, except for Al-Hasan Al-Basri, read it as idh ta’as’dun with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ‘ayn.
This is the reading according to us, because the majority of the reciters have agreed on reading it with this reading, and they have denounced anything that contradicts it.
It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he used to read it: When you ascend, with the opening of the ta’ and the ‘ayn.

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for Al-Hasan, I think that he went in his reading: When you ascend with the opening of the ta’ and the ‘ayn, to the point that when the people were defeated by the polytheists, they ascended the mountain.

Abu Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned that the first of the two readings is correct, the reading of those who read: When you ascend, with a damma on the ta’ and Surat Al Imran 3:153 When you were ascending and did not look back at anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you.
And God is Acquainted with what you do. a kasra on the ‘ayn, meaning: racing and fleeing at ground level or in the descents, because the hujjah has agreed that this is the correct reading.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant: Then God revealed, O believers: after the grief with which your Lord rewarded you after the grief that preceded it, security, which is safety, for the people of sincerity and certainty among you, not the people of hypocrisy and doubt. Then, most of His praise explained, about the security that He bestowed upon them, what it is? He said, sleepy, with the sleepiness in the accusative case as a replacement for the security. Then the reading differed in the reading of his saying: covers. This was read by most of the reciters of Hijaz, Medina, Basra, and some of the Kufians with the masculine ending ya: yaghsha.

A group of Kufian readers read it with the feminine ending: taghasha with the letter taa. Those who read it as a reminder went to the point that drowsiness is what overwhelms the group of believers without security, so he mentioned it as a reminder of drowsiness. Those who read it with the feminine form said that it is the security that covers them, so they feminized it because of the feminization of security.

The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions, and they do not differ in meaning or anything else. Because security in this place is drowsiness, and drowsiness is security. So it is the same, and the reader recites with their verses, then he is correct in his recitation. And likewise all that is in the Qur’an of similar examples, such as His saying: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful, Like molten metal, boiling within the bellies [Ad-Dukhan 43-45] and Was he not a drop of emitted semen? [Al-Qiyamah 37] and And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree, it will fall
r
(Maryam 19:25)

What was the reason for which the two groups mentioned by God Almighty separated in the description in which they separated, so that one of them felt secure in itself until it dozed off, and the other was preoccupied with itself until it thought about God other than the truth, the thought of the ignorant?
The reason for that was what was mentioned to us, as:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “The polytheists turned back on the day of Uhud after what had happened to them and to the Muslims, and they made an appointment with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for Badr the following year. He said, ‘Yes! Yes!’ The Muslims feared that they would descend to Medina, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a man and said, ‘Look, if you see them sitting on their baggage and keeping their horses away, then the people are going. If you see them sitting on their horses and keeping their baggage away, then the people are going to Medina, so fear God and be patient.’ He prepared them for battle. When the Messenger saw them quickly and hastily on their baggage, he called out at the top of his voice that they were going. When the believers saw that, they believed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and slept, while some of the hypocrites remained, thinking that the people were coming to them.” Then God Almighty said, mentioning when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them that if they had ridden the heavy loads, they would be leaving, and they slept: “
h
Then He sent down upon you

, after the distress, security, a drowsiness that overcame a party of you, and another party was concerned about themselves, thinking about God other than the truth - an assumption of the times of ignorance.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: He will make them feel safe on that day because of a drowsiness that will overwhelm them, and only one who feels safe will feel drowsy. It will overwhelm a party of you and another party whose souls are concerned, thinking about God other than the truth - the thought of the times of ignorance.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Talha, he said:
m: I was among those upon whom drowsiness descended on the day of the preparation of security, until it fell from my hand repeatedly.

x: He meant his whip, or his sword.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Abu Talha, he said:
m: I raised my head on the day of Uhud, and I could not see anyone among the people except under his veil, tossing and turning from drowsiness.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Dawud told us, Imran told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Abu Talha, who said:
m: I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the day of Uhud.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Anas bin Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Talha:
m: that he was one of those who were overcome by drowsiness on that day. He said: The sword would fall from my hand, then I would pick it up, from drowsiness.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, on the authority of Anas: That Abu Talha narrated to them: That on that day he was one of those who were overcome by drowsiness. He said: So my sword kept falling from my hand and I would take it, and it would fall and I would take it, and it would fall. The other group, the hypocrites, had no concern but themselves. They thought about God other than the truth, the thought of the times of ignorance, the entire verse.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Hasan Al-Tirmidhi told us, he said, Dharar bin Sard told us, he said, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Miswar bin Makhramah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I asked Abdul Rahman bin Awfi about the statement of God Almighty:
h
Then He sent down upon you
, after the distress, security, drowsiness, he said: He cast sleep upon us on the day of Uhud.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then He sent down upon you

, after the distress, security, drowsiness, the verse, and that was the day of Uhud. On that day they were two groups, but as for the believers, God covered them with drowsiness as security from Him and mercy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: his saying:
h
He cast drowsiness upon them
, he said:
h
He cast drowsiness upon them
, so that was a security for them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Razin, he said, Abdullah said:
m: Drowsiness in battle is a safety, and drowsiness in prayer is from Satan.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
Then He sent down upon you
, after the distress, security, drowsiness. He said: He sent down drowsiness as security from Him upon the people who have certainty in Him, so they are asleep and not afraid.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Surat Al Imran 3:
m: 154 Then, after the distress, He sent down upon you security - a drowsiness that overcame a party of you, and a party who were concerned about themselves, assuming about God other than the truth - an assumption of the times of ignorance. They said, “Do we have any say in the matter?” Say, “Indeed, the matter, all of it, belongs to God.” They conceal within themselves what they do not disclose to you, saying, “If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.” Say, “If you had been in Your houses, so that those upon whom death was decreed may go forth to their beds, and that God may test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts. Qatada, regarding his statement: A security of drowsiness, he said: God made drowsiness fall upon them, so it was a security for them. And he mentioned that Abu Talha said: I was thrown into drowsiness that day, and I would doze off until my sword fell from my hand.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ishaq bin Idris told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Talha,
m: and Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Al-Zubayr, that they both said: We raised our heads on the day of Uhud, and we looked, and there was not one of them except that he leaned to the side of his shield. He said: And he recited this verse:
h
Then He sent down upon you
, after the distress, security, drowsiness.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: And a group of you, O believers, “are concerned about themselves, meaning: They are the hypocrites, they have no concern other than themselves, they are those who fear death for themselves and fear death for them, they are busy, sleep has fled from their eyes, they think false thoughts about God, the thoughts of the ignorant among the polytheists, doubting the command of God, and denying His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and thinking that God will forsake His Prophet and make the people of disbelief in Him superior to him, they say: Do we have any part in the matter! Like that which:- Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: The other group are the hypocrites. They have no concern but themselves. They are the most cowardly, terrifying and neglectful of the truth. They think falsely about God.

They are people of doubt and suspicion regarding God’s command: “They say, ‘If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.’ Say, ‘If you had been in your houses, those for whom killing was decreed would have come forth to their deathbeds.’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said:
m: The other group are the hypocrites, they have no concern except for themselves,
h
they think about God other than the truth

, the thoughts of the ignorant, They say, ‘If we had had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.’ God Almighty said: Say, ‘If you had been in your houses, those upon whom killing was decreed would have come forth to their deathbeds.’

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And a group who are concerned about themselves
, he said: The hypocrites are concerned about themselves because of the fear of being killed, and that is because they do not hope for a consequence.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a group who are concerned about themselves
, to the end of the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites. As for his saying: The pre-Islamic assumption, he means the people of polytheism, such as the one who:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The assumption of the Age of Ignorance
, he said: The assumption of the people of polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The assumption of the Age of Ignorance
, he said: The assumption of the people of polytheism.

x: There are two aspects to the nominative case of his saying: and a group. One of them is that it is raised by the pronoun referring to it in his saying:
h
It has concerned them
. The other: In his saying:
h
They think about God other than the truth

. If it were in the accusative case, it would have been permissible, and the waw in his saying: and a group, would have been an adverb for the verb, meaning: and a group thought about themselves, as he said: And the heaven We constructed with power (al-Dhariyat 51:47).
He means by that the hypocritical group who are concerned about themselves, saying: We have no part in the matter. Say: The matter is entirely up to God.
If we had any part in the matter, we would not have gone out to fight those who fought us and killed us, as:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: It was said to Abdullah bin Ubayy: Banu Khazraj were killed today! He said: Do we have any part in the matter? It was said: The matter is entirely in God’s hands! This is a matter initiated by God Almighty, who says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites: The matter is entirely in God’s hands, He directs it as He wills and manages it as He likes. Then he returned to the report about the hypocrisy of the hypocrites, saying: They hide within themselves what they do not reveal to you. He says: O Muhammad, these hypocrites whose characteristics I have described to you hide within themselves disbelief and doubt in God, what they do not reveal to you.
