Then his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, revealed what they were hiding among themselves of their hypocrisy, and the regret that had befallen them for their presence with the Muslims in their battle at Uhud. He said, informing about their talk of disbelief and their declaration of hypocrisy among themselves: They say, ‘If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here.’ By that he meant that these hypocrites say: If we had gone out to fight the polytheists we went out to fight against, we would not have gone out to them, nor would any of us have been killed in the place where they were killed at Uhud. It was mentioned that among those who said this statement was Mu’tab bin Qushair, the brother of Banu Amr bin Auf. The report mentioned that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said,
m: Ibn Ishaq said, Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of al-Zubayr, he said: By God, I hear the words of Mu’tab ibn Qushayr, the brother of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and drowsiness overcomes me, I hear him only as if it were a dream when he said: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here!

c: Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Yahya bin Ibad bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father,
m: similarly.

x: The reading of this differed. The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: Say that the whole matter is, with the whole in the accusative case as an adjective for the matter and an attribute for it.

Some of the people of Basra read it: Say: The whole matter belongs to God, raising the whole, on the basis of directing the whole to be a name, and his saying to God is its predicate, like the saying of the one who says: The matter is partly for the servant of God. It may be permissible for the whole word to be in the accusative case, in the accusative case as a substitute.

The reading that is the reading according to us is the accusative in all of them, due to the consensus of most of the reciters on it, without the other reading being an error in meaning or Arabic. If the reading in the nominative case in that was widespread in the recitation, then it would be the same to me whichever of the two readings was recited, due to the agreement of the meanings of that in the rest of the two readings.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Say, O Muhammad, to those hypocrites whose description I have described to you: If you had been in your homes, you would not have witnessed their battle with the believers, nor attended with them the war of their enemies from among the polytheists, so that what you were hiding of your hypocrisy and concealing of your doubts about your religion would have become apparent to the believers. Those upon whom death was decreed would have come forth, meaning: those among them upon whom death was decreed would have come forth to the place where his death was decreed, and he would have gone out from his home to it until he was struck down in the place where he was decreed to be struck down. As for his saying:
h
And that God may test what is in your hearts
, he means by it:
h
And that God may test what is in your hearts
, O hypocrites, you used to go forth from your homes to your beds.
What he means by his saying:
h
And that God may test what is in your hearts

, is that God may test what is in your hearts of doubt, and distinguish you - by what He shows the believers of your hypocrisy - from the believers. We have previously demonstrated that the meanings of the words that God may test and that God may know and the like, even if they appear to be attributed to God in the apparent meaning of the statement, are intended to refer to His friends and those who obey Him. The meaning of this is: “And that God may test the friends and those who obey Him of what is in your hearts of doubt and illness, so that they may know you, [and distinguish you] from the people of sincerity and certainty, and that He may purify what is in your hearts,” meaning, “and that He may make clear what is in your hearts of belief in God and in His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the believers of enmity or loyalty.”

And God is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts, meaning: God is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts of His creation of good and evil, faith and disbelief. Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, their secrets and their outward appearances, and He is the Guardian of all of that, until He rewards all of them according to what they deserve.
In a similar vein to what we said about that, Ibn Ishaq used to say:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: God mentioned their blaming - meaning the blaming of the hypocrites - and their regret for what happened to them, then He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If you had been in your homes, you would not have been present in this place where God, may He be glorified and praised, revealed from you what He revealed of your secrets, for He would have brought out those upon whom death was decreed to another place where they would be struck down, so that He might test what is in your hearts, and to purify what is in your hearts, and God is Knowing of that within the breasts, meaning: nothing is hidden from Him in their breasts, of what they concealed from you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Al-Harith bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Bahr Al-Saqqa, on the authority of Amr bin Ubaid,
m: on the Surat Al Imran 3:154 Then, after the distress, He sent down upon you security - a drowsiness that overcame a party of you, and a party who were concerned about themselves, assuming about God other than the truth - an assumption of the times of ignorance. They said, “Do we have any say in the matter?” Say, “Indeed, the matter, all of it, belongs to God.” They conceal within themselves what they do not disclose to you, saying, “If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.” Say, “If you had been in Your houses, so that those upon whom death was decreed may go forth to their beds, and that God may test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts. authority of Al-Hasan, he said: He was asked about His statement: “Say, ‘If you had been in your houses, those upon whom death was decreed would have gone forth to their deathbeds. ’” He said: God has decreed upon the believers that they fight in His cause, and not everyone who fights is killed, but rather those upon whom God has decreed death are killed.

evidence.text: Then the reading differed in the reading of his saying: covers.
This was read by most of the reciters of Hijaz, Medina, Basra, and some of the Kufians with the masculine ending ya: yaghsha.
A group of Kufian readers read it with the feminine ending: taghasha with the letter taa.
Those who read it as a reminder went to the point that drowsiness is what overwhelms the group of believers without security, so he mentioned it as a reminder of drowsiness.
Those who read it with the feminine form said that it is the security that covers them, so they feminized it because of the feminization of security.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is that they are two well-known readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions, and they do not differ in meaning or anything else.
So it is the same, and the reader recites with their verses, then he is correct in his recitation.
He said: And he recited this verse: Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security, drowsiness.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.
The general reading of the Hijaz and Iraq is: Say that the whole matter is, with the whole in the accusative case as an adjective for the matter and an attribute for it.

Some of the people of Basra read it: Say: The whole matter belongs to God, raising the whole, on the basis of directing the whole to be a name, and his saying to God is its predicate, like the saying of the one who says: The matter is partly for the servant of God.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that is the reading according to us is the accusative in all of them, due to the consensus of most of the reciters on it, without the other reading being an error in meaning or Arabic.

If the reading in the nominative case in that was widespread in the recitation, then it would be the same to me whichever of the two readings was recited, due to the agreement of the meanings of that in the rest of the two readings.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Those of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who turned away from the polytheists on the day of Uhud and fled from them. His saying:
h
They turned away
h
they turned away
, from their saying: So-and-so turned his back. His saying:
h
On the day the two armies met

, meaning: on the day the polytheists and Muslims met at Uhud, it was only Satan who caused them to slip, meaning: it was Satan who called them to slip. His saying: He slipped is derived from the verb to slip. A slip is a sin. For some of what they have earned, meaning for some of the sins they committed,
h
and God has pardoned them

, meaning: God has overlooked the punishment for their sins and has forgiven them for them. Indeed, God is Forgiving, meaning: He covers the sins of those who believe in Him and follow His Messenger, by pardoning them for their punishment.

Forbearing, meaning that He is patient and does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him and go against His command. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the notables of the people meant by this verse.
Some of them said: It means everyone who turned his back on the polytheists at Uhud.
Who said that?

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafai told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Asim bin Kulayb told us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Umar delivered a sermon on Friday and recited Al Imran, and he liked to recite it when he preached. When he reached the verse: Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met

, he said: When the day of Uhud came, we defeated them, so I fled until I climbed the mountain. I saw myself running away as if I were a camel, and the people were saying: Muhammad has been killed! I said: I will not find anyone who says: Muhammad has been killed, except that I will kill him! Until we gathered on the mountain, then the verse: Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met
, was revealed, the whole verse.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met

, the verse, and that was on the day of Uhud, we are safe from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they turned back from the fighting and from the Prophet of God on that day, and that was from the matter of Satan and his intimidation, so God Almighty revealed what you hear: that He had pardoned them for that and forgiven them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those among you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met
, the verse, then he mentioned something similar to what Qatada said.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that specifically those who turned their backs on that day. They said: Rather, he meant by that those of them who went to Medina, not others.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When they were defeated that day, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dispersed.

x: Some of them entered the city, and some of them went up the mountain to the rock and stood on it. Then God Almighty mentioned those who were defeated and entered the city, and He said: Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met
, the verse.
Others said: Rather, this was revealed about specific, well-known men.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: Ikrimah said, regarding his statement: Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met
, he said: It was revealed regarding Rafi’ ibn al-Mu’alla and others from the Ansar, and Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah and another man. Ibn Jurayj said: And his statement:
h
It was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned
, but God has already pardoned them, because He did not punish them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Uthman ibn Affan, Uqbah ibn Uthman, and Saʿd ibn Uthman - two men from the Ansar - fled until they reached Al-Jalʿab, a mountain in the vicinity of Madinah, near Al-Aʿwas - and they stayed there for three days, then they Surat Al Imran 3:155 Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met

, it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. And God has already pardoned them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forbearing. returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to them: You have gone too far in it!!

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: his saying: Indeed, those of you who turned back
h
on the day the two armies met

- Satan only caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned verse, and those whom Satan caused to slip were: Uthman ibn Affan, Saʿd ibn Uthman, and Uqbah ibn Uthman, the two Ansars, then the two Zarqas. As for his saying:
h
And God has pardoned them
, its meaning is: And God has pardoned those of you who turned away
h
on the day the two armies met
, that He would not punish them for turning away from their enemy, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, his statement:
h
And God has pardoned them
, means:
h
And God has pardoned them
, because He did not punish them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement about their turning away on the day of UHud 11:
h
And God has pardoned them
, so I do not know whether that pardon is for that group, or pardon for all Muslims? We have previously explained the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forbearing.

evidence.text: Abu Hisham Al-Rafai told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Asim bin Kulayb told us, on the authority of his father, he said: Umar delivered a sermon on Friday and recited Al Imran, and he liked to recite it when he preached.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger and acknowledged what Muhammad brought from God, do not be like those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger, so they denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to their brothers among the disbelievers,
h
When they travel through the land

, and left their country on a journey for trade, or were on a raid, meaning: or their departure from their country was on a raid and they perished and died on their journey, or were killed in their raid, If they had been with us, they would not have died nor been killed, informing of the saying of these disbelievers that they say to those among them who fought and were killed, or died on a journey in which they went out in obedience to God, or for trade: If they had not left us and had stayed in their country, they would not have died nor been killed,
h
so that God may make that a regret in their hearts

, meaning: that they say that, so that God may make their saying that a sorrow and grief in their hearts, and they are ignorant that that is up to God, may He be glorified and exalted. His praise and his hand.
It has been said: Those whom God forbade the believers in this verse from imitating in what He forbade them from of having bad faith in God, are Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and his companions.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told me, he said, Ahmad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites, the companions of Abdullah bin Ubay.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they said to their brothers
when they were travelling in the land or were engaged in war, the statement of the hypocrite Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said about that: They are all hypocrites.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers the verse, meaning: Do not be like the hypocrites who forbid their brothers from jihad in the way of God and from traveling the earth in obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, and they say when they die or are killed: If they had obeyed us, they would not have died and they would not have been killed. As for his saying:
h
When they travel through the land
, there is a difference of opinion regarding its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: It is travelling for trade and walking on the earth to seek a living.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: If they travel the earth, which is trade.

x: Others said: Rather, it is walking in obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: When they travel the earth, traveling the earth in obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger. The origin of striking the ground is to walk far away. As for his saying:
h
Or they were raiders
, he means:
h
Or they were raiders

in the way of God. Ghazi is the plural of Ghaz, the plural of Faʿl, just as Shahid is the plural of Shahid, and Qayil is the plural of Qawl. And the verse of Ruʿbah may be recited: Today I have finished my dream and my first dream is not a foolish one And say: Except for this, there is no this He also chants: And they say: Except for this, there is no such thing It was said:
h
Do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled throughout the land
or were fighting, so the past tense of the verb was accompanied by the letter that is not accompanied with the past tense except the future tense, so it was said:
h
And they said to their brothers
, then it was said: When they traveled, and the speech is said to me: I honored you when you visited me, and it is not said: I honored you when you visited me. Because the statement in His statement:
h
And they said to their brothers

, even if it is in the past tense, it has the meaning of the future. This is because the Arabs use who as a clause, and treat it in that as who and what, due to the similarity of the meanings of that in many things, and that all of them are unknown things that are not timed like the timing of Amr and Zaid. So since that was the case, and it was correct and eloquent in speech to say to a man: Honor whoever honors you and honor every man who honors you, then the speech would be in the past tense with min and kull being unknown and meaning the future, since the one described by the action was not temporary, and those in His statement:
h
Do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled throughout the land

, were not temporary, it was made like min and ma in its translation that follows the method of the penalty, and its connection with the past tense of the verbs was excluded and it has the meaning of the future, as the poet said in ma: I come to you to thank you for what has passed and to fulfill what will be in the future. He said: What was in tomorrow, meaning: What will be in tomorrow. If he had meant the past, he would have said: What was in yesterday, and it would not have been permissible for him to say: What was in tomorrow. If that which was temporary, it would not be permissible to say that. It is wrong to say: You will honor this one who honored you when you visit him, because that which here is temporary, so it has left the meaning of reward. If this were not in the speech, it would have been permissible and eloquent, because that which then becomes unknown is not temporary. And from that is the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God (al-Hajj 22:25), so He responded to avert with disbelieve, because those is not temporary. So His statement: disbelieved, even though it is in the past tense, its meaning is the future. Likewise His statement:
h
Except for those who repent
, believe and do righteous deeds
r
(Maryam 19:60)
, and His statement:
h
Except for those who repent
before you have them in your power (al-Ma’idah 5:34), meaning:
h
except for those who repent
before you have them in your power, and
h
except for those who repent
and believe. There are many similar examples in the Qur’an and speech, but the reason for all of that is the same. As for his saying:
h
So that God may make that a regret in their hearts
, he means by that: sadness in their hearts, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: in their hearts, he said: Their words sadden them, but they do not benefit them at all.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So that God may make that a regret in their hearts
, due to their lack of certainty in their Lord, may His praise be exalted.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
And God gives life and causes death

, is that God hastens death to whomever He wills from wherever He wills, and causes death to whomever He wills whenever He wills, unlike any other of His creation. This is from God Almighty, encouraging His believing servants to fight His enemy and to be patient in fighting them, and to remove their awe from their hearts, even if their number is small and the number of their enemies and the enemies of God is large, and informing them that death and life are in His hand, and that no one will die or be killed except after the end of his appointed time, and forbidding them, since this is the case, to be distressed by the death of those among them who died or were killed in the war with the polytheists. Then He, the Most High, said: And God is Seeing of what you do. He says: God sees what you do of good and evil, so fear Him, O believers, for He is the One who examines all of that, until He rewards every worker for his work according to what he deserves.
Ibn Ishaq said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And God gives life and causes death
, meaning: He hastens what He wills, and delays what He wills of their lives by His power.

evidence.text: And the verse of Ruʿbah may be recited: Today I have finished my dream and my first dream is not a foolish one And say: Except for this, there is no this He also chants: And they say: Except for this, there is no such thing It was said: Do not be like those who disbelieved and said to their brothers when they traveled throughout the land or were fighting, so the past tense of the verb was accompanied by the letter that is not accompanied with the past tense except the future tense, so it was said: And they said to their brothers, then it was said: When they traveled, and the speech is said to me: I honored you when you visited me, and it is not said: I honored you when you visited me.

x: God, the Most High, addresses His believing servants, saying to them: Do not be in doubt, O believers, that all matters are in God's hand, and that to Him belongs life and death, as the hypocrites doubted that, but strive in the cause of God and fight the enemies of God, certain that no one is killed in war or dies in a journey except he who has reached his appointed time and his death has come.

Then He promised them forgiveness and mercy for their striving in His cause, and He informed them that death in the cause of God or being killed in the cause of God is better for them than what they accumulate in this world of its debris and its comfortable life for which they are reluctant to strive in the cause of God and delay meeting the enemy, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And if you are killed in the cause of God or die -
h
forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they accumulate

, meaning: Death is inevitable, so death in the cause of God or being killed is better - if they knew and were certain - than what they accumulate in this world, for which they delay jihad, fearing death and being killed because of what they accumulated of the pleasures of this world, and out of asceticism in the Hereafter.

x: God Almighty said:
h
For forgiveness from God and mercy is better than what they accumulate
, and He began the speech: And if you die or are killed, by deleting the answer to if, because in His saying:
h
For forgiveness from God and mercy is better than what they accumulate
, there is the meaning of an answer to the reward, and that is because it is a promise that came out in the form of a report. The interpretation of the statement:
h
And if you are killed in the way of God or die
, God will surely forgive you and have mercy upon you. He indicated that with his statement:
h
Forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they accumulate
. He combined with the indication of it, the report of the superiority of that over what they prefer of this world and what they accumulate in it.
Some of the Arabists from Basra claimed that if it is said: How can for forgiveness from God and mercy be an answer to his statement:
h
And if you are killed in the way of God or die

? The correct way is to say it as if he said: And if you die or are killed, that is for you mercy from God and forgiveness, since that was in my way, so he said: for forgiveness from God and mercy, meaning: for that is better than what you accumulate, meaning: for that forgiveness and mercy is better than what you accumulate. The letter lam was included in His statement: for forgiveness from God, because it was included in His statement: and if, as it was said: and if they aided them, they would turn their backs (al-Hashr 59:12).
By that, may His praise be exalted, He means:
h
And if you die or are killed

, O believers, then to God is your return and your gathering place, and He will reward you for your deeds. So prefer that which brings you closer to God and brings you closer to His pleasure and brings you closer to Paradise, from jihad in the way of God and working in His obedience, over relying on the world and what you accumulate in it of its debris, which will not remain for you, but will rather vanish from you, and over abandoning the obedience of God and jihad, for that will distance you from your Lord, bring you closer to His wrath, and bring you closer to the Fire.
In a similar vein to what we said about that, Ibn Ishaq said:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And if you die or are killed
, whichever it is,
h
to God you will be gathered

, meaning: to God is the return, so do not let the worldly life deceive you and do not be deceived by it, and let jihad and what God has made you desire from it be more important to you than it. The letter lam was inserted in His statement:
h
To God you will be gathered
, because it was inserted in His statement: And if. If the letter lam had been added after His statement:
h
You will be gathered
, the heavy nun would have been inserted in it, as you say in speech: If you do good to me, I will surely do good to you, with a heavy nun. So it was the same in His statement:
h
And if you die or are killed
, you will surely be gathered to God. But since the lam was prevented from being inserted into the description,
h
You will be gathered
, it was inserted into the description, and
h
You will be gathered
was left intact, so the heavy nun was not inserted into it, as you say in speech: If you do good to me, I will do good to you, without a heavy nun.

x: What God, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
Then by the mercy of God
, is
h
Then by the mercy of God

, and what is a relative pronoun. I have explained how it was included in the speech in His statement: Indeed, God is not ashamed to set forth an example - that of a gnat or anything greater than that (al-Baqarah 2:26). The Arabs make what a relative pronoun in definite and indefinite words, as He said: Then because they broke their covenant (An-Nisa': 155 - al-Ma’idah 5:13), and the meaning is: Then because they broke their covenant. This is in definite words. He said in indefinite words:
In a little while they will become regretful
and the meaning is: In a little while.

i: And sometimes it is made a noun while it is in the manner of a relative pronoun, so what comes after it is sometimes raised in the form of a relative pronoun, and what comes before it is lowered in order to follow the relative pronoun, as the poet said:
x: It is enough for us to have a superiority over others that we love our father, the Prophet Muhammad.

If you make it a non-relative, it is raised by implying huwa, and if you lower it, it is followed by min, so you parse it. So that is its rule as we described with indefinite nouns. If the connection is definite, then the eloquent speech is following, as it was said: Because they broke their covenant. The nominative is permissible in Arabic. And similar to what we said about His statement:
h
So by mercy from God
, you were lenient with them, a group of the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So by mercy from God
, you were lenient with them, he said:
h
So by mercy from God
, you were lenient with them. As for his saying:
h
And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart

, they would have disbanded from around you, he means by rude the harsh, and by harsh in heart the hard-hearted, without mercy or compassion. And this was his description, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God described him: to the believers, kind and merciful (al-Tawbah 9:128). The interpretation of the words: By the mercy of God, O Muhammad, and His compassion for you and those of your companions who believed in you, you were gentle with them, for your followers and your companions, so you made your character easy for them, and your morals were good for them, to the point that you tolerated the harm of those who harmed you, and you pardoned the sinner among them for his sin, and you overlooked many of those who, if you had been harsh with them and been harsh with them, would have left you and departed from you and not followed you or what you were sent with of mercy, but God had mercy on them and had mercy on you with them, so by the mercy of God you were gentle with them, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And if you had been rude and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from around you. Yes, by God, God would have purified him from rudeness and harshness, and made him close, merciful, and compassionate to the believers. And He mentioned to us that the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah is: He is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil with the like of it, but he pardons and forgives.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
So by mercy from God

, you were gentle with them. And if you had been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have disbanded from around you,” he said: He mentioned his gentleness with them and his patience with them, due to their weakness and their lack of patience with harshness if it had been from him, in everything in which they disobeyed what was required of them in terms of obeying their Prophet. As for his saying:
h
They would have dispersed from around you
, he means: They would have dispersed from you, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Ibn Abbas said, regarding his statement:
h
They would have dispersed from around you
, he said: They would have turned away from you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
They would have dispersed from around you
, meaning: they would have left you.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
So pardon them

, so pardon, O Muhammad, your followers and your companions who believe in you and in what you have brought from Me, for whatever harm they have done to you and whatever is disliked in your soul, and ask forgiveness for them, and supplicate to your Lord for forgiveness for them for the crime they have committed, for which they have deserved punishment from Him, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So pardon them

, meaning: overlook them, and seek forgiveness for them, the sins of those who committed them from the people of faith among them. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning for which God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult them, and what is the meaning for which He commanded him to consult them?

x: Some of them said: God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying:
h
And consult them in the matter

, to consult his companions in the plots of war and when meeting the enemy, in order to please them and to reconcile them in their religion, and so that they would see that he listens to them and seeks their help, even though God Almighty has made him independent of them - by managing his affairs, governing him, and correcting his causes.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And consult them in the matter

. And when you have decided, then rely upon God. Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him].” God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult his companions in matters when the revelation from heaven comes to him, because it is better for the souls of the people, and that if the people consult each other and want thereby the pleasure of God, He will resolve for them what is most right.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
And consult them in the matter
. He said: God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult his companions in matters while the revelation came to him from heaven, because it was better for their souls.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And consult them in the matter
, meaning: to show them that you listen to them and seek their help, even if you are independent of them, and thereby bring them together in their religion.

x: Others said: Rather, He ordered him to do that in that regard, to clarify to him the opinion and the most correct matters in management, because of the knowledge of the Most High in consultation of the virtue mentioned.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And consult them in the matter
, he said: God Almighty did not command His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult, except because He knew of its virtue.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Iyas bin Daghfal, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: No people have ever consulted except that they were guided to the most correct of their affairs.

x: Others said: God commanded him to consult his companions in what He commanded him to consult them in, while he was independent of their opinions through his correction of it and his management of its causes, so that the believers would follow him after him in what troubled them in the matter of their religion, and follow his example in that, and imitate the example that they saw him do in his life of consulting his companions in his affairs - with the status he has with God - and following him in the matter that he brings down to them in the matter of their religion and their worldly affairs, so they would consult among themselves and then issue what their leaders agreed upon. Because if the believers consult each other in the matters of their religion, following the truth in that, God the Almighty will not be without His kindness and His success in the correct opinion and statement in it.
They said: This is similar to His statement, the Almighty, with which He praised the people of faith: And their affairs are by consultation among themselves (al-Shura 42:38).
Who said that?

c: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us that Sufyan bin Uyaynah said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And consult them in the matter
, he said: It is for the believers to consult about what has not come to them from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in it.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard is to say: God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult his companions regarding the affairs of his enemy and the plots of his war, in order to win over those who did not have the insight into Islam that would protect them from the temptations of Satan, and Surat Al Imran 3:159
h
So by mercy from God
, you are gentle with them.
h
And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart
, they would have disbanded from around you.
h
So pardon them
and ask forgiveness for them
h
and consult them in the matter

. And when you have decided, then rely upon God. Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him]. to inform his nation of the origin and purpose of the matters that would afflict them after him, so that they would follow his example in that when calamities befall them, and consult among themselves, as they used to see him doing during his lifetime.

As for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed him of the purposes and aspects of the matters that afflicted him through His revelation or inspiration to him, and the correctness of that. As for his nation, if they consulted, they would follow his actions in that, in friendship and brotherhood for the sake of the truth, and all of them would desire what is right, without inclination to whims or deviating from guidance, so God is their guide and their successor. As for his saying:
h
So when you have decided

, then put your trust in God, it means: If your determination is sound because of our strengthening you and our guiding you in what befalls you and your affairs of religion and your worldly life, then proceed with what we have commanded you to do, as we have commanded you, whether that agrees with the opinions of your companions and what they have advised you to do, or contradicts them, and put your trust in your Lord in whatever you do of your affairs and leave, and try or undertake, so trust in Him in all of that, and be satisfied with His judgment in all of it, without the opinions of the rest of His creation and their assistance, Indeed, God loves those who put their trust, and they are those who are satisfied with His judgment and submit to His rule over them, whether that agrees with their desires or contradicts them, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So when you have decided
, then put your trust in God. Indeed, God loves those who put their trust in Him.”
h
So when you have decided

, that is, on a matter that came to you from me, or a matter of your religion in jihad against your enemy that will not benefit you or them except that, then proceed with what you have been commanded to do, in opposition to those who disagree with you and in agreement with those who agree with you, and put your trust in God, that is, be satisfied with Him among the servants, for God loves those who put their trust in Him.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when you have decided
, then rely upon God, God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he decided on a matter, to go ahead with it, adhere to God’s command, and rely upon God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when you have decided
, then rely upon God, the verse, God commanded him, if he decided on a matter, to go ahead with it and rely on Him.

x: God Almighty means by that: If God helps you, O believers in God and His Messenger, against those who oppose and are hostile to you from among His enemies and disbelievers in Him, no one can overcome you, from among the people, meaning: No one can overcome you with His help for you, even if all His creation gathered against you from all corners of the earth. So do not fear the enemies of God due to your small number and their large number, as long as you are upon His command and steadfast in obeying Him and His Messenger, for victory and triumph are yours, without them. And if He forsakes you, who is there to help you after Him? Meaning: If your Lord forsakes you by disobeying His command and abandoning His obedience and the obedience of His Messenger, He leaves you to yourselves, who is there to help you after Him? He says: So despair of the help of the people, for you will not find [a helper] after God forsakes you.

If He forsakes you, He says: Do not abandon My command, my obedience, and the obedience of my Messenger, so you will perish because of my abandonment of you. And in God let the believers put their trust.

That is: But in your Lord, O believers, put your trust without the rest of His creation, and be satisfied with Him over all those besides Him, and submit to His judgment, and strive in it against His enemies, and He will suffice you with His help, and extend to you His victory, as:

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: If God helps you, none can overcome you; but if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? And in God let the believers put their trust. That is, if God helps you, none can overcome you among the people - the abandonment of those who forsake you will not harm you, and if He forsakes you, the people will not help you. Then who is there that can help you after Him? That is, do not leave my affair to the people, and abandon [the affair of] the people to my affair, and in God, [not in the people], let the believers put their trust.

x: There are different readings of this.
A group of reciters from Hijaz and Iraq read it as:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

, meaning: to betray his companions in the wealth of their enemies that God has bestowed upon them. Some reciters of this reading argued that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding a quilt that was lost from the spoils of war on the day of Badr. Some of those who were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Perhaps the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took it!
They narrated narrations about this, including the following:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Khasif narrated to us, saying: Muqsim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abbas narrated to me:
m: This verse:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, was revealed concerning a red cloak that was lost on the day of Badr. He said: Some people said: He took it! They talked a lot about that, then God the Almighty revealed: “
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he took on the Day of Resurrection.”

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said,
m: I asked Saeed bin Jubair: How do you read this verse:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
or: take spoils of war? He said: No, rather take spoils of war, for the Prophet, by God, used to take spoils of war and kill.

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

, he said: That was about a red quilt that was lost in the Battle of Badr, and some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps the Prophet took it! So God Almighty revealed:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, Saeed said: Yes, by God, the Prophet takes spoils of war and is killed.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Khallad told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A velvet garment was lost on the day of Badr, and they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it. Then God Almighty revealed:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Malik bin Ismail told us, he said, Zuhair told us, he said, Khasif told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

, they said: Take spoils of war. Ikrimah or someone else said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: There was a velvet garment that was lost on the day of Badr, and they said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it! He said: So God revealed this verse:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, Yazid told us, Qaza’ah bin Suwaid al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Hamid al-A’raj, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, who said:
m: This verse was revealed:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, regarding a red cloak that was lost on the day of Badr from the spoils.

c: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told us, he said, Mu'tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sulayman Al-A'mash, he said:
m: Ibn Mas'ud used to recite:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

, so Ibn Abbas said: Yes, and to be killed. Ibn Abbas said: "So it was in a piece of cloth. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it on the day of Badr." So God revealed:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

x: Others who read it in this way, with the opening of the ya’ and the closing of the ghayn, said: This verse was revealed about the vanguards whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was facing. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the spoils and did not divide them among the vanguards. So God Almighty revealed this verse to His Prophet, may God bless him Surat Al Imran 3:161
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils

. And whoever takes spoils will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged. and grant him peace, informing him that what he did was wrong, and that what was obligatory upon him in the ruling was to divide among the vanguards as he divided among others, and informing him of what was obligatory upon him in the ruling regarding the spoils that God bestowed upon him, and that he does not have the right to single out anyone who witnessed the battle - or who was a support to them in their conquest - over anyone else.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he took on the Day of Resurrection,” meaning: It is not for a prophet to divide among a group of Muslims and leave out a group and be unjust in the division, but he should divide with justice, and take it according to the command of God, and rule in it according to what God has revealed. He says: God would not make a prophet who would take spoils of war from his companions, so if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that, then they would follow his example.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: that he used to recite:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, he said: to give some and leave some, if he acquired spoils.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a scout group, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took spoils, but he did not divide them among the scouts, so God Almighty revealed: It is not for a prophet to take spoils.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: It was not for a prophet to take spoils of war, meaning: It was not for a prophet to divide among a group of his companions and leave out a group, but rather he should be just and take into account the command of God Almighty, and rule in it according to what God has revealed.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, he said: It is not for him, if he acquires spoils, to divide them among some of his companions and leave some, but to divide them equally among them.

x: Others who read it with the opening of the ya’ and the closing of the ghayn said: This was revealed to inform the people that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not conceal anything from God’s revelation.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “And it is not for a prophet to conceal from the people what God sent him with, out of fear of the people or desire, and whoever does that will bring it on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” That is, it is not for a prophet to conceal from the people what God sent him with, out of fear of the people or desire, and whoever does that will bring it on the Day of Resurrection.

x: The interpretation of whoever reads it in this way is: It is not appropriate for a prophet to be a traitor - meaning that it is not among the actions of the prophets to betray their nations. It is said: The man cheated, so he cheats, if he betrayed, cheating. It is also said: The man cheated, so he cheated, cheating, as Shuraih said: The borrower who is not a cheater is not liable, meaning: the one who is not a traitor. It is also said: The butcher cheated, if he stole some of the meat along with the skin. And what we said about that came the interpretation of the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: It was not appropriate for a prophet to betray, meaning: It was not appropriate for him to betray, so just as it was not appropriate for him to betray, do not betray.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, he said: to betray.

x: Others read it as: And it was not for a prophet to take spoils of war, with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ghayn. This is the reading most widely recited by the people of Medina and Kufa. Readers of this also differed in their interpretation of it.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: It is not for a prophet to be betrayed by his companions. Then he omitted the companions, so the verb remained without its subject being named. Its interpretation is: It is not for a prophet to be betrayed.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: that he used to recite:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils
, Aouf said, Al-Hasan said: To be betrayed.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

, meaning: And it is not for a prophet to be taken spoils of war by his believing companions who are with him - he mentioned to us this verse that was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, and groups of his companions had taken spoils of war.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, he said: that his companions should take spoils of war from him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war
, al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said:
h
It is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

from his companions who are with him. He said: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that this verse was revealed to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, and groups of his companions had taken spoils of war.

x: Others among them said: The meaning of this is: It is not for a prophet to be accused of embezzlement, so that he would betray and steal. And the interpreters of this were like that, they directed his statement:
h
It is not for a prophet to embezzle

, to the meaning of it: embezzles, then the ‘ayn was lightened from yaf’al, so it became yaf’al as was read by those who read his statement: For they do not deny you (al-An’am 6:33), with the interpretation: they deny you.
The most correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

, meaning: spoils of war are not among the attributes of prophets, and a prophet cannot be one who takes spoils of war. We chose this because God the Almighty threatened those who commit treachery after His statement:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils

, saying: And whoever takes spoils will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection, and the verse that follows it. So in His threat after that to those who commit treachery, there is clear evidence that He only forbade treachery, and informed His servants that treachery is not one of the characteristics of His prophets by His statement:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils

. Because if He only forbade the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from accusing the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) of treachery, He would have followed that with a threat for the accusation and bad opinion of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), not a threat for treachery.

And in His following that with a threat for treachery, there is a clear statement that He only made known to the believers and other than His servants that treachery is absent from the characteristics and morals of the prophets, because that is a great crime, and the prophets do not commit such a thing. If someone who reads it in this way says: It is more appropriate than: And it is not for a prophet that his companions should betray him, if that is as you mentioned, and God did not follow up His statement:
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils except with a threat against taking spoils

, but it is only necessary to rule that it is correct because of the reading of the one who reads: yaghl with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the ghain, because the meaning of that is: And it is not for a prophet that his companions should take spoils of war and betray him in the spoils? It was said to him: Was it possible for them to betray anyone other than the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they were specifically prohibited from betraying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace?

Yes, then they have left the statement of the people of Islam, because God has never permitted betrayal of anyone in the statement of any of the people of Islam. If someone says: They did not have that in any prophet or anyone else.

What is the reason for their being singled out, then, for the prohibition of betraying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his embezzlement and the embezzlement of some Jews, in the same way that God has forbidden the embezzler from their money, and what is required of the trustee in fulfilling the trust to them? And since that is the case, it is known that the meaning of that is what we said, that God Almighty denied that treachery and betrayal were among the characteristics of His prophets, forbidding His servants from treachery, and commanding them to follow the example of their prophet, as Ibn Abbas said in the narration that we mentioned from the narration of Atiyah, then God Almighty followed up His prohibition of treachery with a threat against him, saying: And whoever commits treachery will come with what he has stolen on the Day of Resurrection, both verses together.

By that, the Most High means: And whoever betrays any of the spoils of the Muslims, their booty, or anything else, he will be brought on the Day of Resurrection in the place of assembly, as: Abu Kuraib narrated:

c: Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed Abi Hayyan, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace: “He stood up as a preacher and preached and reminded, then he said: ‘Is it possible that a man among you will come on the Day of Resurrection with a bleating sheep on his neck, saying: O Messenger of God, help me!’ But I will say: ‘I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you! Is it possible that a man among you will come on the Day of Resurrection with a neighing horse on his neck, saying: O Messenger of God, help me!’ But I will say: ‘I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you! Is it possible that a man among you will come on the Day of Resurrection with a silent horse on his neck, saying: O Messenger of God, help me!’ But I will say: ‘I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you! Is it possible that a man among you will come on the Day of Resurrection with a cow mooing on his neck, saying: O Surat Al Imran 3:161
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils

. And whoever takes spoils will bring what he took on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged. Messenger of God, help me!’ But I will say: ‘I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you!’ On the Day of Resurrection, there will be fluttering papers around his neck, and he will say: O Messenger of God, help me! I will say: I have no power to do anything for you, I have conveyed the message to you!

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, like this, and he added to it: I do not want to find any of you with a soul on his neck screaming.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Abu Hayyan told us, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us one day and mentioned theft, and he made it very serious and its matter very serious, and he said: ‘I do not want to find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a roaring camel on his neck, saying: O Messenger of God, help me.’” Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Abd al-Rahman.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Hafs bin Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Yaqub al-Qummi, he said, Hafs bin Hamid narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a bleating sheep calling out: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! I will say: I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a braying camel calling out: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! I will say: I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you. I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a neighing horse calling out: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! I will say: I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’ I do not know any one of you who will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying a leather husk calling out: O Muhammad! O Muhammad! I will say: I have no power over God for you, I have conveyed the message to you.”

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Asbat bin Muhammad narrated to us, he said, Abu Ishaq Al-Shaibani narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dhakwan, on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Abu Hamid, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a collector of alms, and he came back with a large quantity of black money. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent someone to collect it from him. When they came to him, he began to say: This is for me, and this is for you. They said: Where did you get this from? He said: It was given to me! So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that. So he went out and delivered a sermon, saying: O people, why do I send people to collect alms, and one of them comes back with a large quantity of black money, and when I send someone to collect it, he says: This is for me, and this is for you! If he is truthful, should I not give him a gift while he is in his father’s house or in his mother’s house? Then he said: O people, whoever we send to do a job and he steals something, he will come on the Day of Resurrection with it on his neck, carrying it. So fear God, lest one of you come on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck, roaring, or…” A cow bellowing, or a sheep bleating.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said,
m: Abu Muawiyah, Ibn Numayr and Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hamid al-Sa’idi, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed a man from Azd called Ibn al-Atbiyyah to collect the alms of Banu Salim. When he came, he said: ‘This is for you, and this is a gift that was given to me.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Why does not one of you sit in his house and receive his gift?’ Then he praised God and extolled Him, then said: ‘As for what follows, I appoint men from among you to handle matters that God has entrusted me with, and one of them says: ‘This is for you, and this is a gift that was given to me! Why does he not sit in his father’s house or his mother’s house and receive his gift?’ By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none of you takes anything from that except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck. So I do not know when a man comes carrying a camel that is bellowing, or a cow that is mooing, or a sheep that is bleating!’ Then he raised his hand and said: ‘Have I not conveyed the message?’”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abd al-Rahim told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hamid,
m: he told him a similar hadith, he said: Why didn’t you sit in the house of your father and mother until your gift came to you? Then he raised his hand until I could see the whiteness of his armpits, then he said: O God, have I conveyed the message? Abu Hamid said: My eyes see and my ears hear.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying, my uncle Abd God ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, that Musa ibn Jubayr narrated to him, that Abd God ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Habbab al-Ansari narrated to him, that Abd God ibn Unais narrated to him, that
m: he and Umar were discussing charity one day, and he said, Did you not hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he mentioned the embezzlement of charity: Whoever embezzles a camel or a sheep from it, he will carry it on the Day of Resurrection? Abd God ibn Unais said: Yes.

c: Saeed ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying, my father narrated to us, saying, Yahya ibn Saeed al-Ansari narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah as a collector of charity, and he said: Beware, Saʿd, of coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel carrying it bellowing for him! He said: I will neither take it nor bring it! So he pardoned him. Ahmad bin Al-Mughira Al-Himsi Abu Hamid narrated, Al-Rabi bin Ruh narrated, Ibn Ayyash narrated, Ubaidullah bin Umar bin Hafs narrated, on the authority of Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: That he appointed Sa’d bin Ubadah, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and greeted him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Beware, Sa’d, of coming on the Day of Resurrection carrying a roaring camel on your neck! Sa’d said: If I do that, O Messenger of God, will that happen? He said: Yes! Sa’d said: I know, O Messenger of God, that I ask and am given! So pardon me. So he pardoned him. Abu Kuraib narrated, Zaid bin Habban narrated, Abdurrahman bin Al-Harith narrated, my grandfather Ubaid bin Abi Ubaid - who was the first person born in Madinah - narrated: I was appointed to collect the Zakat of the tribe of Daws, and Abu Hurairah came to me on the day I went out and greeted me. So I went out to him and greeted him, and he said: How are you with the camel? How are you with the cow? How are you with the sheep? Then he said: I heard my beloved the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever takes a camel unjustly will bring it on the Day of Resurrection roaring. Whoever takes a cow unjustly will bring it on the Day of Resurrection mooing. Whoever takes a sheep unjustly will bring it on the Day of Resurrection on his neck bleating. So beware of cows, for they have sharp horns and sharp hooves.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, he said, Muhammad told me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith, on the authority of his grandfather Ubayd bin Abi Ubayd, he said:
m: I was appointed over the charity of Daws, and when I had finished the work I came back, and Abu Hurayrah came to me and greeted me and said: Tell me, how are you and the camels? Then he mentioned something similar to what Hudhayfah narrated on the authority of Zayd, except that he said: He will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with it roaring on its neck.
b.via: his grandfather Ubayd bin Abi Ubayd

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war

. And whoever takes spoils of war will come with what he took on the Day of Resurrection,” Qatada said: “Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took spoils of war, he would send out a crier: ‘Let no man take a needle or anything less than that of war, let no man take a camel and bring it on his back on the Day of Resurrection, roaring with it, let no man take a horse and bring it on its back on the Day of Resurrection, neighing with it.’”

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
Then every soul will be paid in full

, then every soul will be given the recompense for what it earned by its earnings, in full and without any reduction in what it deserved and deserved from that, and they will not be wronged, meaning: nothing will be done to them except what should be done to them, without transgression against them so that they are reduced from what they deserved, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. Then he will be rewarded for what he has earned, neither wronged nor transgressed against.

evidence.text: A group of reciters from Hijaz and Iraq read it as: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, meaning: to betray his companions in the wealth of their enemies that God has bestowed upon them.

Some reciters of this reading argued that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding a quilt that was lost from the spoils of war on the day of Badr.

Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us, he said, Abdul Wahid told us, he said, Khasif told us, he said, I asked Saeed bin Jubair: How do you read this verse: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war or: take spoils of war?

Others who read it in this way, with the opening of the ya’ and the closing of the ghayn, said: This verse was revealed about the vanguards whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was facing.

Others who read it with the opening of the ya’ and the closing of the ghayn said: This was revealed to inform the people that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not conceal anything from God’s revelation.

Abu Jaafar said: The interpretation of whoever reads it in this way is: It is not appropriate for a prophet to be a traitor - meaning that it is not among the actions of the prophets to betray their nations.
Others read it as: And it was not for a prophet to take spoils of war, with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the ghayn.
This is the reading most widely recited by the people of Medina and Kufa.
Readers of this also differed in their interpretation of it.

And the interpreters of this were like that, they directed his statement: It is not for a prophet to embezzle, to the meaning of it: embezzles, then the ‘ayn was lightened from yaf’al, so it became yaf’al as was read by those who read his statement: For they do not deny you (al-An’am 6:33), with the interpretation: they deny you.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, meaning: spoils of war are not among the attributes of prophets, and a prophet cannot be one who takes spoils of war.

If someone who reads it in this way says: It is more appropriate than: And it is not for a prophet that his companions should betray him, if that is as you mentioned, and God did not follow up His statement: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils except with a threat against taking spoils, but it is only necessary to rule that it is correct because of the reading of the one who reads: yaghl with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the ghain, because the meaning of that is: And it is not for a prophet that his companions should take spoils of war and betray him in the spoils?

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that: Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Is he who pursues the pleasure of God by abandoning theft like he who incurs the wrath of God by his theft?
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So whoever pursues the pleasure of God
, he said: whoever does not commit adultery, is like one who incurs the wrath of God, like one who commits adultery.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told me, on the authority of Mutraf bin Tarif, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So whoever pursues the pleasure of God
he said: whoever pays the fifth, is like one who incurs the wrath of God, so he deserves the wrath of God.

x: Others said about it, including:

c: Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
So whoever pursues the pleasure of God

, in what people like and dislike, is like one who incurs the wrath of God, in the pleasure and displeasure of people? He says: So whoever is obedient to Me, his reward is Paradise and the pleasure of his Lord, like one who incurs the wrath of God, thus deserving His wrath, and whose abode is Hell, and what an evil destination? Are these two examples worse? That is: So know.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of the verse in my opinion is the statement of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim. Because that follows God’s threat against embezzlement and His prohibition of it to His servants. Then He said to them after His prohibition and threat: Is the one who obeys God in what He has commanded and prohibited worse than the one who disobeys Him in that? That is, they are not equal, and their states are not equal before Him. Because the one who obeys God in what He has commanded and prohibited will go to Paradise, and the one who disobeys Him in what He has commanded and prohibited will go to Hell. So the meaning of His statement:
h
So whoever pursues the pleasure of God is like one who incurs the wrath of God

, is: So whoever abandons embezzlement and the sins that God has prohibited him from, and acts in obedience to God in abandoning that, and in other obligatory duties that He has commanded and prohibited him to do, pursuing the pleasure of God in all of that and avoiding His wrath, is like one who incurs the wrath of God, meaning: like the one who turns away bearing the wrath and anger of God, and thus deserves to reside in Hell?
He says: They are not the same. As for his saying:
h
And an evil destination
, he means:
h
And an evil destination
- to which he who incurs the wrath of God will go and return - is Hell.
God Almighty means by that: Whoever pursues the pleasure of God and whoever incurs the wrath of God, will have different positions with God.
For whoever pursues the pleasure of God, there is honor and great reward, and for whoever incurs the wrath of God, there is humiliation and painful punishment, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: They have degrees with God, and God is All-Seeing of what they do, meaning: for each there are degrees of what they did in Heaven and Hell, for God does not hide from the people who obey Him from the people who disobey Him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: They have degrees with God, he says: according to their deeds.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They have degrees with God, meaning: For those who seek God’s pleasure, there are noble positions with God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They are degrees with God
, he said: It is like his statement:
h
They are degrees with God

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They have degrees with God, meaning: They have degrees with God. It was said: His saying,
h
They are degrees

, is like the saying of someone: They are classes, as Ibn Harmah said: Will my people be stoned to death by the vicissitudes of time, or by the torrents? As for his saying: And God is Seeing of what they do, it means: God is All-Knowing of what those who obey and disobey Him do. Nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him. He counts the deeds of both groups, until each soul is given the reward for what it has earned of good and evil, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God is All-Seeing of what they do, meaning: God does not hide from the people who obey Him from the people who disobey Him.
