x: By that he means: God has been long-winded with the believers, when He sent among them a Messenger, when He sent among them a Messenger, from among themselves, a Prophet from among the people of their language, and He did not make him from among those who were not from among their language so that they would not understand what he was saying, reciting to them His verses, meaning: He recites to them the verses of His Book and His revelation, and purifies them, meaning: He cleanses them from their sins by following Him and obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, meaning: He teaches them the Book of God that He revealed to him, and explains to them its interpretation and meanings, and wisdom, meaning by wisdom, the Sunnah that God, the Most High, has established for the believers through the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His explanation to them, and they were before in manifest error, meaning: and they were before God bestowed His favor upon them by sending His Messenger who has this description, in manifest error, meaning: in ignorance. Ignorant, blindly confused about guidance, they do not know the truth, nor do they reject falsehood.

We have previously explained the origin of misguidance, which is taking without guidance, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. And the clear one, who shows to whoever contemplates it with his mind and ponders it with his understanding, that he is not on the right path or guidance.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
God has conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves

, God conferred a great favor upon them without this nation’s invitation or desire. God made him a mercy to them to bring them out of darkness into the light and guide them to a straight path. His saying:
h
And to teach them the Book and wisdom

, wisdom, the Sunnah, in if they were before in manifest error, it is not, by God, as the people of Harura say: an overwhelming trial, whoever misses it will have his blood shed, but God sent His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a people who do not know, so he taught them, and to a people who have no manners, so he punished them.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: God has conferred a great favor upon the believers, until His saying: in manifest error, meaning: God has conferred a great favor upon you, O people of faith, when He sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves who recites to you His verses and purifies you in what you have innovated and in what you have done, and teaches you good and evil, so that you may know good and do it, and evil and avoid it, and informs you of His pleasure with you if you obey Him, so that you may increase your obedience to Him and avoid what He is angry with you in disobeying Him, so that you may be freed from His wrath and attain His reward from His Paradise, while they were before in manifest error, meaning: in blindness from ignorance, not knowing good nor seeking forgiveness for bad, deaf to the truth, blind to guidance.

x: God Almighty means by that: When a calamity befell you, O believers, - namely, the dead who were killed among them on the day of Uhud, and the wounded who were wounded among them at Uhud - and the polytheists killed seventy of them that day - you have suffered twice as much, meaning: You, O believers, have suffered from the polytheists twice as much as this calamity that they have suffered from you, and it is the calamity that the Muslims suffered from the polytheists at Badr, and that is that they killed seventy of them and took seventy captive, you said, 'How is this?' meaning: you said when your calamity befell you at Uhud, How is this?, from what aspect is this? And from where did this that befell us befall us, and we are Muslims and they are polytheists, and among us is the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to whom revelation comes from the heaven, and our enemies are people of disbelief in God and polytheism?

Say, O Muhammad, to your believing companions, It is from yourselves, meaning: Say to them: What has befallen you has come upon you from yourselves, because you disobeyed My command and abandoned My obedience, not from anyone else, nor from anyone other than you. Indeed, God is over all things competent, meaning: God is over all that He wills for His creation of forgiveness and punishment, favor and vengeance. Powerful, meaning: He has power. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement: “Say: It is from yourselves,” after all of them agreed that the interpretation of the rest of the verse is based on what we said about that interpretation.

Some of them said: The interpretation of that is: “Say: It is from yourselves,” unlike you with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he advised you to stop going out to your enemy and to go out to them in the morning until they enter your city and are among your roofs, but you refused that and said: Let us go out to them so that we can go out to them in the morning and fight them outside the city.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Or when a disaster befell you

, although you had inflicted twice as much, you said, ‘From where is this?’ They were afflicted on the Day of Uhud, seventy of them were killed that day, and they inflicted twice as much on the Day of Badr, they killed seventy of the polytheists and captured seventy. You said, ‘From where is this?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the Day of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan and the polytheists came, “Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: ‘I am in a fortified garden,’ meaning Medina, so invite the people to enter upon us so that we may fight them. Some of his companions from the Ansar said to him: ‘O Prophet of God, we hate to be killed in the vicinity of Medina, and we used to refrain from fighting during the Jahiliyyah, so with Islam it is more appropriate for us to refrain from it!’ So bring us out to the people. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out and dressed for his nation, and the people blamed each other and said: ‘The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has presented a matter and you have presented it.’” Hamza came and said to him: O Prophet of God, the people have blamed each other and said: A command, not your command. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not for a prophet who wears it for his nation to put it down until he fights, and there will be a calamity among you. They said: O Prophet of God, specific or general? He said: You will see it. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in a dream that cows were being slaughtered, and he interpreted it as killing among his companions. He saw that his sword, Dhu al-Ghifar, was broken, and it was the killing of his uncle Hamza, who was killed that day, and he was called: The Lion of God. He saw that a ram was cut, and he interpreted it as the ram of the battalion, Uthman ibn Abi Talha, who was killed that day, and he was with the banner of the polytheists.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly, except that he said: You have inflicted twice as much, meaning: As much as you have inflicted. “You said, ‘From where is this?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves,’” meaning: Because of your disobedience.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Muʿmar informed us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: who Surat Al Imran 3:165
h
Or when a disaster befell you

, although you had inflicted twice as much, you said, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves." Indeed, God is over all things competent. said: The Muslims were afflicted with a calamity on the Day of Uhud, and they had inflicted twice as much on the Day of Badr, among those killed and taken prisoner. Then God, the Almighty, said:
h
Or when a disaster befell you
, you inflicted twice as much.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Umar ibn Ata’, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: The Muslims killed seventy polytheists on the day of Badr and took seventy captive, and the polytheists killed seventy Muslims on the day of Uhud. This is what His statement, “
h
You have inflicted double

that. You said, ‘From where is this?’” is because we are Muslims, fighting all together for the sake of God, and these are polytheists. Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ This is a punishment for you for disobeying the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said, What?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Or when a disaster befell you

, although you had inflicted twice as much, you said, ‘From where is this?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ They said: This only befell us when we accepted ransom on the day of Badr from the prisoners, and we disobeyed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud. So whoever among us was killed was a martyr, and whoever among us remained was purified. We are pleased with our Lord!

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj, they said:
m: Their disobedience was that he said to them: Do not follow them, on the day of Uhud, so they followed them.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Then he mentioned what was afflicted among the believers - meaning at Uhud - and seventy people were killed -
h
Or when a disaster struck you

, although you had inflicted twice as much, they were on the day of Badr, they had taken seventy men prisoner and killed seventy, You said, ‘From where is this?’ meaning: From where is this? Say, ‘It is from yourselves,’ that you disobeyed.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Or when a disaster struck you
, you had inflicted double thereof, meaning: You inflicted on the polytheists on the day of Badr twice as much as they inflicted on you on the day of Uhud.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Then he mentioned the calamity that befell them and said:
h
Or when a disaster befell you

, although you had inflicted twice as much, you said, ‘From where is this?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ That is, if a disaster befell you among your brothers, then because of your sins, you had inflicted twice as much before from your enemy, on the day before it at Badr, in dead and captured, and you forgot your disobedience and your opposition to what your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had commanded you to do. You made that permissible for yourselves, Indeed, God is over all things competent. That is, God is capable of everything He intends for His servants, whether punishment or forgiveness.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Or when a disaster struck you
, you had inflicted double thereof, the verse, meaning by that: That you inflicted on the polytheists on the day of Badr twice as much as they inflicted on you on the day of Uhud.

x: Some of them said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: Say, it is from yourselves, by your taking the polytheists captive on the day of Badr, taking ransom from them, and leaving them to be killed.

Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated that Ibn Fadil narrated on the authority of Ash'ath ibn Suwar on the authority of Ibn Sirin on the authority of Ubaydah who said: The Muslims took seventy polytheists prisoner and killed seventy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Choose between taking ransom from them and strengthening yourself against your enemy, or if you accept it, seventy of you will be killed, or you will kill them. They said: Rather, we will take ransom from them and kill seventy of us. He said: So they took ransom from them and killed seventy of them. Ubaydah said: They sought both options.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah: that he said
m: regarding the prisoners of Badr: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you wish, you may kill them, and if you wish, you may ransom them and some of you may be martyred according to their number. They said: Rather, we will take the ransom and enjoy it, and some of us may be martyred according to their number. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Ismail narrated, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah Al-Salmani, and Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah Al-Salmani, on the authority of Ali, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: O Muhammad, God has disliked what your people have done in taking prisoners, and He has commanded you to give them a choice between two things: that they come forward and have their necks struck, or that they take ransom on the condition that a number of them be killed. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people and mentioned that to them, and they said: O Messenger of God, our tribes are our traitors!! Rather, we will take their ransom and thus gain strength to fight our enemy, and a number of us will be martyred, and there is nothing in that that we dislike! He said: So seventy men were killed from them on the Day of Uhud, the number of the prisoners of Badr.

x: God Almighty means by that: What befell you on the day the two armies met, which is the day of Uhud, when the Muslims and the polytheists met. He means by what befell them, what was killed from those who were killed, and what was wounded from those who were wounded, was by the permission of God, he says: So it was by the permission of God, meaning: by His judgment and decree for you. And he answered what with the letter fa, because what is a particle of recompense, and I have explained something similar to that previously. And that He may know the believers, And that He may know those who were hypocrites, meaning: And that God may know the believers, and that He may know those who were hypocrites, what befell you on the day the two armies met at Uhud befalls you, so that the people of faith in God and His Messenger may distinguish the believers among you from the hypocrites and recognize them, and the matter of the two groups will not be hidden from them.
We have explained the interpretation of his saying:
h
And that He may know the believers previously
, and the reason for that, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Ibn Ishaq said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by permission of God, and that He might make evident the believers, meaning: Whatever befell you when you and your enemy met was by My permission, and that was when you did what you did, after My victory had come to you, and I had fulfilled My promise to you, to distinguish between the hypocrites and the believers, and to make evident those among you who were hypocrites, so that they might reveal what was in them.

x: God Almighty means by that Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul the hypocrite and his companions, who turned back from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from his companions, when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, marched to the polytheists at Uhud to fight them, and the Muslims said to them: Come and fight the polytheists with us, or repel our numbers with your numbers! They said: If we knew that you would fight, we would have marched with you to them, and we will be with you against them, but we do not see that there should be between you and the people, so he said! So they revealed from their hypocrisy what they had been concealing, and they revealed with their tongues by saying: If we knew that there would be fighting, we would have followed you, other than what they had been concealing and hiding of enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of faith in him, such as: Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, and others from our scholars narrated, all of them said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out - meaning when he went out to Uhud - with a thousand men from his companions, until they were in the path between Uhud and Medina, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul with a third of the people withdrew from them and said: He obeyed them and went out and disobeyed me!

By God, we do not know why we are killing ourselves here, O people! So he returned with those who followed him from his people from the hypocrites and the doubtful, and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, the brother of Banu Salamah, followed them saying: O people, I remind you by God not to abandon your Prophet and your people when the enemy is present! They said: If we had known that you would fight, we would not have surrendered you, but we do not think that would happen. So he said: When they were stubborn and refused to leave him, he said: May God distance you, enemies of God! God will do without you! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, departed.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And it was said to them, ‘Come, fight in the cause of God or defend yourselves,’ meaning: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions who turned back from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he marched against his enemy, the polytheists, at Uhud. And his saying:
h
If we had known that there would be fighting

, we would have followed you, means: If we had known that you would fight, we would have marched with you and defended you, but we do not think that would happen, so he said. So what they had been hiding in themselves became apparent from them. God the Almighty says: “They will be nearer to disbelief that Day than to faith. They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts,” they show you faith, but it is not in their hearts,
h
and God knows best what they conceal
, meaning: what they conceal.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out - meaning on the day of Uhud - with a thousand men, and he promised them victory if they were patient. When they went out, Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul returned with three hundred, and Abu Jabir al-Sulami followed them calling them, but when they defeated him and said to him: We do not know, they said: If you obey us, you will return with us! He said: So he mentioned the companions of Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and the words of Abdullah Abu Jabir bin Abdullah al-Ansari when he called them and they said: We do not know, they said: If you obey us, you will return with us, so he said: ‘Those who said to their brothers and sat back, “If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed.” Say: Then ward off death from yourselves.’”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ikrimah said: They said, ‘If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you.’ He said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me, on the authority of Mujahid: If we knew there would be fighting, he said: If we knew that we would find fighting with you, if we knew where there would be fighting, we would have followed you. They differed in the interpretation of his saying: Or pay.

x: Some of them said: It means: Or increase in number, because if you increase in number, you will repel the people. Surat Al Imran 3:167 And that those who are hypocrites, and it is said to them, "Come, fight in the cause of God or defend yourselves," may know, they say, "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you." They are nearer to disbelief that Day than to faith. They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts, and God is most knowing of what they conceal.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or pay, he said: Or multiply.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Or repel, he said: With your great numbers, the enemy, even if there is no fighting.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: Or remain stationed if you do not fight.
Who said that?

c: Ismail bin Hafs Al-Ayli and Ali bin Sahl Al-Ramli told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Utbah bin Damrah told us:
m: I heard Abu Awn Al-Ansari regarding his statement:
h
Fight in the way of God or defend yourself
, he said: Stay in the army. As for His statement:
h
And God knows best what they conceal

, what he means by it is: And God knows best about these hypocrites who say to the believers: If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you, what they conceal in their souls for the believers and conceal it, covering it up from enmity and hatred, and that if they knew there would be fighting, they would not have followed them or defended them, and He, the Most High, is aware of what they conceal of that, and is aware of it, and is counting it against them, until He tears their veils in this worldly life and disgraces them with it, and sends them with it to the lowest level of Hell in the Hereafter.

x: God Almighty means by that: And God will know those who are hypocrites,
h
those who said to their brothers and sat back

. The position of those who is in the accusative case as a replacement for those who are hypocrites, and it may be permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a translation of what is in his saying: conceal of the mention of those who are hypocrites. The meaning of the verse is: And that God may know those who said to their brothers who were wounded with the Muslims in their war against the polytheists at Uhud on the day of Uhud, and who killed there from their tribes and people - and sat back, meaning: and these hypocrites who said what they said - from what God the Almighty informed us about what they said - about jihad with their brothers and tribes in the way of God - If they had obeyed us, meaning: if those of our brothers and tribes who were killed at Uhud had obeyed us, they would not have been killed, meaning: they were not killed there.
God the Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites who said this statement, Then repel, meaning: then repel.

i: From the saying of the speaker: I averted killing from so-and-so, meaning I pushed him away, I averted him, and from it the saying of the poet:
x: She said, and I protected her from my wrath: Is this his religion and my religion forever?

God Almighty says: Say to them: So pay, if you, O hypocrites, are truthful in what you say: If our brothers had obeyed us in abandoning jihad in the way of God with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fighting Abu Sufyan and those of Quraysh with him, they would not have been killed there by the sword, and they would have been alive by sitting with you, and staying behind Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and witnessing the jihad against the enemies of God with him, from yourselves death, for you have sat back from fighting them and have stayed behind from jihad against them, and you are inevitably dead, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Those who said to their brothers, those who were afflicted with you from their tribes and people, If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed, the verse, meaning: Death is inevitable, so if you are able to repel it from yourselves, then do so. That is because they were hypocrites and abandoned jihad in the way of God, out of eagerness to remain in this world and fleeing from death. It was mentioned that those who said this to their brothers are the ones about whom God said: And that He may know those who are hypocrites.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Those who said to their brothers and sat back
, ‘If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed,’ the verse, he mentioned to us that it was revealed about the enemy of God, Abdullah bin Ubayy.

c: Muhammad told us, he said, Muhammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They are Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: He is Abdullah bin Ubayy who sat and said to his brothers who went out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of UHud 11:If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed, the verse. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Mujahid, he said, Jabir bin Abdullah said: He is Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who said to their brothers and sat back
, the verse, he said: It was revealed about the enemy of God, Abdullah bin Ubayy.

x: God Almighty means: And do not think, and do not assume, as Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: And do not think, and do not assume. And His statement:
h
Those who were killed in the way of God

, meaning: those who were killed in one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are dead, meaning: And do not think of them, O Muhammad, as dead, not feeling anything, nor enjoying anything, nor enjoying anything, for they are alive with Me, enjoying My provision, happy and pleased with what I have given them of My honor and grace, and what I have bestowed upon them of My abundant reward and bounty, as:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ismail ibn Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When your brothers were afflicted at Uhud, God placed their souls in the bodies of green birds that frequent the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and take refuge in golden lamps in the shade of the Throne. When they found their drink and food pleasant and their resting place pleasant, they said: ‘If only our brothers knew what God has done to us! So that they would not give up on jihad and become weak in war!’ God Almighty said: ‘I will convey to them on your behalf.’” So God Almighty revealed these verses to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir ibn Abdul Hamid told us, and Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us,
m: they both said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq ibn Al-Ajda’, he said, we asked Abdullah ibn Mas’ud about these verses: And never think that
h
those who were killed in the way of God

, the verse, he said: As for us, we asked about it and it was said to us: When your brothers were killed at Uhud, God placed their souls in the bodies of green birds that go to the rivers of Paradise and eat from its fruits, and take refuge in golden lamps in the shade of the Throne. Then God looks down upon them and says: O My servants, what do you desire that I may give you more? They say: Our Lord, not more than what You have given us! Paradise, we eat from it wherever we wish! Three times. Then He looks down and says: O My servants, what do you desire that I may give you more? They say: Our Lord, not more than what You have given us! Paradise, we eat from it wherever we wish! However, we love for our souls to return to our bodies! Then you return us to the world, so we fight for you until we are killed for you again.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya Al-Maqdisi told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: We asked Abdullah about this verse. Then he mentioned something similar to it and added to it: Indeed, I have decreed that you will not return.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Murrah, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: We asked Abdullah about the souls of the martyrs, and if it were not for Abdullah, no one would have told us! He said: The souls of the martyrs are with God in the bellies of green birds in lanterns beneath the Throne, roaming in Paradise wherever He wishes, then they return to their lanterns, and their Lord looks down upon them and says: What do you want? They say: We want to return to the world and be killed once again. Abu Kuraib narrated that Abd al-Raheem ibn Sulayman and Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith ibn Fadil, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The martyrs are not dead, but alive with their Lord, and they are provided for. He said: The souls of the martyrs are with God like green birds with lanterns hanging from the Throne, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish. He said: Then your Lord looked at them and said: Do you desire anything that I may give you more? They said: Our Lord, do we not roam in Surat Al Imran 3:169 And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision. Paradise wherever we wish? Then He looked at them a third time and said: Do you desire anything that I may give you more? They said: You will return our souls to our bodies so that we may fight in Your cause once again! So He remained silent.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ata bin al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: That they said the third time - when he said to them: Do you desire anything that I should give you more of? - they said: Give our Prophet our greetings, and tell him that we are pleased and he is pleased with us.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, encouraging the believers to seek the reward of Paradise and making killing easy for them: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” That is, I have revived them, so they are with Me, receiving provision in the spirit of Paradise and its bounty, happy with what God has given them of His reward for their jihad on His behalf.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: The Muslims used to ask their Lord to show them a day like the day of Badr, in which they would be tested with goodness, and in which they would be granted martyrdom, and in which they would be granted Paradise and life in provision. Then they encountered the polytheists on the day of Uhud, and God took martyrs from among them, and they are the ones whom God mentioned when He said: And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead, the verse. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said: He mentioned the martyrs and said: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord,” until His saying: nor will they grieve. He claimed that the souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds, in golden lanterns suspended from the Throne. They graze morning and evening in Paradise, spending the night in the lanterns. When they set out to roam, a caller calls out: What do you want? What do you desire? They say: Our Lord, we are in what our souls desire! Their Lord asks them again: What do you desire? What do you want? They say: We are in what our souls desire! They are asked a third time, and they say what they said: But we would like our souls to return to our bodies! Because of what they saw of the great reward.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibad told us, he said, Ibrahim bin Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: The son of Adam continues to praise God until he becomes alive and does not die. Then he recited this verse: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” Muhammad bin Marzuq narrated, he said: Umar bin Yunus narrated, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ishaq bin Abi Talhah narrated, he said:

c: Anas bin Malik narrated to me
m: regarding the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to the people of Bir Ma'unah. He said: I do not know, forty or seventy. He said: And by that water was 'Amir bin At-Tufayl Al-Ja'fari. So those men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until they came to a cave overlooking the water. They sat in it, then some of them said to each other: Who among you will deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people of this water? He said - I think he was Ibn Milhan Al-Ansari -: I will deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he went out until he came to a group of them, and he crouched in front of the houses and then he said: O people of Bir Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to you. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, so believe in God and His Messenger. Then a man came out to him from the broken house with a spear and struck him in the side until he came out from the other side. He said: God is Great, I have won, by the Lord of the Kaaba! So they followed his tracks until they reached his companions, and Amir ibn Tufail killed them all. Ishaq said: Anas ibn Malik told me: God the Almighty revealed a Qur’an about them, which was lifted after we had recited it for a while. God revealed: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated, Yazid narrated, Juwaybir narrated, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: When those of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who were killed on the day of Uhud, met their Lord and He honored them, so they attained life, martyrdom, and good provision, they said: If only there were between us and our brothers someone who would tell them that we have met our Lord and He was pleased with us and pleased us! God Almighty said: I am your messenger to your Prophet and your brothers. Then God Almighty revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision,” until His saying: nor will they grieve. This is the report that God conveyed to His Messenger and the believers, as the martyrs said.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead.
Ishaq said: Anas ibn Malik told me: God the Almighty revealed a Qur’an about them, which was lifted after we had recited it for a while.

x: There are two aspects to the accusative case of his saying: rejoicing. One of them: that it is in the accusative case, as an exception to the statement: with their Lord. The other is from his saying: They are provided for, and if it was raised in response to his saying: Rather, they are alive and joyful, it would be permissible.

By that, the Most High means: They rejoice over those of their brothers who have not joined them, who have departed from them while they were alive in this world, following their path of jihad against the enemies of God with His Messenger, because they know that if they are martyred and join them, they will have attained the same honor of God as they have attained. Therefore, they are happy about them, happy that if they become like that, there is no fear for them and they do not grieve. He means by that: There is no fear for them, because they have been secured from the punishment of God and have become certain of His pleasure with them. They have been secured from the fear that they used to fear from that in this world, and they do not grieve over what they left behind of the causes of this world and the hardships of its life, because of the humility, ease, and closeness to which they have attained.
The object of an is la meaning: they are happy for them that they have no fear and they do not grieve.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them
, the verse, he says: for their brothers who left them for their religion and their matter, for what they have come to of honor, favor, and bliss that He has given them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them

, the verse, he said, they say: Our brothers will be killed as we were killed, they will join us and will receive from the honor of God Almighty what we received. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ:
m: It was mentioned to us on the authority of some of them regarding His statement: “And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” He said: They are those killed at Badr and Uhud. They claimed that when God, the Blessed and Exalted, took their souls and admitted them into Paradise, He placed their souls in green birds grazing in Paradise and taking refuge in golden lamps beneath the Throne. When they saw the honor that God had given them, they said: If only our brothers who will come after us knew what we are in! So when they witness a battle, they hasten to what we are in! So God, the Exalted, said: I am sending down to your Prophet and informing your brothers of what you are in. So they rejoiced at it and were glad, and said: God informs your Prophet and your brothers of what you are in, so when they witness a battle, they come to you! He said: That is what His statement:
h
Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty
, up to His statement:
h
The reward of the believers

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them

, meaning: They are happy for those of their brothers who have joined them to join them in what they have done of their jihad, so that they may share with them in what they are in of the reward of God that He has given them, and God has removed from them fear and sadness.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them

, he said: They are their brothers from the martyrs who will be martyred after them, No fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve, until he reached: And that God does not allow to be lost
h
the reward of the believers

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: As for they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, then the martyr is brought a book in which is who will come to him from among his brothers and family, and it is said: So-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, and so-and-so will come to you on such-and-such a day, so he rejoices when he comes to him, just as the family of the absent one rejoices at his arrival in this world.

x: God Almighty says: They rejoice, they rejoice, with a blessing from God, meaning: with what He Almighty bestowed upon them of His great honor when they came to Him, and favor, meaning: with what He bestowed upon them of favor and generous reward for what they had done before of obedience to God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and of jihad against His enemies,
h
and that God does not waste the reward of the believers
, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: They rejoice in the grace and bounty of God, the verse, when they witnessed the fulfillment of the promise and the great reward. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
And that God does not waste the reward of the believers

x: Some of them read it with the opening of the alif of an meaning: they are happy with the blessing and grace of God,
h
and that God does not waste the reward of the believers

. And with the kasra on the alif, as a resumption. And those who read it like that argued that it is in Abdullah’s reading: And God does not waste the reward of the believers. They said: So that is evidence that his saying: And God, is a resumption not connected to the first. The meaning of his saying:
h
The reward of the believers will not be lost is that the reward for the deeds of those who believed in their Messenger
, followed him, and did what came to them from God will not be nullified.
The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads it: And that God with the opening of the alif, because the evidence from the readings agrees on that.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: And that God does not waste the reward of the believers.
Some of them read it with the opening of the alif of an meaning: they are happy with the blessing and grace of God, and that God does not waste the reward of the believers.
And those who read it like that argued that it is in Abdullah’s reading: And God does not waste the reward of the believers.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads it: And that God with the opening of the alif, because the evidence from the readings agrees on that.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And that God does not waste the reward of the believers, those who respond to God and the Messenger after they have been wounded and injured. And what God Almighty meant by that was: those who followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Hamra’ al-Asad in pursuit of the enemy - Abu Sufyan and those of the polytheists of Quraysh who were with him - on their way back from Uhud.

That is because when Abu Sufyan turned back from Uhud, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out after him until he reached Hamra’ al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina, so that the people would see that he and his companions had power over their enemy, like someone who:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said: Husayn ibn Abdullah narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: The day of Uhud was Saturday, the middle of Shawwal. When it was the next day of Uhud, Sunday, sixteen nights had passed of Shawwal, the muezzin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people to seek out the enemy, and his muezzin announced: No one should go out with us except those who were present on our day the day before. So Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram spoke to him and said: O Messenger of God, my father left me behind in charge of my seven sisters, and he said to me: O my son, it is not appropriate for me and for you to leave these women without a man among them, and I am not one who would prefer you to fight with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, over myself! So stay behind in charge of your sisters, so I stayed behind in charge of them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission, so he went out with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to terrify the enemy, to inform them that he had gone out in pursuit of them, so that they would think he was strong, and that what had happened to them had not weakened them against their enemy. Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said:

c: Abdullah ibn Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, on the authority of Abu al-Sa’ib,
m: the freed slave of Aisha bint Uthman: A man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Abd al-Ashhal, who had witnessed Uhud, said: I witnessed Uhud with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I and a brother of mine, and we returned wounded. When the muezzin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him Surat Al Imran 3:172 Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them - for those among them who did good and feared God is a great reward. and grant him peace, gave the call to go out in pursuit of the enemy, I said to my brother - or he said to me -: Are we missing a raid with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? By God, we do not have a mount to ride, and none of us is seriously wounded! So we went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was less wounded than he was. Whenever he was defeated, I would carry him up a hill and he would walk up a hill, until we reached where the Muslims had reached. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he reached Hamra al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina, and he stayed there for three days, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, then he returned to Medina.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: God Almighty said:
m: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them, meaning the wounds, and they are those who traveled with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the next day from the day of Uhud to Hamra al-Asad, despite the pain of the wounds they were suffering from, for those among them who did good and feared God is a great reward.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wounds had afflicted them

, the verse, and that was on the day of Uhud, after the killing and wounds, and after the polytheists - Abu Sufyan and his companions - had departed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions: Is there not a group that will volunteer for the command of God, seeking out its enemy? For that is more effective for the enemy, and more distant for hearing! So a group of them set out, with what God knows of the effort. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of al-Suddi: Abu Sufyan set out on his way back from Uhud, until he reached part of the road, then they regretted it and said: What a bad thing you have done! You killed them, and when none remained but the fugitives, you left them! Go back and exterminate them. So God cast terror into their hearts, and they were defeated. Then God informed His Messenger, so he pursued them until he reached Hamra’ al-Asad, then they returned from Hamra’ al-Asad, so God, the Most High, revealed about them: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God, the Almighty, cast terror into the heart of Abu Sufyan - meaning the day of Uhud - after what happened from him, he returned to Mecca, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan has indeed afflicted a part of you, and he has returned and God has cast terror into his heart! The Battle of Uhud was in Shawwal, and the merchants used to come to Medina in Dhul-Qi'dah, and they would camp at Badr al-Sughra once every year, because they came after the Battle of Uhud, and the believers were afflicted with wounds, and they complained about that to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what afflicted them was severe. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged the people to set out with him, and to follow what they had been following, and he said: They are only setting out now to perform Hajj, and they will not be able to do the same until the next year, so Satan came and frightened his followers, and he said: The people have gathered against you! The people refused to follow him, so he said: I am going even if no one follows me, to urge the people. So Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Az-Zubayr, Saʿd, Talhah, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Abdullah ibn Masʿud, Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman, and Abu Ubaidah ibn Al-Jarrah volunteered with him, with seventy men, and they set out in search of Abu Sufyan, and they searched for him until they reached As-Safraʿ, then God the Almighty revealed: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them - for those among them who did good and feared God is a great reward.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, he said, Abu Saeed told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that she said
m: to Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr: O son of my sister, by God, your father and grandfather - meaning Abu Bakr and Al-Zubayr - are among those about whom God Almighty said: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: “I was informed that when Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and his companions set out on the day of Uhud, the Muslims said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: They are heading to Medina! He said: If they ride the horses and leave the heavy loads, then they are heading to Medina, and if they sit on the heavy loads and leave the horses, then God has terrified them, and they are not heading to them. So they rode the heavy loads, and God terrified them. Then He called upon people to follow them to see that they had the strength, so they followed them for two or three nights, and then this verse was revealed: ‘Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them.’”

c: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Aisha said to me: Your parents were among those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them - meaning Abu Bakr and Al-Zubayr.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Abdullah was among those who responded to God and the Messenger.

x: God Almighty promised the doer of good among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them, if he feared God and feared Him, performed His obligations and obeyed Him in His commands and prohibitions in the future of his life, a great reward. That is the abundant reward and great recompense for the good deeds he had done in this world.
God Almighty means: And that God does not waste the reward of the believers, “
h
Those to whom the people said

, ‘The people have gathered against you.’” Those is in the accusative case, referring back to the believers, and this attribute is an attribute of those who responded to God and the Messenger. The first people are people - as we have been told - whom Abu Sufyan asked to discourage the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions who went out in pursuit of him after he had returned from Uhud to Hamra al-Asad. The second people are Abu Sufyan and his companions from Quraysh, who were with him at Uhud. And by his saying:
h
They have gathered against you

, he means they have gathered men to meet you and the ball is upon you to fight you, so fear them, he says: so beware of them, and avoid meeting them, for you will not be able to defeat them, so it increased their faith, he says: so it increased their fear from their fear of the matter of Abu Sufyan and his companions from the polytheists, certainty to their certainty, and belief in God and His promise and the promise of His Messenger to their belief, and that did not deter them from the path that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to follow, but they continued until they attained the pleasure of God from Him, and they said, trusting in God and relying on Him, since their fear from their fear of Abu Sufyan and his companions from the polytheists:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, he means by his saying:
h
God is sufficient for us
h
God is sufficient for us
, meaning:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, he says: and the best Master for whomever He takes care of and provides for.

The Almighty described Himself with this because the agent, in the speech of the Arabs, is the one to whom the task of carrying out the task of someone is entrusted. So since the people whom God described in these verses had entrusted their matter to God and trusted in Him, and entrusted that to Him, He described Himself as carrying that out for them, and entrusting their matter to Him by proxy, so He said: And what an excellent agent is God Almighty for them.
The people of interpretation differed about the time when someone said to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: The people have gathered against you.

Some of them said: This was said to them on the day they went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Uhud to Hamra al-Asad, in pursuit of Abu Sufyan and the polytheists who were with him. Mention who said that, and mention the reason for which it was said, and among those who said it: Muhammad bin Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm, who said: Ma'bad Al-Khuza'i passed by him - meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - in Hamra' Al-Asad. Khuza'ah, both Muslims and polytheists, were a group of sincere advisers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Tihamah. They made a deal with him, not hiding anything that was there from him - and Ma'bad was a polytheist at that time - so he said: By God, O Muhammad, by God, what happened to you and your companions has been hard on us, and we wish that God had pardoned you regarding them!

Then he left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Hamra' Al-Asad until he met Abu Sufyan bin Harb and those with him in Ar-Rawha'. They had decided to return to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and they said: We have done well! We have punished his companions, their leaders, and their nobles, and then we return before we eradicate them?! Let us attack the rest of them, and we will flee from them. So when Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad, he said: What is behind you, O Ma'bad? He said: Muhammad has come out with his companions seeking you in a gathering the likes of which I have never seen before. They are burning with desire for you. Those who stayed behind on your day have gathered with him, and they regretted what they did. They have a hatred for you that I have never seen before! He said: Woe to you! What do you say? He said: By God, I do not see you moving on until you see the forelocks of the horses!

He said: By God, we have decided to attack them to eradicate their remnants! He said: I forbid you from that, for by God, what I saw has made me so angry that I have recited some verses of poetry about them! He said: What did you say? He said: I said: My camel was almost knocked down by the sounds as the ground was covered with the locusts. Dress like a noble lion, do not be rude when meeting, nor do you break the barriers. So I remained an enemy, I think the earth is tilted towards what they called a leader who will not be disappointed I said: Woe to Ibn Harb from meeting you when the plain is covered with horses. I am a warner to the people of valor, a warning to every one of them who has a desire and a sense. From the army of Ahmed, do not fear his bombs, and what you warned about cannot be described as a joke He said: That made Abu Sufyan and those with him think twice.

A group of Abd al-Qais passed by him and he said: Where are you going? They said: We are going to Medina. He said: Why? They said: We are going to provide provisions. He said: Will you deliver a message from me to Muhammad that I am sending you with, and shall I load your camels with raisins tomorrow in Ukaz when you reach them? They said: Yes. He said: When you reach him, tell him that we have decided to march against him and his companions to eradicate their remnants! The group passed by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was at Hamra al-Asad and told him what Abu Sufyan had said. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions said:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: Then God said: “
h
Those to whom the people said
, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them.’ But it only increased their faith, and they said, ‘
h
God is sufficient for us

, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’” The people are those who said to them what they said - the group of Abd al-Qays to whom Abu Sufyan said what he said - Abu Sufyan and those with him are returning to you! God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: So they returned with favor and bounty from God, no harm having touched them verse.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When they - meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions - regretted turning back from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, and they said: Go back and eradicate them, God cast terror into their hearts and they were defeated. Then they met a Bedouin and gave him a reward, and they said to him: If you meet Muhammad and his companions, tell them that we have gathered against them! So God, the Most High, informed His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he pursued them until he reached Hamra’ Al-Asad. They met the Bedouin on the road, and he told them the report, and they said:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs! Then they returned from Hamra’ Al-Asad. Then God, the Most High, revealed about them and the Bedouin whom they had met: “
h
Those to whom the people said
, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them.’ But it only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: Abu Sufyan, on his way back from Uhud, met a caravan coming to Medina with their merchandise, and there were covenants between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: I will be pleased with you if you turn Muhammad and those with him away from me, if you find him in pursuit of me, and inform him that I have gathered a large army against him. So the caravan met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said to him: O Muhammad, we inform you that Abu Sufyan has gathered a large army against you, and that he is coming to Medina. If you wish to return, then do so! But that only increased his and those with him in certainty, and they said:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed:
h
Those to whom the people said
, ‘The people have gathered against you’ (al-Baqarah 2:17).

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of his companions set out after Abu Sufyan and his companions had left Uhud behind them, until they reached Dhu al-Hulayfah. The Bedouins and the people came to them and said to them: This is Abu Sufyan, who has attacked you with the people! They said:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. So God, the Most High, revealed about them: “
h
Those to whom the people said
, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them.’ But it only increased them in faith, and they said, ‘
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’”

x: Others said: Rather, the one who said that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions said that to him, in the minor Battle of Badr, and that was during the Prophet’s march, may God bless him and grant him peace, the following year after the Battle of Uhud, to meet his enemy Abu Sufyan and his companions, at the appointment he had made to meet them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those to whom the people said
, ‘The Surat Al Imran 3:173
h
Those to whom the people said

, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them." But it only increased them in faith, and they said, "Sufficient for us is God, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs." people have gathered against you,’ he said: This is Abu Sufyan who said to Muhammad: Your meeting place is at Badr, where you killed our companions. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out for his meeting place until he stopped at Badr, and they happened upon the market there and bought, and that is what God Almighty said: So they returned with favor and bounty from God, no harm having touched them, and it is the minor Battle of Badr.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly - and he added to it: And it is the Lesser Badr - Ibn Jurayj said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prepared for the meeting with Abu Sufyan, they began to meet the polytheists and ask them about the Quraysh, and they would say:
h
They have gathered against you
! They plotted against them with that, wanting to frighten them, but the believers would say:
h
God is sufficient for us

, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, until they arrived at Badr, and they found its markets in good condition, and no one had disputed with them in it. He said: And a man from the polytheists came and informed the people of Mecca about the cavalry of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said about that: My camel was frightened away from my horses, Muhammad, and dates were scattered like the Anjd I took dried water as my appointment Abu Jaafar said: This is how Al-Qasim recited to us, but it is a mistake. Rather, it is: I have been repelled by the company of Muhammad and Ajwa from Yathrib like the Anjad She is infatuated with her father's religion, and has made the water of Qadeed my destination. And the water of Djnan is poured for her at noon tomorrow Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Badr was a place of trade in the pre-Islamic era. Some Muslims went out intending to go there, but some polytheists met them and said to them: The people have gathered against you, so fear them! As for the coward, he turned back, and as for the brave man, he prepared himself for battle and prepared himself for trade, and they said:
h
God is sufficient for us

, and He is the best Disposer of affairs! So they went to them and did not encounter anyone, so God, the Almighty, revealed about them: The people have gathered against you, so fear them. Ibn Yahya said, Abdul-Razzaq said, Ibn Uyaynah said:

c: Zakariya told me, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said:
m: These are the words of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire, he said:
h
God is sufficient for us
, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: What was said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, that the people have gathered, so fear them, was when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and those who went out with him, following Abu Sufyan and those who were with him from the polytheists of Quraysh, were leaving Uhud to Hamraʿ al-ʿAsad. Because God, the Most High, only praised those whom He described by saying:
h
God is sufficient for us

, and He is the best Disposer of affairs, when it was said to them: The people have gathered against you, so fear them, after what had befallen them of wounds and injuries, by His saying: Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wounds had afflicted them, and this description was only a description of those who followed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from his wounded companions from Uhud to Hamraʿ al-ʿAsad.

As for those who went out with him to the minor battle of Badr, there was not one wounded person among them except one wounded person whose wound had already healed and whose word had already healed. This is because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only went out to the second Badr to meet Abu Sufyan, who had promised him to meet there, one year after the Battle of Uhud, in Sha’ban of the year 4 AH. This is because the Battle of Uhud was in the middle of Shawwal of the year 3, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out to the minor battle of Badr to it in Sha’ban of the year 4. Between that, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not have a battle with the polytheists in which there was a war between them in which his companions were wounded. However, a group of his companions were killed in the Battle of Raji’, none of whom had witnessed the minor Battle of Badr.
The Battle of Raji’ was between the Battle of Uhud and the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) minor battle of Badr.

What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: And they returned with favor from God, was that those who responded to God and the Messenger returned after the wound had befallen them, from the direction in which they had set out - which was their march in the footsteps of their enemy - to Hamra al-Asad, with favor from God, meaning: with well-being from their Lord, in which they did not encounter an enemy, and bounty, meaning: they obtained profits therein from the trade in which they traded, the reward that they had earned.
h
No harm touched them

means: no harm or injury came to them from their enemy, and they pursued the pleasure of God, meaning by that: they pleased God by doing that, and by following His Messenger to what he called them to of following the enemy’s trail and obeying them, and God is the possessor of great bounty, meaning: God is the possessor of kindness and generosity towards them - by turning away their enemy who had intended to attack them, and other than that of His favors towards them and others - with His blessings, great in the eyes of those upon whom He bestowed His blessings from among His creation.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they returned with favor and bounty from God
. He said: And the bounty is what they obtained of trade and reward.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: They came across the market and bought, and that is His statement:
h
And they returned with favor and bounty from God

. He said: The bounty is what they obtained from trade and reward. Ibn Jurayj said: What they obtained from the sale was a favor and bounty from God. They obtained His pardon and His grace, and no one disputed it with them. He said: And His statement:
h
No harm touched them
, he said: killing, and they pursued the pleasure of God, he said: obedience to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And God is the possessor of great bounty, because He turned them away from meeting their enemy.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: They obeyed God and sought their need, and no one harmed them, “So they returned with favor and bounty from God. No harm had touched them, and they pursued the pleasure of God, and God is the possessor of great bounty.”

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given dirhams at Badr - that is, when he went out to the minor Battle of Badr - with which they bought goods from the season of Badr, and they acquired trade. This is what God said: “So they returned with favor from God and bounty. No harm had touched them, and they pursued the pleasure of God.” As for the favor, it is well-being, and as for the bounty, it is trade, and the evil is killing.

x: By that, the Most High means: The One who said to you, O believers, The people have gathered against you, frightened you with the crowds of your enemy and their march towards you, from the action of the devil who was speaking through the mouths of the one who said that to you, frightening you with his allies from the polytheists - Abu Sufyan and his companions from Quraysh - so that you would be terrified of them and be cowardly towards them, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That is only Satan frightening his allies
, God frightens the believer with the disbeliever, and terrifies the believer with the disbeliever.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: h
That is only Satan frightening his allies
, he said: He frightens the believers with the disbelievers.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
That is only Satan frightening you with his allies
, he says: Satan frightens the believers with his allies.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
That is only Satan frightening you with his allies

, meaning: that group, meaning the group of Abd al-Qays, who said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what they said, and what Satan put in their mouths, frightening his allies, meaning: he terrifies you with his allies.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ali bin Ma’bad told us, on the authority of Atab bin Bashir,
m: a client of Quraysh, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, regarding his statement:
h
That is only Satan frightening you with his allies
, he said: He frightens you with his allies.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: It is only Satan who magnifies the matter of the polytheists, O hypocrites, in your souls, so you fear them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: He mentioned the matter of the polytheists and their greatness in the eyes of the hypocrites, so he said:
h
That is only Satan frightening his allies
, he magnifies his allies in your hearts, so you fear them.

x: If someone were to say: How is it said: He frightens His friends? Does Satan frighten his friends? [And how] is it said - if its meaning is that He frightens you with His friends - He frightens His friends? It was said: This is similar to His saying: To warn of a severe punishment (al-Kahf 18:2), meaning: To warn you of His severe punishment, because punishment is not a warning, but rather it is a warning.

Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: The meaning of this is: He frightens people with his followers, like the saying of someone: He gives dirhams and dresses them in clothes, meaning: He gives people dirhams and dresses them in clothes, so this was omitted because it is not needed.

What is similar to that is not ambiguous, because the dirhams in the statement of the speaker: He gives the dirhams, it is known that what is given is the dirhams, and likewise the guardians - in his statement: He frightens His guardians - are not frightened, rather the frightening is from the guardians to others, and for that reason they differed.

He says: So do not fear, O believers, the polytheists, and do not let their matter be too great for you, and do not be intimidated by their gathering, while you obey Me, as long as you obey Me and follow My command, and I guarantee you victory and triumph, but fear and beware lest you disobey Me and go against My command and perish, if you are believers, meaning: And you fear, more than the polytheists and more than all of My creation, that you go against My command, if you believe in My Messenger and what he brought to you from Me.

God Almighty says: And let not the disbelief of those who hasten to disbelief, turning back on their heels, from among the hypocrites, grieve you, for they will not harm God in the least by their haste to disbelief.
And just as their haste, if they had hastened to faith, would not have been of any benefit to Him, so too their haste to disbelief is not harmful to Him, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you
, meaning: that they are the hypocrites.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you
, meaning: the hypocrites.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God does not want to give those who hasten to disbelief a share in the reward of the Hereafter, so He let them down and they hastened to it. Then He informed that even though they are deprived of what they were deprived of of the reward of the Hereafter, they will have a great punishment in the Hereafter, and that is the punishment of the Fire.
Ibn Ishaq said about that as follows:

c: Ibn Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: God wants to give them no share in the Hereafter, meaning to nullify their deeds.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means the hypocrites about whom He had previously told His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he should not be saddened by their haste to disbelieve. So He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: These are the ones who bought disbelief with their faith, then turned away from their faith after entering it, and were satisfied with disbelief in God and His Messenger in exchange for faith. They will not harm God in the least with their disbelief and their turning away from the glory of their faith. Rather, they will only harm themselves by doing so, by making them subject to a punishment from God that they cannot bear. Rather, God, the Most High, urged His believing servants with these verses, from His saying:
And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by permission of God
to this verse, to sincerely believe, to turn to Him in their affairs, and to be content with Him alone as a supporter, without any other of His creation.

And He encouraged them with them to fight against His enemies and the enemies of His religion, and encouraged their hearts with them, and informed them that whoever supports Him with His support will not be let down even if all those who oppose and deviate from Him were to unite against him, and that whoever lets him down, no supporter will support him whose support will benefit him, even if his helpers and supporters were many, as:
