c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Indeed, those who purchase disbelief in exchange for faith, meaning the hypocrites, will never harm God at all, and they will have a painful punishment, meaning painful.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: They are the hypocrites.

x: By this, the Almighty means: And let not those who disbelieve in God and His Messenger and what he brought from God think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves. By imla’ it means to prolong life and delay the appointed time. From this is the saying of God Almighty: And leave me alone for a long time
r
(Maryam 19:46)
, meaning: for a long time. From this is the saying: I lived a long time and I was bored with a lover. The word imla itself is time, and al-mulwan is the night and the day.

i: From this is the saying of Tamim bin Muqbil:
x: Oh, the homes of the living, be filled with the seventy-year-olds, and be filled with colorful decay.
Meaning: in the colors, night and day. There is a difference in the reading of His statement:
h
And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves
A group of them read it: And do not think, with a ya, and with a fat-ha on the alif from his saying: only, according to the meaning that I described of its interpretation.

Others read it: Do not think with the letter ta and anma also with the letter alif open from anma meaning: And do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve, that Our granting them respite is better for themselves.

Why is the alif in his saying anma opened in the reading of those who read with the ta’, and you know that if it is read with the ta’, then you have applied tahsabna in those who disbelieve, and if you apply it in that, it does not make it sufficient. That it falls on anma, because anma inma has an agent that works on two things in the accusative case?

As for the correct way in Arabic and the well-known way of speaking from the speech of the Arabs, is to break the word in when it is read tahsabna with a taa, because tahsabna when it is read with a taa then it has made those who disbelieve a noun in an. But I think that whoever read it with a taa in tahsabna and opened the alif of anma, only wanted to repeat tahsabna on anma, as if he intended that the meaning of the speech is: And do not think, O Muhammad, you, those who disbelieved, do not think that what We grant them is better for themselves, as He, the Most High, said: Do they then await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly?
r
(Muhammad 47:18)

, with the interpretation: Do they await anything but the Hour, do they await anything but that it should come upon them suddenly? This is because it was a permissible way in Arabic, so the way of speaking of the Arabs is what we described before.

The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read: And let not those who disbelieve think with the ya’ of yahsabna and with the fatha on the alif of anma, meaning that the reckoning is for those who disbelieved and not for others. Then the accusative is used in anma because yahsabna then was not occupied with anything that worked on it, and it requires two accusatives. We chose this because of the consensus of the readers on opening the alif of anma the first, so this indicates that the correct reading of yaḥsabna is with the ya’ for what we described. As for the second alif of inma, the kasra is at the beginning, according to the consensus of the reciters. The interpretation of His statement:
h
We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin is that We only delay their lives and lengthen them so that they may increase in
sin.

He says: So that they may acquire sins and their sins may increase and multiply. And for them is a humiliating punishment. He says: And for those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger in the Hereafter is a humiliating and disgraceful punishment.
And in the same way as we said in that, the effect came:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of al-Aswad, who said, Abdullah said:
m: There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but that death is better for it. And he recited: “
h
And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves
. We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin.” And he recited: “A provision from God. And what is with God is better for the righteous.”
r
(Al Imran 3:198)

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of His statement: And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves.
A group of them read it: And do not think, with a ya, and with a fat-ha on the alif from his saying: only, according to the meaning that I described of its interpretation.

Others read it: Do not think with the letter ta and anma also with the letter alif open from anma meaning: And do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve, that Our granting them respite is better for themselves.

If someone were to say: Why is the alif in his saying anma opened in the reading of those who read with the ta’, and you know that if it is read with the ta’, then you have applied tahsabna in those who disbelieve, and if you apply it in that, it does not make it sufficient.

It was said: As for the correct way in Arabic and the well-known way of speaking from the speech of the Arabs, is to break the word in when it is read tahsabna with a taa, because tahsabna when it is read with a taa then it has made those who disbelieve a noun in an.

But I think that whoever read it with a taa in tahsabna and opened the alif of anma, only wanted to repeat tahsabna on anma, as if he intended that the meaning of the speech is: And do not think, O Muhammad, you, those who disbelieved, do not think that what We grant them is better for themselves, as He, the Most High, said: Do they then await anything but the Hour, that it should come upon them suddenly?

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading of those who read: And let not those who disbelieve think with the ya’ of yahsabna and with the fatha on the alif of anma, meaning that the reckoning is for those who disbelieved and not for others.
We chose this because of the consensus of the readers on opening the alif of anma the first, so this indicates that the correct reading of yaḥsabna is with the ya’ for what we described.
As for the second alif of inma, the kasra is at the beginning, according to the consensus of the reciters.

x: What he means by his saying:
h
God would not leave the believers is that God would not leave the believers in the state you are in of confusing the believer among you with

the hypocrite, so that one cannot be distinguished from the other, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, meaning by that: until He distinguishes the wicked, which is the hypocrite who hides his disbelief, from the good, which is the sincere believer who is true to his faith, through trials and testing, just as He distinguished between them on the Day of Uhud when they met the enemy when they went out to them.
The interpreters differed about the evil that God meant in this verse.
Some of them said about it, like what we said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told me, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: God would not leave the believers in that state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, he said: He distinguished between them on the day of Uhud, the hypocrite from the believer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
God would not leave the believers in the state you are in

until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Ibn Jurayj said: He says: To distinguish the truthful in his faith from the liar. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: On the day of Uhud, He distinguished some of them from others, the hypocrite from the believer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
God would not leave the believers in the state you are in
until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, meaning: the hypocrites.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: so that the believer may be distinguished from the disbeliever through migration and jihad.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God would not leave the believers in the state you are in
, meaning the disbelievers. He says:
h
God would not leave the believers in the state you are in
of misguidance, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, distinguishing between them in jihad and migration.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until the wicked is distinguished from the good
, he said: Until the wicked is distinguished from the believer.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
God would not leave the believers in the state you are in
until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. They said: If Muhammad is truthful, then let him tell us who believes in God and who disbelieves!! So God revealed:
h
God would not leave the believers in the state you are in
until He distinguishes the wicked from the good, until He distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever.

x: The first interpretation is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because the verses before it mention the hypocrites, and this one is in its context, so it is more likely that it is about them than it is about others.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And God would not inform you of the unseen
, and God would not inform Muhammad of the unseen, but God chose him and made him a messenger.
Others said: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
h
And God would not inform you of the unseen
, meaning: of what He wants to test you with, so that you may beware of what He wills upon you,
h
but God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills
, He knows him.

The most correct interpretation of this statement is: God would not let you know the secrets of the hearts of His servants so that you would know the believers among them from the hypocrites and the disbelievers. Rather, He distinguishes between them through trials and tribulations - as He distinguished between them through hardship on the Day of Uhud - and jihad against His enemy, and similar types of trials, so that you would know their believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites.

However, He, the Most High, chooses from among His messengers whomever He wills and selects him, so He shows him some of what is in the secrets of some of them, through His revelation to him and His message, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But God chooses from among His messengers whom He wills

, he said: He purifies them for Himself. Rather, we said that this interpretation is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because its beginning is a report from God Almighty that He will not leave His servants - meaning without trials - until He distinguishes through trial between their believers and their disbelievers and the hypocrites. Then He followed that with His saying:
h
And God would not inform you of the unseen

. So in what He began with of the description of God revealing the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the disbelief of the disbeliever, there is a clear indication that what took charge of that was the report that He would not inform them of what is hidden from them of the innermost secrets of their hearts, except by that which He mentioned that He distinguishes them with His description, except for those whom He excepted from His messengers whom He singled out with His knowledge.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And if you believe

, and if you give truth to those whom I have chosen from among My messengers with My knowledge and which I have revealed to the hypocrites among you, and fear your Lord by obeying Him in what your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has commanded you to do and in what He has forbidden you to do, then for you is a great reward, meaning: For that you will have, from your faith and fear of your Lord, a great reward, just as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: So believe in God and His messengers,
h
and if you believe
and fear God, meaning: if you return and repent, then you will have a great reward.

x: The reading of that differed.
A group of people from Hijaz and Iraq read it: And do not think that those who are stingy with the letter ta are among those who think.
Another group read it as: And do not think with the letter ya. Then the Arabs differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning of this is: The misers should not think that miserliness is good for them. So it is sufficient to mention yabghlūn from bukhl, just as you say: So-and-so arrived and I was pleased with him, but you mean: I was pleased with his arrival. And it is, not Imad.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: What he meant by his saying: “
h
And let not those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them

. Rather, it is bad for them,” is that they should not think that miserliness is good for them. So he dropped the name that he attributed to it, which is miserliness, because he mentioned the calculation and mentioned what God has given them of His bounty, so he implied both of them when he mentioned them. He said: And there has been an omission that is more severe than this, he said: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought
r
(Al-Hadid 57:10)
and he did not say: and those who spent after the conquest, because when he said: Those are greater in degree than those who spent afterwards
r
(Al-Hadid 57:10)

, there was evidence in that that he meant them. Some of those who denied the statement of the one we mentioned from the people of Basra said: The min in His statement: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest (al-Hadid 57:10) is in the sense of a plural.

The meaning of the statement is: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest in their homes and conditions, so how about those who spent after the conquest? The first is sufficient. He said: In His statement:
h
Let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think that it is better for them

, there is an omitted word, except that it was not omitted except in the statement that which took the place of the omitted word, because huwa refers to stinginess, and khayran lahum refers to nouns. These two referring words indicate that there are two nouns before them, and it is sufficient to say: yabghlun from stinginess. He said: If this is read with the letter ta’, then the word al-bukhl comes before al-ladhin, and if it is read with the letter ya’, then the word al-bukhl comes after al-ladhin.

i: It is sufficient to say al-ladhin yabkhalun from al-bukhl, as the poet said:
x: If a fool is forbidden, he will run after it and disobey it, and the fool will disobey.
As if he said: He ran to foolishness, so he was satisfied with foolishness by saying the foolish one, and likewise he was satisfied with those who are stingy, from stinginess.
The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: And do not think, O Muhammad, that the stinginess of
h
those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty

is better for them. Then he left out mentioning stinginess, since in his statement: It is better for them, there was an indication that it was intended in the speech, since it had been preceded by his statement:
h
Those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty
. We said: Reading it with the taa is more correct than reading it with the yaa, because the nature of al-muhsaba requires a noun and a predicate. So if His statement,
h
And let not those who are stingy think is read with the yaa
, then al-muhsaba does not have a noun, and His statement,
h
It is better for them is a predicate of it

. And if it is read with the taa, then His statement, Those who are stingy is a noun for it, and it has conveyed the meaning of stinginess, which is the name of al-muhsaba that was abandoned, and His statement,
h
It is better for them is a predicate of it
, so it is in accordance with the well-known eloquent speech of the Arabs.

Therefore, we chose the reading with the taa in that, as we have explained, even though the reading with the yaa is not wrong, but it is not the most eloquent nor the most famous of the speech of the Arabs.

As for the interpretation of the verse, which is its interpretation according to what we have chosen from the reading in that: And do not think, O Muhammad, that the miserliness of those who are miserly with what God has given them in this world of wealth, and do not give from it the right of God that He has imposed upon them in it of zakat, is better for them with God on the Day of Resurrection.
Rather, it is worse for them with Him in the Hereafter, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And do not think that
h
those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty
are better for them. Rather, it is worse for them. They are those to whom God has given of His bounty, but they are stingy in spending it in the way of God, and they do not pay its zakat.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant by that the Jews who were stingy in explaining to the people what God revealed in the Torah about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his description.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think to that they will be collared by what they were stingy with
on the Day of Resurrection, meaning by that the People of the Book were stingy with the Book and did not explain it to the people.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not think that those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty
, he said: They are Jews, to His statement: And the enlightening Book
r
(Al Imran 3:184)

. The first of the two interpretations of this verse is the first interpretation, which is that what is meant by miserliness in this place is the withholding of zakat, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, show that he interpreted his statement,
h
They will be collared by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection

, as he said: The miser who withheld God’s right from him, that it will become a snake around his neck. And because God said after this verse, God has heard the statement of those who said, ‘God is poor, and we are rich,’ so He, may His praise be glorified, described the statement of the polytheists among the Jews who claimed, when God commanded them to pay zakat, that God is poor.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: They will be collared, is that God will make what those who withhold zakat were stingy with, a collar around their necks, like the well-known collars, like the one that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah told me, he said, Muslimah bin Alqamah told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Abdi, he said:
m: There is no servant to whom a relative comes asking him for something he has in excess and he is miserly with him, except that he will bring forth for him what he was miserly with in the form of a bald-headed snake. He said: And he recited: And do not think that those who are miserly with what God has given them of His bounty is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. They will be collared by what they were miserly with on the Day of Resurrection, to the end of the verse.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Qaz’ah, on the authority of a man,
m: “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: ‘There is no relative who comes to his relative and asks him for some of the bounty that God has given him, and he is stingy with it, except that a snake will be brought out for him from Hell, licking its lips until it encircles him.’”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah Muhammad bin Khazim told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Qaza’ah Hajar bin Bayan, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no relative who comes to his relative and asks him for some of the bounty that God has given him, and he is stingy with it, except that a snake will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection from the Fire, which will lick its lips until it encircles him. Then he recited: And never think that
h
those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty
will be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection.”

c: Ziyad bin Ubaidullah Al-Mari told me, he said: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, and Abdullah bin Abdullah Al-Kalabi told me, he said: Abdullah bin Bakr Al-Sahmi told us, and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Abdul Wahid bin Wasil Abu Ubaidah Al-Haddad told us
m: - and the wording is from Yaqub - all of them, on the authority of Bahz bin Hakim bin Muawiyah bin Haidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: I heard the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “No man comes to his master and asks him for some surplus wealth that he has, and he refuses it to him, except that a brave man will be called for him on the Day of Resurrection, licking the surplus that he refused.”
b.via: Abdul Wahid bin Wasil Abu Ubaidah Al-Haddad

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud:
m: They will be collared by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection. He said: A snake will peck at the head of one of them, saying: I am your wealth that you were stingy with!

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said:
m: I heard Abu Wa’il narrating: that he heard Abdullah say about this verse: They will be collared with what they hoarded on Surat Al Imran 3:180
h
And let not those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them
. Rather, it is bad for them.
h
They will be collared by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection
. And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. And God is Acquainted with what you do. the Day of Resurrection, he said: A spike that twists around the head of one of them.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, he said, Khallad bin Aslam told us, he said, Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, similarly - except that they both said:
m: He said: A brave black man.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said:
m: On the Day of Resurrection, his wealth will come to him like a snake, which will peck at his head and say: I am your wealth that you were stingy with! Then it will wrap itself around his neck.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah,
m: who said: Jami’ ibn Abi Rashid and Abd al-Malik ibn A’yan narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no one who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that a bald-headed, brave man will be placed around his neck. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to us:
h
And do not think that those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty
are better for them, the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for they will be collared by what they were stingy with, then on the Day of Resurrection his wealth will be made into a bald-headed snake that will collar him, seize him by the neck, and follow him until it throws him into the Fire.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Abu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said:
m: He is the man whom God provides with wealth, but he prevents his relatives from the right that God has given them in his wealth, so he puts a snake around it and encircles it, and says: What do you have to do with me? He says: I am your wealth.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Masoud about his statement:
h
They will be collared with what they hoarded on the Day of Resurrection
, he said: They will be collared with a bald man whose head will be torn off.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
They will be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection
, so a collar of fire will be placed around their necks.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: They will be encircled by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection, he said: A collar of fire.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
They will be collared with what they hoarded on the Day of Resurrection
, he said: A collar of fire.

c: Al-Hasan told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: They will be collared, he said: A collar of fire.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
They will be collared with what they hoarded on the Day of Resurrection
, he said: A collar of fire.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Those who concealed the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the scholars of the effort, will bear what they concealed of that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They will be collared for what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection

, have you not heard that he said: They are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people (An-Nisa’: 37 - al-Hadid 57:24), meaning the People of the Book, he says: they conceal and enjoin concealment on people.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: They will be asked on the Day of Resurrection to bring what they were stingy with in this world of their money.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They will be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection
, he said: They will be commanded to bring what they were stingy with, to his statement: and the enlightening Book.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: They will be collared, they will be ordered to bring the same amount of their money that they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection.

x: The most correct interpretation of this verse is the interpretation we mentioned at the beginning of His statement: They will be made to wear what they were stingy with, based on the reports we mentioned about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. No one is more knowledgeable about what God Almighty meant by His revelation than he, peace be upon him.
By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that He is the Living One who does not die, and the One who remains after the annihilation of all His creation.
What is the meaning of his saying:
h
He has the inheritance of the heavens and the earth
, and the known inheritance is what is transferred from the possession of an owner to his heir upon his death, and to God belongs the world before the annihilation of His creation and after it?

The meaning of that is what we have described, of His describing Himself as eternal, and informing His creation that they are destined to perish. That is because the kingdom of the owner only becomes an inheritance after his death.

Rather, the Most High said: And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth, informing His servants that the kingdoms of all His creation are transferred from them with their death, and that there is no one except Him who will perish, other than Him. For He is the One who, if He destroys all of His creation and their kingdoms are removed from them, no one will remain who will have what they owned other than Him. The meaning of the verse is: Do not think that
h
those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty

is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them. They will be surrounded by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection, after they perish and their possessions are taken away from them, at a time when they do not own anything, and God’s inheritance and the inheritance of all of His creation will be for Him.

c: Then the Most High informed us that
m: He is aware and knowledgeable about what these people who are stingy with what God has given them of bounty do, and about what others from among His descendants do, and He is aware of all of that, so that He may reward each of them according to what he deserves, the doer of good with good, and the doer of evil according to what He, the Most High, sees fit.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of that differed.
A group of people from Hijaz and Iraq read it: And do not think that those who are stingy with the letter ta are among those who think.
Another group read it as: And do not think with the letter ya.
He said: If this is read with the letter ta’, then the word al-bukhl comes before al-ladhin, and if it is read with the letter ya’, then the word al-bukhl comes after al-ladhin.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads: And do not think, O Muhammad, that the stinginess of those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty is better for them.
So if His statement, And let not those who are stingy think is read with the yaa, then al-muhsaba does not have a noun, and His statement, It is better for them is a predicate of it.

And if it is read with the taa, then His statement, Those who are stingy is a noun for it, and it has conveyed the meaning of stinginess, which is the name of al-muhsaba that was abandoned, and His statement, It is better for them is a predicate of it, so it is in accordance with the well-known eloquent speech of the Arabs.

Therefore, we chose the reading with the taa in that, as we have explained, even though the reading with the yaa is not wrong, but it is not the most eloquent nor the most famous of the speech of the Arabs.

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the interpretation of the verse, which is its interpretation according to what we have chosen from the reading in that: And do not think, O Muhammad, that the miserliness of those who are miserly with what God has given them in this world of wealth, and do not give from it the right of God that He has imposed upon them in it of zakat, is better for them with God on the Day of Resurrection.

x: It was mentioned that this verse and the verses after it were revealed about some Jews who lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mention the effects of that. Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit narrated, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he narrated to him on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him entered the school and found many Jews gathered around a man called Finhas, who was one of their scholars and rabbis, and with him was a rabbi called Ashya. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said to Finhas: Woe to you, Finhas! Fear God and submit to Islam, for by God you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and he has come to you with the truth from God, which you will find written in your Torah and Gospel!

Finhas said: By God, Abu Bakr, we are not poor before God, and He is poor before us! We do not supplicate to Him as He supplicates to us, and we are rich before Him. If He were rich before us, He would not have borrowed from us, as your companion claims! He forbids you from usury, but we give it to you! If He were rich before us, He would not have given us usury! Abu Bakr became angry and slapped Finhas hard in the face and said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would have struck your neck, O enemy of God! So lie to us as much as you can, if you are truthful. Finhas went to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and said: O Muhammad, look at what your companion did to me! The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said to Abu Bakr: What made you do what you did? He said: O Messenger of God, the enemy of God said a terrible thing.

He claimed that God is poor and they are rich without need of Him! When he said that, I became angry for the sake of God because of what he said, so I slapped him in the face. Finhas denied it and said: I did not say that! Then God Almighty revealed what Phinehas said, in response to him and in confirmation of Abu Bakr’s statement: “God has certainly heard the statement of
h
those who say
, ‘God is poor, and we are rich.’
h
We will record what they said and their killing
of the prophets without right, and We will say, ‘Taste the punishment of the burning fire.’” And regarding Abu Bakr’s statement and the anger he received about that:

“And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse. But if you are patient and fear God - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination.”

Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, he said: Abu Bakr entered and mentioned something similar, except that he said: And we are rich from him, and he is not rich from us, even if he were rich, then he mentioned the rest of the hadith similarly.
Muhammad bin Al-Husayn narrated, Ahmad bin Mufaddal narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi: God has heard the statement of
h
those who say

, ‘God is poor, and we are rich.’ This was said by Phinehas the Jew from Banu Marthad. Abu Bakr met him and spoke to him, saying: O Phinehas, fear God, believe, and be truthful, and lend God a good loan! Phinehas said: O Abu Bakr, you claim that our Lord is poor and borrows our money from us! And only the poor borrows from the rich! If what you say is true, then God is indeed poor! So God, the Almighty, revealed this, and Abu Bakr said: “Had it not been for a truce between the Prophet, may God bless him and Surat Al Imran 3:181 God has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, God is poor, and we are rich."
h
We will record what they said and their killing
of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire." grant him peace, and Banu Marthad, I would have killed him.”

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Abu Bakr slapped a man from among those who said: God is poor and we are rich. Why did he not ask us for a loan while he was rich?! And they were Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: Those who said, ‘God is poor, and we are rich,’ why did He not ask us for a loan even though He was rich? Shibl said: It has reached me that he was Phinehas the Jew, and he is the one who said, God is the third of three (al-Ma’idah 5:173), The hand of God is chained (al-Ma’idah 5:4).

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: When the verse: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? (al-Baqarah 2:245 - al-Hadid 57:1 a) was revealed, the Jews said: Your Lord is borrowing from you! So God revealed: “God has certainly heard the statement of those who said: God is poor, and we are rich.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, he said:
m: When the verse: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? (al-Baqarah 2:245) - al-Hadid 57:11] was revealed, he said: The Jews were amazed and said: God is poor and needs a loan! So the verse was revealed: “God has certainly heard the statement of those who said: God is poor, and we are rich.”

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who say

, ‘God is poor, while we are rich,’ he mentioned to us that it was revealed about Huyy ibn Akhtab, when God revealed: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? (al-Baqarah 2:245), he said: Our Lord is asking us for a loan, only the poor person is asking the rich for a loan!

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When the verse: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? (al-Baqarah 2:245) - al-Hadid 57:1] was revealed, the Jews said: Only the poor borrow from the rich!! He said: So God revealed: God has certainly heard the statement of those who said, ‘Indeed, God is poor, and we are rich.’

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His statement:
h
God has heard the statement of those who said
, ‘God is poor, and we are rich,’ he said: These are Jews.

x: The interpretation of the verse is:
h
God has heard the statement of those who said

among the Jews: God is poor in relation to us, and we are rich in relation to Him. We will record what they said of falsehood and slander against their Lord, and their killing of their prophets without right. There is a difference in the reading of his saying:
h
We will record what they said and their killing

. This was read by the people of Hijaz and the majority of the people of Iraq: We will record what they said with the letter nun, “and their killing of the prophets without right” with the word killing in the accusative case.

Some of the Kufi reciters read it as He will write what they said and their killing of the prophets unjustly with the ya’ of He will write and with the damma, and raising the killing, according to the doctrine of what its agent is not named, considering a reading that is mentioned as being from the reading of Abdullah in his saying:
h
And we say

, taste, it is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah: And it is said. The reader of this has overlooked the correctness of what he intended to interpret in the reading attributed to Abdullah, and he has contradicted the proof of the reading of Islam. That is because what is appropriate for the one who reads He will write what they said and the prophets killed them, in the manner of what its agent is not named, is to read and it is said. Rather, his saying
h
and we say

is in apposition to his saying we will write. So the correct reading is to reconcile between them in meaning by reading them both in the manner of what its agent is not named, or in the manner of what its agent is named.

As for one of them reading in the manner of what its agent is not named, and the other in the manner of what its agent is named, without the meaning of ignorance on that, then this is a choice outside the eloquent speech of the Arabs.
The correct reading of this in our view is: We will write with a nun and and kill them in the accusative, because of his saying:
h
and we say
. If the reading of will write had been with a ya and a damma on it, it would have been said: And it is said according to what we have explained.
How was it said: And they killed the prophets unjustly, and it was mentioned in the narrations that were narrated that those meant by his saying:
h
God has heard the statement of those who said

, ‘God is poor,’ were some of the Jews who were at the time of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and none of them killed a prophet of the prophets, but they did not find a prophet of God’s prophets to kill him?

The meaning of that is not in the way you have gone to. Rather, it was said thus, and that those whom God, the Blessed and Exalted, meant by this verse were satisfied with what their predecessors did in killing those prophets whom they killed, and they were among them and on their path of making that permissible and lawful. So God, the Most High, attributed the action of what those who followed his path and method did to all of them, since they were people of one religion and one sect, and with the satisfaction of all of them, what the doer of that did from them did, as we explained of its counterparts in what came before.
By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And We say, to
h
those who say

that God is poor and we are rich, who kill God’s prophets unjustly until the Day of Resurrection, Taste the punishment of the burning fire, meaning by that: the punishment of a burning, blazing fire. Fire is a collective noun for both flaming and non-flaming fires. Fire is an adjective that means it is burning, just as it is said: painful torment meaning: painful, and painful meaning: painful.

evidence.text: There is a difference in the reading of his saying: We will record what they said and their killing.

This was read by the people of Hijaz and the majority of the people of Iraq: We will record what they said with the letter nun, “and their killing of the prophets without right” with the word killing in the accusative case.

Some of the Kufi reciters read it as He will write what they said and their killing of the prophets unjustly with the ya’ of He will write and with the damma, and raising the killing, according to the doctrine of what its agent is not named, considering a reading that is mentioned as being from the reading of Abdullah in his saying: And we say, taste, it is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah: And it is said.
The reader of this has overlooked the correctness of what he intended to interpret in the reading attributed to Abdullah, and he has contradicted the proof of the reading of Islam.
So the correct reading is to reconcile between them in meaning by reading them both in the manner of what its agent is not named, or in the manner of what its agent is named.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading of this in our view is: We will write with a nun and and kill them in the accusative, because of his saying: and we say.
If the reading of will write had been with a ya and a damma on it, it would have been said: And it is said according to what we have explained.

x: As for His statement: That is for what your hands have put forth, meaning: Our statement to them on the Day of Resurrection, Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire, for what your hands have put forth and acquired during your life in this world, and that God is just and does not wrong, so He punishes a servant of His without him deserving punishment, but He rewards every soul for what it has earned, and He pays every worker the recompense of what he has done. So He punished those to whom He said [that] on the Day of Resurrection - from among the Jews, whose characteristics He described, and He informed about them that they said: Indeed, God is poor and we are rich, and they killed the prophets unjustly - with what He punished them with of the punishment of the Burning Fire, for what they acquired of sins, and committed of evil deeds, and lied about God after He had warned them. So the Most High was not unjust in what He punished them with by making them taste the punishment of the Burning Fire, nor was He imposing His punishment on those who did not deserve it. And so He, may His praise be glorified, does not wrong any of His creation, but He is just among them, and bestows upon all of them what He loves of His bounties and blessings.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He meant: God heard the words of those who said: God has commanded us not to believe in any Messenger. His saying: Those who said that God is in the accusative case in response to his saying: Those who said that God is poor. What he means by his saying: They said, ‘God has enjoined upon us that we should not believe any Messenger,’ he commanded us, and it came to us in His books and on the tongues of His prophets, that we should not believe any Messenger, meaning that we should not believe any Messenger in what he says he brought from God of commands and prohibitions and other things, until he brings us an offering that the Fire will consume, meaning that he brings us an offering: which is what the servant draws near to his Lord with in charity. It is a source like aggression and loss from your saying: I offered a sacrifice.

And he said: The fire will eat it, and the fire eating what one of them offered to God at that time was evidence of God’s acceptance of what he offered to Him, and evidence of the truthfulness of the one offering in what he claimed that he was right in what he disputed or said, like:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Until he brings us an offering that the fire will consume
, a man would give charity, and when it was accepted from him, fire would descend upon him from the sky and consume him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
With an offering that the fire consumes

, that if a man gave charity and it was accepted from him, God would send a fire from the sky that descended upon the offering and consumed it. God the Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say: God has enjoined upon us that we should not believe in a Messenger until he brings us an offering that is consumed by fire: There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs, meaning: with arguments indicating the truth of their prophethood and the reality of their words, and with that which you have said, meaning: and with that which you claimed that if he brought it, you would have to believe him and acknowledge his prophethood, from the one whose offering is consumed by fire if he offers it to God as evidence of his truthfulness, so why did you kill them if you should be truthful? He says to him: Say to them: The messengers who were before me came to you with that which you claimed was their argument against you, so you killed them, so why did you kill them while you acknowledge that what they brought to you was their argument against you, if you should be truthful, in that God enjoined upon you to believe in whoever came to you from His messengers with an offering that is consumed by fire as an argument for his prophethood?

x: God informed His servants by this verse that those who described their description from the Jews who were at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will not be more than a spoil of their lies against God, their fabrications against their Lord, and their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they knew him to be truthful and just, and their denial of his prophethood while they found it written with them in the covenant of God Almighty to them that he is His Messenger to His creation, and obedience to him is obligatory, except like those who passed from their ancestors who used to kill the prophets of God after cutting off their excuse with the arguments that God supported them with, and the evidence with which He demonstrated their truthfulness, fabricating against God and belittling His rights.

This is a consolation from God, the Most High, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the harm he was suffering from the Jews and the polytheists from all other religions. God the Most High says to him: Do not be sad, O Muhammad, for the lies of those who said: God is poor, and said: God has commanded us not to believe in any Messenger until he brings us a sacrifice that the fire will consume.* And their fabrication against their Lord was deceived by God's respite for them. And do not let their denial of you and their false claims of God's covenants to them be too great for you, for if they did that to you, then they have lied about you and lied about God, for their predecessors from the Messengers of God before you lied about those who came to them with conclusive arguments, dazzling evidence, and miraculous signs of creation, and that is the clear evidence.

As for Zabar, it is the plural of Zabur, which is the book, and every book is a Zabur. From this comes the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: For whom did I see the ruins that made me sad like the lines of a psalm on a Yemeni palm branch? By the Book he means the Torah and the Gospel. This is because the Jews denied Jesus and what he brought, and distorted what Moses, peace be upon him, brought about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and changed his covenant with them about him, and the Christians denied what was in the Gospel about his description, and changed what he commanded them to do about him. As for his saying: the semen, he means: that which illuminates and clarifies the truth for those who are confused and explains it. Rather, it comes from light and illumination. It is said: This matter has illuminated you, meaning: it has become clear and evident to you.
So it illuminates, and the thing is illuminated.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
If they deny you
, then messengers before you were denied. He said: He was consoling his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If they deny you

, then messengers before you were denied, he said: He is consoling his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This letter is in the Qur’ans of the people of Hijaz, Iraq, and Az-Zubar without the letter la, and in the Qur’an of the people of Ash-Sham it is: and Az-Zubar with the

x: By that, the Most High means: that the fate of these slanderers against God from among the Jews, who denied His Messenger, whose characteristics He described and informed about their audacity towards their Lord, and the fate of all others from among His creation, the Most High, and the return of all of them, is to Him. Because He has decreed death for all of them, so He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not be saddened by the denial of those who lied to you, O Muhammad, from among these Jews and others, and the slander of those who slandered me, for messengers before you denied the signs and proofs to whom they were sent, like what you brought to whom you were sent. So in them you have an example from which you can take comfort. The fate of those who lied about me and others and their return is to Me. I will give each soul the reward of their deeds on the Day of Resurrection, as the Most High said: And you will only be given your full compensation on the Day of Resurrection, meaning: the rewards for your deeds, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

So whoever is drawn away from the Fire, meaning: whoever is removed from the Fire and kept farther from it, has attained success, meaning: he has been saved and has attained his need. It is said: So-and-so won his request, he won a victory, a triumph, and a triumph, if he got it. Rather, the meaning of this is: Whoever is kept away from the Fire, kept far from it, and admitted to Paradise, has been saved and attained great honor. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion, meaning: And what are the pleasures and desires of this world, and what are its adornments and decorations, except the enjoyment of delusion, meaning: Except for the enjoyment that delusion and deception give you, which has no reality when tested, and no validity when tried. So you enjoy what delusion gives you of your world, then it will return to you with calamities, misfortunes, and hardships.

God the Most High says: And do not incline toward this world, lest you become content with it. For you are only enjoying yourself in delusion from it, then after a short while you will depart from it.
It has been narrated in the interpretation of this, what:

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Juwaybir narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Sabit,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion

, he said: Like the provisions of a shepherd, who supplies him with a handful of dates, or some flour, or something with which he drinks milk. So Ibn Sabit went in this interpretation of his, to the meaning of the verse: And the life of this world is nothing but a little enjoyment, which does not reach his enjoyment, nor is it sufficient for his journey. And this interpretation, even if it is one of the aspects of interpretation, then the correct statement about it is what we have said. Because deception is only deception in the speech of the Arabs, and since that is the case, there is no reason to divert it to the meaning of little, because something may be little and its owner is not deceived or deluded by it. As for the one who is in delusion, neither a little nor a lot of what is in his delusion is valid. Deception is a source of the saying of the one who says: So-and-so deceived me, so he deceives me with deception, with the damma of the ghain. As for if the ghain of delusion is opened, it is an attribute of the deceitful devil, who deceives the son of Adam until he enters into the disobedience of God in what deserves His punishment. And: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abda and Abd al-Rahim told us, they said, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The space of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. And read, if you wish: ‘
h
And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion

x: What is meant by the words of God Almighty: You will surely be tested in your wealth, you will be tested with calamities in your wealth, and yourselves, meaning: and with the destruction of relatives and clans from the people of your support and your religion, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you, meaning: from the Jews and their saying: Indeed, God is poor and we are rich, and their saying: The hand of God is chained (al-Ma’idah 5:64), and what is similar to that of their fabrications against God, and from those who associate others with God, meaning the Christians, much harm, and the harm from the Jews is what we mentioned, and from the Christians their saying: The Messiah is the son of God (al-Tawbah 9:35), and what is similar to that of their disbelief in God, and if you are patient and fear God, meaning: and if you are patient with the command of God that He commanded you with regard to them and others of His obedience, and fear God, meaning: and fear God in what He commanded you and forbade you, so you act in This is by obeying Him, for this is among the matters that are determined. He says: For this patience and piety are among the matters that God has determined and commanded you to do.
It was said: All of this was revealed about Phinehas the Jew, the master of Banu Qaynuqa, as the one who:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ikrimah said
m: regarding the words of God, You will surely be tested in your wealth and your lives, and you will hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse, he said: This verse was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and about Finhas the Jew, the master of Banu Qaynuqa. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God have mercy on him, to Finhas to ask for help, and he wrote to him a letter, and said to Abu Bakr: Do not tempt me with anything until you return. So Abu Bakr came wearing his sword, and he gave him the letter, and when he read it he said: Your Lord needs us to help Him! Abu Bakr wanted to strike him with the sword, then he remembered the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not tempt me with anything until you return, so he refrained, and the verse was revealed: “And let not those who withhold what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them. Rather, it is bad for them.”
r
(Al Imran 3:80)
. And between the two verses up to His saying:
h
You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves

, these verses were revealed about Banu Qaynuqa’ up to His saying: If they deny you, [O Muhammad], [other] messengers before you were denied, Ibn Jurayj said: He was consoling His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said:
h
You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves

, he said: God informed the believers that He would test them, to see how patient they were in their religion. Then He said: And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you, meaning the Jews and Christians, and from those who associate others with God, much abuse, so the Muslims would hear the Jews say: Ezra is the son of God (al-Tawbah 9:30), and from the Christians: The Messiah is the son of God (al-Tawbah 9:30). So the Muslims would set up war against them when they heard their association with God, so God said: But if you are patient and fear God - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination, meaning: of the strength of what God has determined and commanded you to do.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed about Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf, because he used to satirize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and flirt with Muslim women.

Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, regarding the statement of God, And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God, much abuse, he said: He is Ka’b bin al-Ashraf, and he used to incite the polytheists against Surat Al Imran 3:186
h
You will surely be tested in your wealth and yourselves

, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God much abuse. But if you are patient and fear God - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination. the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in his poetry, and he used to satirize the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Five men from the Ansar went to him, among them Muhammad bin Maslama and a man called Abu Abbas.

They came to him while he was in a gathering of his people in al-Awali. When he saw them, he was terrified of them and disapproved of their behavior. They said: We have come to you for a need! He said: Let one of you come close to me and tell me about his need. Then one of them came to him and said: We have come to you to sell you some armor from us so that we may spend on it. He said: By God, if you do that, you will have been exhausted since this man has come to you! They promised to come to him at dinner when the people had calmed down. So they came to him and called him. His wife said: Why have these people come to you at this hour for something you like? He said: They told me about their story and their affairs. Muammar said: Ayoub informed me, on the authority of Ikrimah: He looked down upon them and spoke to them and said: Do you pledge your sons to me? They wanted to sell them dates.

He said: They said: We are too shy to lend our sons and it would be said: This is a hostage of one wasq, and this is a hostage of two wasqs! He said: Do you pledge your women to me? They said: You are the most beautiful of people, and we do not trust you! And what woman would resist you because of your beauty! But we will pledge our weapons to you, for you know our need for weapons today. He said: Bring me your weapons, and take whatever you wish. They said: Then come down to us, so that we may take from you and you may take from us. So he went down, but his wife clung to him and said: Send for others like them from your people to be with you. He said: If these people had found me asleep, they would not have woken me! She said: So speak to them from the top of the house, but he refused, so he came down to them and his fragrance spread. They said: What is this smell, O so-and-so? He said: This is the perfume of so-and-so’s wife.

Some of them approached him, smelled his scent, then embraced him and said: Kill the enemy of God! Abu Abs stabbed him in the side, and Muhammad ibn Maslama struck him with the sword, and they killed him and then returned. The Jews were terrified, so they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Our master was killed by treachery! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reminded them of what he had done, and how he had incited them and urged them to fight them and harm them, then he called upon them to write a peace treaty between him and them. He said: So that letter was with Ali, may God be pleased with him.

evidence.text: So Abu Bakr came wearing his sword, and he gave him the letter, and when he read it he said: Your Lord needs us to help Him!

x: By that, the Most High means: And also mention the [matter] of these Jews and others from the People of the Book among them, O Muhammad, when God took a covenant from them to make clear to the people your matter which He took a covenant from them to make clear to the people in their book which is in their hands, which is the Torah and the Gospel, and that you are a Messenger of God sent with the truth and they will not conceal it, but they cast it behind their backs, meaning: So they abandoned the matter of God and wasted it, and broke His covenant which He took from them regarding that, so they concealed your matter and denied you, and purchased with it a small price, meaning: And they purchased with their concealment what they took a covenant from not concealing the matter of your prophethood, in exchange for it a small, worthless worldly gain. Then the Most High condemned their purchase of what they purchased with that, saying: So evil is that which they purchase.
The interpreters differed as to who was meant by this verse.
Some of them said: It was meant specifically for the Jews.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, on the authority of Ikrimah: that he told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture
, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it,’ until His saying: A painful punishment, meaning Phinehas, Ash’a, and those like them among the rabbis.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad,
m: the client of Zaid ibn Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah, the client of Ibn Abbas, the same.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture

, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it.’ But they cast it behind their backs, He commanded them to follow the unlettered Prophet who believed in God and His words, and He said: Follow him that you may be guided.
r
(Al-Aʿraf: 158)

. So when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He said: “Fulfill My covenant, and I will fulfill your covenant. And fear only Me.” (al-Baqarah 2:45), He made a covenant with them on that, and He said when He sent Muhammad: Believe in him, and you will find what you love with Me.

c: Muhammad told us, Ahmad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture

, ‘You shall make it clear to the people,’ the verse. He said: God took a covenant from the Jews to make it clear to the people, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not to conceal it, but they threw it behind their backs and purchased with it a small price.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu al-Juhaf, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, he said:
m: Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf asked his companions about this verse:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture
, so a man stood up to Saeed bin Jubair and asked him, so he said:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture
, the Jews, to make it clear to the people, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not to conceal it, so they rejected it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: his saying:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture

, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it.’ He said: It was in it that Islam is the religion of God that He imposed upon His servants, and that they find Muhammad written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

x: Others said: He meant by that everyone who was given knowledge of the matter of religion.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And [mention] when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it.’ But they threw it behind their backs. This is a covenant that God took from the people of knowledge. Whoever knows something, let him teach it. Beware of concealing knowledge, for concealing knowledge is destruction. And let no man undertake what he has no knowledge of, lest he depart from the religion of God and be among those who undertake. It was said: The Surat Al Imran 3:187
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture

, "You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it behind their backs and purchased with it a small price. So evil is that which they purchase. likeness of knowledge that is not spoken is like the likeness of a treasure from which no money is spent! And the likeness of wisdom that is not brought forth is like the likeness of an idol that neither eats nor drinks. And it was said: Blessed is the speaking scholar, and blessed is the attentive listener. This is a man who learned knowledge, taught it, gave it away, and called to it, and a man who heard good, memorized it, retained it, and benefited from it.

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Masoudi told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, he said:
m: A man came to some people in the mosque in which Abdullah bin Masoud was, and said: Your brother Ka’b sends you his greetings and gives you good report that this verse does not apply to you:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture
to make it clear to the people and not to conceal it. Abdullah said to him: And you too.

c: So he greeted him and told him that
m: it was revealed while he was a Jew.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah,
m: similarly, on the authority of Abdullah and Ka’b. Others said: The meaning of this is: And when God took a covenant from the prophets from their people.

x: Those who said this mentioned:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said, Yahya bin Abi Thabit told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: I said to Ibn Abbas: The companions of Abdullah read: And when your Lord took from those who were given the Scripture their covenant, he said: From the prophets over their people.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Qubaysah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed, who said,
m: I said to Ibn Abbas: The companions of Abdullah used to recite:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture
, “And when God took a covenant from the prophets,” he said, so he said: God took a covenant from the prophets from their people. As for His statement:
h
You will make it clear to the people
, it is as follows:

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad bin Abdul Warith told us, he said, my father told me, he said, Muhammad bin Dhakwan told us, he said, Abu Naamah Al-Saadi told us:
m: Al-Hasan used to interpret his statement:
h
And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture
, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it,’ as: You shall speak the truth and confirm it with your actions.

x: The reciters differed in the recitation of that: Some of them read it as that you may make it clear to the people and not conceal it with a ta’. This is the reading most often recited by the people of Medina and Kufa, in the manner of the addressee, meaning: God said to them: that you may make it clear to the people and not conceal it.

Others read it: He will make it clear to the people and not conceal it with both yas, as a report on the absent person. However, at the time God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that about them, they were not present, so the report on them became like the report on the absent person.

The statement in this regard, according to us, is that they are two readings, their aspects are correct, they are widespread in the reading of Islam, and they do not differ in meanings. So whichever of them the reader reads, he has reached the truth and the right in that. However, even if this is the case, the reading I prefer is: that you may make it clear to the people and not conceal it, with both ya’s, based on his statement: so they cast it aside, since it had been presented as report of the absent person, in the manner of his statement: so they cast it aside, so that it would all be consistent with one meaning and one example. If the first had been in the sense of address, it would have been more appropriate to say: so you cast it behind your backs, than to say: so they cast it behind their backs. As for his saying:
h
And they threw it behind their backs
, it is an example of their neglect of fulfilling the covenant and their failure to act upon it.

We have already explained the meaning for which this was said in the previous part of this book, so we did not want to repeat it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub Al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they threw it behind their backs
, he said: They used to recite it, but they threw away the practice of it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And they cast it behind their backs, he said: They cast the covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told me, he said, Uthman bin Umar told us, he said, Malik bin Mughul told us:
m: I was told on the authority of Al-Sha’bi regarding this verse: And they cast it behind their backs, he said: They threw it in front of them, and stopped acting upon it. As for his saying:
h
And they bought with it a small price
, its meaning is what we said, that they took what they took for concealing the truth and distorting the Book, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they bought with it a small price
, they took it out of greed, and concealed the name of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And his saying:
h
So evil is what they buy
, meaning:
h
So evil is what they buy
in their neglect of the covenant and their alteration of the Book, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: How evil is that which they buy, he said: The Jews’ alteration of the Torah.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reciters differed in the recitation of that: Some of them read it as that you may make it clear to the people and not conceal it with a ta’.
This is the reading most often recited by the people of Medina and Kufa, in the manner of the addressee, meaning: God said to them: that you may make it clear to the people and not conceal it.
Others read it: He will make it clear to the people and not conceal it with both yas, as a report on the absent person.

Abu Jaafar said: The statement in this regard, according to us, is that they are two readings, their aspects are correct, they are widespread in the reading of Islam, and they do not differ in meanings.

However, even if this is the case, the reading I prefer is: that you may make it clear to the people and not conceal it, with both ya’s, based on his statement: so they cast it aside, since it had been presented as report of the absent person, in the manner of his statement: so they cast it aside, so that it would all be consistent with one meaning and one example.

Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub Al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: And they threw it behind their backs, he said: They used to recite it, but they threw away the practice of it.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: What he meant by that were a group of hypocrites who used to sit behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the enemy attacked. Then, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left, they would apologize to him and would like to be praised for what they had not done.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar and Ibn Abd al-Raheem al-Barqi told us, they said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Abi Katheer told us, he said: Zayd ibn Aslam told me, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri:
m: That there were men from among the hypocrites during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to fight, they stayed behind him, and they were happy to stay behind the Messenger of God. And when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from a journey, they would apologize to him, and they wanted to be praised for what they had not done. So God, the Most High, revealed about them:
h
Think not of those who rejoice in what they have done
, the verse.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done

, he said: These are the hypocrites, they say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you had gone out, we would have gone out with you! So when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, they stayed behind and lied, and they rejoiced at that, and they saw it as a trick they had devised.

x: Others said: He meant by that a group of Jewish rabbis, who were happy to mislead people and attribute knowledge to them.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad,
m: the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah, the client of Ibn Abbas or Saʿid ibn Jubayr: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture until His saying:
h
And for them is a painful punishment
